label: TauCeti.Contour.continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance
docstring: **The generalized winding number is continuous in the point, off the curve.** If `γ` is continuous on `Set.uIcc a b`, avoids `w₀` there, and the index integrand `(γ · - w₀)⁻¹ * deriv γ` at `w₀` is interval-integrable, then `fun w ↦ windingNumber γ a b w` is continuous at `w₀`, on an arbitrary oriented interval. The stated hypothesis matches `windingNumber_eq_integral_of_avoidance` and `exists_int_windingNumber_of_closed`.
code:
theorem continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w₀ : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Set.uIcc a b)) (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w₀)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w₀)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ContinuousAt (fun w ↦ windingNumber γ a b w) w₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance_of_le
docstring: The `a ≤ b` case of `continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance`.
code:
private theorem continuousAt_windingNumber_of_avoidance_of_le {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w₀ : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hab : a ≤ b) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b)) (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t ≠ w₀)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ContinuousAt (fun w ↦ windingNumber γ a b w) w₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.continuousOn_deriv_comp_reparam
docstring: Continuity of the derivative of the reparametrized curve on `[[a, b]]`, the regularity every consumer of the reparametrized contour integrand needs for integrability. As elsewhere, `φ` has an ambient derivative `φ' t` at each `t ∈ [[a, b]]` with `φ'` continuous there, and `γ` is ambient-differentiable with continuous derivative on the swept image `φ '' [[a, b]]`.
code:
theorem continuousOn_deriv_comp_reparam
    (hφ : ∀ t ∈ Set.uIcc a b, HasDerivAt φ (φ' t) t)
    (hφ' : ContinuousOn φ' (Set.uIcc a b))
    (hγ : ∀ u ∈ φ '' Set.uIcc a b, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ u)
    (hγ' : ContinuousOn (deriv γ) (φ '' Set.uIcc a b)) :
    ContinuousOn (deriv (γ ∘ φ)) (Set.uIcc a b) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.continuousOn_im_log_segRatio
docstring: Each summand in the telescoping arg-lift sum is continuous.
code:
private theorem continuousOn_im_log_segRatio {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b)) {w : ℂ} {δ' ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ)
    (h_dist_lb : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖)
    (h_unif : ∀ t s : ℝ, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b →
      |t - s| < δ' → ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2)
    {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b) (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (h_mesh : s_jp1 - s_j < δ') :
    ContinuousOn (fun t ↦ (Complex.log (segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t)).im)
      (Icc a b) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.continuousOn_segRatio
docstring: Continuity of `t ↦ segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t` on `Icc a b`.
code:
private theorem continuousOn_segRatio {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    {w : ℂ} {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b)
    (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b) (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) :
    ContinuousOn (fun t ↦ segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t) (Icc a b) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.countable_setOf_deriv_ne_zero_on_fiber
docstring: On the level set `{x | g x = c}`, the derivative of `g` vanishes off a countable set: a point of the level set with nonzero derivative cannot be an accumulation point of the level set (else its derivative would be `0` by `deriv_zero_of_frequently_const`), hence it is isolated on the left in the level set, and left-isolated points of a set in `ℝ` form a countable set.
code:
private theorem countable_setOf_deriv_ne_zero_on_fiber (g : ℝ → ℂ) (c : ℂ) :
    {x : ℝ | g x = c ∧ deriv g x ≠ 0}.Countable := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle
docstring: **Crossing angle** of `γ : ℝ → ℂ` at a time `t₀`, valued in `[0, 2π)`: the opening angle of the model sector, from the reversed entry tangent `−L₋` to the exit tangent `L₊`, taken `mod 2π`. Here `L₋ = lim_{t → t₀⁻} γ'(t)`, `L₊ = lim_{t → t₀⁺} γ'(t)` are the one-sided limits of `deriv γ`. The normalization keeps it nonnegative: a **smooth** crossing (`L₊ = L₋`) gives `π`, as in HW §3. As a `limUnder`-based value it is junk when a one-sided tangent fails to exist; it is meaningful at the corners/crossings of a piecewise-`C¹` curve.
code: def crossingAngle (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) : ℝ :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_eq_pi
docstring: **Smooth-crossing value.** If the one-sided tangents of `γ` at `t₀` agree and are nonzero, the crossing angle is `π`: there is no genuine corner.
code:
theorem crossingAngle_eq_pi {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ}
    (h : limUnder (𝓝[<] t₀) (deriv γ) = limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ))
    (hL : limUnder (𝓝[>] t₀) (deriv γ) ≠ 0) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ = Real.pi := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_lt_two_pi
code:
@[simp] theorem crossingAngle_lt_two_pi (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ < 2 * Real.pi :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_mem_Ico
docstring: `crossingAngle γ t₀` lies in `[0, 2π)`, the range of the model-sector normalization. Its two projections `crossingAngle_nonneg`/`crossingAngle_lt_two_pi` are the `@[simp]` normal forms.
code:
theorem crossingAngle_mem_Ico (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) :
    crossingAngle γ t₀ ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossingAngle_nonneg
code: @[simp] theorem crossingAngle_nonneg (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (t₀ : ℝ) : 0 ≤ crossingAngle γ t₀ :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_atMostOne_of_dual_deriv_pos
docstring: **At-most-one-crossing core.** If a continuous linear functional is positive on `deriv γ` throughout an open interval on which `γ` is differentiable, then that functional of `γ - z₀` is strictly monotone on the closed interval, so `γ` meets `z₀` at most once there.
code:
private theorem crossing_atMostOne_of_dual_deriv_pos {f : StrongDual ℝ ℂ} {c d : ℝ}
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc c d))
    (h_cond : ∀ t ∈ Ioo c d, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t ∧ 0 < f (deriv γ t)) :
    ∀ t₁ ∈ Icc c d, ∀ t₂ ∈ Icc c d, γ t₁ = z₀ → γ t₂ = z₀ → t₁ = t₂ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_isolated_left
docstring: Crossings of an immersion are isolated from the left: if `γ t₀ = z₀` with `t₀ ∈ (min, max]`, then `γ t ≠ z₀` for `t` in a punctured left neighbourhood of `t₀`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossing_isolated_right
docstring: Crossings of an immersion are isolated from the right: if `γ t₀ = z₀` with `t₀ ∈ [min, max)`, then `γ t ≠ z₀` for `t` in a punctured right neighbourhood of `t₀`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossings_bounded_from_endpoints
docstring: A finite subset of the open interval `(a, b)` is uniformly separated from both endpoints.
code:
private theorem crossings_bounded_from_endpoints {a b : ℝ} {crossings : Finset ℝ}
    (h_nonempty : crossings.Nonempty)
    (h_Ioo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t ∈ Ioo a b) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ t ∈ crossings, a + c ≤ t ∧ t ≤ b - c := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.crossings_bounded_from_exceptional
docstring: A finite set disjoint from a finite exceptional set is uniformly separated from it.
code:
private theorem crossings_bounded_from_exceptional {crossings P : Finset ℝ}
    (h_nonempty : crossings.Nonempty)
    (h_off : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t ∉ P) :
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ p ∈ P, c ≤ |t - p| := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.depthTerm_le_of_sub
docstring: Pole depth `(-order.untop₀).toNat` does not increase when the order stays at or above a minimum taken with a nonnegative order: if `min oF oP ≤ oG` and `0 ≤ oP`, the depth of `oG` is at most that of `oF`. (`oG` is the order of `F − P` where `P` is analytic — `oP ≥ 0` — at the point.)
code:
private lemma depthTerm_le_of_sub {oF oP oG : WithTop ℤ} (hP : 0 ≤ oP) (hG : min oF oP ≤ oG) :
    (-oG.untop₀).toNat ≤ (-oF.untop₀).toNat := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.depthTerm_lt_of_lt
docstring: Pole depth strictly decreases when the order strictly rises above a negative integer order: if `n < 0` and `n < oG`, the depth of `oG` is strictly less than the depth `(-n).toNat` of `n`.
code:
private lemma depthTerm_lt_of_lt {n : ℤ} {oG : WithTop ℤ} (hn : n < 0)
    (hlt : (n : WithTop ℤ) < oG) : (-oG.untop₀).toNat < (-n).toNat := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_comp_reparam
docstring: Chain rule for a reparametrized curve, in `deriv` form: `deriv (γ ∘ φ) t = φ' t • deriv γ (φ t)`. A one-step restatement of Mathlib's `HasDerivAt.scomp`, kept private as the internal step behind the set-level `eqOn_deriv_comp_reparam`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.deriv_ne_zero_off_breakpoints
docstring: Differentiability and a non-zero derivative at interior non-breakpoint parameters, relative to a breakpoint witness of the immersion clause.
code:
private theorem deriv_ne_zero_off_breakpoints {p : Finset ℝ}
    (hpieces : ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
      ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧ ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b)) (htp : t ∉ (↑p : Set ℝ)) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t ∧ deriv γ t ≠ 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.differentiableAt_dixonH1_integral
docstring: Pointwise differentiability of `dixonH1`'s integral form at `w₀ ∈ U`, via the parametric Leibniz rule with `F' w t = deriv (dslope f (γ t)) w · deriv γ t`, dominated near `w₀` by Cauchy's estimate on a ball avoiding the boundary of `U`.
code:
private theorem differentiableAt_dixonH1_integral (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hw₀ : w₀ ∈ U) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w ↦ ∫ t in a..b, dslope f w (γ t) * deriv γ t) w₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.differentiableAt_dixonH2
docstring: **`dixonH2` is holomorphic in the point, off the curve.** If `γ` is continuous on `uIcc a b` and avoids `w` there, and the Cauchy integrand `f (γ ·) / (γ · - w) · deriv γ` is interval-integrable, then `fun w ↦ dixonH2 f γ a b w` is complex-differentiable at `w`.
code:
theorem differentiableAt_dixonH2 (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w)
    (h_cauchy_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (dixonH2 f γ a b) w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.differentiableOn_dixonH1
docstring: **`dixonH1` is holomorphic on the region.** For `f` differentiable on the open set `U`, and `γ` continuous on `uIcc a b` with `deriv γ` interval-integrable and image in `U`, the map `fun w ↦ dixonH1 f γ a b w` is complex-differentiable on `U`.
code:
theorem differentiableOn_dixonH1 (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    DifferentiableOn ℂ (dixonH1 f γ a b) U := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.differentiable_dixonFunction
docstring: **The Dixon function is entire.** For `f` differentiable on the open set `U`, a closed curve `γ` that is continuous on `uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable subset, with interval-integrable derivative, image in `U`, and null-homologous in `U`, the glued function `dixonFunction f U γ a b` is complex-differentiable on all of `ℂ`. This specialises `differentiable_dixonFunction_of_windingNumber_zero_near`, discharging its local winding hypothesis via `exists_ball_windingNumber_zero`.
code:
theorem differentiable_dixonFunction (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_null : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) :
    Differentiable ℂ (dixonFunction f U γ a b) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.differentiable_dixonFunction_of_windingNumber_zero_near
docstring: **Analytic gluing of the Dixon function.** If `f` is differentiable on the open set `U`, the curve `γ` is continuous on `uIcc a b` with image in `U` and interval-integrable derivative, and around every point `w ∉ U` the winding number vanishes on an entire ball that stays off the curve, then `dixonFunction f U γ a b` is complex-differentiable on all of `ℂ`. On `U` it agrees with the holomorphic `dixonH1`; off `U` (hence off the curve) it agrees with the holomorphic `dixonH2`, and the two pieces match across `∂U` because the local winding hypothesis collapses the `h₁`/`h₂` identity.
code:
private theorem differentiable_dixonFunction_of_windingNumber_zero_near (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (h_local : ∀ w ∉ U, ∃ ε > 0, ∀ w' ∈ Metric.ball w ε,
      (∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w') ∧ windingNumber γ a b w' = 0) :
    Differentiable ℂ (dixonFunction f U γ a b) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.div_mem_slitPlane_of_close_to_one
docstring: **Slit-plane condition for quotients near `1`.** If `‖z - 1‖ ≤ 1/4` and `‖w - 1‖ ≤ 1/4`, then `z / w ∈ Complex.slitPlane`: the quotient stays in the unit ball around `1`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.div_norm_eq_exp_arg_mul_I
docstring: **A nonzero complex number over its norm is the exponential of its argument**: `w / ↑‖w‖ = exp(arg w · I)`.
code:
theorem div_norm_eq_exp_arg_mul_I {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    w / (‖w‖ : ℂ) = Complex.exp ((Complex.arg w : ℂ) * Complex.I) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_eq_dixonH1
docstring: On `U`, the glued Dixon function is `dixonH1`.
code:
theorem dixonFunction_eq_dixonH1 {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ}
    (hw : w ∈ U) : dixonFunction f U γ a b w = dixonH1 f γ a b w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_eq_dixonH2
docstring: Off `U`, the glued Dixon function is `dixonH2`.
code:
theorem dixonFunction_eq_dixonH2 {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ}
    (hw : w ∉ U) : dixonFunction f U γ a b w = dixonH2 f γ a b w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_eq_dixonH2_of_windingNumber_zero
docstring: **Off the curve with vanishing winding number, `dixonFunction` equals `dixonH2`.** For `w` off the curve with `windingNumber γ a b w = 0` and the Cauchy integrand `f (γ ·) / (γ · - w) · deriv γ` interval-integrable, the two branches of `dixonFunction` agree: on `U` the `h₁`/`h₂` identity collapses because the winding term vanishes, and off `U` it is `dixonH2` by definition. Only integrability is needed, not holomorphy of `f`; when `f` is differentiable on `U ⊇ γ` the integrand hypothesis is discharged by `cauchy_integrand_intervalIntegrable`. This is the pointwise gluing fact shared by the analyticity of `dixonFunction` and its vanishing at infinity.
code:
theorem dixonFunction_eq_dixonH2_of_windingNumber_zero (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (h_cauchy_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) (hwn : windingNumber γ a b w = 0) :
    dixonFunction f U γ a b w = dixonH2 f γ a b w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_eq_zero
docstring: **The Dixon function is identically zero (Liouville).** For a closed curve `γ`, null-homologous in an open set `U` (continuous on `uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable set, with interval-integrable derivative and image in `U`) and `f` differentiable on `U`, the entire function `dixonFunction f U γ a b` tends to `0` at infinity, so Liouville's theorem forces it to vanish at every point.
code:
theorem dixonFunction_eq_zero (hU : IsOpen U) (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_null : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) (w : ℂ) : dixonFunction f U γ a b w = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_eventually_eq_dixonH2
docstring: **The Dixon function eventually agrees with `dixonH2` along `cocompact ℂ`.** For a closed curve `γ` continuous on `uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable set, with interval-integrable derivative and image in `U`, every `w` far from the origin lies off the curve with winding number `0` (`windingNumber_eventually_zero_cocompact`). There `dixonFunction = dixonH2`: off `U` by definition, and on `U` because the vanishing winding number collapses the `h₁`/`h₂` identity.
code:
private theorem dixonFunction_eventually_eq_dixonH2 (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t) :
    ∀ᶠ w in cocompact ℂ, dixonFunction f U γ a b w = dixonH2 f γ a b w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonFunction_tendsto_zero
docstring: **The Dixon function tends to `0` along `cocompact ℂ`.** It eventually agrees with `dixonH2`, which tends to `0` by the `L¹` decay bound: the image of the compact interval `uIcc a b` is bounded (`IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn`), and the weight `f (γ ·) * deriv γ` is interval-integrable (continuous `f ∘ γ` times the interval-integrable derivative).
code:
private theorem dixonFunction_tendsto_zero (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t) :
    Tendsto (dixonFunction f U γ a b) (cocompact ℂ) (nhds 0) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH1_eq_dixonH2_sub_windingNumber_mul_f
docstring: **The `h₁`/`h₂` identity.** For `γ` continuous on `uIcc a b` and `w` off the curve, with the index and Cauchy-type integrands interval-integrable, `dixonH1 f γ a b w` differs from `dixonH2 f γ a b w` by exactly `2πi · n(γ, w) · f w`, the generalized winding number of `γ` about `w` scaled by `f w`.
code:
theorem dixonH1_eq_dixonH2_sub_windingNumber_mul_f {f : ℂ → ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ}
    (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w)
    (h_cauchy_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (h_base_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    dixonH1 f γ a b w =
      dixonH2 f γ a b w - 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b w * f w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero
docstring: **Cauchy's integral formula from pointwise Dixon-vanishing.** If Dixon's glued function vanishes at `w ∈ U` (`dixonFunction f U γ a b w = 0`), then for `γ` continuous on `uIcc a b` and avoiding `w` with the Cauchy-type and index integrands interval-integrable, the Cauchy-type integral evaluates to `dixonH2 f γ a b w = 2πi · n(γ, w) · f w`: on `U` the vanishing collapses the `h₁`/`h₂` identity, whose winding term is exactly this value. Discharging the vanishing hypothesis via `dixonFunction_eq_zero` gives Cauchy's integral formula for a null-homologous curve.
code:
theorem dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ}
    {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ} (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (hw : w ∈ U)
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) (h_zero_at : dixonFunction f U γ a b w = 0)
    (h_cauchy_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (h_base_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    dixonH2 f γ a b w = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b w * f w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_nullHomologous
docstring: **Null-homologous Cauchy integral formula at an off-curve point.** Let `γ` be a closed curve in an open set `U`, continuous on `uIcc a b`, differentiable off a countable set, with interval-integrable derivative, and null-homologous in `U`. If `f` is holomorphic on `U` and `w ∈ U` is not on the curve, then the Cauchy-type integral evaluates to `2πi · windingNumber γ a b w · f w`. This is the Cauchy-integral-formula output of Dixon's vanishing theorem. The off-curve point is kept as an explicit hypothesis; proving that such a point exists in the ambient domain is a separate geometric prerequisite for the full global homology Cauchy theorem.
code:
theorem dixonH2_eq_windingNumber_mul_f_of_nullHomologous {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ} {w : ℂ} (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) (hclosed : γ a = γ b)
    (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (h_null : IsNullHomologous γ a b U) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) :
    dixonH2 f γ a b w = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * windingNumber γ a b w * f w :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_norm_le
docstring: **Norm bound for `dixonH2`.** When `‖w‖ > R`, `R` bounds `‖γ‖`, and `M` bounds the numerator product `‖f (γ ·) * deriv γ‖` on `uIcc a b`, the Cauchy-type integral is bounded by `M / (‖w‖ - R) · |b - a|`.
code:
theorem dixonH2_norm_le {R M : ℝ}
    (hR : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, ‖γ t‖ ≤ R) (hM : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, ‖f (γ t) * deriv γ t‖ ≤ M)
    {w : ℂ} (hw : R < ‖w‖) :
    ‖dixonH2 f γ a b w‖ ≤ M / (‖w‖ - R) * |b - a| := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_norm_le_of_integrable
docstring: **`L¹` norm bound for `dixonH2`.** When `‖w‖ > R`, `R` bounds `‖γ‖` on `Ι a b`, and the weight `f (γ ·) * deriv γ` is interval-integrable, `dixonH2` is bounded by that weight's `L¹` norm divided by `‖w‖ - R`. Unlike `dixonH2_norm_le` this needs no uniform bound on the integrand, so it applies to raw curves whose derivative is only interval-integrable: rewrite the integrand as `(γ t - w)⁻¹ * (f (γ t) * deriv γ t)` and apply `norm_integral_inv_sub_mul_le`. Only the bound on the half-open interval `Ι a b` is needed.
code:
theorem dixonH2_norm_le_of_integrable {R : ℝ} (hR : ∀ t ∈ Ι a b, ‖γ t‖ ≤ R)
    (hg : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) * deriv γ t) volume a b) {w : ℂ} (hw : R < ‖w‖) :
    ‖dixonH2 f γ a b w‖ ≤ (∫ t in Ι a b, ‖f (γ t) * deriv γ t‖) / (‖w‖ - R) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_tendsto_zero
docstring: **`dixonH2 f γ a b` tends to `0` along `cocompact ℂ`.** The norm bound `dixonH2_norm_le` has the form `C / (‖w‖ - R)` with `C = M * |b - a|`, so `tendsto_zero_cocompact_of_norm_le_div` applies.

label: TauCeti.Contour.dixonH2_tendsto_zero_of_integrable
docstring: **`dixonH2 f γ a b` tends to `0` along `cocompact ℂ` (`L¹` form).** The `L¹` norm bound `dixonH2_norm_le_of_integrable` is already of the form `C / (‖w‖ - R)`, so `tendsto_zero_cocompact_of_norm_le_div` applies; the interval-integrable weight replaces the uniform bound of `dixonH2_tendsto_zero`.
code:
theorem dixonH2_tendsto_zero_of_integrable {R : ℝ} (hR : ∀ t ∈ Ι a b, ‖γ t‖ ≤ R)
    (hg : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ f (γ t) * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    Tendsto (dixonH2 f γ a b) (cocompact ℂ) (nhds 0) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_comm
docstring: `dslope` is symmetric in its two point arguments.
code: private theorem dslope_comm (g : ℂ → ℂ) (x y : ℂ) : dslope g x y = dslope g y x := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_comp_curve_continuousOn
docstring: For `w ∈ U`, the fixed-point section `t ↦ dslope f w (γ t)` is continuous on `uIcc a b`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_deriv_mul_deriv_aestronglyMeasurable
docstring: The `F'`-integrand `t ↦ deriv (dslope f (γ t)) w₀ · deriv γ t` is a.e. strongly measurable: `deriv (dslope f (γ t)) w₀` is the a.e.-limit of the measurable difference quotients above, since `dslope f (γ t)` is differentiable at `w₀ ∈ U`.
code:
private theorem dslope_deriv_mul_deriv_aestronglyMeasurable (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγU : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ∈ U) (hw₀ : w₀ ∈ U) :
    AEStronglyMeasurable (fun t ↦ deriv (dslope f (γ t)) w₀ * deriv γ t)
      (volume.restrict (Ι a b)) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_deriv_product_norm_bound
docstring: Near `w₀`, the derivative integrand is dominated by `C · ‖deriv γ t‖`, where `C` bounds `deriv (dslope f c)` (Cauchy's estimate) uniformly for `c` on the curve.
code:
private theorem dslope_deriv_product_norm_bound {C δ : ℝ}
    (h_dslope_bd : ∀ c ∈ γ '' uIcc a b, ∀ w ∈ Metric.ball w₀ δ, ‖deriv (dslope f c) w‖ ≤ C)
    {ε : ℝ} (hball : Metric.ball w₀ ε ⊆ Metric.ball w₀ δ) :
    ∀ᵐ t, t ∈ Ι a b → ∀ w ∈ Metric.ball w₀ ε,
      ‖deriv (dslope f (γ t)) w * deriv γ t‖ ≤ C * ‖deriv γ t‖ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_diffquot_aestronglyMeasurable
docstring: Each difference quotient `t ↦ (dslope f (γ t) (w₀ + s) − dslope f (γ t) w₀) / s · deriv γ t` is a.e. strongly measurable, being a continuous factor times `deriv γ`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_first_arg_hasDerivAt
docstring: The `w`-derivative of `w' ↦ dslope f w' c` at an interior point `w` is `deriv (dslope f c) w`, using symmetry of `dslope` to move the varying argument into first position.

label: TauCeti.Contour.dslope_integrand_eq
docstring: Off the curve, the `dslope` integrand splits into the Cauchy-type integrand minus the winding-number integrand scaled by `f w`.
code:
private theorem dslope_integrand_eq {f : ℂ → ℂ} {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {w : ℂ}
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) :
    ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, dslope f w (γ t) * deriv γ t =
      f (γ t) / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t - f w / (γ t - w) * deriv γ t := fun t ht ↦ by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eqOn_deriv_comp_reparam
docstring: On `[[a, b]]`, the derivative of the reparametrized curve is `φ' • (deriv γ ∘ φ)`. This is the set-level chain rule, packaged for `ContinuousOn` and integral congruences. Here `φ` has an ambient derivative `φ' t` at each `t ∈ [[a, b]]` and `γ` is ambient-differentiable on the swept image.
code:
theorem eqOn_deriv_comp_reparam :
    Set.EqOn (deriv (γ ∘ φ)) (fun t => φ' t • deriv γ (φ t)) (Set.uIcc a b) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.eq_neg_one_or_zero_le
docstring: If `-1 ≤ x` in `WithTop ℤ`, then either `x = -1` (a simple pole) or `0 ≤ x` (no pole).
code: private theorem eq_neg_one_or_zero_le {x : WithTop ℤ} (h : -1 ≤ x) : x = -1 ∨ 0 ≤ x := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eq_of_mem_window_of_eq
docstring: **In-window uniqueness of the crossing**: with windows inside `[a, b]`, distinct crossings more than `r` apart, and completeness — every parameter of `[a, b]` where `γ` takes the value `s` is a listed crossing — the only parameter of the window `[t_i - r, t_i + r]` where `γ` takes the value `s` is `t_i` itself. Stated for a bare function; no regularity is used.
code:
theorem eq_of_mem_window_of_eq {α : Type*} {γ : ℝ → α} {s : α} {a b : ℝ}
    {crossings : Finset ℝ} {r : ℝ}
    (h_endpts : ∀ t ∈ crossings, a + r ≤ t ∧ t ≤ b - r)
    (h_pairwise : ∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → r < |t - t'|)
    (h_complete : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = s → t ∈ crossings)
    {t_i : ℝ} (ht_i : t_i ∈ crossings)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc (t_i - r) (t_i + r)) (h_eq : γ t = s) :
    t = t_i := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventuallyEq_meromorphicAnalyticPartAt_add_meromorphicPolarPartAt
docstring: **The canonical Laurent decomposition**: near `s`, `f` is the analytic part plus the polar part.

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_interior_off_pos
docstring: The parameters near `t₀` (from the given side) that lie in the interior, avoid the breakpoints, and see a positive dual value of `deriv γ`.
code:
private theorem eventually_interior_off_pos {p : Finset ℝ} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : ℂ}
    {f : StrongDual ℝ ℂ} {l : Filter ℝ} (hl : l ≤ 𝓝 t₀) (hne : ∀ᶠ t in l, t ≠ t₀)
    (h_Ioo : ∀ᶠ t in l, t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b))
    (hL_tendsto : Tendsto (deriv γ) l (𝓝 L)) (hfL_pos : 0 < f L) :
    ∀ᶠ t in l, (t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧ t ∉ (↑p : Set ℝ)) ∧ 0 < f (deriv γ t) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_intervalIntegrable_truncated_window
docstring: The truncated integrand is eventually interval-integrable on a crossing window interior to `[a, b]`, by restriction.
code:
private theorem eventually_intervalIntegrable_truncated_window {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    {g : ℂ → ℂ} {a b r t : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (h_lo : a < t - r) (h_hi : t + r ≤ b)
    (hr_pos : 0 < r)
    (h_int_tr : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε →
      IntervalIntegrable (fun u => if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume a b) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ),
      IntervalIntegrable (fun u => if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0)
        MeasureTheory.volume (t - r) (t + r) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_ne_of_hasDerivWithinAt
docstring: With one-sided derivative `L ≠ 0` at `t₀` within `u ∌ t₀`, the curve cannot return to `s = γ t₀` near `t₀` within `u`.
code:
private theorem eventually_ne_of_hasDerivWithinAt
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {s L : ℂ} {u : Set ℝ} (hu : t₀ ∉ u) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀) (h_s : γ t₀ = s) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[u] t₀, γ t ≠ s := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_norm_at_firstExitTimeLeft_eq
docstring: **Eventual exact radius (left)**: the counterpart of `eventually_norm_at_firstExitTimeRight_eq`.
code:
theorem eventually_norm_at_firstExitTimeLeft_eq {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ δ : ℝ} {s : E} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc (t₀ - δ) t₀))
    (h_s : γ t₀ = s) (h_leave : ∀ t ∈ Ico (t₀ - δ) t₀, γ t ≠ s) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ‖γ (firstExitTimeLeft γ t₀ δ s ε) - s‖ = ε := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_norm_at_firstExitTimeRight_eq
docstring: **Eventual exact radius (right)**: for all sufficiently small `ε > 0`, the right exit time is at distance exactly `ε` — the radius hypothesis of `Contour.antiderivative_diff_across_crossing_tendsto_zero`.
code:
theorem eventually_norm_at_firstExitTimeRight_eq {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ δ : ℝ} {s : E} (hδ : 0 < δ)
    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc t₀ (t₀ + δ)))
    (h_s : γ t₀ = s) (h_leave : ∀ t ∈ Ioc t₀ (t₀ + δ), γ t ≠ s) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ‖γ (firstExitTimeRight γ t₀ δ s ε) - s‖ = ε := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_norm_sub_pow_le_of_hasDerivWithinAt
docstring: Near `t₀`, the curve's displacement grows at most linearly along the right derivative: for `n ≥ 1`, if `γ` has right derivative `L` at `t₀`, then there is a constant `C > 0` such that eventually as `t → t₀⁺` one has `‖γ t - γ t₀‖ ^ n ≤ C * (t - t₀)`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_normalized_chord_close
docstring: **The normalized chord is eventually close to `1`**: for any `ρ > 0`, eventually along `𝓝[u] t₀`, `‖(γ t - s) / (L (t - t₀)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ`.
code:
private theorem eventually_normalized_chord_close {u : Set ℝ} (hu : t₀ ∉ u)
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0)
    {ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[u] t₀, ‖(γ t - s) / (L * ((t - t₀ : ℝ) : ℂ)) - 1‖ ≤ ρ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_notMem_nhdsNE
docstring: A punctured neighbourhood eventually avoids a finite set.
code:
private theorem eventually_notMem_nhdsNE (S : Finset ℂ) (z : ℂ) :
    ∀ᶠ w in 𝓝[≠] z, w ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_not_exists_mem_le
docstring: If `z` is none of the finitely many points of `S`, then for all small enough `ε > 0` the point `z` is farther than `ε` from every point of `S`; i.e. the excision at `S` eventually keeps `z`.
code:
private theorem eventually_not_exists_mem_le (z : ℂ) (S : Finset ℂ) (h : ∀ s ∈ S, z ≠ s) :
    ∀ᶠ ε in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), ¬ ∃ s ∈ S, ‖z - s‖ ≤ ε := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.eventually_re_mul_conj_nonneg
docstring: **Eventual hemisphere condition.** If `T` is the outgoing tangent direction on `u` — i.e. `(t - t₀) • L = |t - t₀| • T` for `t ∈ u` and `‖T‖ = ‖L‖` — then for `t` close to `t₀` within `u`, the chord `γ t - s` lies in the `+T` hemisphere (`Re((γ t - s) · conj T) ≥ 0`). On `Ioi t₀` this holds with `T = L`, on `Iio t₀` with `T = -L`.
code:
private theorem eventually_re_mul_conj_nonneg
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {s L : ℂ} {u : Set ℝ} {T : ℂ} (hL : L ≠ 0)
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L u t₀) (h_s : γ t₀ = s)
    (hT : ∀ t ∈ u, (t - t₀) • L = |t - t₀| • T) (hTL : ‖T‖ = ‖L‖) :
    ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[u] t₀, 0 ≤ ((γ t - s) * starRingEnd ℂ T).re := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_left_avoiding
docstring: Given a finite breakpoint set, every parameter `min a b < t₀` in `[[a, b]]` has a breakpoint-free closed piece `[c, t₀]` to its left inside `[[a, b]]`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_right_avoiding
docstring: Given a finite breakpoint set, every parameter `t₀ < max a b` in `[[a, b]]` has a breakpoint-free closed piece `[t₀, d]` to its right inside `[[a, b]]`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_Icc_subset_uIcc_disjoint
docstring: Around any interior parameter outside a closed set `s` there is a closed subinterval of `[[a, b]]` whose interior contains `t` and is disjoint from `s`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_analyticAt_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul
docstring: Any meromorphic `f` admits an analytic presentation `f z = (z − z₀) ^ m • φ z` near `z₀` at any exponent `m` at or below its meromorphic order (padding the reduced presentation with a nonnegative power of `z − z₀`). The factor `φ` is analytic but may vanish at `z₀` when `m` is strictly below the order. Brings two meromorphic functions to a common exponent before adding their residues, and is the factorisation entry point for the canonical Laurent data (`MeromorphicLaurent.lean`).

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal
docstring: Near each pole, `f` minus the total polar part has an analytic germ: the per-point analytic part minus the other poles' (locally analytic) polar parts.
code:
private theorem exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {s : ℂ} (hs : s ∈ S) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero z = g z := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_ball_dist_curve_lower_bound
docstring: **Uniform distance to the curve on a neighbourhood of an avoided point.** If `γ` is continuous on the interval with endpoints `a`, `b` and avoids `w₀` there, then there is a radius `ε > 0` such that every `w` within `ε` of `w₀` stays at distance at least `ε` from the whole curve: for all `t ∈ Set.uIcc a b`, `ε ≤ ‖γ t - w‖`. Stated on the oriented interval `Set.uIcc a b`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_ball_windingNumber_zero
docstring: **The winding number vanishes on a ball around an off-curve null point.** For a closed curve `γ` (differentiable off a countable set, continuous on `uIcc a b`, with interval-integrable derivative), if the winding number about an off-curve point `w` is `0`, then it is `0` throughout a ball around `w` that stays off the curve. This is the local matching input for Dixon's argument: the off-curve set is open, so the subtype-open set on which local constancy pins the winding number to `0` pushes forward, along the open inclusion `Subtype.val`, to a `ℂ`-ball.
code:
theorem exists_ball_windingNumber_zero {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b)
    (hoff : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w) (hw_zero : windingNumber γ a b w = 0) :
    ∃ ε > 0, ∀ w' ∈ Metric.ball w ε,
      (∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w') ∧ windingNumber γ a b w' = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_div_tangent_mem_slitPlane_right
docstring: **Boundary chord-to-tangent quotients in the slit plane (right)**: there is a window radius `r > 0` such that `(γ (t₀ + r') - s) / L ∈ Complex.slitPlane` for every `0 < r' ≤ r` — the `h_slit` input of `arg_annular_quotient_tendsto_right` at any admissible window radius.
code:
theorem exists_chord_div_tangent_mem_slitPlane_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ r', 0 < r' → r' ≤ r → (γ (t₀ + r') - s) / L ∈ Complex.slitPlane := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_left
docstring: **Chord quotients on a small left interval lie in the slit plane**: there is `r > 0` such that `(γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane` whenever `t₀ - r ≤ a ≤ b < t₀`. Stated with `a` the left endpoint — the form in which the argument-lift fundamental theorem of calculus consumes it on the left excised piece.
code:
theorem exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_left
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ a b, t₀ - r ≤ a → a ≤ b → b < t₀ →
      (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_right
docstring: **Chord quotients on a small right interval lie in the slit plane**: there is `r > 0` such that `(γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane` whenever `t₀ < a ≤ b ≤ t₀ + r`.
code:
theorem exists_chord_quotient_mem_slitPlane_right
    (h_deriv : HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀) (h_at : γ t₀ = s) (hL : L ≠ 0) :
    ∃ r > 0, ∀ a b, t₀ < a → a ≤ b → b ≤ t₀ + r →
      (γ b - s) / (γ a - s) ∈ Complex.slitPlane := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_common_window_radius
docstring: **The common window radius**: for a finite set of crossings in `(a, b)` avoiding a finite exceptional set `P`, there is `r > 0` such that every window `[t_i - r, t_i + r]` stays within `[a, b]`, distinct crossings are more than `2r` apart (so the windows are pairwise disjoint), and no exceptional point comes within `r` of a crossing.
code:
theorem exists_common_window_radius {a b : ℝ} {crossings P : Finset ℝ}
    (h_nonempty : crossings.Nonempty)
    (h_Ioo : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t ∈ Ioo a b)
    (h_off : ∀ t ∈ crossings, t ∉ P) :
    ∃ r > 0,
      (∀ t ∈ crossings, a + r ≤ t ∧ t ≤ b - r) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ t' ∈ crossings, t' ≠ t → 2 * r < |t - t'|) ∧
      (∀ t ∈ crossings, ∀ p ∈ P, r < |t - p|) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_complement_windows_dist_lower_bound
docstring: **Positive distance bound off the crossing windows**: with every value-`s` parameter of `[a, b]` a listed crossing, `‖γ t - s‖` is bounded below by a positive `m` on the complement of the open crossing windows in `[a, b]` — the far bound on the smooth part of a multi-crossing excision.
code:
theorem exists_complement_windows_dist_lower_bound {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    {crossings : Finset ℝ} (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (h_complete : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t = s → t ∈ crossings)
    (r_at : ℝ → ℝ) (hr_pos : ∀ t ∈ crossings, 0 < r_at t) :
    ∃ m > 0, ∀ t ∈ Icc a b,
      (∀ t_i ∈ crossings, t ∉ Ioo (t_i - r_at t_i) (t_i + r_at t_i)) →
      m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.exists_continuousOn_arg_lift_with_partition
docstring: **Argument lift on `[a, b]`, with a partition.** For `γ` continuous on `[a, b]` (`a ≤ b`) and avoiding `w`, there is a monotone partition `a = s 0 ≤ ⋯ ≤ s N = b` and a real function `θ t = arg (γ a - w) + ∑_{j < N} (log (segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j+1)) t)).im`, continuous on `[a, b]`, satisfying `γ t - w = ‖γ t - w‖ · exp (I · θ t)` there. Each node has `γ (s j) ≠ w`, and on each segment `j` the ratio `(γ t - w) / (γ (s j) - w)` lies in `Complex.slitPlane`.
code:
theorem exists_continuousOn_arg_lift_with_partition
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hγ : ContinuousOn γ (Icc a b))
    (h_avoid : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, γ t ≠ w) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (s : ℕ → ℝ),
      0 < N ∧ s 0 = a ∧ s N = b ∧ Monotone s ∧
      (∀ j ≤ N, s j ∈ Icc a b) ∧
      (∀ j ≤ N, γ (s j) - w ≠ 0) ∧
      (∀ j, j < N → ∀ t ∈ Icc (s j) (s (j + 1)),

docstring: **The per-crossing slit-plane radius package**: at a transverse crossing with non-zero one-sided derivatives, a single radius `r > 0` carries all four slit-plane properties — the two-sided chord quotients and the two boundary tangent quotients at every admissible offset — so a common minimum over the crossings of a pole inherits them all.

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_deriv_div_sub_eq_log

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_inv_sub_mul_deriv_eq_log_window

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_pow_inv_mul_deriv_eq_sub
docstring: The fundamental theorem of calculus for the order-`k` polar term along the curve, on an interval avoiding the pole: the integral is the boundary difference of the antiderivative `c · (-(k-1)⁻¹ (· - s)^{-(k-1)}) ∘ γ`.

    (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc l u))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume l u) :
    ∫ t in l..u, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t =
      c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ u - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) -

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_ae_gt
docstring: The truncated integral is the plain integral on an interval where the curve stays at distance `> ε` almost everywhere.

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_left_exit
docstring: **The left window truncation is inert.** On `[t₀ - r, cₗ]`, where `cₗ < t₀` is the left exit point with radius `ε`, the curve stays at distance `> ε` almost everywhere — strictly before `cₗ` inside the antitone window, and at least `m > ε` beyond it — so the `ε`-truncated integral equals the plain one.

private theorem integral_truncated_eq_of_left_exit {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}

    (h_far : ∀ t ∈ Icc (t₀ - r) (t₀ - ρ), m ≤ ‖γ t - s‖) :
    ∫ u in (t₀ - r)..cₗ, (if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) =
      ∫ u in (t₀ - r)..cₗ, g (γ u) * deriv γ u := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_of_right_exit
docstring: **The right window truncation is inert.** On `[cᵣ, t₀ + r]`, where `cᵣ > t₀` is the right exit point with radius `ε`, the curve stays at distance `> ε` almost everywhere — strictly after `cᵣ` inside the monotone window, and at least `m > ε` beyond it — so the `ε`-truncated integral equals the plain one.

    ∫ u in cᵣ..(t₀ + r), (if ‖γ u - s‖ > ε then g (γ u) * deriv γ u else 0) =

label: TauCeti.Contour.integral_truncated_eq_zero_between_exits

label: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv
docstring: The order-`k` polar integrand is interval-integrable off the pole: the polar factor is continuous there.
code:
private theorem intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {l u : ℝ}
    (c : ℂ) (k : ℕ) (hlu : l ≤ u) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (Icc l u))
    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume l u) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t => c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t)
      MeasureTheory.volume l u := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv_truncated
docstring: The `ε`-truncated order-`k` polar integrand is interval-integrable: off the `ε`-ball it is dominated by `(‖c‖ / ε^k) · ‖deriv γ‖`.
code:
theorem intervalIntegrable_pow_inv_mul_deriv_truncated {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {a b : ℝ}
    (c : ℂ) (k : ℕ) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    IntervalIntegrable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - s‖ > ε then c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegrable_truncated_mul_deriv
docstring: **The `ε`-truncated integrand is interval-integrable from a bound off the ball**: whenever `f ∘ γ` is bounded by `M` at distance `> ε` from `z₀` and the truncated integrand is a.e.-strongly measurable, the truncated integrand is dominated by `M · ‖deriv γ‖`.
code:
theorem intervalIntegrable_truncated_mul_deriv {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    {a b M ε : ℝ}
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t => deriv γ t) MeasureTheory.volume a b)
    (h_aesm : MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable
      (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      (MeasureTheory.volume.restrict (Set.uIoc a b)))
    (h_bd : ∀ t : ℝ, ε < ‖γ t - z₀‖ → ‖f (γ t)‖ ≤ M) :
    IntervalIntegrable (fun t => if ‖γ t - z₀‖ > ε then f (γ t) * deriv γ t else 0)
      MeasureTheory.volume a b := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_eq_zero_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero
docstring: **The pointwise homology Cauchy theorem** `∮_γ f = 0`. Applying the Cauchy integral formula to the twist `g z = (z - w₀) · f z`, which satisfies `g w₀ = 0`, forces `dixonH2 g γ a b w₀ = 0`; and since `g (γ t) / (γ t - w₀) = f (γ t)` for `γ` off `w₀`, that Cauchy-type integral is the contour integral of `f`. Hence `∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t) = 0`, given the pointwise vanishing `dixonFunction (fun z ↦ (z - w₀) * f z) U γ a b w₀ = 0`, interval-integrability of the contour integrand `deriv γ • f ∘ γ`, and of the index integrand. Discharging the vanishing via `dixonFunction_eq_zero` yields the roadmap `homologyCauchyTheorem`.
code:
theorem intervalIntegral_deriv_smul_eq_zero_of_dixonFunction_eq_zero {f : ℂ → ℂ} {U : Set ℂ}
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} (h_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b)) (w₀ : ℂ) (hw₀_in_U : w₀ ∈ U)
    (hw₀_off : ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w₀)
    (h_zero_at : dixonFunction (fun z ↦ (z - w₀) * f z) U γ a b w₀ = 0)
    (h_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t • f (γ t)) volume a b)
    (h_base_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ (γ t - w₀)⁻¹ * deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    ∫ t in a..b, deriv γ t • f (γ t) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.inv_sub_const_mul_eq

private lemma inv_sub_const_mul_eq (hc : c ≠ 0) (w : ℂ) :
    c⁻¹ * (c⁻¹ * (c * w) - z₀)⁻¹ = (c * w - c * z₀)⁻¹ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.isLittleO_chord_pow_of_le
docstring: One-sided core of the downward restrictions: near `c` the chord is small, so on any filter within `𝓝 c` an `o(‖γ · - γ c‖ ^ n)` bound is an `o(‖γ · - γ c‖ ^ m)` bound for `m ≤ n`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.isLocallyConstant_windingNumber_of_closed
docstring: **The winding number is locally constant off a closed curve.** Let `γ` be a closed curve (`γ a = γ b`), differentiable off a countable set `P`, continuous on `Set.uIcc a b`, with interval-integrable derivative. Then, as a function of the point ranging over the complement of the curve, the generalized winding number `fun w ↦ windingNumber γ a b w` is locally constant.
code:
theorem isLocallyConstant_windingNumber_of_closed {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {P : Set ℝ}
    (hclosed : γ a = γ b) (hP : P.Countable) (hγ_cont : ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b))
    (hγ_diff : ∀ t ∈ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) \ P, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)
    (hderiv_int : IntervalIntegrable (fun t ↦ deriv γ t) volume a b) :
    IsLocallyConstant
      (fun w : {w : ℂ // ∀ t ∈ uIcc a b, γ t ≠ w} ↦ windingNumber γ a b w.1) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.isPiecewiseC1On_comm
docstring: Piecewise-`C¹` regularity is symmetric in the endpoints, since `[[a, b]] = [[b, a]]`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.isPiecewiseC1On_iff
docstring: `IsPiecewiseC1On` unfolded to its defining clauses: continuity on `[[a, b]]`, and a finite breakpoint set off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction.
code:
theorem isPiecewiseC1On_iff :
    IsPiecewiseC1On γ a b ↔
      ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b) ∧
        ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
          ∀ c d : ℝ, Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
            ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.isPwC1ImmersionOn_comm
docstring: Piecewise-`C¹`-immersion regularity is symmetric in the endpoints, since `[[a, b]] = [[b, a]]`.
code: theorem isPwC1ImmersionOn_comm : IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b ↔ IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ b a := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.isPwC1ImmersionOn_iff
docstring: `IsPwC1ImmersionOn` unfolded to its defining clauses: continuity on `[[a, b]]`, and a finite breakpoint set off which every breakpoint-free closed subinterval carries a `C¹` restriction with non-vanishing within-piece derivative.
code:
theorem isPwC1ImmersionOn_iff :
    IsPwC1ImmersionOn γ a b ↔
      ContinuousOn γ (uIcc a b) ∧
        ∃ p : Finset ℝ, ↑p ⊆ Ioo (min a b) (max a b) ∧
          ∀ c d : ℝ, c < d → Icc c d ⊆ uIcc a b → Disjoint (↑p : Set ℝ) (Ioo c d) →
            ContDiffOn ℝ 1 γ (Icc c d) ∧
              ∀ t ∈ Icc c d, derivWithin γ (Icc c d) t ≠ 0 :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.iteratedDeriv_pow_sub_mul_div_factorial
docstring: **Taylor-shift invariance of the residue coefficient.** For `h` analytic at `z₀`, dividing the `(p + i)`-th derivative at `z₀` of `(· − z₀) ^ p · h` by `(p + i)!` gives the same value as dividing the `i`-th derivative of `h` by `i!`: multiplying an analytic germ by `(· − z₀) ^ p` shifts its Taylor coefficients up by `p` without changing them. Only the top Leibniz term of the product rule survives, since `(· − z₀) ^ p` and its first `p − 1` derivatives vanish at `z₀`.
code:
private lemma iteratedDeriv_pow_sub_mul_div_factorial {z₀ : ℂ} (p i : ℕ) {h : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hh : AnalyticAt ℂ h z₀) :
    iteratedDeriv (p + i) (fun z => (z - z₀) ^ p * h z) z₀ / ((p + i).factorial : ℂ)
      = iteratedDeriv i h z₀ / (i.factorial : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt
docstring: **Any Laurent witness has the canonical coefficients**: an eventual finite principal-part expansion of a meromorphic `f` at `s` with remainder continuous at `s` agrees, coefficient by coefficient through zero-padding, with the canonical polar data. This is what transfers the sector condition (B)'s resonance constraints from its own Laurent witness to `meromorphicPolarCoeffAt`.
code:
theorem laurent_coeff_eq_meromorphicPolarCoeffAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) {N : ℕ} {a : Fin N → ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : ContinuousAt g s)
    (h_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)) (k : ℕ) :
    (if hk : k < N then a ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0)
      = (if hk : k < meromorphicPolarOrderAt f s then
          meromorphicPolarCoeffAt hMero ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq
docstring: A finite principal part agreeing with a function continuous at `s` is zero: all its coefficients vanish.
code:
private theorem laurent_coeff_eq_zero_of_eventuallyEq {s : ℂ} {g : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hg : ContinuousAt g s) :
    ∀ {N : ℕ} {c : ℕ → ℂ},
      (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, c k / (z - s) ^ (k + 1) = g z) →
      ∀ k < N, c k = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_coeff_unique
docstring: **Uniqueness of finite principal-part expansions**: two expansions of the same function near `s` with remainders continuous at `s` have the same coefficients, compared through their zero-paddings.
code:
theorem laurent_coeff_unique {s : ℂ} {N M : ℕ} {a : Fin N → ℂ} {b : Fin M → ℂ}
    {g h : ℂ → ℂ} (hg : ContinuousAt g s) (hh : ContinuousAt h s)
    (h_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s,
      g z + ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)
        = h z + ∑ k : Fin M, b k / (z - s) ^ (k.val + 1)) (k : ℕ) :
    (if hk : k < N then a ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0) = (if hk : k < M then b ⟨k, hk⟩ else 0) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.laurent_data_of_zpow_factor
docstring: Laurent data of length exactly `k` from a `(z - s)^(-k)`-factorisation with analytic cofactor: Taylor-expand the cofactor to order `k` and divide.
code:
private theorem laurent_data_of_zpow_factor {f g₀ : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} (k : ℕ)
    (hg₀_an : AnalyticAt ℂ g₀ s)
    (hg₀_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = (z - s) ^ (-(k : ℤ)) • g₀ z) :
    ∃ (a : Fin k → ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ),
      AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧
      ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] s, f z = g z + ∑ i : Fin k, a i / (z - s) ^ (i.val + 1) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.le_norm_at_firstExitTimeLeft

label: TauCeti.Contour.limUnder_comp_of_map_eq
docstring: Reindexing a `limUnder` by a self-map of the source filter that fixes it leaves the value unchanged: if `Filter.map φ F = F`, then `limUnder F (g ∘ φ) = limUnder F g`, even when the limit does not exist.

private theorem limUnder_comp_of_map_eq {α : Type*} {β : Type*} [TopologicalSpace β] [Nonempty β]
    {F : Filter α} {φ : α → α} (hφ : Filter.map φ F = F) (g : α → β) :

label: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_eq_of_eventuallyEq
docstring: The logarithmic derivative depends only on the germ.
code:
private lemma logDeriv_eq_of_eventuallyEq {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z : ℂ} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝 z] g) :
    logDeriv f z = logDeriv g z := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_eventuallyEq_principalPart
docstring: **Simple-pole splitting of the logarithmic derivative.** Near a point `s` where `F` is meromorphic of order `n`, the logarithmic derivative equals its simple-pole principal part `n · (· - s)⁻¹` plus an analytic term: there is `g` analytic and non-vanishing at `s` (the local factor of `F = (· - s) ^ n • g`) with `logDeriv F = n · (· - s)⁻¹ + logDeriv g` on a punctured neighbourhood of `s`. Exposed for the residue-form of the argument principle (`TauCeti.Contour.residue_logDeriv_eq_meromorphicOrderAt`).
code:
theorem logDeriv_eventuallyEq_principalPart {F : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hF : MeromorphicAt F s) (hn : meromorphicOrderAt F s = (n : WithTop ℤ)) :
    ∃ g : ℂ → ℂ, AnalyticAt ℂ g s ∧ g s ≠ 0 ∧
      logDeriv F =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] s] fun z => (n : ℂ) * (z - s)⁻¹ + logDeriv g z := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.logDeriv_zpow_sub_mul
docstring: Logarithmic derivative of a local factorisation `(· - c) ^ n · g`, away from the base point `c`. Since `logDeriv` turns products into sums and `logDeriv ((· - c) ^ n) = n · (· - c)⁻¹`, we get `logDeriv ((· - c) ^ n · g) = n · (· - c)⁻¹ + logDeriv g`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.log_sum_decomp
docstring: **Real/imaginary decomposition of a sum of two chord logarithms with matching inner radii**: for nonzero chords with `‖B‖ = ‖C‖`, the inner `log`-radius terms cancel, leaving the outer log-norm difference plus the argument parts.
code:
private theorem log_sum_decomp {A B C D : ℂ} (hA : A ≠ 0) (hB : B ≠ 0) (hC : C ≠ 0)
    (hD : D ≠ 0) (hnorm : ‖B‖ = ‖C‖) :
    Complex.log (B / A) + Complex.log (D / C) =
      ((Real.log ‖D‖ - Real.log ‖A‖ : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        (((B / A).arg + (D / C).arg : ℝ) : ℂ) * Complex.I := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.lt_firstExitTimeRight

theorem meromorphicPolarPartAt_eq_sum {f : ℂ → ℂ} {s : ℂ}
    (hMero : MeromorphicAt f s) (z : ℂ) :

label: TauCeti.Contour.meromorphicPolarPartTotal
docstring: **The total polar part** over the singular set: the sum of the canonical per-point polar parts.

    (h_ne : ∀ t ∈ Icc l u, γ t ≠ s) :
    ∫ t in l..u, c / (γ t - s) ^ k * deriv γ t =
      c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ u - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) -
        c * (-(↑(k - 1) : ℂ)⁻¹ * ((γ l - s) ^ (k - 1))⁻¹) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.polar_form_of_prod
docstring: If `z = z0 · ∏ zs j` with `z0` and each factor `zs j` nonzero, then `z = ‖z‖ · exp (I · θ)` with `θ = arg z0 + ∑ Im (log (zs j))`: the arguments of the factors add and the norms multiply out to `‖z‖`. This packages the argument bookkeeping of the continuous lift, whose telescoped product `(γ a - w) · ∏ segRatio = γ t - w` has exactly this shape.
code:
private lemma polar_form_of_prod {N : ℕ} {z0 : ℂ} {zs : ℕ → ℂ} {z : ℂ}
    (hz0 : z0 ≠ 0) (hzs : ∀ j ∈ Finset.range N, zs j ≠ 0)
    (hprod : z0 * ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, zs j = z) :
    z = (‖z‖ : ℂ) * Complex.exp (Complex.I *
      ((Complex.arg z0 + ∑ j ∈ Finset.range N, (Complex.log (zs j)).im : ℝ) : ℂ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.pow_div_pow_neg
code:
private theorem pow_div_pow_neg {w : ℂ} (hw : w ≠ 0) {k j : ℕ} (hjk : j < k) :
    w ^ j * (w ^ k)⁻¹ = (w ^ (k - j))⁻¹ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.pow_unit_eq_of_angle_resonance
docstring: Angle core of the resonance bridges: if `θ` is the angle from `-L_L` to `L_R` up to `2πℤ` and `k · θ ∈ 2π · ℤ`, the `k`-th powers of the unit directions agree.
code:
private theorem pow_unit_eq_of_angle_resonance {L_R L_L : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} {k : ℕ}
    (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (hθ : ∃ j : ℤ, θ = (Complex.arg L_R - Complex.arg (-L_L)) - (j : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi))
    (h_res : ∃ m : ℤ, (k : ℝ) * θ = (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi)) :
    (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_basepoint_resonance
docstring: **Basepoint resonance to tangent powers**: the join analogue of `pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_resonance`, with the outgoing tangent limit at `a` and the incoming tangent limit at `b` — the raw sector equation at the basepoint of a closed curve.
code:
theorem pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_basepoint_resonance {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {a b : ℝ} {L_R L_L : ℂ}
    {k : ℕ} (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (h_R : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] a) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_L : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] b) (𝓝 L_L))
    (h_res : ∃ m : ℤ, (k : ℝ) * basepointAngle γ a b = (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi)) :
    (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_resonance
docstring: **Resonance to tangent powers**: if `k · crossingAngle γ t₀` is a multiple of `2π` and the one-sided derivative limits at `t₀` are `L_R` and `L_L`, both non-zero, then the `k`-th powers of the unit tangent directions agree — the raw sector equation the higher-order principal-value theorems consume.
code:
theorem pow_unit_tangent_eq_of_resonance {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {t₀ : ℝ} {L_R L_L : ℂ} {k : ℕ}
    (hL_R : L_R ≠ 0) (hL_L : L_L ≠ 0)
    (h_R : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[>] t₀) (𝓝 L_R))
    (h_L : Filter.Tendsto (deriv γ) (𝓝[<] t₀) (𝓝 L_L))
    (h_res : ∃ m : ℤ, (k : ℝ) * crossingAngle γ t₀ = (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi)) :
    (L_R / (‖L_R‖ : ℂ)) ^ k = ((-L_L) / (‖L_L‖ : ℂ)) ^ k := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.prod_range_div_complex
docstring: Telescoping product in `ℂ` over `Finset.range`. For `a : ℕ → ℂ` nonzero on indices `0..k`, `∏ j ∈ range k, a (j+1)/a j = a k / a 0`. The nonzero-field analogue of the group telescoping lemma `Finset.prod_range_div`, obtained from it by lifting the nonzero values into `ℂˣ`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.prod_segRatio_telescope
docstring: Telescoping product: for `t ∈ [s_k, s_{k+1}]` along a monotone partition `s : ℕ → ℝ` with `γ(s_j) ≠ w` for `0 ≤ j ≤ N`, the product `∏_{j < N} segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j+1)) t` collapses to `(γ t - w) / (γ (s 0) - w)`. This is the key identity making `Im(log)` of each `segRatio` add up to a continuous argument lift of `t ↦ γ t - w`.
code:
private theorem prod_segRatio_telescope
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {N : ℕ} {s : ℕ → ℝ}
    (hs_mono : Monotone s)
    (h_avoid : ∀ j ≤ N, γ (s j) - w ≠ 0)
    {t : ℝ} {k : ℕ} (hk : k < N) (hk_lo : s k ≤ t) (hk_hi : t ≤ s (k + 1)) :
    ∏ j ∈ Finset.range N, segRatio γ w (s j) (s (j + 1)) t = (γ t - w) / (γ (s 0) - w) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.proj_sq_add_dev_sq
docstring: **Pythagoras for the plane projection.** The squared norm of `w` decomposes into the squared norms of its projection on `L` and its orthogonal deviation.
code:
private theorem proj_sq_add_dev_sq (w L : ℂ) :
    ‖orthogonalProjectionComplex w L‖ ^ 2 + ‖tangentDeviation w L‖ ^ 2 = ‖w‖ ^ 2 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.realWindingIntegrand
docstring: The real winding integrand `(x ẏ - y ẋ) / (x² + y²)` for a position `z = x + iy` and velocity `v = ẋ + iẏ`. It is defined as the imaginary part `(z⁻¹ * v).im` of the complex winding integrand; in particular it is `0` at `z = 0`. Its relation to the complex integrand is `realWindingIntegrand_def` and its coordinate form is `realWindingIntegrand_eq_div`.
code: public noncomputable def realWindingIntegrand (z v : ℂ) : ℝ := (z⁻¹ * v).im

label: TauCeti.Contour.realWindingIntegrand_def
docstring: The real winding integrand is the imaginary part of the complex winding integrand `z⁻¹ * v`. This is a convenient public rewrite lemma relating the real integrand to the complex index integrand `(γ - w)⁻¹ * γ'`.
code:
theorem realWindingIntegrand_def (z v : ℂ) :
    realWindingIntegrand z v = (z⁻¹ * v).im := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.realWindingIntegrand_eq_div
docstring: The coordinate formula for the real winding integrand.
code:
@[simp] theorem realWindingIntegrand_eq_div (z v : ℂ) :
    realWindingIntegrand z v =
      (z.re * v.im - z.im * v.re) / Complex.normSq z := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.realWindingIntegrand_mul_mul
docstring: Scaling position and velocity by the same nonzero complex parameter leaves the real winding integrand unchanged: it is the imaginary part of `(c * z)⁻¹ * (c * v) = z⁻¹ * v`, where the two factors of `c` cancel in `ℂ`.
code:
theorem realWindingIntegrand_mul_mul {c : ℂ} (hc : c ≠ 0) (z v : ℂ) :
    realWindingIntegrand (c * z) (c * v) = realWindingIntegrand z v := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.reindex_sum_fin_neg
code:
private theorem reindex_sum_fin_neg {k : ℕ} (c : Fin k → ℂ) (w : ℂ) :
    (∑ j : Fin k, c j / w ^ (k - j.val)) =
      ∑ i : Fin k,
        c ⟨k - 1 - i.val, by have := i.isLt; omega⟩ / w ^ (i.val + 1) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.remainder_differentiableAt_mem
docstring: At a singular point, the limit-patched remainder is differentiable: on a punctured neighbourhood it agrees with the analytic germ of `f` minus the total polar part (`exists_analyticAt_sub_polarPartTotal`), and at the point itself it takes the germ's value.
code:
private theorem remainder_differentiableAt_mem {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {z : ℂ} (hzS : z ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    DifferentiableAt ℂ (fun w => if w ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ) then
        limUnder (𝓝[≠] w) (fun u => f u - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero u)
      else f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w) z := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.remainder_eventuallyEq_off
docstring: Off the singular set, the extended remainder is `f` minus the total polar part.
code:
private theorem remainder_eventuallyEq_off {f : ℂ → ℂ} {S : Finset ℂ}
    (hMero : ∀ s ∈ S, MeromorphicAt f s) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∉ (↑S : Set ℂ)) :
    (fun w => if w ∈ (↑S : Set ℂ) then
        limUnder (𝓝[≠] w) (fun u => f u - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero u)
      else f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w) =ᶠ[𝓝 z]
      fun w => f w - meromorphicPolarPartTotal hMero w := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue
docstring: The **residue** of `f` at `z₀`: the order-`(−1)` Laurent coefficient. When `f` is meromorphic at `z₀` with a pole (`meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = n < 0`), it is the Taylor coefficient at index `−1 − n` of the analytic part `g` (with `f z = (z − z₀) ^ n • g z` near `z₀`); it is `0` when `f` is analytic at `z₀` (`n ≥ 0`) and junk (`0`) when `f` is not meromorphic at `z₀`. See `residue_eq_of_order_lt_zero` for the characteristic value from an arbitrary presentation and `residue_eq_meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_of_order_eq_neg_one` for the simple-pole value.
code: noncomputable def residue (f : ℂ → ℂ) (z₀ : ℂ) : ℂ :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.residueTheorem_aux
docstring: The residue theorem for a function `F` analytic off the finite set `S` (so `S` contains every pole and `F` is continuous on the boundary circle): `∮ F = 2πi · ∑_{s ∈ S} residue F s`. The parameter `d` is the total pole depth `∑_{s ∈ S} (-(order F s).untop₀).toNat`, carried by the strong induction that peels one pole per step via `residueTheorem_step`.
code:
private lemma residueTheorem_aux {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (S : Finset ℂ)
    (hS : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ ball c R) (d : ℕ) : ∀ F : ℂ → ℂ, MeromorphicOn F (closedBall c R) →
      (∀ z ∈ closedBall c R, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ F z) →
      (∑ s ∈ S, (-(meromorphicOrderAt F s).untop₀).toNat) = d →
      circleIntegral F c R = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * ∑ s ∈ S, residue F s := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residueTheorem_step
docstring: One pole-peeling step of the residue theorem. Given `F` analytic off the finite set `S` with a pole at `s₀ ∈ S`, subtracting the leading Laurent term at `s₀` yields `G` that is still analytic off `S`, has strictly smaller total pole depth, and whose residue formula implies that of `F`.
code:
private lemma residueTheorem_step {c : ℂ} {R : ℝ} (hR : 0 < R) (S : Finset ℂ)
    (hS : (S : Set ℂ) ⊆ ball c R) {F : ℂ → ℂ} (hF_mero : MeromorphicOn F (closedBall c R))
    (hF_off : ∀ z ∈ closedBall c R, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ F z)
    {s₀ : ℂ} (hs₀S : s₀ ∈ S) (hs₀_neg : meromorphicOrderAt F s₀ < 0) :
    ∃ G : ℂ → ℂ, MeromorphicOn G (closedBall c R) ∧
      (∀ z ∈ closedBall c R, z ∉ S → AnalyticAt ℂ G z) ∧
      (∑ s ∈ S, (-(meromorphicOrderAt G s).untop₀).toNat)
        < (∑ s ∈ S, (-(meromorphicOrderAt F s).untop₀).toNat) ∧
      (circleIntegral G c R = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * ∑ s ∈ S, residue G s →
        circleIntegral F c R = 2 * (Real.pi : ℂ) * Complex.I * ∑ s ∈ S, residue F

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_add
docstring: **Additivity of the residue.** The residue is additive on functions meromorphic at `z₀`.
code:
theorem residue_add {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀) (hg : MeromorphicAt g z₀) :
    residue (f + g) z₀ = residue f z₀ + residue g z₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_congr_nhdsNE
docstring: The residue depends only on the germ of `f` on a punctured neighborhood of `z₀`: functions agreeing near (but not necessarily at) `z₀` have the same residue.
code:
theorem residue_congr_nhdsNE {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (h : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] z₀] g) :
    residue f z₀ = residue g z₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_const_div_sub_pow
docstring: **The residue of a Laurent monomial**: `residue (a / (z - z₀)^(k+1)) z₀` is `a` for `k = 0` and `0` for higher-order terms.
code:
theorem residue_const_div_sub_pow (a z₀ : ℂ) (k : ℕ) :
    residue (fun z => a / (z - z₀) ^ (k + 1)) z₀ = if k = 0 then a else 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_const_mul
docstring: **Scaling of the residue.** Scaling `f` by a constant scales its residue by that constant.
code:
theorem residue_const_mul {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (c : ℂ) (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀) :
    residue (fun z => c * f z) z₀ = c * residue f z₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_const_mul_sub_inv
docstring: The residue of `c · (· − z₀)⁻¹` at `z₀` is `c`: scaling the elementary simple pole scales its residue.
code:
theorem residue_const_mul_sub_inv (c z₀ : ℂ) :
    residue (fun z => c * (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ = c := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt_of_order_eq_neg_one
docstring: At a **simple pole** (`meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = −1`), the residue is the leading Laurent coefficient `meromorphicTrailingCoeffAt f z₀`, i.e. `lim_{z→z₀} (z − z₀) · f z`. The `n = −1` specialization of `residue_eq_of_order_lt_zero`: the Taylor coefficient at index `−1 − (−1) = 0` of the analytic part `g` is just `g z₀`, which is the trailing coefficient.

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul
docstring: **Generalized characteristic value of the residue.** If `f z = (z − z₀) ^ n • g z` near `z₀` (on the punctured neighborhood) with `g` analytic at `z₀` and `n ≤ −1`, then the residue is the Taylor coefficient `iteratedDeriv (−1 − n) g z₀ / (−1 − n)!`. Unlike `residue_eq_of_order_lt_zero` this drops the hypothesis `g z₀ ≠ 0`, so the presentation exponent `n` need not be the meromorphic order of `f`: `g` may vanish at `z₀`, raising the true pole order above `n`; only when `g`'s vanishing order is at least `-n` is `f` analytic (residue `0`).
code:
theorem residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hn : n ≤ -1) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀)
    (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] z₀] fun z => (z - z₀) ^ n • g z) :
    residue f z₀ = iteratedDeriv (-1 - n).toNat g z₀ / ((-1 - n).toNat.factorial : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul_of_order_lt_zero
docstring: The pole case (`meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ < 0`) of `residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul`: the residue of `f` at `z₀` equals the Taylor coefficient `iteratedDeriv (-1 - n) g z₀ / (-1 - n)!` of the presentation factor `g`.
code:
private theorem residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul_of_order_lt_zero {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀) (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] z₀] fun z => (z - z₀) ^ n • g z)
    (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀)
    (hord_eq : meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = (n : WithTop ℤ) + meromorphicOrderAt g z₀)
    (ha : meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ < 0) :
    residue f z₀ = iteratedDeriv (-1 - n).toNat g z₀ / ((-1 - n).toNat.factorial : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul_of_order_nonneg
docstring: The pole-free case of `residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul`: when `meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ ≥ 0`, `f` has no pole so its residue is `0`, and `g` vanishes to order `> -1 - n`, so the Taylor coefficient on the right is `0` as well.
code:
private theorem residue_eq_of_eventuallyEq_zpow_smul_of_order_nonneg {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hn : n ≤ -1) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀)
    (hord_eq : meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = (n : WithTop ℤ) + meromorphicOrderAt g z₀)
    (ha : meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ ≥ 0) :
    residue f z₀ = iteratedDeriv (-1 - n).toNat g z₀ / ((-1 - n).toNat.factorial : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_of_order_lt_zero
docstring: **Characteristic value of the residue at a pole.** If `f z = (z − z₀) ^ n • g z` near `z₀` (on the punctured neighborhood) with `g` analytic at `z₀`, `g z₀ ≠ 0`, and `n < 0`, then the residue is the Taylor coefficient of `g` at index `−1 − n`. This is the standard reduced analytic presentation; the order equality `meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = n` is derived from it, and the value is independent of the chosen presentation `g`.
code:
theorem residue_eq_of_order_lt_zero {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {n : ℤ}
    (hlt : n < 0) (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀) (hg_ne : g z₀ ≠ 0)
    (hfg : f =ᶠ[𝓝[≠] z₀] fun z => (z - z₀) ^ n • g z) :
    residue f z₀ = iteratedDeriv (-1 - n).toNat g z₀ / ((-1 - n).toNat.factorial : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_of_tendsto_sub_mul
docstring: **Computing a residue as a limit (converse).** If `f` is meromorphic at `z₀` and the product `(z − z₀) · f z` converges to `L` as `z → z₀`, then `residue f z₀ = L`. This is the direction used in practice to read off a residue.
code:
theorem residue_eq_of_tendsto_sub_mul {L : ℂ} (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀)
    (h : Tendsto (fun z => (z - z₀) * f z) (𝓝[≠] z₀) (𝓝 L)) :
    residue f z₀ = L := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_zero_of_analyticAt
docstring: The residue vanishes where `f` is analytic.
code:
theorem residue_eq_zero_of_analyticAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (hf : AnalyticAt ℂ f z₀) :
    residue f z₀ = 0 :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_eq_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg
docstring: The residue vanishes at a point where `f` has nonnegative meromorphic order (in particular where `f` is analytic): there is no order-`(−1)` Laurent coefficient.
code:
theorem residue_eq_zero_of_meromorphicOrderAt_nonneg {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ}
    (h : 0 ≤ meromorphicOrderAt f z₀) : residue f z₀ = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_logDeriv_eq_meromorphicOrderAt
docstring: **The residue of the logarithmic derivative is the meromorphic order.** If `f` is meromorphic at `z₀` of order `n` (`meromorphicOrderAt f z₀ = n`), then `residue (logDeriv f) z₀ = n`: the residue of `f'/f` counts the order of `f` at `z₀` — positive at a zero, negative at a pole. This is the local, residue-form of the argument principle `TauCeti.Contour.argumentPrinciple`, the identity `Res_{z₀}(f'/f) = ord_{z₀} f`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_of_laurent_expansion
docstring: **The residue from a Laurent expansion.** If `f z = g z + ∑ k, a k / (z - z₀)^(k+1)` near `z₀` with `g` analytic at `z₀`, then `residue f z₀` is the first Laurent coefficient `a 0` (or `0` for an empty expansion): the analytic part and the higher-order terms contribute nothing.
code:
theorem residue_of_laurent_expansion {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {N : ℕ} {a : Fin N → ℂ}
    (hg : AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀)
    (hf_eq : ∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin N, a k / (z - z₀) ^ (k.val + 1)) :
    residue f z₀ = if h : 0 < N then a ⟨0, h⟩ else 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_of_not_meromorphicAt
docstring: If `f` is not meromorphic at `z₀`, its residue is `0` by definition.
code:
theorem residue_of_not_meromorphicAt {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (h : ¬ MeromorphicAt f z₀) :
    residue f z₀ = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_smul
docstring: **Scaling of the residue (pointwise `•`).** The residue commutes with scalar multiplication; the `Pi.smul` companion to `residue_const_mul`.
code:
theorem residue_smul {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (c : ℂ) (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀) :
    residue (c • f) z₀ = c • residue f z₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_sub
docstring: **Subtractivity of the residue.** The residue distributes over subtraction of meromorphic functions; the `−1` scaling case of `residue_add` and `residue_const_mul`.
code:
theorem residue_sub {f g : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} (hf : MeromorphicAt f z₀) (hg : MeromorphicAt g z₀) :
    residue (f - g) z₀ = residue f z₀ - residue g z₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_sub_inv
docstring: The residue of the elementary simple pole `(· − z₀)⁻¹` at `z₀` is `1`: since `(z − z₀) · (z − z₀)⁻¹ → 1` as `z → z₀`, the simple-pole limit formula gives the residue.
code: theorem residue_sub_inv (z₀ : ℂ) : residue (fun z => (z - z₀)⁻¹) z₀ = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_sum
docstring: **The residue of a finite sum.** For a finite family of functions meromorphic at `z₀`, the residue of the sum is the sum of the residues — the form consumed by the residue theorem.

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_twoPrincipalParts_left
docstring: At the first designated point, the residue of `twoPrincipalParts` is the first coefficient if the other principal part vanishes or is designated at a distinct point.
code:
theorem residue_twoPrincipalParts_left {A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ} (h : B = 0 ∨ s₁ ≠ s₂) :
    residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₁ = A := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.residue_twoPrincipalParts_right
docstring: At the second designated point, the residue of `twoPrincipalParts` is the second coefficient if the other principal part vanishes or is designated at a distinct point.

theorem residue_twoPrincipalParts_right {A B s₁ s₂ : ℂ} (h : A = 0 ∨ s₁ ≠ s₂) :
    residue (twoPrincipalParts A B s₁ s₂) s₂ = B := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.right_endpoint_mem

label: TauCeti.Contour.right_set_bddBelow

private theorem right_set_bddBelow (γ : ℝ → E) (t₀ δ ε : ℝ) (s : E) :
    ∀ t ∈ {t ∈ Icc t₀ (t₀ + δ) | ε ≤ ‖γ t - s‖}, t₀ ≤ t :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.sectorCompatible_iff
docstring: Characterization of `SectorCompatible` by its two fields, for rewriting the hypothesis into the `angle_rational ∧ laurent_compatible` conjunction (and back via the anonymous constructor).
code:
theorem sectorCompatible_iff {f : ℂ → ℂ} {z₀ : ℂ} {θ : ℝ} :
    SectorCompatible f z₀ θ ↔
      (∃ p q : ℕ,
        q ≠ 0 ∧ Nat.Coprime p q ∧ θ = (p : ℝ) * Real.pi / (q : ℝ)) ∧
      ∃ (N : ℕ) (coeff : Fin N → ℂ) (g : ℂ → ℂ), AnalyticAt ℂ g z₀ ∧
        (∀ᶠ z in 𝓝[≠] z₀, f z = g z + ∑ k : Fin N, coeff k / (z - z₀) ^ (k.val + 1)) ∧
        ∀ k : Fin N, coeff k ≠ 0 → 1 ≤ k.val →
          ∃ m : ℤ, (k.val : ℝ) * θ = (m : ℝ) * (2 * Real.pi) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp
docstring: Helper: clamp `t` to `[s_j, s_{j+1}]`. For partition segment `j`.
code: private def segClamp (s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ) : ℝ := max s_j (min t s_jp1)

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_continuous
code:
private theorem segClamp_continuous (s_j s_jp1 : ℝ) :
    Continuous (segClamp s_j s_jp1) :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_left
code:

    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = s_j := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_right
code:
private theorem segClamp_eq_right {s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ} (h : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (ht : s_jp1 ≤ t) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = s_jp1 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_eq_self
code:
private theorem segClamp_eq_self {s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ} (ht_lo : s_j ≤ t) (ht_hi : t ≤ s_jp1) :
    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t = t := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.segClamp_mem_Icc
code:

    segClamp s_j s_jp1 t ∈ Icc s_j s_jp1 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio
docstring: The **segment ratio** `(γ (segClamp s_j s_jp1 t) - w) / (γ s_j - w)`: on the partition segment `[s_j, s_{j+1}]` it measures `γ t - w` against its value at the left endpoint `s_j`, held constant in `t` outside the segment. Summing the `Complex.log`s of these ratios over a partition yields a continuous argument lift of `t ↦ γ t - w`.
code: noncomputable def segRatio (γ : ℝ → ℂ) (w : ℂ) (s_j s_jp1 t : ℝ) : ℂ :=

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_div_of_mem_Icc
docstring: On its segment (`t ∈ [s_j, s_{j+1}]`), the segment ratio is `(γ t - w) / (γ s_j - w)` — the primary meaning of `segRatio`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_endpoint_div_of_le
docstring: After its segment (`s_{j+1} ≤ t`), the segment ratio equals the full endpoint ratio `(γ s_{j+1} - w) / (γ s_j - w)`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_eq_one_of_le
docstring: Before its segment (`t ≤ s_j`), the segment ratio equals `1`.

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_mem_ball_one
docstring: For partition with mesh < δ' and segments [s_j, s_{j+1}] of length ≤ mesh, on the j-th segment, `γ(clamp t) - γ s_j` is small, so `segRatio j t ∈ ball(1, 1/2)`.
code:
private theorem segRatio_mem_ball_one
    {γ : ℝ → ℂ} {w : ℂ} {a b δ' ρ : ℝ} (hρ_pos : 0 < ρ)
    (h_dist_lb : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, ρ ≤ ‖γ t - w‖)
    (h_unif : ∀ t s : ℝ, t ∈ Icc a b → s ∈ Icc a b →
      |t - s| < δ' → ‖γ t - γ s‖ < ρ / 2)
    {s_j s_jp1 : ℝ} (hsj : s_j ∈ Icc a b) (hsjp1 : s_jp1 ∈ Icc a b)
    (h_le : s_j ≤ s_jp1) (h_mesh : s_jp1 - s_j < δ') (t : ℝ) :
    ‖segRatio γ w s_j s_jp1 t - 1‖ < 1 / 2 := by

label: TauCeti.Contour.segRatio_mem_slitPlane
docstring: Combined: for partition with mesh < δ', `segRatio j t ∈ slitPlane`.
