label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.asIdeal_equivOfRingEquiv
docstring: Transporting a height-one prime along a ring equivalence `σ` maps its ideal to the image ideal: `(equivOfRingEquiv σ p).asIdeal = Ideal.map σ p.asIdeal`.
code:
private lemma asIdeal_equivOfRingEquiv (σ : R ≃+* R)
    (p : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R) :
    (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p).asIdeal =
      Ideal.map σ p.asIdeal := by

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.disjoint_image_mul_asIdeal
docstring: For a distinct prime `q ≠ p` and a family `G'` no member of which is divisible by `p.asIdeal`, multiplying `G'` by `p.asIdeal` and by `q.asIdeal` gives disjoint images.

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.exists_transversal_family
docstring: **Conjugate-transversal ideal family.** For a fixed-point-free involution `σ` of a finite set `S` of height-one primes of a Dedekind domain, there are at least `2 ^ (S.card / 2)` ideals `A` with `A * σ A = ∏ p ∈ S, p.asIdeal`.
code:
theorem exists_transversal_family (σ : R ≃+* R)
    (S : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum R))
    (hinv : ∀ p ∈ S, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p ∈ S)
    (hinvol : ∀ p ∈ S,
      IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ
        (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p) = p)
    (hfree : ∀ p ∈ S, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.equivOfRingEquiv σ p ≠ p) :
    ∃ G : Finset (Ideal R), 2 ^ (S.card / 2) ≤ G.card ∧
      ∀ A ∈ G, A * Ideal.map σ A = ∏ p ∈ S, p.asIdeal := by

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.isPrime_not_dvd_prod
docstring: A nonzero prime ideal of a Dedekind domain does not divide a finite product of nonzero prime ideals unless it equals one of the factors.

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.mul_map_eq_prod_of_mem_image_union
docstring: Every ideal in the union `G'.image (· * P) ∪ G'.image (· * Q)` has conjugate product `prodS`, given the conjugate-pair relations `Q = Ideal.map σ P` and `Ideal.map σ Q = P`, the factorisation `prodS = prodS' * P * Q` of the product through the pair, and the product property `a * Ideal.map σ a = prodS'` of every `a ∈ G'`. This is a pure identity about ideals under a ring homomorphism `σ`, valid over any commutative semiring (no Dedekind structure needed).

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_natCard_iff_of_isGaloisGroup {A B : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] [CommRing B] [IsDedekindDomain B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B]
    [IsTorsionFree A B] (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] [MulSemiringAction G B]
    [IsGaloisGroup G A B] (P : Ideal A) [P.IsMaximal] (_hP : P ≠ ⊥) :
    (primesOver P B).ncard = Nat.card G ↔
      P.ramificationIdxIn B = 1 ∧ P.inertiaDegIn B = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.notMem_pair_of_apply_involutive
docstring: Under an involutive `f` with `q = f p`, the image `f x` of an element outside the pair `{p, q}` again lies outside `{p, q}`.

label: TauCeti.DedekindDomain.two_pow_div_two_le_two_mul_two_pow_div_two_of_le_add_two
code:
private lemma two_pow_div_two_le_two_mul_two_pow_div_two_of_le_add_two {m n : ℕ} (hmn : n ≤ m + 2) :
    2 ^ (n / 2) ≤ 2 * 2 ^ (m / 2) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv
docstring: The `A`-points of the base change `K ⊗[k] k[G]` of the diagonalizable group `D(G)` are the character group `G →* Aˣ`. The source is the convolution group of `K`-algebra maps out of the base-changed Hopf algebra. The target is the ordinary pointwise-multiplication group of characters.
code:
@[expose] noncomputable def baseChangePointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k G →ₐ[K] A) ≃* (G →* Aˣ) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply
docstring: Applying `baseChangePointsMulEquiv` first restricts a base-changed point along `g ↦ 1 ⊗ single g 1`, then reads off its character.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply
    (f : WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k G →ₐ[K] A)) :
    baseChangePointsMulEquiv f =
      charOfPoint
        (((AlgHom.baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K)
          (A := MonoidAlgebra k G) (R := A)).symm f).ofConv) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
docstring: The base-changed diagonalizable-points equivalence reads a point by evaluating it on the base-changed group-like element `1 ⊗ single g 1`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
    (f : WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k G →ₐ[K] A)) (g : G) :
    (baseChangePointsMulEquiv f g : A) =
      f.ofConv (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : k)) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapDomain
docstring: Under base change, the points map induced contravariantly by `φ : G →* G'` is precomposition of characters by `φ`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_mapDomain (φ : G →* G')
    (f : WithConv (K ⊗[k] MonoidAlgebra k G' →ₐ[K] A)) :
    baseChangePointsMulEquiv
        (AlgHom.mapDomain (A := A)
          (_root_.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map (_root_.BialgHom.id K K)
            (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainBialgHom k φ)) f) =
      (baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (G := G') f).comp φ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one
docstring: The inverse base-changed diagonalizable-points equivalence takes `1 ⊗ single g 1` to the value of the character at `g`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one (χ : G →* Aˣ) (g : G) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (G := G)).symm χ).ofConv
        (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single g (1 : k)) =
      (χ g : A) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single
docstring: The inverse base-changed diagonalizable-points equivalence extends a character after base change. On a pure tensor it sends `s ⊗ single g r` to `s • (r • χ g)`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single (χ : G →* Aˣ) (s : K)
    (g : G) (r : k) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (G := G)).symm χ).ofConv
        (s ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single g r) =
      s • (r • (χ g : A)) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint
docstring: The character of `G` read off from an `R[G]`-point: it sends `g` to the unit `f (single g 1)` of `A`, whose inverse is `f (single g⁻¹ 1)`. It is the monoid hom `(MonoidAlgebra.lift R A G).symm f : G →* A` made unit-valued through `MonoidHom.toHomUnits`, using that `G` is a group.
code: @[expose] noncomputable def charOfPoint (f : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) : G →* Aˣ :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_apply_coe
docstring: The character read off from a point sends `g` to the value of the point on `single g 1`.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_apply_coe (f : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) (g : G) :
    (charOfPoint f g : A) = f (MonoidAlgebra.single g 1) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_apply_inv_coe
docstring: The inverse of the unit `charOfPoint f g` is the value of the point on `single g⁻¹ 1`.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_apply_inv_coe (f : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) (g : G) :
    (↑(charOfPoint f g)⁻¹ : A) = f (MonoidAlgebra.single g⁻¹ 1) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_comp
docstring: Reading off the character of a point pre-composed by the induced bialgebra map is the character of the original point pre-composed by `φ`.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_comp (φ : G →* G') (f : MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A) :
    charOfPoint (f.comp
        (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainBialgHom R φ : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] MonoidAlgebra R G')) =
      (charOfPoint f).comp φ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_convMul
docstring: Reading off characters turns the convolution product of points into the pointwise product of characters.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_convMul (f g : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) :
    charOfPoint ((f * g).ofConv) = charOfPoint f.ofConv * charOfPoint g.ofConv := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_mapValue
docstring: Reading off characters is natural in the value algebra: post-composing a point with an `R`-algebra map sends the associated character through the induced map on units.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) :
    charOfPoint ((AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G) φ f).ofConv) =
      (Units.map φ.toMonoidHom).comp (charOfPoint f.ofConv) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charOfPoint_point
docstring: Reading off the character of the point of `χ` recovers `χ`.
code:
theorem charOfPoint_point (χ : G →* Aˣ) :
    charOfPoint (point (R := R) χ) = χ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints
docstring: **The character of `D(M)` attached to an element `m : M`, on points.** As a homomorphism of group functors `D(M) → 𝔾ₘ`, it is induced (contravariantly) by the generator homomorphism `zpowersHom M m : Multiplicative ℤ →* M`, `Multiplicative.ofAdd 1 ↦ m`.
code:
noncomputable def charPoints (m : M) :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] A) →*
      WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints_comp_cocharPoints
docstring: **The pairing is realized as a power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`.** Composing the character `m` after the cocharacter `ψ` is the `⟨m, ψ⟩`-power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`, so on points it is `u ↦ u ^ ⟨m, ψ⟩`. This realizes the character–cocharacter pairing `X*(D(M)) × X_*(D(M)) → End(𝔾ₘ)`, valued in the power endomorphisms (the ring `End(𝔾ₘ) ≅ ℤ` on the level of power maps).
code:
theorem charPoints_comp_cocharPoints (m : M) (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    (charPoints (R := R) (A := A) m).comp (cocharPoints ψ) = powEnd (pairing m ψ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.cocharPoints
docstring: **The cocharacter of `D(M)` attached to a homomorphism `ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ`, on points.** As a homomorphism of group functors `𝔾ₘ → D(M)`, it is induced (contravariantly) by `ψ`.
code:
noncomputable def cocharPoints (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A) →*
      WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.comul_single_one
docstring: The comultiplication of `R[G]` on a group-like element: `single g 1` is group-like.

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.convMul_ofConv_single_one
docstring: A convolution product of points, evaluated on the group-like `single x 1`, is the product of the two values: convolution restricted to group-like elements is pointwise multiplication. This is the reusable fact behind `charOfPoint_convMul`.
code:
theorem convMul_ofConv_single_one (f g : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) (x : G) :
    (f * g).ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single x 1) =
      f.ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single x 1) * g.ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single x 1) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.mapDomain_baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: Mapping the base-changed point attached to a character is precomposition of that character by the homomorphism of character groups.
code:
theorem mapDomain_baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : G →* G') (χ : G' →* Aˣ) :
    AlgHom.mapDomain (A := A)
        (_root_.Bialgebra.TensorProduct.map (_root_.BialgHom.id K K)
          (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainBialgHom k φ))
        ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (G := G')).symm χ) =
      (baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (G := G)).symm (χ.comp φ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.mapValue_pointsMap
docstring: **Naturality in the value algebra.** The contravariant points homomorphism `pointsMap φ` commutes with the value-algebra functoriality `AlgHom.mapValue χ`: pre-composition by the induced bialgebra map and post-composition by `χ : A →ₐ[R] B` may be applied in either order. This makes `pointsMap φ` a natural transformation of functors of points.
code:
theorem mapValue_pointsMap {B : Type*} [CommSemiring B] [Algebra R B] (φ : G →* G')
    (χ : A →ₐ[R] B) :
    (pointsMap (A := B) φ).comp (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G') χ) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G) χ).comp (pointsMap (A := A) φ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.multiplicativeGroup_pointEquiv_apply
docstring: The group-algebra presentation of `D(Multiplicative ℤ)` agrees with the Laurent-polynomial multiplicative group `𝔾ₘ` of `TauCeti.MultiplicativeGroup`: reading a point on the generator `single (ofAdd 1) 1` gives the same unit as first precomposing it with `AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv` and then using the canonical `TauCeti.MultiplicativeGroup.pointEquiv`.
code:
theorem multiplicativeGroup_pointEquiv_apply
    (f : MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A) :
    charOfPoint f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) =
      MultiplicativeGroup.pointEquiv
        (f.comp (AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv R ℤ).toAlgHom) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing
docstring: **The character–cocharacter pairing `⟨m, ψ⟩ : ℤ`** of a character `m : M` of `D(M)` with a cocharacter `ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ`.
code: def pairing (m : M) (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) : ℤ :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_def
docstring: The pairing `⟨m, ψ⟩` is the integer `(ψ m).toAdd`.
code: theorem pairing_def (m : M) (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) : pairing m ψ = (ψ m).toAdd := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_mul_left
docstring: The pairing is additive in the character: `⟨m * m', ψ⟩ = ⟨m, ψ⟩ + ⟨m', ψ⟩`.
code:
theorem pairing_mul_left (m m' : M) (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    pairing (m * m') ψ = pairing m ψ + pairing m' ψ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_mul_right
docstring: The pairing is additive in the cocharacter: `⟨m, ψ * ψ'⟩ = ⟨m, ψ⟩ + ⟨m, ψ'⟩`.
code:
theorem pairing_mul_right (m : M) (ψ ψ' : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    pairing m (ψ * ψ') = pairing m ψ + pairing m ψ' := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_ofAdd
docstring: **The rank-`1` pairing is multiplication.** For `𝔾ₘ = D(Multiplicative ℤ)`, with character lattice `X*(𝔾ₘ) = ℤ` (via `Multiplicative.ofAdd`) and cocharacter lattice `X_*(𝔾ₘ) = ℤ` (via `ψ ↦ (ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)).toAdd`), the pairing is the product of the two integers.
code:
theorem pairing_ofAdd (a : ℤ) (ψ : Multiplicative ℤ →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd a) ψ = a * (ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1)).toAdd := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_one_left
docstring: The pairing vanishes on the identity character: `⟨1, ψ⟩ = 0`.
code: theorem pairing_one_left (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) : pairing (1 : M) ψ = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_one_right
docstring: The pairing vanishes on the identity cocharacter: `⟨m, 1⟩ = 0`.
code: theorem pairing_one_right (m : M) : pairing m (1 : M →* Multiplicative ℤ) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point
docstring: The `R[G]`-point of the diagonalizable group `D(G)` corresponding to a character of `G`. It is the algebra map extending `χ` via the universal property of the group algebra; it sends `single g r` to `r • χ g`.
code: @[expose] noncomputable def point (χ : G →* Aˣ) : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointEquiv
docstring: Algebra maps out of `R[G]` are the same as characters `G →* Aˣ` of `G`.
code: @[expose] noncomputable def pointEquiv : (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) ≃ (G →* Aˣ) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointEquiv_apply
docstring: The equivalence sends a point to the character read off from it.
code:
theorem pointEquiv_apply (f : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) :
    pointEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G) f = charOfPoint f :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse equivalence sends a character to the point extending it.
code:
theorem pointEquiv_symm_apply (χ : G →* Aˣ) :
    (pointEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G)).symm χ = point χ :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point_charOfPoint
docstring: The point of the character read off from `f` recovers `f`.
code:
theorem point_charOfPoint (f : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) :
    point (R := R) (charOfPoint f) = f := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point_single
docstring: The point associated to a character sends `single g r` to `r • χ g`.
code:
theorem point_single (χ : G →* Aˣ) (g : G) (r : R) :
    point (R := R) χ (MonoidAlgebra.single g r) = r • (χ g : A) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.point_single_one
docstring: The point associated to a character sends the group-like `single g 1` to `χ g`.
code:
theorem point_single_one (χ : G →* Aˣ) (g : G) :
    point (R := R) χ (MonoidAlgebra.single g 1) = (χ g : A) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap
docstring: **The diagonalizable group is contravariant in the abelian group.** A group homomorphism `φ : G →* G'` induces, by pre-composition with the bialgebra map `R[G] →ₐc[R] R[G']`, a homomorphism of convolution groups of points `D(G')(A) → D(G)(A)`.
code:
@[expose] noncomputable def pointsMap (φ : G →* G') :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A) →* WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap_apply
docstring: `pointsMap φ` acts by pre-composition with the induced bialgebra map.
code:
theorem pointsMap_apply (φ : G →* G') (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMap (A := A) φ f =
      toConv (f.ofConv.comp
        (MonoidAlgebra.mapDomainBialgHom R φ : MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] MonoidAlgebra R G')) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap_comp
docstring: **Contravariant functoriality.** Pre-composition by a composite homomorphism is the composite of the induced points homomorphisms, in the opposite order.
code:
theorem pointsMap_comp (φ : G →* G') (ψ : G' →* G'') :
    (pointsMap (A := A) (ψ.comp φ) :
        WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G'' →ₐ[R] A) →* WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) =
      (pointsMap (R := R) (A := A) φ).comp (pointsMap (R := R) (A := A) ψ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap_id
docstring: Pre-composition by the identity homomorphism is the identity on points.
code:
theorem pointsMap_id :
    (pointsMap (MonoidHom.id G) :
        WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) →* WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) =
      MonoidHom.id _ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap_injective
docstring: If `φ` is surjective, then the induced contravariant map on diagonalizable-group points is injective. Under the character identification this is injectivity of precomposition by a surjective homomorphism.
code:
theorem pointsMap_injective (φ : G →* G') (hφ : Function.Surjective φ) :
    Function.Injective (pointsMap (R := R) (A := A) φ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMap_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: Mapping the point attached to a character is precomposition of that character by `φ`.
code:
theorem pointsMap_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : G →* G') (χ : G' →* Aˣ) :
    pointsMap (R := R) (A := A) φ ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G')).symm χ) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G)).symm (χ.comp φ) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv
docstring: The functor of points of the diagonalizable group `D(G)` is the character group `G →* Aˣ`. The source is the convolution group of `R`-algebra maps out of `R[G]`; the target is the group of characters of `G` valued in the units of `A`, under pointwise multiplication.
code: @[expose] noncomputable def pointsMulEquiv : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A) ≃* (G →* Aˣ) where

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_apply
docstring: The multiplicative equivalence sends a convolution point to the character read off from it.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_apply (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G) f = charOfPoint f.ofConv :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_charPoints
docstring: **A character acts on points by evaluation.** Reading the resulting `𝔾ₘ`-point on the generator gives the value of the original character `χ : M →* Aˣ` at `m`.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_charPoints (m : M) (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R M →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (charPoints (R := R) (A := A) m f) (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) =
      pointsMulEquiv f m := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_charPoints_cocharPoints
docstring: The pairing evaluated through `charPoints_comp_cocharPoints`: on points, the composite of the cocharacter `ψ` and the character `m` raises a unit to the `⟨m, ψ⟩` power.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_charPoints_cocharPoints (m : M) (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (charPoints (R := R) (A := A) m (cocharPoints ψ f))
        (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) =
      pointsMulEquiv f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) ^ pairing m ψ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_cocharPoints
docstring: **A cocharacter acts on points by a power character.** The `𝔾ₘ`-point with generator value `u` is sent to the character `m ↦ u ^ (ψ m).toAdd`.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_cocharPoints (ψ : M →* Multiplicative ℤ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)) (m : M) :
    pointsMulEquiv (cocharPoints (R := R) (A := A) ψ f) m =
      pointsMulEquiv f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) ^ (ψ m).toAdd := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_ext
docstring: **Extensionality for `𝔾ₘ = D(Multiplicative ℤ)` points.** Two points are equal once they read off the same unit on the group-algebra generator `Multiplicative.ofAdd 1`: a character of `Multiplicative ℤ` is determined by its value at the generator (`MonoidHom.ext_mint`), and points are equivalent to characters.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_ext {f g : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)}
    (h : pointsMulEquiv f (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ)) =
        pointsMulEquiv g (Multiplicative.ofAdd (1 : ℤ))) :
    f = g :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
docstring: The multiplicative point equivalence is natural in the value algebra.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B) (G := G)
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G) φ f) =
      (Units.map φ.toMonoidHom).comp
        (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G) f) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_pointsMap
docstring: **The points homomorphism is precomposition of characters.** Under the identification of points of `D(G)` with characters of `G`, the homomorphism `pointsMap φ` induced by `φ : G →* G'` is intertwined with precomposition `χ ↦ χ ∘ φ` of characters.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_pointsMap (φ : G →* G') (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (pointsMap (A := A) φ f) = (pointsMulEquiv f).comp φ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_powEnd
docstring: **The power endomorphism acts as `u ↦ u ^ n` on points.**
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_powEnd (n : ℤ)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (powEnd (R := R) (A := A) n f) (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) =
      pointsMulEquiv f (Multiplicative.ofAdd 1) ^ n := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_prodPointsMulEquiv
docstring: The diagonalizable product-points equivalence agrees with the existing character description of diagonalizable-group points: reading the character of a product point is the coproduct of the characters read from its two restrictions.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_prodPointsMulEquiv
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H') →ₐ[R] A)) :
    pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G' × H') f =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G') (prodPointsMulEquiv f).1).coprod
        (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := H') (prodPointsMulEquiv f).2) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse multiplicative equivalence sends a character to the point extending it.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (χ : G →* Aˣ) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A) (G := G)).symm χ = toConv (point χ) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd
docstring: **The `n`-th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`, on points.** Because `𝔾ₘ = D(Multiplicative ℤ)`, this is exactly the character of `𝔾ₘ` at the generator power `Multiplicative.ofAdd n` (`charPoints (Multiplicative.ofAdd n)`, recorded by `powEnd_eq_charPoints`); on points it acts as `u ↦ u ^ n`.
code:
noncomputable def powEnd (n : ℤ) :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A) →*
      WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative ℤ) →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd_comp
docstring: **Power endomorphisms compose by multiplying exponents:** `powEnd a ∘ powEnd b = powEnd (a*b)`. This is the multiplication of the endomorphism ring `End(𝔾ₘ) ≅ ℤ` on power maps.
code:
theorem powEnd_comp (a b : ℤ) :
    (powEnd (R := R) (A := A) a).comp (powEnd b) = powEnd (a * b) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd_eq_charPoints
docstring: The `n`-th power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ` is the character of `𝔾ₘ` at `Multiplicative.ofAdd n`.
code:
theorem powEnd_eq_charPoints (n : ℤ) :
    powEnd (R := R) (A := A) n = charPoints (Multiplicative.ofAdd n) := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd_one
docstring: The first power endomorphism is the identity.
code: theorem powEnd_one : powEnd (R := R) (A := A) 1 = MonoidHom.id _ := by

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.prodPointsMulEquiv
docstring: **The diagonalizable group of a product is the product of diagonalizable groups, on points.** For commutative groups `G` and `H` and every commutative `R`-algebra `A`, the convolution group of `A`-points of `D(G × H)` is the product of the convolution groups of `A`-points of `D(G)` and `D(H)`.
code:
noncomputable def prodPointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H') →ₐ[R] A) ≃*
      WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A) × WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R H' →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.prodPointsMulEquiv_fst_ofConv_single
docstring: On generators, the first component of the diagonalizable product-points equivalence restricts along `g ↦ (g, 1)`.
code:
theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_fst_ofConv_single
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H') →ₐ[R] A)) (g : G') :
    (prodPointsMulEquiv f).1.ofConv (single g (1 : R)) =
      f.ofConv (single (g, (1 : H')) 1) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.prodPointsMulEquiv_mapValue
docstring: The diagonalizable product-points equivalence is natural in the value algebra.
code:
theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_mapValue {B : Type*} [CommSemiring B] [Algebra R B] (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H') →ₐ[R] A)) :
    prodPointsMulEquiv (A := B) (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H')) φ f) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G') φ (prodPointsMulEquiv f).1,
        AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R H') φ (prodPointsMulEquiv f).2) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.prodPointsMulEquiv_snd_ofConv_single
docstring: On generators, the second component of the diagonalizable product-points equivalence restricts along `h ↦ (1, h)`.
code:
theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_snd_ofConv_single
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G' × H') →ₐ[R] A)) (h : H') :
    (prodPointsMulEquiv f).2.ofConv (single h (1 : R)) =
      f.ofConv (single ((1 : G'), h) 1) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.prodPointsMulEquiv_symm_ofConv_single
docstring: On generators, the inverse diagonalizable product-points equivalence multiplies the two factor-point values.
code:
theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_symm_ofConv_single
    (f₁ : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R G' →ₐ[R] A)) (f₂ : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R H' →ₐ[R] A))
    (g : G') (h : H') :
    (prodPointsMulEquiv.symm (f₁, f₂)).ofConv (single (g, h) (1 : R)) =
      f₁.ofConv (single g 1) * f₂.ofConv (single h 1) :=

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv_T
docstring: Evaluating `AddMonoidAlgebra.toMultiplicativeAlgEquiv` on the Laurent generator `T n`: it sends `T n` to the group-like `single (ofAdd n) 1` of `R[Multiplicative ℤ]`.

label: TauCeti.DiagonalizableGroup.zpowersHom_ofAdd_comp
docstring: Composing the generator-`Multiplicative.ofAdd b` power homomorphism after the generator-`Multiplicative.ofAdd a` one multiplies exponents.
code:
private theorem zpowersHom_ofAdd_comp (a b : ℤ) :
    (zpowersHom (Multiplicative ℤ) (Multiplicative.ofAdd b)).comp
        (zpowersHom (Multiplicative ℤ) (Multiplicative.ofAdd a)) =
      zpowersHom (Multiplicative ℤ) (Multiplicative.ofAdd (a * b)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diff
docstring: `Diff I M n` is the group of `Cⁿ` self-diffeomorphisms of the manifold `M` modelled on `I`, under composition. With `n = ∞` this is the group underlying `Diff(M)` of the geometric-topology roadmap.
code:
abbrev Diff (I : ModelWithCorners 𝕜 E H) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M] [ChartedSpace H M]
    (n : ℕ∞ω) : Type _ := M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.applyContinuousConstSMul
docstring: The action of each self-diffeomorphism on `M` is continuous.
code: instance applyContinuousConstSMul : ContinuousConstSMul (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) M :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.applyFaithfulSMul
docstring: The tautological action of `M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M` on `M` is faithful.
code: instance applyFaithfulSMul : FaithfulSMul (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) M :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.applyMulAction
docstring: The tautological action of the self-diffeomorphism group on the manifold by evaluation.
code: instance applyMulAction : MulAction (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) M where

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.applySubgroupContinuousConstSMul
docstring: A subgroup of the self-diffeomorphism group acts continuously on `M` in the point, by the generic subgroup transfer for `ContinuousConstSMul`.
code:
abbrev applySubgroupContinuousConstSMul (G : Subgroup (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M)) :
    ContinuousConstSMul G M :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.apply_eq_of_mem_fixingSubgroup
docstring: A member of `fixingSubgroup s` fixes each point of `s`.
code:
theorem apply_eq_of_mem_fixingSubgroup {s : Set M} {f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M}
    (hf : f ∈ fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s) {x : M} (hx : x ∈ s) : f x = x :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.coe_inv
docstring: The inverse self-diffeomorphism coerces to the inverse diffeomorphism.
code: theorem coe_inv (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : ⇑(f⁻¹) = f.symm := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.coe_mul
docstring: Multiplication of self-diffeomorphisms coerces to function composition.
code: theorem coe_mul (f g : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : ⇑(f * g) = f ∘ g := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.coe_one
docstring: The unit self-diffeomorphism coerces to the identity function.
code: theorem coe_one : ⇑(1 : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) = id := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr
docstring: Conjugation by a diffeomorphism `e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N` as a group isomorphism between the self-diffeomorphism groups: `diffCongr e φ = e ∘ φ ∘ e⁻¹`. This is the diffeomorphism analogue of `Equiv.permCongr` and expresses that diffeomorphic manifolds have isomorphic self-diffeomorphism groups.
code: @[expose] def diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) : (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) ≃* (N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) where

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_apply
docstring: The underlying diffeomorphism of `diffCongr e φ` is `e ∘ φ ∘ e⁻¹`.
code:
theorem diffCongr_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :
    diffCongr e φ = (e.symm.trans φ).trans e := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_apply_apply
docstring: The conjugating isomorphism acts pointwise by `diffCongr e φ x = e (φ (e.symm x))`.
code:
theorem diffCongr_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (x : N) :
    diffCongr e φ x = e (φ (e.symm x)) := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_inv
docstring: The inverse of `diffCongr e φ` is `diffCongr e φ⁻¹`, since conjugation is a homomorphism.
code:
theorem diffCongr_inv (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :
    (diffCongr e φ)⁻¹ = diffCongr e φ⁻¹ := (map_inv (diffCongr e) φ).symm

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_mem_fixingSubgroup_image
docstring: Conjugating by `e` sends diffeomorphisms fixing `s` pointwise to diffeomorphisms fixing `e '' s` pointwise.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_refl
docstring: Conjugating by the identity diffeomorphism is the identity isomorphism.
code:
theorem diffCongr_refl :
    diffCongr (_root_.Diffeomorph.refl I M n) = MulEquiv.refl (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_symm
docstring: The isomorphism conjugating by `e.symm` is the inverse of the one conjugating by `e`.
code: theorem diffCongr_symm (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) : (diffCongr e).symm = diffCongr e.symm := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_symm_mem_fixingSubgroup
docstring: Conjugating by `e.symm` sends diffeomorphisms fixing `e '' s` pointwise back to diffeomorphisms fixing `s` pointwise.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.diffCongr_trans
docstring: Conjugation is functorial: conjugating by a composite diffeomorphism is the composite of the conjugating isomorphisms.
code:
theorem diffCongr_trans (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (e' : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, K⟯ P) :
    diffCongr (e.trans e') = (diffCongr e).trans (diffCongr e') := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup
docstring: The subgroup of self-diffeomorphisms fixing every point of `s`. This is Mathlib's generic `fixingSubgroup`, specialized to the tautological action of `M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M` on `M`. For a boundary set this is the algebraic part of the relative diffeomorphism group `Diff(M, ∂M)`.
code: abbrev fixingSubgroup (s : Set M) : Subgroup (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_antitone
docstring: Fixing a larger set pointwise gives a smaller subgroup.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_antitone {s t : Set M} (hst : s ⊆ t) :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) t ≤ fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_congr
docstring: Pointwise fixing is invariant under replacing the subset by an equal subset.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_congr {s t : Set M} (hst : s = t) :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s = fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) t := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_empty
docstring: The relative diffeomorphism group fixing the empty set is the full diffeomorphism group.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_empty :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (M := M) (n := n) (∅ : Set M) = ⊤ := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_le_stabilizer
docstring: The pointwise fixer of a subset is contained in its setwise stabilizer.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_le_stabilizer (s : Set M) :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s ≤
      MulAction.stabilizer (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) s := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_union
docstring: Fixing `s ∪ t` pointwise is the same as fixing both `s` and `t` pointwise.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_union (s t : Set M) :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) (s ∪ t) =
      fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s ⊓ fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) t := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.fixingSubgroup_univ
docstring: The relative diffeomorphism group fixing all points is trivial.
code:
theorem fixingSubgroup_univ :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (M := M) (n := n) (Set.univ : Set M) = ⊥ := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.instGroup
docstring: The `Cⁿ` self-diffeomorphisms of `M` form a group under composition, with multiplication acting as function composition.
code: instance instGroup : Group (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) where

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.instInv
docstring: The inverse in the self-diffeomorphism group is the inverse diffeomorphism.
code: instance instInv : Inv (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) where inv f := f.symm

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.instMul
docstring: Multiplication of self-diffeomorphisms is composition: `f * g` follows `g` then `f`, so that it acts as `f ∘ g`, matching the `Equiv.Perm` convention.
code: instance instMul : Mul (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) where mul f g := g.trans f

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.instOne
docstring: The identity diffeomorphism is the unit of the self-diffeomorphism group.
code: instance instOne : One (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) where one := _root_.Diffeomorph.refl I M n

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.inv_apply
docstring: The inverse in the self-diffeomorphism group acts as the inverse diffeomorphism.
code: theorem inv_apply (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (x : M) : f⁻¹ x = f.symm x := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.inv_def
docstring: Inversion in the self-diffeomorphism group is the inverse diffeomorphism.
code: theorem inv_def (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : f⁻¹ = f.symm := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.map_fixingSubgroup_diffCongr
docstring: Conjugation by `e` maps the subgroup fixing `s` pointwise onto the subgroup fixing `e '' s` pointwise.
code:
theorem map_fixingSubgroup_diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (s : Set M) :
    (fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s).map (diffCongr e).toMonoidHom =
      fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) (e '' s) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.map_fixingSubgroup_diffCongr_of_image_eq
docstring: Conjugation by `e` maps the subgroup fixing `s` pointwise onto the subgroup fixing a named target `t` pointwise, when `t` is the image of `s`.
code:
theorem map_fixingSubgroup_diffCongr_of_image_eq (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) {s : Set M} {t : Set N}
    (hst : e '' s = t) :
    (fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s).map (diffCongr e).toMonoidHom =
      fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) t := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.mem_fixingSubgroup_iff
docstring: Membership in the pointwise fixing subgroup is the pointwise fixedness equation on `s`.
code:
theorem mem_fixingSubgroup_iff {s : Set M} {f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M} :
    f ∈ fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s ↔ ∀ x ∈ s, f x = x := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.mem_fixingSubgroup_of_forall
docstring: To prove that a diffeomorphism lies in the pointwise fixing subgroup, prove it fixes each point of the subset.
code:
theorem mem_fixingSubgroup_of_forall {s : Set M} {f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M}
    (hf : ∀ x ∈ s, f x = x) : f ∈ fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.mul_apply
docstring: Multiplication of self-diffeomorphisms acts by applying the right factor, then the left.
code: theorem mul_apply (f g : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (x : M) : (f * g) x = f (g x) := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.mul_def
docstring: Multiplication in the self-diffeomorphism group is `Diffeomorph.trans` in composition order.
code: theorem mul_def (f g : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : f * g = g.trans f := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.one_apply
docstring: The unit self-diffeomorphism fixes every point.
code: theorem one_apply (x : M) : (1 : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) x = x := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.one_def
docstring: The unit of the self-diffeomorphism group is the identity diffeomorphism.
code: theorem one_def : (1 : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) = _root_.Diffeomorph.refl I M n := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongr
docstring: Conjugation by a diffeomorphism identifies the relative diffeomorphism group fixing `s` pointwise with the relative diffeomorphism group fixing the image subset `e '' s` pointwise.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq
docstring: Conjugation by a diffeomorphism identifies the relative diffeomorphism group fixing `s` pointwise with the relative diffeomorphism group fixing a named target `t` pointwise, when `t` is the image of `s`.
code:
def relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) {s : Set M} {t : Set N}
    (hst : e '' s = t) :
    fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s ≃*
      fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) t :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_apply
docstring: Applying `relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq` and then forgetting the subgroup is `Diffeomorph.diffCongr`.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise formula for the named-target relative conjugation equivalence.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) {s : Set M} {t : Set N}
    (hst : e '' s = t) (φ : fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s) (y : N) :
    ((relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq e hst φ : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) y) =
      e ((φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (e.symm y)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_symm_apply
docstring: Applying the inverse of `relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq` and then forgetting the subgroup is conjugation by `e.symm`.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_symm_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise formula for the inverse named-target relative conjugation equivalence.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq_symm_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N)
    {s : Set M} {t : Set N} (hst : e '' s = t)
    (ψ : fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) t) (x : M) :
    (((relativeDiffCongrOfImageEq e hst).symm ψ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) x) =
      e.symm ((ψ : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) (e x)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongr_apply
docstring: Applying `relativeDiffCongr` and then forgetting the subgroup is `Diffeomorph.diffCongr`.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongr_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (s : Set M)
    (φ : fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s) :
    (relativeDiffCongr e s φ : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) = diffCongr e φ := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongr_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise formula for the relative conjugation equivalence.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongr_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (s : Set M)
    (φ : fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s) (y : N) :
    ((relativeDiffCongr e s φ : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) y) =
      e ((φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (e.symm y)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongr_symm_apply
docstring: Applying the inverse of `relativeDiffCongr` and then forgetting the subgroup is conjugation by `e.symm`.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongr_symm_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (s : Set M)
    (ψ : fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) (e '' s)) :
    ((relativeDiffCongr e s).symm ψ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) = diffCongr e.symm ψ := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.relativeDiffCongr_symm_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise formula for the inverse relative conjugation equivalence.
code:
theorem relativeDiffCongr_symm_apply_apply (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (s : Set M)
    (ψ : fixingSubgroup (I := J) (n := n) (e '' s)) (x : M) :
    (((relativeDiffCongr e s).symm ψ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) x) =
      e.symm ((ψ : N ≃ₘ^n⟮J, J⟯ N) (e x)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.smul_def
docstring: The tautological action of `M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M` on `M` is given by evaluation.
code: theorem smul_def (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) (x : M) : f • x = f x := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toEquiv_inv
docstring: The underlying equivalence preserves inversion of self-diffeomorphisms.
code: theorem toEquiv_inv (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : (f⁻¹).toEquiv = f.toEquiv⁻¹ := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toEquiv_mul
docstring: The underlying equivalence preserves multiplication of self-diffeomorphisms.
code: theorem toEquiv_mul (f g : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) : (f * g).toEquiv = f.toEquiv * g.toEquiv := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toEquiv_one
docstring: The underlying equivalence of the unit self-diffeomorphism is the unit permutation.
code: theorem toEquiv_one : (1 : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M).toEquiv = 1 := rfl

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorphHom
docstring: The forgetful group homomorphism from self-diffeomorphisms to self-homeomorphisms.
code: def toHomeomorphHom : (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) →* (M ≃ₜ M) where

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorphHom_apply
docstring: The forgetful homomorphism to self-homeomorphisms sends a diffeomorphism to its underlying homeomorphism.
code:
theorem toHomeomorphHom_apply (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :
    toHomeomorphHom f = f.toHomeomorph := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorphHom_comp_diffCongr
docstring: Naturality of `diffCongr` against the forgetful homomorphism to self-homeomorphisms, as a commutative square of group homomorphisms: conjugating diffeomorphisms by `e` and then forgetting smoothness equals forgetting smoothness and then conjugating homeomorphisms by `e` through `Homeomorph.homeoCongr`. This is the naturality of `diffCongr` against the stronger forgetful homomorphism `Diffeomorph.toHomeomorphHom`, refining `toPerm_comp_diffCongr`.
code:
theorem toHomeomorphHom_comp_diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) :
    toHomeomorphHom.comp (diffCongr e).toMonoidHom =
      (Homeomorph.homeoCongr e.toHomeomorph).toMonoidHom.comp toHomeomorphHom := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorphHom_injective
docstring: The forgetful homomorphism to self-homeomorphisms is injective.
code:
theorem toHomeomorphHom_injective :
    Function.Injective (toHomeomorphHom : (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) → (M ≃ₜ M)) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorph_diffCongr
docstring: Forgetting only smoothness (keeping the topology) sends `diffCongr e φ` to the conjugate of underlying self-homeomorphisms `e ∘ φ ∘ e⁻¹`; the elementwise shadow of `toHomeomorphHom_comp_diffCongr`.
code:
theorem toHomeomorph_diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :
    (diffCongr e φ).toHomeomorph =
      (e.toHomeomorph.symm.trans φ.toHomeomorph).trans e.toHomeomorph := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toHomeomorph_mem_fixingSubgroup
docstring: The forgetful homomorphism to homeomorphisms sends a relative diffeomorphism to a homeomorphism fixing the same subset pointwise.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toPerm
docstring: The forgetful group homomorphism from the self-diffeomorphism group to the permutation group of the underlying set, sending a diffeomorphism to its underlying equivalence.
code: def toPerm : (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) →* Equiv.Perm M where

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toPermHom_eq_toPerm
docstring: The action homomorphism of the tautological diffeomorphism action is the forgetful homomorphism to permutations.
code:
theorem toPermHom_eq_toPerm :
    MulAction.toPermHom (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) M = toPerm := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toPerm_comp_diffCongr
docstring: Naturality of `diffCongr` against the forgetful homomorphism to permutations, as a commutative square of group homomorphisms intertwining `diffCongr` with `Equiv.permCongrHom`; this is the `toPerm`-level shadow of `toHomeomorphHom_comp_diffCongr`.
code:
theorem toPerm_comp_diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) :
    toPerm.comp (diffCongr e).toMonoidHom = e.toEquiv.permCongrHom.toMonoidHom.comp toPerm := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toPerm_diffCongr
docstring: Forgetting all topology intertwines `diffCongr` with `Equiv.permCongr` on the permutation groups; the elementwise shadow of `toPerm_comp_diffCongr`.
code:
theorem toPerm_diffCongr (e : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, J⟯ N) (φ : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) :
    toPerm (diffCongr e φ) = e.toEquiv.permCongr (toPerm φ) := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toPerm_injective
docstring: The forgetful homomorphism to permutations is injective.
code: theorem toPerm_injective : Function.Injective (toPerm : (M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M) → Equiv.Perm M) :=

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toRelativeHomeomorphHom
docstring: Forgetting smoothness maps the relative diffeomorphism group into the corresponding relative homeomorphism group.

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.toRelativeHomeomorphHom_apply
docstring: Applying the forgetful homomorphism to a relative diffeomorphism is its underlying homeomorphism.
code:
theorem toRelativeHomeomorphHom_apply (s : Set M)
    (f : fixingSubgroup (I := I) (n := n) s) :
    (toRelativeHomeomorphHom (M := M) s f : M ≃ₜ M) =
      (f : M ≃ₘ^n⟮I, I⟯ M).toHomeomorph := by

label: TauCeti.Diffeomorph.trans_assoc

docstring: **The maximal elementary-2 quotient `G / G²`** of a commutative group, written additively on `Additive G`.
code: abbrev ElementaryTwoQuotient : Type _ :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat
docstring: The category of finitely generated right comodules over a fixed coalgebra. For a field base, this is the category of finite-dimensional right comodules.
code: abbrev FGComoduleCat :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.add_apply
docstring: Addition of morphisms acts by pointwise addition.
code: theorem add_apply (f g : M ⟶ N) (m : M) : (f + g) m = f m + g m :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.carrier
docstring: The underlying type of a finitely generated comodule.
code: def carrier (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, w} R C) : Type w :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofree
docstring: The cofree right `C`-comodule with finitely generated tensor-product carrier, bundled as an object of `FGComoduleCat`. The underlying module is `M ⊗[R] C`, with coaction `id ⊗ Δ` followed by reassociation.
code:
noncomputable abbrev cofree (M : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
    [Module.Finite R (M ⊗[R] C)] : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, max w v} R C :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeEquiv
docstring: The finite-category cofree universal property.
code:
@[expose] noncomputable def cofreeEquiv (P : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, max w v} R C) :
    (P ⟶ cofree (R := R) (C := C) M) ≃ (P →ₗ[R] M) := by

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeEquiv_apply
docstring: The forward direction of the finite cofree adjunction sends a comodule morphism to the `R`-linear map obtained by applying the counit to the `C` factor.
code:
theorem cofreeEquiv_apply (φ : P ⟶ cofree (R := R) (C := C) M) :
    cofreeEquiv (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) P φ =
      Comodule.Hom.cofreeEquiv (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) (P := P) φ.hom := by

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse direction of the finite cofree adjunction is `cofreeLift`.
code:
theorem cofreeEquiv_symm_apply (g : P →ₗ[R] M) :
    (cofreeEquiv (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) P).symm g =
      cofreeLift (R := R) (C := C) P g :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeLift
docstring: The finite-category cofree lift of an `R`-linear map from a finite comodule to the coefficient module.
code:
noncomputable abbrev cofreeLift (P : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, max w v} R C) (g : P →ₗ[R] M) :
    P ⟶ cofree (R := R) (C := C) M :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeLift_apply
docstring: `cofreeLift g` acts as `(g ⊗ id) ∘ ρ_P`.
code:
theorem cofreeLift_apply (g : P →ₗ[R] M) (p : P) :
    cofreeLift (R := R) (C := C) P g p =
      g.rTensor C (Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := P) p) :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeMap
docstring: Functoriality of finite cofree comodules in the coefficient module. An `R`-linear map `f : M → N` induces the comodule morphism `f ⊗ id`.
code:
noncomputable abbrev cofreeMap (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    cofree (R := R) (C := C) M ⟶ cofree (R := R) (C := C) N :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeMap_apply
docstring: `cofreeMap f` acts as `f ⊗ id`.
code:
theorem cofreeMap_apply (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (x : M ⊗[R] C) :
    cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) f x = f.rTensor C x :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeMap_comp
docstring: The finite cofree construction preserves composition of coefficient-module maps.
code:
theorem cofreeMap_comp {P : Type w} [AddCommMonoid P] [Module R P]
    [Module.Finite R (P ⊗[R] C)] (g : N →ₗ[R] P) (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) (g.comp f) =
      cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) f ≫ cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) g := by

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeMap_id
docstring: The finite cofree construction sends the identity linear map to the identity morphism.
code:
theorem cofreeMap_id :
    cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) (LinearMap.id : M →ₗ[R] M) =
      𝟙 (cofree (R := R) (C := C) M) :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofreeMap_tmul
docstring: On simple tensors, `cofreeMap f` applies `f` to the coefficient factor.
code:
theorem cofreeMap_tmul (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (m : M) (c : C) :
    cofreeMap (R := R) (C := C) f (m ⊗ₜ[R] c) = f m ⊗ₜ[R] c :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofree_coact
docstring: The coaction on the finitely generated cofree comodule is `id ⊗ Δ` followed by reassociation.
code:
theorem cofree_coact :
    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := cofree (R := R) (C := C) M)
      = (TensorProduct.assoc R M C C).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ Coalgebra.comul.lTensor M :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofree_coact_tmul
docstring: The coaction on the finitely generated cofree comodule sends a simple tensor `m ⊗ c` to `∑ (m ⊗ c₁) ⊗ c₂`.
code:
theorem cofree_coact_tmul (m : M) (c : C) :
    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := cofree (R := R) (C := C) M) (m ⊗ₜ[R] c)
      = (TensorProduct.assoc R M C C).symm (m ⊗ₜ Coalgebra.comul c) :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofree_coe
docstring: The underlying type of the finitely generated cofree comodule is `M ⊗[R] C`.
code: theorem cofree_coe : (cofree (R := R) (C := C) M : Type (max w v)) = M ⊗[R] C :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.cofree_obj
docstring: Forgetting the finitely generated cofree comodule to all comodules gives the ambient cofree comodule.
code:
theorem cofree_obj :
    (cofree (R := R) (C := C) M).obj = ComoduleCat.cofree R C M :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict
docstring: Corestriction of finitely generated right comodules along a coalgebra morphism. The underlying module is unchanged, so the finite-generation proof is inherited from the source object.
code: def corestrict (f : C →ₗc[R] D) : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C ⥤ FGComoduleCat.{u, w, x} R D where

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_map_apply
docstring: Corestriction leaves the underlying function of a finitely generated comodule morphism unchanged.

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_map_comp_coalg_apply
docstring: Corestriction functors compose in the coalgebra morphism on elements.
code:
theorem corestrict_map_comp_coalg_apply (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (g : D →ₗc[R] E)
    {M N : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C} (h : M ⟶ N) (m : M) :
    (corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := E) (g.comp f)).map h m =
      (corestrict (R := R) (C := D) (D := E) g).map
        ((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).map h) m :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_map_comp_coalg_toLinearMap
docstring: Corestriction functors compose in the coalgebra morphism on underlying linear maps.
code:
theorem corestrict_map_comp_coalg_toLinearMap (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (g : D →ₗc[R] E)
    {M N : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C} (h : M ⟶ N) :
    (((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := E) (g.comp f)).map h).hom).toLinearMap =
      (((corestrict (R := R) (C := D) (D := E) g).map
        ((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).map h)).hom).toLinearMap :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_map_hom
docstring: Corestriction on finitely generated morphisms is corestriction on ambient comodule morphisms.
code:
theorem corestrict_map_hom (f : C →ₗc[R] D) {M N : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C}
    (g : M ⟶ N) :
    ((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).map g).hom =
      (ComoduleCat.corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).map g.hom :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_map_toLinearMap
docstring: Corestriction leaves the underlying linear map of a finitely generated comodule morphism unchanged.
code:
theorem corestrict_map_toLinearMap (f : C →ₗc[R] D) {M N : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C}
    (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).map g).hom).toLinearMap =
      g.hom.toLinearMap :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_obj_coact
docstring: The coaction after corestricting a finitely generated comodule is `(id ⊗ f) ∘ ρ`.
code:
theorem corestrict_obj_coact (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C) :
    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := D)
        (M := (corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).obj M) =
      Comodule.corestrictCoact (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) (M := M) f :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_obj_coact_apply
docstring: The coaction after corestricting a finitely generated comodule evaluates as `(id ⊗ f) (ρ m)`.
code:
theorem corestrict_obj_coact_apply (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C)

    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := D)
        (M := (corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).obj M) m =
      TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id f.toLinearMap
        (Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C) (M := M) m) :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_obj_coact_id
docstring: Corestricting finitely generated comodules along the identity coalgebra morphism leaves the coaction unchanged.
code:
theorem corestrict_obj_coact_id (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C) :
    Comodule.coact (R := R) (C := C)
        (M := (corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := C) (CoalgHom.id R C)).obj M) =

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_obj_coe
docstring: Corestriction leaves the underlying type of a finitely generated comodule unchanged.
code:
theorem corestrict_obj_coe (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C) :
    ((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).obj M : Type x) = M :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.corestrict_obj_obj
docstring: Corestriction on finitely generated comodules is corestriction on the ambient comodule.
code:
theorem corestrict_obj_obj (f : C →ₗc[R] D) (M : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C) :
    ((corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).obj M).obj =
      (ComoduleCat.corestrict (R := R) (C := C) (D := D) f).obj M.obj :=

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.forget₂_semimoduleCat_cofree_obj
docstring: The finite cofree comodule forgets to the tensor product module `M ⊗[R] C`.
code:
theorem forget₂_semimoduleCat_cofree_obj :
    (forget₂ (FGComoduleCat.{u, v, max w v} R C) (SemimoduleCat.{max w v} R)).obj
        (cofree (R := R) (C := C) M) =

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.forget₂_semimoduleCat_corestrict_map
docstring: Corestriction leaves the underlying semimodule morphism unchanged.
code:
theorem forget₂_semimoduleCat_corestrict_map (f : C →ₗc[R] D)
    {M N : FGComoduleCat.{u, v, x} R C} (g : M ⟶ N) :
    (forget₂ (FGComoduleCat.{u, w, x} R D) (SemimoduleCat.{x} R)).map

label: TauCeti.FGComoduleCat.forget₂_semimoduleCat_corestrict_obj
docstring: Corestriction leaves the underlying semimodule object unchanged.

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.liftQuotient_unique

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse product-points map is natural in the value algebra: assembling an `A`-valued product point from a pair of factor points and post-composing by `φ` is the same as post-composing both factor points by `φ` and then assembling the resulting `B`-valued point.
code:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (H K : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, v} R)
    (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := H) A × HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := K) A) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := tensorProduct H K) φ ((pointsMulEquiv A H K).symm p) =
      (pointsMulEquiv B H K).symm
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H) φ p.1, AlgHom.mapValue (H := K) φ p.2) :=

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul
docstring: On pure tensors, naturality of the inverse product-points map evaluates post-composition by `φ` as applying `φ` to the product of the two factor values.
code:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul (H K : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, v} R)
    (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := H) A × HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := K) A)
    (x : H) (y : K) :
    (AlgHom.mapValue (H := tensorProduct H K) φ ((pointsMulEquiv A H K).symm p)).ofConv
        (x ⊗ₜ[R] y) =
      φ (p.1.ofConv x * p.2.ofConv y) :=

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
docstring: The product-points equivalence is natural in the value algebra: post-composing a point of the product by `φ`, then splitting it into its two factor points, agrees with splitting first and then post-composing each factor point by `φ`.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (H K : FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u, v} R) (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := tensorProduct H K) A) :
    pointsMulEquiv B H K (AlgHom.mapValue (H := tensorProduct H K) φ f) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H) φ (pointsMulEquiv A H K f).1,
        AlgHom.mapValue (H := K) φ (pointsMulEquiv A H K f).2) :=

    (f : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := tensorProduct H K) A) :

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply

label: TauCeti.FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.pointsMulEquiv_symm_mapValue_apply_tmul
docstring: On pure tensors, assembling after post-composing both factor points by `φ` multiplies the two post-composed factor values.

    (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (p : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := H) A × HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := K) A)

      φ (p.1.ofConv x) * φ (p.2.ofConv y) :=

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus
docstring: A **framed boundary torus**: a boundary torus together with an ordered meridian-longitude basis `(μ, λ) = (basis 0, basis 1)` of its actual singular homology group. The framing is exactly this ordered basis; it is what identifies `H₁(T; ℤ)` with `ℤ × ℤ` and so what the `ℚ ∪ {∞}` parametrisation depends on.
code: structure FramedBoundaryTorus where

code: theorem coord_basis_one : T.coord (T.basis 1) = (0, 1) := by

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_basis_zero
code: theorem coord_basis_zero : T.coord (T.basis 0) = (1, 0) := by

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse coordinate isomorphism reads a pair of coordinates as the corresponding combination `p · μ + q · λ` of the framing basis.
code: theorem coord_symm_apply (v : ℤ × ℤ) : T.coord.symm v = v.1 • T.basis 0 + v.2 • T.basis 1 := by

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.isPrimitive_basis_one
code: theorem isPrimitive_basis_one : IsPrimitive (T.basis 1) :=

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.isPrimitive_basis_zero
code: theorem isPrimitive_basis_zero : IsPrimitive (T.basis 0) :=

code: noncomputable def longitude : Slope T.H := Slope.mk (T.basis 1) T.isPrimitive_basis_one

docstring: The meridian slope `μ = basis 0` of the framing.
code: noncomputable def meridian : Slope T.H := Slope.mk (T.basis 0) T.isPrimitive_basis_zero

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv
docstring: **The framed slope parametrisation.** A framing makes primitive homology classes modulo sign biject with `ℚ ∪ {∞}`, a reduced fraction `p / q` corresponding to the class with `(μ, λ)`-coordinates `(p, q)` and `∞` to the meridian.
code: noncomputable def slopeEquiv : Slope T.H ≃ OnePoint ℚ :=

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv_apply
code: theorem slopeEquiv_apply (s : Slope T.H) : T.slopeEquiv s = T.value s := (rfl)

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.slopeEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: **The framed parametrisation in the inverse direction.** The slope with value `x ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}` is the one whose `(μ, λ)`-coordinates are the standard reduced pair `slopeOfValue x`; for a rational `p / q` in lowest terms that is the class `p · μ + q · λ`, by `TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.coord_symm_apply`.
code:
theorem slopeEquiv_symm_apply (x : OnePoint ℚ) :
    T.slopeEquiv.symm x = Slope.congr T.coord.symm (slopeOfValue x) := by

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value
docstring: The framing-dependent value `p / q ∈ ℚ ∪ {∞}` of a slope: the ratio of its `(μ, λ)`-coordinates. Different framings give different values, which is why this is an operation of the framing rather than of the basis-free `Slope`.
code: noncomputable def value (s : Slope T.H) : OnePoint ℚ :=

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value_longitude
docstring: The framed longitude has slope value `0`.
code: theorem value_longitude : T.value T.longitude = (0 : ℚ) := by

label: TauCeti.FramedBoundaryTorus.value_meridian
docstring: The framed meridian has slope value `∞`.
code: theorem value_meridian : T.value T.meridian = ∞ := by

code:
theorem value_mk (v : T.H) (hv : IsPrimitive v) :
    T.value (Slope.mk v hv) = slopeValue (T.coord v) := (rfl)

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_mk
docstring: On normalizer representatives, basepoint-change transport is induced by the path-conjugation isomorphism of fundamental groups.

lemma basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_mk (γ : Path x₀ x₁)
    (H : Subgroup (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀))
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀))) :
    basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv γ H (g : Subgroup.normalizerQuotient H) =
      ((MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (by rw [basepointChangeSubgroup])
          (Subgroup.normalizerEquivMap H
            (_root_.FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ) g) :
          _root_.Subgroup.normalizer
            ((basepointChangeSubgroup γ H) : Set (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₁))) :
        Subgroup.normalizerQuotient (basepointChangeSubgroup γ H)) := by

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_mk_coe
docstring: On representatives, basepoint-change transport applies the path-conjugation isomorphism of fundamental groups.
code:
lemma basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_mk_coe (γ : Path x₀ x₁)
    (H : Subgroup (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀))
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀))) :
    basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv γ H (Subgroup.normalizerQuotientMk H g) =
      Subgroup.normalizerQuotientMk (basepointChangeSubgroup γ H)
        (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (by rw [basepointChangeSubgroup])
          (⟨_root_.FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ
              (g : _root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀),
            by

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_symm_mk
docstring: The inverse basepoint-change transport sends a target representative to the inverse path-conjugation representative.
code:
lemma basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv_symm_mk (γ : Path x₀ x₁)
    (H : Subgroup (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀))
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer
      ((basepointChangeSubgroup γ H) : Set (_root_.FundamentalGroup X x₁))) :
    (basepointChangeNormalizerQuotientEquiv γ H).symm
        (g : Subgroup.normalizerQuotient (basepointChangeSubgroup γ H)) =
      (((Subgroup.normalizerEquivMap H
          (_root_.FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ)).symm
          ((MulEquiv.subgroupCongr (by rw [basepointChangeSubgroup])).symm g)) :
        Subgroup.normalizerQuotient H) := by

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.basepointChangeSubgroup_le_iff

      H ≤ K.comap (((_root_.FundamentalGroup.fundamentalGroupMulEquivOfPath γ) :
        _root_.FundamentalGroup X x₀ →* _root_.FundamentalGroup X x₁)) := by

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.le_basepointChangeSubgroup_iff

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq_comp
docstring: The maps induced on fundamental groups by two continuous maps compose to the map induced by their composite: `mapOfEq g hg (mapOfEq f hf p) = mapOfEq (g.comp f) _ p`.

      _root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq (g.comp f)
        (show (g.comp f) x = z by rw [ContinuousMap.comp_apply, hf, hg]) p := by

label: TauCeti.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq_mapOfEq_of_comp_eq_id

    _root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq g hg (_root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq f hf p) = p := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_fortyNine_mul_ncard_inter_box_one
docstring: **A concrete doubling instance.** Passing from the unit box to the double box multiplies the Gaussian-lattice point count by at most the engine's proved factor `49^{#ι} = 49` at `#ι = 1`: `#(Λ ∩ box 2) ≤ 49 · #(Λ ∩ box 1)`.
code:
theorem gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_fortyNine_mul_ncard_inter_box_one :
    (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤
      49 * (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 1).ncard : ℝ) := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_sixtyFour_mul_ncard_inter_box_one

theorem gaussianLattice_ncard_inter_box_two_le_sixtyFour_mul_ncard_inter_box_one :
    (((gaussianLattice : Set (Fin 1 → ℂ)) ∩ box (fun _ => 1) 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.gaussianLattice_separated
docstring: The separation hypothesis the packing lemma consumes: every nonzero lattice point escapes the box of scale `1/2`.

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.injOn_cellIndexMap_of_separated
docstring: The cell-index map is injective on a set whose distinct points are `ε`-separated in some coordinate: two points sharing every cell index would differ by less than the cell diameter `ε·rᵢ` in that coordinate, contradicting the separation.

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.mem_box
docstring: Membership in `box r c` unfolds to the coordinatewise norm bounds `‖x i‖ ≤ c · r i`.
code:
@[simp] theorem mem_box {r : ι → ℝ} {c : ℝ} {x : ι → ℂ} :
    x ∈ box r c ↔ ∀ i, ‖x i‖ ≤ c * r i := Iff.rfl

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.mem_gaussianLattice
docstring: Membership in the Gaussian lattice unfolds to the single coordinate being a Gaussian integer.
code:
theorem mem_gaussianLattice {x : Fin 1 → ℂ} :
    x ∈ gaussianLattice ↔ ∃ m n : ℤ, x 0 = (m : ℂ) + (n : ℂ) * Complex.I := Iff.rfl

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.ncard_inter_box_two_le_pow_mul_ncard_inter_box_one
docstring: **Doubling.** Assuming `Λ ∩ box r 2` is finite, counting lattice points in the double box loses at most `49 ^ #ι` against the unit box: `#(Λ ∩ box r 2) ≤ 49 ^ #ι · #(Λ ∩ box r 1)`.
code:
theorem ncard_inter_box_two_le_pow_mul_ncard_inter_box_one (r : ι → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (Λ : AddSubgroup (ι → ℂ)) (hfin : ((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).Finite) :
    (((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 2).ncard : ℝ) ≤
      49 ^ Fintype.card ι * ((Λ : Set (ι → ℂ)) ∩ box r 1).ncard := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.norm_lt_of_re_im_bound
docstring: A complex number whose real and imaginary parts are each `< d` in absolute value has norm `< d·√2`.
code:
private theorem norm_lt_of_re_im_bound {z : ℂ} {d : ℝ} (hd : 0 ≤ d)
    (hre : |z.re| < d) (him : |z.im| < d) : ‖z‖ < d * Real.sqrt 2 := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.norm_sub_le_of_coarseCell_eq
docstring: If two complex numbers share their coarse cell (side `2·ri/3`) in both the real and the imaginary part, their distance is at most `ri`.
code:
private theorem norm_sub_le_of_coarseCell_eq {ri : ℝ} (hri : 0 < ri) {z w : ℂ}
    (hre : ⌊z.re / (2 * ri / 3)⌋ = ⌊w.re / (2 * ri / 3)⌋)
    (him : ⌊z.im / (2 * ri / 3)⌋ = ⌊w.im / (2 * ri / 3)⌋) :
    ‖z - w‖ ≤ ri := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.one_le_norm_of_mem_gaussianLattice_of_ne_zero
docstring: **Minimal distance of the Gaussian lattice.** A nonzero Gaussian integer has norm at least `1`, since its squared norm `m² + n²` is a positive integer. This is the separation input the packing lemma needs.
code:
theorem one_le_norm_of_mem_gaussianLattice_of_ne_zero {x : Fin 1 → ℂ}
    (hx : x ∈ gaussianLattice) (hne : x ≠ 0) : 1 ≤ ‖x 0‖ := by

label: TauCeti.GeometryOfNumbers.sub_mem_box_one_of_coarseCellMap_eq
docstring: Two points sharing every coarse cell `coarseCellMap r` differ by at most `r i` in each coordinate, so their difference lies in `box r 1`.

label: TauCeti.Grid.Noninterleaving
docstring: Two oriented cyclic intervals have non-interleaving endpoint pairs. The endpoints `a₀`, `a₁` lie on the same side of the pair `b₀`, `b₁`, and conversely. This two-sided formulation handles shared-endpoint cases uniformly.
code: @[expose] def Noninterleaving (a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ : Fin n) : Prop :=

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo
docstring: The clockwise open cyclic interval from `a` to `b` in `Fin n`. If `a < b` in the standard representatives, this is the ordinary open interval `a < x < b`. If `b ≤ a` and `a ≠ b`, it wraps around `0`, so it is the union of `a < x` and `x < b`. The interval from a point to itself is empty.
code: noncomputable def cIoo (a b : Fin n) : Finset (Fin n) :=

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo_eq_empty_of_le_two
docstring: In a grid of size at most two, every open cyclic interval is empty. There are no grid points strictly between two endpoints on either of the two complementary arcs.
code: theorem cIoo_eq_empty_of_le_two (hn : n ≤ 2) (a b : Fin n) : cIoo a b = ∅ := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo_image_rev
docstring: A clockwise open cyclic interval reversed by `Fin.rev` is the clockwise open cyclic interval with the two endpoints reversed and exchanged. Coordinate reversal reverses the cyclic order, so it turns the clockwise arc from `a` to `b` into the clockwise arc from `bᵒ` to `aᵒ`.
code:
theorem cIoo_image_rev (a b : Fin n) :
    (cIoo a b).image Fin.rev = cIoo b.rev a.rev := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo_self
docstring: The open cyclic interval from a point to itself is empty.
code: theorem cIoo_self (a : Fin n) : cIoo a a = ∅ := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo_swap_eq_erase_erase_sdiff
docstring: The opposite cyclic interval is the endpoint complement with the first interval removed.
code:
theorem cIoo_swap_eq_erase_erase_sdiff {a b : Fin n} (h : a ≠ b) :
    cIoo b a = (Finset.univ.erase a).erase b \ cIoo a b := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.cIoo_union_swap
docstring: The two opposite cyclic intervals cover exactly the complement of their endpoints.
code:
theorem cIoo_union_swap {a b : Fin n} (h : a ≠ b) :
    cIoo a b ∪ cIoo b a = (Finset.univ.erase a).erase b := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.card_cIoo_add_card_cIoo_swap
docstring: The two complementary cyclic intervals have total cardinality `n - 2`.
code:
theorem card_cIoo_add_card_cIoo_swap {a b : Fin n} (h : a ≠ b) :
    (cIoo a b).card + (cIoo b a).card = n - 2 := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.disjoint_cIoo_swap
docstring: Opposite open cyclic intervals with the same endpoints are disjoint.
code: theorem disjoint_cIoo_swap (a b : Fin n) : Disjoint (cIoo a b) (cIoo b a) := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.left_notMem_cIoo
docstring: The initial endpoint is not in its open cyclic interval.
code: theorem left_notMem_cIoo (a b : Fin n) : a ∉ cIoo a b := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.mem_cIoo
docstring: Membership in a clockwise open cyclic interval, unfolded as inequalities between the standard representatives.
code:
theorem mem_cIoo (a b x : Fin n) :
    x ∈ cIoo a b ↔
      a ≠ b ∧
        if a.val < b.val then
          a.val < x.val ∧ x.val < b.val
        else
          a.val < x.val ∨ x.val < b.val := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.mem_cIoo_or_mem_cIoo_swap_iff
docstring: Membership in one of the two opposite cyclic intervals is the same as being neither endpoint.
code:
theorem mem_cIoo_or_mem_cIoo_swap_iff {a b x : Fin n} (h : a ≠ b) :
    x ∈ cIoo a b ∨ x ∈ cIoo b a ↔ x ≠ a ∧ x ≠ b := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.mem_cIoo_rev_rev
docstring: Membership in a clockwise open arc with both endpoints and the queried point reversed by `Fin.rev`. Since coordinate reversal reverses the cyclic order, the reversed point lies in the reversed arc exactly when the original point lies in the opposite arc.
code:
theorem mem_cIoo_rev_rev (a b x : Fin n) :
    x.rev ∈ cIoo a.rev b.rev ↔ x ∈ cIoo b a := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.noninterleaving_comm
docstring: Non-interleaving is symmetric in the two endpoint pairs.
code:
theorem noninterleaving_comm {a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ : Fin n} :
    Noninterleaving a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ ↔ Noninterleaving b₀ b₁ a₀ a₁ := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.noninterleaving_iff
docstring: The defining endpoint-side conditions for `Grid.Noninterleaving`.
code:
theorem noninterleaving_iff (a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ : Fin n) :
    Noninterleaving a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ ↔
      (a₀ ∈ cIoo b₀ b₁ ↔ a₁ ∈ cIoo b₀ b₁) ∧
        (b₀ ∈ cIoo a₀ a₁ ↔ b₁ ∈ cIoo a₀ a₁) :=

label: TauCeti.Grid.noninterleaving_rev
docstring: Non-interleaving is preserved by reversing every endpoint with `Fin.rev`, with the cyclic orientation reversal accounted for by exchanging the two endpoints within each pair.
code:
theorem noninterleaving_rev (a₀ a₁ b₀ b₁ : Fin n) :
    Noninterleaving a₀.rev a₁.rev b₀.rev b₁.rev ↔ Noninterleaving a₁ a₀ b₁ b₀ := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.noninterleaving_self
docstring: An endpoint pair is non-interleaving with itself.
code: theorem noninterleaving_self (a₀ a₁ : Fin n) : Noninterleaving a₀ a₁ a₀ a₁ := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.not_mem_cIoo_and_cIoo_swap
docstring: A point cannot lie in both open cyclic intervals with the same endpoints but opposite orientations.
code:
private theorem not_mem_cIoo_and_cIoo_swap (a b x : Fin n) :
    ¬(x ∈ cIoo a b ∧ x ∈ cIoo b a) := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.not_mem_cIoo_iff
docstring: A point outside the clockwise interval from `a` to `b` is either an endpoint or lies in the opposite clockwise interval.
code:
theorem not_mem_cIoo_iff {a b x : Fin n} (h : a ≠ b) :
    x ∉ cIoo a b ↔ x = a ∨ x = b ∨ x ∈ cIoo b a := by

label: TauCeti.Grid.right_notMem_cIoo
docstring: The terminal endpoint is not in its open cyclic interval.
code: theorem right_notMem_cIoo (a b : Fin n) : b ∉ cIoo a b := by

label: TauCeti.GridChain.map_ker_of_intertwine

label: TauCeti.GridChain.relabelEquiv
docstring: The linear automorphism of grid chains induced by relabeling each generator `x` along an equivalence `e` of grid states, sending the generator `x` to the generator `e x`. The transpose and rotation relabelings below are the two special cases in which `e` is the permutation of grid states coming from an involution. This is an implementation helper that factors those two equivalences; it is private because no downstream consumer refers to it.

label: TauCeti.GridChain.relabelEquiv_apply
docstring: The `y`-coefficient of a relabeled chain is the `e.symm y`-coefficient of the original chain.

label: TauCeti.GridChain.relabelEquiv_single
docstring: The relabeling along `e` sends the generator `x` to the generator `e x`.

label: TauCeti.GridChain.relabelEquiv_symm
docstring: The inverse of the relabeling along `e` is the relabeling along `e.symm`.

label: TauCeti.GridChain.rotateEquiv
docstring: The linear automorphism of grid chains induced by the half-turn rotation of grid states. Because `GridState.rotate` is an involution, relabeling each generator `x` by `x.rotate` gives a linear automorphism of the chain module `GridChain R n`.

noncomputable def rotateEquiv (R : Type*) [Semiring R] (n : ℕ) :
    GridChain R n ≃ₗ[R] GridChain R n :=

label: TauCeti.GridChain.rotateEquiv_apply
docstring: The `y`-coefficient of a relabeled chain is the `y.rotate`-coefficient of the original chain.
code:
theorem rotateEquiv_apply {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {n : ℕ} (f : GridChain R n)
    (y : GridState n) : rotateEquiv R n f y = f y.rotate :=

label: TauCeti.GridChain.rotateEquiv_single
docstring: The rotation relabeling sends the generator `x` to the generator `x.rotate`.

theorem rotateEquiv_single {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {n : ℕ} (x : GridState n) (a : R) :

label: TauCeti.GridChain.rotateEquiv_symm

theorem rotateEquiv_symm {R : Type*} [Semiring R] {n : ℕ} :
    (rotateEquiv R n).symm = rotateEquiv R n := by

theorem JO_eq_card (x : GridState n) :

      (((Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ x p.1 < G.O p.2).card +
        (Finset.univ.filter fun p : Fin n × Fin n => p.1 < p.2 ∧ G.O p.1 < x p.2).card : ℕ) :

label: TauCeti.GridDiagram.alexander_change_rectangle
docstring: The Alexander grading change across a rectangle move, localized to the four corners: it is the four `X`-corner pairings minus the four `O`-corner pairings, in each case the two source corners against the two target corners.     G.alexander x - G.alexander y =
      ((GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.bottom)} G.XSet + GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.top)} G.XSet) -
          (GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.top)} G.XSet + GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.bottom)} G.XSet)) -
        ((GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.bottom)} G.OSet + GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.top)} G.OSet) -
          (GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.top)} G.OSet + GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.bottom)} G.OSet)) := by

              GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.bottom)} (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet) +
              GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.top)} (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet)) -
            (GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.top)} {(R.right, R.bottom)} +
              GridPoint.J {(R.left, R.top)} (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet) +
              GridPoint.J {(R.right, R.bottom)} (x.pointSet ∩ y.pointSet))) := by

docstring: The non-inversions and the inversions of a grid state partition the ordered column pairs: the number of pairs `c < d` with `x c < x d` plus the number with `x d < x c` is the total number of pairs `c < d`.
