    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃* HomotopyGroup N Y (e x) :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq
docstring: A homeomorphism `e : X ≃ₜ Y` carrying `x` to `y` induces an isomorphism of homotopy groups `π_N(X, x) ≃* π_N(Y, y)` in positive dimensions.
code:
@[expose] noncomputable def homeomorphMulEquivOfEq [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x ≃* HomotopyGroup N Y y :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_apply
code:
theorem homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphMulEquivOfEq e h a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ h a :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_symm_apply
code:
theorem homeomorphMulEquivOfEq_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (h : e x = y)
    (b : HomotopyGroup N Y y) :
    (homeomorphMulEquivOfEq e h).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_eq.mpr h.symm) b :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquiv_apply
code:
theorem homeomorphMulEquiv_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    homeomorphMulEquiv e x a = map ⟨e, e.continuous⟩ rfl a :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.homeomorphMulEquiv_symm_apply
code:
theorem homeomorphMulEquiv_symm_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (e : X ≃ₜ Y) (x : X)
    (b : HomotopyGroup N Y (e x)) :
    (homeomorphMulEquiv e x).symm b =
      map ⟨e.symm, e.symm.continuous⟩ (e.symm_apply_apply x) b :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map
docstring: The map on homotopy classes induced by a based continuous map.
code:
@[expose] def map (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x → HomotopyGroup N Y y :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom
docstring: In positive dimensions, the map induced by a based continuous map is a monoid homomorphism for the standard group structure on homotopy groups.
code:
@[expose] def mapHom [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    HomotopyGroup N X x →* HomotopyGroup N Y y where

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_apply
code:
theorem mapHom_apply [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    mapHom f hf a = map f hf a :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_comp
docstring: Composition law for the bundled homomorphism: the induced monoid homomorphism of a composite continuous map is the composite of the induced homomorphisms.
code:
theorem mapHom_comp [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : g y = z)
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    (mapHom g hg).comp (mapHom f hf) = mapHom (N := N) (g.comp f) (by simp [hf, hg]) :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_continuousMap_const_eq_one
docstring: In positive dimensions, a constant continuous map induces the trivial homomorphism on homotopy groups. This is not a `simp` lemma: baking the basepoint proof `rfl` into the statement forces the target basepoint to be `(ContinuousMap.const X y) x` rather than `y`, so `simp` cannot close even its own statement. Use it as an explicit rewrite.
code:
theorem mapHom_continuousMap_const_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (y : Y) :
    mapHom (N := N) (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_eq_of_homotopicRel
docstring: Continuous maps homotopic relative to a set containing the basepoint have equal induced monoid homomorphisms on positive-dimensional homotopy groups.

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_eq_one_of_subsingleton
docstring: A based map into a subsingleton space induces the trivial homomorphism on every positive-dimensional homotopy group.
code:
theorem mapHom_eq_one_of_subsingleton [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) : mapHom (N := N) f hf = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mapHom_id
docstring: Identity law for the bundled homomorphism: the induced monoid homomorphism of the identity continuous map is the identity homomorphism.
code:
theorem mapHom_id [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    mapHom (ContinuousMap.id X) rfl = MonoidHom.id (HomotopyGroup N X x) :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_apply_eq_one_of_subsingleton
docstring: In positive dimensions, a based map into a subsingleton space sends every homotopy class to the identity. This is not a `simp` lemma: the positive-dimensional normal form is already reached by `map_apply_of_subsingleton` followed by `mk_const_eq_one`, so a separate composite `= 1` rule would be redundant. It is kept as an explicit rewrite.
code:
theorem map_apply_eq_one_of_subsingleton [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (N := N) f hf a = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_apply_of_subsingleton
docstring: A based map into a subsingleton space sends every homotopy class to the class of the constant generalized loop.
code:
theorem map_apply_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Y] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (N := N) f hf a =
      (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N Y y) := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_comp_apply
docstring: Composition law: the map induced by a composite continuous map is the composite of the induced maps on homotopy classes.
code:
theorem map_comp_apply (g : C(Y, Z)) (hg : g y = z) (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map g hg (map f hf a) = map (g.comp f) (by simp [hf, hg]) a := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_congr
docstring: The induced map `HomotopyGroup.map` depends only on the underlying continuous map, not on the chosen proof of the basepoint equation.
code:
theorem map_congr {f₁ f₂ : C(X, Y)} (hfe : f₁ = f₂) (h₁ : f₁ x = y) (h₂ : f₂ x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map f₁ h₁ a = map f₂ h₂ a := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_continuousMap_const_apply
docstring: A constant continuous map sends every homotopy class to the class of the constant generalized loop. This statement also covers dimension zero, where the target need not carry the positive-dimensional group structure.
code:
theorem map_continuousMap_const_apply (y : Y) (hy : (ContinuousMap.const X y) x = y)
    (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) hy a =
      (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N Y y)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N Y y) := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_continuousMap_const_apply_eq_one
docstring: In positive dimensions, a constant continuous map sends every homotopy class to the identity. This is not a `simp` lemma: the positive-dimensional normal form is already reached by `map_continuousMap_const_apply` followed by `mk_const_eq_one`, so a separate `⟦const⟧`-keyed `= 1` rule would be redundant. It is kept as an explicit rewrite.
code:
theorem map_continuousMap_const_apply_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N]
    (y : Y) (hy : (ContinuousMap.const X y) x = y) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) hy a = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_eq_continuousMap_const_of_subsingleton
docstring: A based map into a subsingleton space induces the same map as the constant map at the target basepoint.
code:
theorem map_eq_continuousMap_const_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton Y]
    (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    map (N := N) f hf = map (x := x) (ContinuousMap.const X y) rfl := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_eq_of_homotopicRel
docstring: Continuous maps homotopic relative to a set containing the basepoint induce the same function on homotopy groups.

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_id_apply
docstring: Identity law: the map induced by the identity continuous map is the identity on homotopy classes.
code:
theorem map_id_apply (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map (ContinuousMap.id X) rfl a = a := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_map_of_comp_eq_id
docstring: If `g ∘ f` is the identity, then the induced map of `g` undoes the induced map of `f` on homotopy classes.
code:
theorem map_map_of_comp_eq_id (g : C(Y, X)) (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (hg : g y = x)
    (hgf : g.comp f = ContinuousMap.id X) (a : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map g hg (map f hf a) = a := by

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_mk
code:
theorem map_mk (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) (p : Ω^ N X x) :
    map f hf (⟦p⟧ : HomotopyGroup N X x) = ⟦GenLoop.map f hf p⟧ :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_mul
code:
theorem map_mul [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y)
    (a b : HomotopyGroup N X x) :
    map f hf (a * b) = map f hf a * map f hf b :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.map_one
code:
theorem map_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] (f : C(X, Y)) (hf : f x = y) :
    map f hf (1 : HomotopyGroup N X x) = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.HomotopyGroup.mk_const_eq_one
docstring: In positive dimensions, the class of the constant generalized loop is the identity element. This is `HomotopyGroup.one_def` oriented towards `1`, so that `1` is the simp normal form for the constant-map results below.
code:
theorem mk_const_eq_one [DecidableEq N] [Nonempty N] :
    (⟦(_root_.GenLoop.const : Ω^ N X x)⟧ : HomotopyGroup N X x) = (1 : HomotopyGroup N X x) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.antipode_convMul_id
docstring: The antipode is a left convolution inverse of the identity in the convolution ring of linear maps: `S * id = 1`. This is a restatement of the antipode axiom `HopfAlgebra.mul_antipode_rTensor_comul`.
code:
lemma antipode_convMul_id :
    (toConv (antipode R) : WithConv (H →ₗ[R] H)) * toConv LinearMap.id = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.baseChange_antipode_tmul
docstring: The antipode on the base-changed Hopf algebra `K ⊗[k] A` sends a pure tensor `s ⊗ a` to `s ⊗ S a`.
code:
lemma baseChange_antipode_tmul {k K A : Type*} [CommSemiring k] [CommSemiring K]
    [Semiring A] [Algebra k K] [_root_.HopfAlgebra k A] (s : K) (a : A) :
    antipode K (A := K ⊗[k] A) (s ⊗ₜ[k] a) =
      s ⊗ₜ[k] antipode k a := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.id_convMul_antipode
docstring: The antipode is a right convolution inverse of the identity in the convolution ring of linear maps: `id * S = 1`. This is a restatement of the antipode axiom `HopfAlgebra.mul_antipode_lTensor_comul`.
code:
lemma id_convMul_antipode :
    (toConv LinearMap.id : WithConv (H →ₗ[R] H)) * toConv (antipode R) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints
docstring: The group homomorphism on points induced by a morphism of value algebras. It sends an `A`-point `f : H →ₐ[R] A` to the `B`-point `φ ∘ f`.
code:
@[expose] noncomputable def mapPoints {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    points (H := H) A ⟶ points (H := H) B :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_apply
docstring: On points, `mapPoints` is post-composition with the algebra homomorphism `φ`.
code:
lemma mapPoints_apply {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (f : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ f = toConv (φ.hom.comp f.ofConv) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_comp
docstring: `mapPoints` preserves composition of morphisms of value algebras.
code:
lemma mapPoints_comp {A B C : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (ψ : B ⟶ C) :
    mapPoints (H := H) (φ ≫ ψ) = mapPoints (H := H) φ ≫ mapPoints (H := H) ψ := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_id
docstring: `mapPoints` preserves identity morphisms of value algebras.
code:
lemma mapPoints_id (A : CommAlgCat.{w} R) :
    mapPoints (H := H) (𝟙 A) = 𝟙 (points (H := H) A) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_inv
docstring: The map on points preserves inverses of points.
code:
lemma mapPoints_inv {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (f : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ f⁻¹ = (mapPoints (H := H) φ f)⁻¹ := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_mul
docstring: The map on points preserves multiplication of points.
code:
lemma mapPoints_mul {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) (f g : points (H := H) A) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ (f * g) = mapPoints (H := H) φ f * mapPoints (H := H) φ g := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.mapPoints_one
docstring: The map on points sends the identity point to the identity point.
code:
lemma mapPoints_one {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    mapPoints (H := H) φ (1 : points (H := H) A) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.points
docstring: The group of `A`-points of the affine group object represented by a Hopf algebra `H`. The underlying type is `WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A)`: algebra homomorphisms from `H` to `A`, with the convolution group structure supplied by the antipode of `H`.
code: noncomputable abbrev points (A : CommAlgCat.{w} R) : GrpCat.{max v w} :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor
docstring: The functor of points of the affine group object represented by a Hopf algebra. It maps a commutative `R`-algebra `A` to the convolution group on algebra homomorphisms `H →ₐ[R] A`, and maps `φ : A ⟶ B` to post-composition with `φ`.
code: @[expose] noncomputable def pointsFunctor : CommAlgCat.{w} R ⥤ GrpCat.{max v w} where

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_map
docstring: The morphism part of `pointsFunctor` is post-composition in the value algebra.
code:
lemma pointsFunctor_map {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B) :
    (pointsFunctor (H := H)).map φ = mapPoints (H := H) φ :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply
docstring: The pointwise value of the image of an `A`-point under `pointsFunctor.map φ`.
code:
lemma pointsFunctor_map_apply_apply {A B : CommAlgCat.{w} R} (φ : A ⟶ B)
    (f : WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A)) (h : H) :
    (((pointsFunctor (H := H)).map φ f : WithConv (H →ₐ[R] B)).ofConv) h =
      φ.hom (f.ofConv h) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.pointsFunctor_obj
docstring: The object part of `pointsFunctor` is the convolution group of algebra homomorphisms.
code:
lemma pointsFunctor_obj (A : CommAlgCat.{w} R) :
    (pointsFunctor (H := H)).obj A = GrpCat.of (WithConv (H →ₐ[R] A)) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal
docstring: A Hopf ideal in a Hopf algebra over a commutative semiring. The comultiplication condition is stated in the ambient tensor product algebra as `Δ(I) ⊆ I ⊗ H + H ⊗ I`. Over a commutative ring, the bridge instances `HopfIdeal.instIsCoideal` and `HopfIdeal.instIsHopfIdeal` below let Mathlib endow the quotient `H ⧸ I.toIdeal` with its Hopf-algebra structure.
code: structure HopfIdeal where

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.antipode_mem
docstring: The antipode preserves a Hopf ideal.
code:
theorem antipode_mem (I : HopfIdeal R H) {x : H} (hx : x ∈ I) :
    HopfAlgebra.antipode R x ∈ I :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.bot_toIdeal
code: theorem bot_toIdeal : (⊥ : HopfIdeal R H).toIdeal = (⊥ : Ideal H) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap
docstring: The inverse image of a Hopf ideal along a surjective bialgebra morphism. It is defined as the kernel of the composite `H → K → K/I`; its underlying ideal is the ordinary ideal comap of `I.toIdeal`.
code:
noncomputable def comap (I : HopfIdeal R K) (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : HopfIdeal R H :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_bot
docstring: The inverse image of the zero Hopf ideal is the kernel Hopf ideal.
code:
theorem comap_bot (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (⊥ : HopfIdeal R K).comap f hf = ker f hf := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_comap
docstring: Inverse image of Hopf ideals is compatible with composition of surjective morphisms.
code:
theorem comap_comap (I : HopfIdeal R L) (g : K →ₐc[R] L) (hg : Function.Surjective g)
    (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (I.comap g hg).comap f hf = I.comap (g.comp f) (hg.comp hf) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_eq_comap_iff_of_surjective
docstring: For a surjective morphism, inverse image of Hopf ideals reflects equality.
code:
theorem comap_eq_comap_iff_of_surjective (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) {I J : HopfIdeal R K} :
    I.comap f hf = J.comap f hf ↔ I = J := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_iSup_le
docstring: The inverse image of a supremum of Hopf ideals is contained in the supremum of the inverse images: the nontrivial inclusion of `comap_iSup_of_surjective`.

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_iSup_of_surjective
docstring: Surjective inverse image of Hopf ideals preserves nonempty suprema of families.
code:
theorem comap_iSup_of_surjective {ι : Type*} [Nonempty ι] (I : ι → HopfIdeal R K)
    (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (⨆ i, I i).comap f hf = ⨆ i, (I i).comap f hf := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_id
docstring: Pulling a Hopf ideal back along the identity morphism leaves it unchanged.
code:
theorem comap_id (I : HopfIdeal R H) :
    I.comap (BialgHom.id R H) (fun h => ⟨h, rfl⟩) = I := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_le_comap_iff_of_surjective
docstring: For a surjective morphism, containment after inverse image is equivalent to containment before inverse image.
code:
theorem comap_le_comap_iff_of_surjective (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) {I J : HopfIdeal R K} :
    I.comap f hf ≤ J.comap f hf ↔ I ≤ J :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_mono
docstring: Inverse image of Hopf ideals is monotone.
code:
theorem comap_mono (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f)
    {I J : HopfIdeal R K} (hIJ : I ≤ J) : I.comap f hf ≤ J.comap f hf := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_sSup_of_surjective
docstring: Surjective inverse image of Hopf ideals preserves nonempty suprema of sets.
code:
theorem comap_sSup_of_surjective (S : Set (HopfIdeal R K)) (hS : S.Nonempty)
    (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (sSup S).comap f hf = sSup ((fun I => I.comap f hf) '' S) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_sup_of_surjective
docstring: Surjective inverse image of Hopf ideals preserves joins.
code:
theorem comap_sup_of_surjective (I J : HopfIdeal R K) (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (I ⊔ J).comap f hf = I.comap f hf ⊔ J.comap f hf := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comap_toIdeal
docstring: The underlying ideal of `I.comap f hf` is the ordinary ideal-theoretic inverse image.
code:
theorem comap_toIdeal (I : HopfIdeal R K) (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
    (I.comap f hf).toIdeal = Ideal.comap (f : H →+* K) I.toIdeal := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comul_mem
docstring: The comultiplication of an element of a Hopf ideal lies in `I ⊗ H + H ⊗ I`.
code:
theorem comul_mem (I : HopfIdeal R H) {x : H} (hx : x ∈ I) :
    Coalgebra.comul (R := R) x ∈
      leftTensorIdeal (R := R) (H := H) I.toIdeal ⊔
        rightTensorIdeal (R := R) (H := H) I.toIdeal :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comul_mem_sup_restrictScalars_eq_range
docstring: The bridge to Mathlib's coideal target: TauCeti's `I ⊗ H + H ⊗ I` (a sup of ideals of `H ⊗[R] H`), viewed as an `R`-submodule, equals `range (lTensor …) ⊔ range (rTensor …)`.
code:
private theorem comul_mem_sup_restrictScalars_eq_range (I : Ideal H) :
    (leftTensorIdeal (R := R) (H := H) I ⊔ rightTensorIdeal (R := R) (H := H) I).restrictScalars R =
      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.lTensor H (I.restrictScalars R).subtype) ⊔
        LinearMap.range (LinearMap.rTensor H (I.restrictScalars R).subtype) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.comul_mem_tensor_map_ker
docstring: The tensor-square map sends the comultiplication of an element in the kernel of a bialgebra morphism to zero.
code:
private theorem comul_mem_tensor_map_ker (f : H →ₐc[R] K) {x : H}
    (hx : x ∈ RingHom.ker (f : H →ₐ[R] K)) :
    Coalgebra.comul (R := R) x ∈
      RingHom.ker
        (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (f : H →ₐ[R] K) (f : H →ₐ[R] K)).toRingHom := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.counit_eq_zero
docstring: The counit vanishes on a Hopf ideal.
code:
theorem counit_eq_zero (I : HopfIdeal R H) {x : H} (hx : x ∈ I) :
    Coalgebra.counit (R := R) x = 0 :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.exists_finsupp_map_eq
docstring: A finitely supported family over `K` lifts along a surjective bialgebra morphism to a finitely supported family over `H` that agrees with it pointwise and has the same total sum.
code:
private theorem exists_finsupp_map_eq {ι : Type*} (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : ι →₀ K) :
    ∃ t : ι →₀ H, (∀ i, f (t i) = s i) ∧
      f (t.sum fun _ y => y) = s.sum fun _ y => y := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.ext
docstring: Two Hopf ideals are equal when they contain the same elements.
code: theorem ext {I J : HopfIdeal R H} (h : ∀ x : H, x ∈ I ↔ x ∈ J) : I = J :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.iSup_toIdeal
docstring: The underlying ideal of a supremum of a family of Hopf ideals is the supremum of the underlying ideals.
code:
theorem iSup_toIdeal {ι : Sort*} (I : ι → HopfIdeal R H) :
    (⨆ i, I i).toIdeal = ⨆ i, (I i).toIdeal := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.includeLeft_mem_leftTensorIdeal
docstring: The left tensor inclusion sends elements of `I` into `I ⊗ H`.
code:
theorem includeLeft_mem_leftTensorIdeal {I : Ideal H} {x : H} (hx : x ∈ I) :
    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft (R := R) (S := R) (A := H) (B := H) x ∈
      leftTensorIdeal (R := R) (H := H) I :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.includeRight_mem_rightTensorIdeal
docstring: The right tensor inclusion sends elements of `I` into `H ⊗ I`.
code:

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientKerPointsMulEquiv
docstring: The points of the quotient by the Hopf-ideal kernel of a surjective Hopf algebra morphism are the points of its codomain. Contravariantly, this is induced by the bialgebra equivalence `H ⧸ ker f ≃ₐc[R] K` from the Hopf-algebra first isomorphism theorem.
code:
noncomputable def quotientKerPointsMulEquiv (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R) :
    WithConv (H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal →ₐ[R] A) ≃* WithConv (K →ₐ[R] A) :=

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply
docstring: The quotient-kernel point equivalence acts by pre-composition with the inverse bialgebra equivalence `K ≃ₐc[R] H ⧸ ker f`.
code:
theorem quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : WithConv (H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal →ₐ[R] A)) :
    quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A g =
      AlgHom.mapDomain (A := A)
        ((kerLiftBialgEquiv f hf).symm : K →ₐc[R] H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal) g := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_mapValue
docstring: The quotient-kernel point equivalence is natural in the value algebra.
code:
theorem quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_mapValue {B : Type*} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (χ : A →ₐ[R] B) (g : WithConv (H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal →ₐ[R] A)) :
    quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf (CommAlgCat.of R B)
        (AlgHom.mapValue (H := H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal) χ g) =
      AlgHom.mapValue (H := K) χ (quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A g) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse quotient-kernel point equivalence acts by pre-composition with the bialgebra equivalence `H ⧸ ker f ≃ₐc[R] K`.
code:
theorem quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : WithConv (K →ₐ[R] A)) :
    (quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A).symm g =
      AlgHom.mapDomain (A := A)
        (kerLiftBialgEquiv f hf : H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal →ₐc[R] K) g := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply
docstring: For an arbitrary point of `H ⧸ ker f`, the quotient-points inclusion agrees with first identifying it as a `K`-point and then pre-composing along `f`.
code:
theorem quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal) A) :
    CommHopfAlgCat.quotientPointsHom (_root_.CommHopfAlgCat.of R H) (ker f hf) A g =
      AlgHom.mapDomain f (quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A g) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise form of `quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply`.
code:
theorem quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_apply_apply (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := H ⧸ (ker f hf).toIdeal) A) (h : H) :
    (CommHopfAlgCat.quotientPointsHom (_root_.CommHopfAlgCat.of R H) (ker f hf) A g).ofConv h =
      (quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A g).ofConv (f h) := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: Including the quotient point attached to a `K`-point back into ambient `H`-points is pre-composition along the original surjective Hopf algebra morphism.
code:
theorem quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (f : H →ₐc[R] K)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := K) A) :
    CommHopfAlgCat.quotientPointsHom (_root_.CommHopfAlgCat.of R H) (ker f hf) A
        ((quotientKerPointsMulEquiv f hf A).symm g) =
      AlgHom.mapDomain f g := by

label: TauCeti.HopfIdeal.quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_apply
docstring: Pointwise form of `quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply`.
code:
theorem quotientPointsHom_quotientKerPointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_apply
    (f : H →ₐc[R] K) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (A : CommAlgCat.{x} R)
    (g : HopfAlgebra.points (R := R) (H := K) A) (h : H) :

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.exists_add_mul_of_mem_sup_adjoin_sq
docstring: If `x² ∈ F`, every element of `F ⊔ K⟮x⟯` has the form `a + b * x` with `a, b ∈ F`.

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finite_boundedRoots
docstring: The root set in `A` of the integer polynomials of degree at most `d` whose coefficients all have absolute value at most `B` is finite.

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finite_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_of_finite

    {E : IntermediateField K L | ∃ x ∈ T, E = K⟮x⟯}.Finite :=

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finite_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff
docstring: The simple subfields of an ambient field `A / ℚ` generated by roots of integer polynomials of degree at most `d` and coefficient height at most `B` form a finite set. This is the finiteness half of the root-to-field counting step used by the effective Hermite--Minkowski target.
code:
theorem finite_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff (d B : ℕ) :

        (((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A))), E = ℚ⟮x⟯}.Finite :=

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finrank_adjoin_simple_eq_two_of_sq_mem_notMem

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.finrank_restrictScalars_eq
TauCeti.IntermediateField.finrank_sup_adjoin_simple_eq_mul_two
docstring: If `x² ∈ F` but `x ∉ F`, then adjoining `x` doubles the degree: `[F ⊔ K⟮x⟯ : K] = 2 · [F : K]`.

theorem finrank_sup_adjoin_simple_eq_mul_two (F : IntermediateField K L) {x : L}
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 ∈ F) (hxF : x ∉ F) :
    Module.finrank K ((F ⊔ IntermediateField.adjoin K {x}) : IntermediateField K L)
      = Module.finrank K F * 2 := by

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.isIntegral_of_sq_mem
docstring: If `x² ∈ F`, then `x` is integral over `F` (it is a root of `X² - x²`).

    IsIntegral F x := by

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.isSquare_mul_of_adjoin_simple_eq
docstring: **Same square class from a shared simple quadratic field.** Let `x` and `y` be square roots of `a` and `c` in a field extension `L / K` with `2 ≠ 0`. If `x ∉ K` and the simple extensions `K(x)` and `K(y)` coincide, then `a · c` is a square in `K`: two square roots generate the same quadratic subfield only when their radicands lie in the same square class.
code:
theorem isSquare_mul_of_adjoin_simple_eq [NeZero (2 : K)] {a c : K} {x y : L}
    (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap K L a) (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L c)
    (hxb : x ∉ (⊥ : IntermediateField K L))
    (hxy : IntermediateField.adjoin K {x} = IntermediateField.adjoin K {y}) :
    IsSquare (a * c) := by

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.mem_sup_adjoin_sq
docstring: Membership in `F ⊔ K⟮x⟯`, for `x² ∈ F`, is equivalent to having the form `a + b * x` with `a, b ∈ F`.
code:
theorem mem_sup_adjoin_sq {F : IntermediateField K L} {x : L}
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 ∈ F) {y : L} :
    y ∈ F ⊔ IntermediateField.adjoin K {x} ↔
      ∃ a b : L, a ∈ F ∧ b ∈ F ∧ y = a + b * x :=

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.mem_sup_adjoin_sq_of_exists
docstring: If `a` and `b` lie in `F`, then `a + b * x` lies in `F ⊔ K⟮x⟯`.

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.minpoly_natDegree_le_two_of_sq_mem
docstring: If `x² ∈ F`, then the minimal polynomial of `x` over `F` has degree at most `2`, since it divides the nonzero polynomial `X² - x²`.
code:
private theorem minpoly_natDegree_le_two_of_sq_mem {F : IntermediateField K L} {x : L}
    (hx2 : x ^ 2 ∈ F) : (minpoly F x).natDegree ≤ 2 := by

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.mul_eq_zero_of_add_mul_sq_mem
docstring: **Vanishing cross term in a quadratic step.** If `x² ∈ F` but `x ∉ F`, then a square `(a + b * x) ^ 2` of a normal-form element that lands back in `F` has no cross term: `a * b = 0`. This is where characteristic not two enters, through `2 ≠ 0` in `L`. It holds for an arbitrary subfield `F` of `L`; no ambient base field or algebra tower is needed.

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.ncard_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_le
docstring: The simple intermediate fields generated by elements of a finite set `T` are no more numerous than the elements of `T`.

    {E : IntermediateField K L | ∃ x ∈ T, E = K⟮x⟯}.ncard ≤ T.ncard := by

label: TauCeti.IntermediateField.ncard_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le
docstring: The simple subfields of an ambient field `A / ℚ` generated by roots of integer polynomials of degree at most `d` and coefficient height at most `B` number at most `(2 * B + 1) ^ (d + 1) * d`. This is the root-to-field counting step used by the effective Hermite--Minkowski target, after `TauCeti.Polynomial.ncard_biUnion_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le` has counted the possible generators.
code:
theorem ncard_setOf_exists_mem_eq_adjoin_simple_roots_natDegree_le_abs_intCoeff_le (d B : ℕ) :
    {E : IntermediateField ℚ A |
      ∃ x ∈ (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ d ∧ ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (B : ℤ)),
        (((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A))), E = ℚ⟮x⟯}.ncard ≤
      (2 * B + 1) ^ (d + 1) * d := by

label: TauCeti.IsArithFrobAt.smul_sqrt
docstring: **A Frobenius element acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol**, action form: if `σ : M` is an arithmetic Frobenius at an ideal `Q` over the odd prime `p` and `x² = d` with `p ∤ d`, then `σ • x = legendreSym p d • x`. Only a monoid action is needed.

theorem IsArithFrobAt.smul_sqrt {M : Type*} [Monoid M] [MulSemiringAction M S]

    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ S d) :
    σ • x = legendreSym p d • x := by

The open-half-line derivative condition is the standard one and permits boundary singularities such as the right derivative of `sqrt` at `0`.

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone
docstring: A function `f : ℝ → ℝ` is **completely monotone** if it is `C^∞` on the closed half-line `[0, ∞)` and its iterated derivatives within `[0, ∞)` alternate in sign: `0 ≤ (-1)ⁿ f⁽ⁿ⁾(t)` for every `n` and every `t ≥ 0`. The smoothness clause prevents the sign condition from being satisfied vacuously by a junk iterated derivative.
code: @[expose] def IsCompletelyMonotone (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.add
docstring: Completely monotone functions are closed under addition.
code:
lemma add (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) (hg : IsCompletelyMonotone g) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (f + g) := by

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.antitoneOn
docstring: A completely monotone function is nonincreasing on `[0, ∞)`.
code: lemma antitoneOn (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) : AntitoneOn f (Ici 0) := by

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_add_const
docstring: Completely monotone functions are closed under shifting the argument by a nonnegative constant: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ a`, then `t ↦ f (t + a)` is completely monotone. The alternating derivative is unchanged, evaluated at the shifted point.
code:
theorem comp_add_const (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {a : ℝ} (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (t + a)) := by

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_affine
docstring: Completely monotone functions are closed under nonnegative affine reparametrization of the argument: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ c`, `0 ≤ a`, then `t ↦ f (c · t + a)` is completely monotone.
code:
theorem comp_affine (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {c a : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) (ha : 0 ≤ a) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (c * t + a)) :=

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.comp_const_mul
docstring: Completely monotone functions are closed under scaling the argument by a nonnegative constant: if `f` is completely monotone and `0 ≤ c`, then `t ↦ f (c · t)` is completely monotone. The `n`-th alternating derivative is multiplied by the nonnegative factor `cⁿ`.
code:
theorem comp_const_mul (hf : IsCompletelyMonotone f) {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    IsCompletelyMonotone (fun t => f (c * t)) := by

label: TauCeti.IsCompletelyMonotone.congr
docstring: Complete monotonicity is determined by the values of the function on `[0, ∞)`: if `g` agrees with a completely monotone `f` throughout `[0, ∞)`, then `g` is completely monotone too. Both the smoothness clause and the sign condition only see the function within `[0, ∞)`.

    IsCompletelyMonotone g := by

    (hfH : (_root_.FundamentalGroup.map f a₀).range ≤ H)
    (hHp : H ≤ (_root_.FundamentalGroup.mapOfEq ⟨p, hp.continuous⟩ he).range) :
    ∃! F : C(A, E), F a₀ = e₀ ∧ p ∘ F = f :=

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn
docstring: A family `F : ι → ℂ → ℂ` is **locally bounded** on `s` if it is uniformly bounded — with a single constant, independent of the index — on every compact subset of `s`. This is the hypothesis of Montel's theorem, in the form fixed by the conformal-mapping roadmap.
code: def IsLocallyBoundedOn (F : ι → ℂ → ℂ) (s : Set ℂ) : Prop :=

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.deriv
docstring: **The derivatives of a locally bounded family of holomorphic functions are locally bounded.** On a compact `K ⊆ U` choose `δ > 0` with `cthickening δ K ⊆ U`; a bound `C` for the family on that compact thickening bounds each derivative on `K` by `C / δ`, by Cauchy's estimate on `closedBall z δ` for `z ∈ K`.
code:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.deriv (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) :
    IsLocallyBoundedOn (fun i => _root_.deriv (F i)) U := by

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn
docstring: **The equicontinuity half of Montel's theorem.** A locally bounded family of holomorphic functions on an open set `U ⊆ ℂ` is equicontinuous on `U`. Around a point `z₀ ∈ U` pick `r > 0` with `closedBall z₀ (2 * r) ⊆ U`; local boundedness supplies one constant `C` bounding the whole family on that compact ball, and `dist_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le` then makes every member of the family `C / r`-Lipschitz on `ball z₀ r`. A single Lipschitz constant is a common continuity modulus.
code:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) : EquicontinuousOn F U := by

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn_deriv
docstring: The derivatives of a locally bounded family of holomorphic functions are equicontinuous. The result follows by applying the preceding equicontinuity theorem to the locally bounded derivative family.
code:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn_deriv (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F U) (hU : IsOpen U)
    (hF : ∀ i, DifferentiableOn ℂ (F i) U) : EquicontinuousOn (fun i => _root_.deriv (F i)) U :=

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.exists_forall_norm_le
docstring: A locally bounded family is bounded at each point of the set, uniformly in the index. Together with `IsLocallyBoundedOn.equicontinuousOn`, this supplies the pointwise bounds used in an Arzelà--Ascoli exhaustion argument.
code:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.exists_forall_norm_le {s : Set ℂ} (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F s) {z : ℂ}
    (hz : z ∈ s) : ∃ C, ∀ i, ‖F i z‖ ≤ C := by

label: TauCeti.IsLocallyBoundedOn.mono
docstring: Local boundedness is inherited by subsets.
code:
theorem IsLocallyBoundedOn.mono {s t : Set ℂ} (hb : IsLocallyBoundedOn F s) (hts : t ⊆ s) :
    IsLocallyBoundedOn F t :=

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite
docstring: A function `F : M → ℂ` on an involutive additive monoid is **positive definite** when, for every finite family of scalars `c : Fin n → ℂ` and points `v : Fin n → M`, the Hermitian form `∑_{i,j} c i · conj (c j) · F (v i + star (v j))` is a nonnegative real number (using the order on `ℂ` for which `0 ≤ z` means `z` is real and nonnegative).

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand
code:
private theorem gram_three_add_star_expand
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y))
    {lam : ℂ} :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0 := by

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
code:
private theorem gram_three_add_star_expand_of_values
    {x y : E} {lam : ℂ} {c : Fin 3 → ℂ} {p : Fin 3 → E}
    (hc0 : c 0 = 1) (hc1 : c 1 = -1) (hc2 : c 2 = lam)
    (hp0 : p 0 = x) (hp1 : p 1 = y) (hp2 : p 2 = 0)
    (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y)) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      c i * conj (c j) * F (p i + star (p j)))
      = F 0 - F (x + star y) + conj lam * F x - conj (F (x + star y)) + F 0
        - conj lam * F y + lam * conj (F x) - lam * conj (F y)
        + lam * conj lam * F 0 := by

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_algebra
code:
private theorem gram_three_add_star_re_algebra (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0)
    (hyx : F (y + star x) = conj (F (x + star y)))
    (hnx : F (star x) = conj (F x)) (hny : F (0 + star y) = conj (F y))
    {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C)
    (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re := by

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_add_star_re_eq
code:
private theorem gram_three_add_star_re_eq (hF : IsPositiveDefinite F)
    {x y : E} (hx : x + star x = 0) (hy : y + star y = 0) {C d lam : ℂ}
    (hC : C = F 0) (hd : d = F x - F y) (hlam : lam = -d / C)
    (hCpos : 0 < (F 0).re) :
    (∑ i : Fin 3, ∑ j : Fin 3,
      ![1, -1, lam] i * conj (![1, -1, lam] j) *
        F (![x, y, 0] i + star (![x, y, 0] j))).re
      = 2 * (F 0).re - 2 * (F (x + star y)).re - Complex.normSq d / (F 0).re := by

label: TauCeti.IsPositiveDefinite.gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra
code:
private theorem gram_three_sub_re_complex_algebra {r : ℝ} {z d lam : ℂ}
    (hlam : lam = -d / (r : ℂ)) (hr : 0 < r) :
    ((r : ℂ) - z + conj lam * d - conj z + (r : ℂ) + lam * conj d
        + lam * conj lam * (r : ℂ)).re
      = 2 * r - 2 * z.re - Complex.normSq d / r := by

label: TauCeti.IsPrimitive
docstring: A homology class `v : M` on a boundary torus is **primitive** when some `ℤ`-linear functional `M →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ` sends it to `1`, so the span of `v` splits off a copy of `ℤ`. label: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans

The concatenated total map is an embedding because it is one on each closed half (where it is `F`'s or `G`'s total embedding, reparametrised), and these glue along the closed cover `{(t, y) | t ≤ 1 / 2}`, `{(t, y) | 1 / 2 ≤ t}` of the codomain.

label: TauCeti.Isotopy.trans_apply
docstring: The value of a concatenated isotopy is given by the first isotopy on `[0, 1 / 2]` and by the second isotopy on `[1 / 2, 1]`, with the time parameter rescaled linearly.
code:
theorem trans_apply {f₂ : C(X, Y)}
    (F : Isotopy f₀ f₁) (G : Isotopy f₁ f₂) (x : I × X) :
    (F.trans G) x =
      if h : (x.1 : ℝ) ≤ 1 / 2 then
        F (⟨2 * x.1, (unitInterval.mul_pos_mem_iff zero_lt_two).2 ⟨x.1.2.1, h⟩⟩, x.2)
      else
        G (⟨2 * x.1 - 1,
          unitInterval.two_mul_sub_one_mem_iff.2 ⟨(not_le.1 h).le, x.1.2.2⟩⟩, x.2) :=

noncomputable def prodPointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) →ₐ[R] A) ≃*

label: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodPointsMulEquiv_fst_ofConv_single
docstring: The first component of `prodPointsMulEquiv` restricts an `A`-point of `Spec R[G × H]` to the factor `Spec R[G]`: on the generator `single g 1` it evaluates the original point at `single (g, 1) 1`, the image of `g` under `G → G × H`.
code:
theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_fst_ofConv_single
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) →ₐ[R] A)) (g : G) :
    (prodPointsMulEquiv f).1.ofConv (single g (1 : R)) =
      f.ofConv (single (g, (1 : H)) 1) := by

    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (G × H) →ₐ[R] A)) :
    prodPointsMulEquiv (A := B) (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (G × H)) φ f) =
      (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R G) φ (prodPointsMulEquiv f).1,
        AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R H) φ (prodPointsMulEquiv f).2) := by

theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_snd_ofConv_single

    (prodPointsMulEquiv f).2.ofConv (single h (1 : R)) =

label: TauCeti.MonoidAlgebra.prodPointsMulEquiv_symm_ofConv_single
docstring: The inverse of `prodPointsMulEquiv` assembles an `A`-point of `Spec R[G × H]` from a pair of points of `Spec R[G]` and `Spec R[H]`: on the generator `single (g, h) 1` it multiplies the value of the first point at `single g 1` and the value of the second at `single h 1`.

theorem prodPointsMulEquiv_symm_ofConv_single

    (g : G) (h : H) :
    (prodPointsMulEquiv.symm (f₁, f₂)).ofConv (single (g, h) (1 : R)) =
      f₁.ofConv (single g 1) * f₂.ofConv (single h 1) := by
