label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants
docstring: The `[-4, -3, -7]` list does not contain all three even prime discriminants.
code:
theorem not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants :
    ¬ ((∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = -4) ∧
      (∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = 8) ∧
        (∃ i : Fin 3, negFourNegThreeNegSevenPrimeDiscriminants i = -8)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_all_three_evenPrimeDiscriminants_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
docstring: A prime-discriminant family with at most one even prime discriminant cannot contain the three even prime discriminants `-4`, `8`, and `-8` simultaneously. The hypothesis is stated extensionally: any two indices whose discriminants are even prime discriminants must carry the same discriminant value. This is the form supplied by the prime-discriminant factorization of a quadratic discriminant, where there is only one 2-adic factor.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff
docstring: An integer does not divide an odd prime discriminant exactly when it does not divide the underlying natural number. The negated form is convenient for the unramifiedness side of the splitting law.
code:
theorem not_dvd_oddPrimeDiscriminant_iff {p : ℕ} {q : ℤ} :
    ¬ q ∣ oddPrimeDiscriminant p ↔ ¬ q ∣ (p : ℤ) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_intCast_prime_dvd_two
docstring: If `q` is an odd natural prime, then it does not divide `2` as an integer.
code: private theorem not_intCast_prime_dvd_two (hq : q ≠ 2) : ¬ (q : ℤ) ∣ (2 : ℤ) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: An odd prime discriminant is not one of the even prime discriminants.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_evenPrimeDiscriminantRadicand_rat
docstring: The rational radicand associated to an even prime discriminant is not a square.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_primeDiscriminantRadicand_rat
docstring: The radicand attached to a prime discriminant is not a rational square.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand
docstring: The CM radicand family is square-class independent: for distinct primes `p`, no nonempty subset product of `-1, p₁, …, pₙ` is a square in `ℚ`.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p)
    (S : Finset (Option ι)) (hS : S.Nonempty) : ¬ IsSquare (∏ x ∈ S, cmRadicand p x) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_of_coprime_squarefree
docstring: **Square-class independence of pairwise coprime squarefree integers.** If the radicands `d i` are pairwise coprime, each squarefree, and each a non-unit, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` is a square in `ℤ`. This generalises `not_isSquare_prod_primes` (the distinct-primes case) to the squarefree integers the genus theory uses, and supplies the square-class independence the multiquadratic degree theorem `finrank_adjoin_range` consumes.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_of_coprime_squarefree {ι : Type*} (d : ι → ℤ) {S : Finset ι}
    (hcop : (S : Set ι).Pairwise (IsCoprime on d)) (hsf : ∀ i ∈ S, Squarefree (d i))
    (hnu : ∀ i ∈ S, ¬ IsUnit (d i)) (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_of_coprime_squarefree_rat
docstring: **Square-class independence cast to `ℚ`.** If `d : ι → ℤ` is pairwise coprime with each entry squarefree and a non-unit, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} (d i : ℚ)` is a square in `ℚ`. This is the `∀ S` shape of `hindep` the degree and Galois-group theorems consume directly.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_of_coprime_squarefree_rat {ι : Type*} (d : ι → ℤ)
    (hcop : Pairwise (IsCoprime on d)) (hsf : ∀ i, Squarefree (d i)) (hnu : ∀ i, ¬ IsUnit (d i)) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (d i : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_optionNeg
docstring: **Adjoining a negative radicand preserves square-class independence.** Let `d : ι → K` be a family of positive radicands in an ordered field, no nonempty subset product of which is a square, and let `c < 0`. Index by `Option ι`, sending `none` to `c` and `some i` to `d i`. Then no nonempty subset product of this extended family is a square: a subset that avoids `none` is a nonempty positive non-square by hypothesis, and a subset that contains `none` has a negative product (the negative `c` times a positive product), so it is not a square either.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_optionNeg {K : Type*} [Field K] [LinearOrder K] [IsStrictOrderedRing K]
    {ι : Type*} {d : ι → K} (hpos : ∀ i, 0 < d i)
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, d i))
    {c : K} (hc : c < 0) (S : Finset (Option ι)) (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ x ∈ S, x.elim c d) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands
docstring: **Square-class independence of prime discriminants.** Let `D : ι → ℤ` be an injective family of prime discriminants which does not contain all three even prime discriminants `-4`, `8`, and `-8`. Then no nonempty subset product of the radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` is a rational square. This is the `hindep` hypothesis the multiquadratic degree theorem `finrank_adjoin_range` consumes, applied to the genus-field generators.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands {ι : Type*} (D : ι → ℤ)
    (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven : ¬ ((∃ i, D i = -4) ∧ (∃ i, D i = 8) ∧ (∃ i, D i = -8))) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty →
      ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
docstring: **Square-class independence for prime-discriminant families with at most one even factor.** Let `D : ι → ℤ` be an injective family of prime discriminants, and assume any two even prime discriminants in the family are equal as integers. Then no nonempty subset product of the associated radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` is a rational square. This is the genus-field specialization of `not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands`: the prime discriminants dividing a quadratic discriminant have at most one even member, so the exceptional product `(-1) * 2 * (-2) = 4` cannot occur.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_forall_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant_eq
    {ι : Type*} (D : ι → ℤ) (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i))
    (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    (heven_unique : ∀ i j,
      IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) → IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D j) → D i = D j) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty →
      ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_mem_eight_neg_eight
docstring: Square-class independence in the exceptional even case where `S` carries indices for both `8` and `-8` but none for `-4`: the product of the radicands `primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)` over `S` is not a rational square.
code:
private theorem not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_mem_eight_neg_eight {ι : Type*}
    {D : ι → ℤ} (hD : ∀ i, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hinj : Function.Injective D)
    {S : Finset ι} (hno4S : ∀ i ∈ S, D i ≠ -4)
    (hboth : (∃ i ∈ S, D i = 8) ∧ (∃ i ∈ S, D i = -8)) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, ((primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_of_pairwise_isCoprime
docstring: Products over pairwise coprime prime-discriminant radicands are not rational squares, provided the selected product is not the empty product in disguise.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primes
docstring: **Square-class independence of distinct primes.** If the selected `p i` are prime and pairwise distinct, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} (p i : ℚ)` is a square in `ℚ`. This is the hypothesis the multiquadratic degree theorem `finrank_adjoin_range` consumes.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primes {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ) {S : Finset ι}
    (hp : ∀ i ∈ S, (p i).Prime)
    (hdist : Set.Pairwise (S : Set ι) (fun i j => p i ≠ p j))
    (hS : S.Nonempty) :
    ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (p i : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_primes_of_injective
docstring: **Square-class independence of an injective family of primes.** If `p : ι → ℕ` is injective and each `p i` is prime, then no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} (p i : ℚ)` is a square. This is the `hindep` hypothesis the multiquadratic degree and Galois-group theorems consume directly.
code:
theorem not_isSquare_prod_primes_of_injective {ι : Type*} (p : ι → ℕ)
    (hp : ∀ i, (p i).Prime) (hinj : Function.Injective p) :
    ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (p i : ℚ)) :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The odd prime discriminant `p*`: `p` when `p % 4 = 1` and `-p` otherwise (so the value is `-p` for every `p` with `p % 4 ≠ 1`, including even inputs). The `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` reading of the second case is the intended one for odd primes. The primality hypothesis is not part of the definition so that the expression rewrites by computation; the API below supplies the prime-specific facts.
code: @[expose] def oddPrimeDiscriminant (p : ℕ) : ℤ :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_def
docstring: The defining `if` expression for the odd prime discriminant.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_def (p : ℕ) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = if p % 4 = 1 then (p : ℤ) else -(p : ℤ) := rfl

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_dvd_iff
docstring: The odd prime discriminant divides an integer exactly when `p` does.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_dvd_iff {p : ℕ} {D : ℤ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p ∣ D ↔ (p : ℤ) ∣ D := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_div_two_mul
docstring: The odd prime discriminant in the standard notation `p* = (-1)^(p/2) p`.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_div_two_mul {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p / 2) * p := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_pred_div_two_mul
docstring: The odd prime discriminant in the standard notation `p* = (-1)^((p - 1)/2) p`.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_neg_one_pow_pred_div_two_mul {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (-1 : ℤ) ^ ((p - 1) / 2) * p := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_or_eq_neg
docstring: The odd prime discriminant is always either `p` or `-p`.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_or_eq_neg {p : ℕ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = (p : ℤ) ∨ oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_image_prod
docstring: The image family `{p* : p ∣ n}` of odd prime discriminants over the prime factors of an odd `n`: each member is a non-even prime discriminant, and the assignment is injective, so its `Finset` product is the indexed product over the prime factors.
code:
private lemma oddPrimeDiscriminant_image_prod {n : ℕ} (hn : Odd n) :
    (∀ P ∈ n.primeFactors.image oddPrimeDiscriminant, IsPrimeDiscriminant P ∧
        ¬ IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant P) ∧
      ∏ P ∈ n.primeFactors.image oddPrimeDiscriminant, P =
        ∏ p ∈ n.primeFactors, oddPrimeDiscriminant p := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one
docstring: For an odd `p`, the odd prime discriminant is congruent to `1` modulo `4`.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p % 4 = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs
docstring: The absolute value of the odd prime discriminant is the underlying natural number.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs (p : ℕ) :
    (oddPrimeDiscriminant p).natAbs = p := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_ne_zero
docstring: The odd prime discriminant is nonzero exactly when `p` is nonzero.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_ne_zero {p : ℕ} :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p ≠ 0 ↔ p ≠ 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_neg_iff
docstring: The odd prime discriminant is negative exactly in the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` case.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_neg_iff {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p < 0 ↔ p % 4 = 3 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_one
docstring: If `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `p`.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_one {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 = 1) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = p := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_three
docstring: If `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `-p`.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_eq_three {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 = 3) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ) :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_ne_one
docstring: If `p ≠ 1 (mod 4)`, its odd prime discriminant is `-p`. For an odd prime this is the `p ≡ 3 (mod 4)` case.
code:
@[simp] theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_of_mod_four_ne_one {p : ℕ} (hp : p % 4 ≠ 1) :
    oddPrimeDiscriminant p = -(p : ℤ) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.oddPrimeDiscriminant_pos_iff
docstring: The sign of the odd prime discriminant is controlled by `p mod 4`.
code:
theorem oddPrimeDiscriminant_pos_iff {p : ℕ} :
    0 < oddPrimeDiscriminant p ↔ p % 4 = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.odd_oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The odd prime discriminant of an odd natural number is odd.
code:
theorem odd_oddPrimeDiscriminant {p : ℕ} (hp : Odd p) :
    Odd (oddPrimeDiscriminant p) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.odd_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: A product of odd prime discriminants is odd.

theorem odd_prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant (hodd : ∀ i ∈ s, Odd (p i)) :
    Odd (∏ i ∈ s, oddPrimeDiscriminant (p i)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand
docstring: The squarefree radicand attached to a prime discriminant. In the even cases this divides by `4`; in the odd cases the discriminant is already squarefree and is used as its own radicand.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_def
docstring: The defining equation for the prime-discriminant radicand.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eight
docstring: The prime-discriminant radicand of `8` is `2`.

theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_eight :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand 8 = 2 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_neg_one_iff
docstring: Among prime discriminants, radicand `-1` comes only from the even prime discriminant `-4`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_neg_two_iff
docstring: Among prime discriminants, radicand `-2` comes only from the even prime discriminant `-8`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_eq_two_iff
docstring: Among prime discriminants, radicand `2` comes only from the even prime discriminant `8`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_mod_four_eq_one_of_odd
docstring: An odd prime discriminant has odd radicand congruent to `1` modulo `4`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_natAbs_eq_one_iff
docstring: The only prime discriminant whose radicand has absolute value `1` is `-4`. This is the small exceptional case in the radicand map: the odd prime-discriminant radicands have prime absolute value, and the other even prime-discriminant radicands have absolute value `2`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_ne_zero
docstring: The radicand attached to a prime discriminant is nonzero.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_eight
docstring: The prime-discriminant radicand of `-8` is `-2`.

theorem primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_eight :
    primeDiscriminantRadicand (-8) = -2 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_neg_four
docstring: The prime-discriminant radicand of `-4` is `-1`.

    primeDiscriminantRadicand (-4) = -1 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The radicand attached to an odd prime discriminant is the discriminant itself.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand_of_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The radicand attached to an even prime discriminant is its even-prime radicand.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminant_eq_radicand_or_eq_four_mul_radicand
docstring: A prime discriminant is either its own radicand, or four times its radicand in the even cases.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminant_eq_sq_mul_radicand
docstring: A prime discriminant is a nonzero square (`1` or `2²`) times its radicand.
code:
private lemma primeDiscriminant_eq_sq_mul_radicand {P : ℤ} (hP : IsPrimeDiscriminant P) :
    ∃ c : ℤ, c ≠ 0 ∧ P = c ^ 2 * primeDiscriminantRadicand P := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prime_oddPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The odd prime discriminant of a natural prime is a prime integer.

    Prime (oddPrimeDiscriminant p) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one
docstring: A product of odd prime discriminants is congruent to `1` modulo `4`. No distinctness of the underlying primes is needed.

theorem prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_mod_four_eq_one (hodd : ∀ i ∈ s, Odd (p i)) :

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs_of_not_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant
docstring: The shared normalisation step of `isFundamentalDiscriminant_prod`: over a set `t` of prime discriminants, none of them even and with pairwise distinct values, each `D i` is `oddPrimeDiscriminant` of an odd prime, that odd-prime map is injective on `t`, and the product rewrites as a product of odd prime discriminants. Applied to both branches of the case split.

private theorem prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_natAbs_of_not_isEvenPrimeDiscriminant {D : ι → ℤ}
    {t : Finset ι} (hD : ∀ i ∈ t, IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i))
    (hev : ∀ i ∈ t, ¬ IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (hDinj : Set.InjOn D t) :
    (∀ i ∈ t, ((D i).natAbs).Prime) ∧ (∀ i ∈ t, Odd (D i).natAbs) ∧
      Set.InjOn (fun i => (D i).natAbs) t ∧
      ∏ i ∈ t, D i = ∏ i ∈ t, oddPrimeDiscriminant (D i).natAbs := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_oddPrimeDiscriminant_primeFactors_eq
docstring: **The odd prime discriminants recover the odd `≡ 1 (mod 4)` part.** For an odd squarefree integer `x ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, the product of the odd prime discriminants `p*` over the prime factors `p` of `x` equals `x`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_ne_neg_one
docstring: Products over odd prime-discriminant radicands, with no `-4` radicand, are not `-1`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_primeDiscriminantRadicands_ne_one_of_nonempty
docstring: A product of prime-discriminant radicands is not `1` as soon as the discriminant family is injective and the selected set is nonempty.

theorem prod_root_mem_adjoin (S : Finset ι) :
    (∏ i ∈ S, root i) ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root) :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_root_notMem_bot
docstring: **A subset-product root whose radicand product is not a square lies outside `K`.** If `∏_{i ∈ S} root i` were in `⊥`, its square `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` would be a square in `K`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.prod_root_sq
docstring: **The square of a subset-product root.** The product `∏_{i ∈ S} root i` of the chosen roots over a finite subset `S` squares to the subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` of the radicands.
code:
theorem prod_root_sq (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i)) (S : Finset ι) :
    (∏ i ∈ S, root i) ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (∏ i ∈ S, d i) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset
docstring: **The subset-product quadratic subfield of `M` attached to a nonempty subset.** Under square-class independence, each nonempty subset `S` of the index type names the quadratic subfield `K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)` of `M = K(rootᵢ : i)`.
code:
@[expose] def quadraticSubfieldOfFinset [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (S : {S : Finset ι // S.Nonempty}) :
    {F : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)) // Module.finrank K F = 2} :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_bijective
docstring: **The subset-product assignment is a bijection.** Injective by `quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective`, its domain (the nonempty subsets) and codomain (the quadratic subfields) both have cardinality `2ⁿ - 1`, so the injection is a bijection.
code:
theorem quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_bijective [Finite ι] [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    Function.Bijective (quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective
docstring: **Distinct nonempty subsets give distinct quadratic subfields.** The subset-product assignment `quadraticSubfieldOfFinset` is injective: this is the `M`-level reading of `eq_of_adjoin_prod_root_eq`, transported across the lift.
code:
theorem quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_injective [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    Function.Injective (quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_val
docstring: The subfield underlying `quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep S` is `K(∏_{i ∈ S} root i)`.

@[simp] theorem quadraticSubfieldOfFinset_val [NeZero (2 : K)] (S : {S : Finset ι // S.Nonempty}) :
    (quadraticSubfieldOfFinset hroot hindep S : IntermediateField K (adjoin K (Set.range root)))
      = adjoin K {prodRootMem (K := K) root S.1} := rfl

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.range_cmRoot

theorem range_cmRoot :
    Set.range (cmRoot p)

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.range_roots_neg_four_neg_three_neg_seven

docstring: The complex square root data for the two prime discriminants `-4` and `5`: the associated radicands are `-1` and `5`, with roots `i` and `√5`.

private theorem root_neg_four_five_sq (i : Fin 2) :
    (fun i : Fin 2 => ![Complex.I, ((Real.sqrt 5 : ℝ) : ℂ)] i) i ^ 2 =

        (((primeDiscriminantRadicand (![(-4 : ℤ), 5] i) : ℤ) : ℚ)) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern
docstring: The sign pattern of an automorphism: `0` where it fixes a generator and `1` otherwise. When `gen root i ≠ -gen root i`, the `1` case says that the automorphism negates the generator.

@[expose] noncomputable def signPattern
    (σ : adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root)) (i : ι) : ZMod 2 :=

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_eq_ite_of_zsmul_gen
docstring: **Read the sign pattern off a generator-wise sign.** If `σ (gen root i) = ε • gen root i` with `ε = ±1` (in `ℤ`) and `d i ≠ 0`, then `signPattern root σ i` is `0` when `ε = 1` and `1` when `ε = -1`. This bridges a generator-wise sign — for instance a Frobenius acting on `√dᵢ` by a Legendre symbol (`TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt`) — to the `(ℤ/2)ⁿ` identification, so it composes with `TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquiv_apply`.
code:
theorem signPattern_eq_ite_of_zsmul_gen [NeZero (2 : K)]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (σ : adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root)) {i : ι} {ε : ℤ}
    (hε : ε = 1 ∨ ε = -1) (hd : d i ≠ 0) (hσ : σ (gen root i) = ε • gen root i) :
    signPattern root σ i = if ε = 1 then 0 else 1 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_eq_one
docstring: The sign is `1` where the automorphism negates a generator that differs from its negation.
code:
theorem signPattern_eq_one
    (σ : adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root)) (i : ι)
    (hne : gen (K := K) root i ≠ -gen root i)
    (h : σ (gen root i) = -gen root i) : signPattern root σ i = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_eq_one_iff
docstring: The sign is `1` iff the automorphism negates a generator that differs from its negation.
code:
theorem signPattern_eq_one_iff (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d i))
    (σ : adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root)) (i : ι)
    (hne : gen (K := K) root i ≠ -gen root i) :
    signPattern root σ i = 1 ↔ σ (gen root i) = -gen root i := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_eq_zero
docstring: The sign is `0` exactly where the automorphism fixes the generator.

theorem signPattern_eq_zero
    (σ : adjoin K (Set.range root) ≃ₐ[K] adjoin K (Set.range root)) (i : ι)
    (h : σ (gen root i) = gen root i) : signPattern root σ i = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_eq_zero_iff
docstring: The sign is `0` iff the automorphism fixes the generator.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_mul

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.signPattern_mul_apply

    signPattern root (σ * τ) i = signPattern root σ i + signPattern root τ i := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sq_sqrt_intCast
docstring: The real square root of a nonnegative integer squares back to its rational value, in the form `(√n)² = algebraMap ℚ ℝ n`. This supplies the `hroot` hypothesis of the degree theorem for the real square roots of integer radicands. The natural-number form `sq_sqrt_natCast` is the special case `0 ≤ n`.
code:
theorem sq_sqrt_intCast {n : ℤ} (hn : 0 ≤ n) :
    (Real.sqrt n) ^ 2 = algebraMap ℚ ℝ (n : ℚ) := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.sq_sqrt_natCast
docstring: The real square root of a natural number squares back to its rational value, in the form `(√n)² = algebraMap ℚ ℝ n`. This supplies the `hroot` hypothesis that the multiquadratic degree and Galois-group theorems consume for the family of square roots of a prime family. It is the `0 ≤ n` special case of `sq_sqrt_intCast`.

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem
docstring: **Square-class descent.** In characteristic not two, if `y² = r` over `K` and `y ∈ K(root₀, …, rootₙ₋₁)`, where `root j` is a chosen square root of `d j`, then `r` is a square times a subset product of the `d j` with `j < n`.
code:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem (d : ℕ → K) (root : ℕ → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)] :
    ∀ n, ∀ r : K, ∀ y : L, y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r → y ∈ sqrtTower (K := K) root n →
      ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : K), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio n ∧
        r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fin
docstring: **Finite-index square-class descent.** If `y² = r` over `K` and `y ∈ K(root i | i : Fin n)`, where `root i` is a chosen square root of `d i`, then `r` is a square times a subset product of the `d i`.
code:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem_fin {n : ℕ} (d : Fin n → K) (root : Fin n → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)]
    {r : K} {y : L} (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r)
    (hmem : y ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)) :
    ∃ (T : Finset (Fin n)) (s : K), r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype
docstring: **Arbitrary finite-index square-class descent.** If `y² = r` over `K` and `y ∈ K(root i | i : ι)` for a finite index type `ι`, where `root i` is a chosen square root of `d i`, then `r` is a square times a subset product of the `d i`.
code:
theorem squareClass_of_sq_mem_fintype {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (d : ι → K) (root : ι → L)
    (hroot : ∀ j, root j ^ 2 = algebraMap K L (d j)) [NeZero (2 : K)]
    {r : K} {y : L} (hy : y ^ 2 = algebraMap K L r)
    (hmem : y ∈ IntermediateField.adjoin K (Set.range root)) :
    ∃ (T : Finset ι) (s : K), r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, d j := by

label: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.squareClass_of_sqrt_mem
docstring: **Square-class descent for real rational square roots.** If `r` is a nonnegative rational with `√r ∈ ℚ(√c₀, …, √cₙ₋₁)` and every `c j` is nonnegative, then `r` is a rational square times a subset product of the `c j`.
code:
theorem squareClass_of_sqrt_mem (c : ℕ → ℚ) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j) :
    ∀ n, ∀ r : ℚ, 0 ≤ r → (Real.sqrt r : ℝ) ∈ sqrtTower (K := ℚ) (fun j => Real.sqrt (c j)) n →
      ∃ (T : Finset ℕ) (s : ℚ), ↑T ⊆ Set.Iio n ∧
        r = s ^ 2 * ∏ j ∈ T, c j := by

docstring: **The Frobenius of a multiquadratic field acts on each generator by a Legendre symbol.** For a Galois number field `K` with elements `r i` satisfying `r i ² = d i ∈ ℤ`, an odd prime `p` with `p ∤ d i` for all `i`, and any prime `Q` of `𝓞 K` above `p`, there is an arithmetic Frobenius `σ ∈ Gal(K/ℚ)` at `Q`, and it sends each generator to the corresponding Legendre multiple: `σ (r i) = legendreSym p (d i) • r i`. This is the generator-wise Frobenius input of the multiquadratic splitting law; the sign-vector description under `galoisGroupEquiv` is not formed here (see the module docstring).
code:
theorem exists_isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic [IsGalois ℚ K] (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    ∃ σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K, IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q ∧
      ∀ i, σ (r i) = legendreSym p (d i) • r i := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_mem_rootSet_eq_adjoin_of_abs_discr_le
docstring: **Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating step.** Each number field `K` (a finite extension of `ℚ` inside `A`) with `|discr K| ≤ N` is generated over `ℚ` by a root in `A` of an integer polynomial of degree at most `rankOfDiscrBdd N` and all coefficients of absolute value at most `coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N`. This is `NumberField.hermiteTheorem.finite_of_discr_bdd` recast to expose its explicit generating set.
code:
theorem exists_mem_rootSet_eq_adjoin_of_abs_discr_le [DecidableEq A] {N : ℕ}
    (K : IntermediateField ℚ A) (hK₀ : FiniteDimensional ℚ K)
    (hK : haveI : _root_.NumberField K := @NumberField.mk _ _ inferInstance hK₀
      |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ x ∈ (⋃ (f : ℤ[X]) (_ : f.natDegree ≤ rankOfDiscrBdd N ∧
        ∀ i, |f.coeff i| ≤ (coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N : ℤ)),
        ((f.map (algebraMap ℤ A)).roots.toFinset : Set A)),
      (K : IntermediateField ℚ A) = ℚ⟮x⟯ := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.exists_primitive_element_infinitePlace_le
docstring: **Effective Hermite--Minkowski, generating element.** A number field `K` with `|discr K| ≤ N` has a primitive integral generator `a` all of whose infinite places are at most `max √(1 + boundOfDiscBdd N ^ 2) 1`.
code:
private theorem exists_primitive_element_infinitePlace_le {K : Type*} [Field K] [NumberField K]
    {N : ℕ} (hK : |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)) :
    ∃ a : 𝓞 K, ℚ⟮(a : K)⟯ = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ w : InfinitePlace K, w (a : K) ≤ max (Real.sqrt (1 + (boundOfDiscBdd N : ℝ) ^ 2)) 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.galoisGroupEquiv_frobenius
docstring: **The Frobenius of a multiquadratic field is the Legendre sign vector.** Under square-class independence of the `dᵢ` (so `TauCeti.Multiquadratic.galoisGroupEquiv` is the identification `Gal(M/ℚ) ≅ (ℤ/2)ⁿ`), an arithmetic Frobenius `σ` at a prime `Q` above the odd prime `p ∤ dᵢ` maps to the vector of Legendre symbols `i ↦ (dᵢ/p)`. This is the roadmap's Layer 1 Frobenius statement.
code:
theorem galoisGroupEquiv_frobenius [Finite ι]
    (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ L (d i))
    (hindep : ∀ S : Finset ι, S.Nonempty → ¬ IsSquare (∏ i ∈ S, (d i : ℚ)))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))))
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))}
    (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    galoisGroupEquiv
        (fun i => by rw [hroot i, IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply ℤ ℚ L]; simp) hindep σ =
      Multiplicative.ofAdd (fun i => if legendreSym p (d i) = 1 then 0 else 1) := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt
docstring: **A Frobenius acts on square roots by the Legendre symbol.** Let `K` be a number field, `p` an odd prime, and `σ ∈ Gal(K/ℚ)` an arithmetic Frobenius at an ideal `Q` of `𝓞 K` above `p`. If `x ∈ K` satisfies `x² = d` for an integer `d` with `p ∤ d`, then `σ x = legendreSym p d • x`: the Frobenius fixes `√d` when `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p` and negates it otherwise.
code:
theorem isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt (hodd : p ≠ 2) {d : ℤ} (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    {x : K} (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K} (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    σ x = legendreSym p d • x := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt_eq_self_iff
docstring: **A Frobenius fixes `√d` iff `d` is a quadratic residue mod `p`.** Under the hypotheses of `TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt`, `σ x = x` exactly when `legendreSym p d = 1` (the other case being `σ x = -x`, `legendreSym p d = -1`). This reads the characteristic biconditional off the `•` form, using that `x ≠ 0` (as `d ≠ 0`).
code:
theorem isArithFrobAt_apply_sqrt_eq_self_iff (hodd : p ≠ 2) {d : ℤ} (hd : ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d)
    {x : K} (hx : x ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K d)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K} (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    σ x = x ↔ legendreSym p d = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic_eq_one_iff
docstring: **A multiquadratic Frobenius is trivial iff every radicand is a residue.** Let `K = ℚ(√d₁, …, √dₙ)` be generated over `ℚ` by the square roots `r i` of the integers `d i`, let `p` be an odd prime with `p ∤ d i` for all `i`, and let `σ` be an arithmetic Frobenius at an ideal `Q` of `𝓞 K` above `p`. Then `σ = 1` iff every `d i` is a quadratic residue mod `p`. Combined with the splitting law, this is the Frobenius-theoretic reading of complete splitting.
code:
theorem isArithFrobAt_multiquadratic_eq_one_iff (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K} (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) :
    σ = 1 ↔ ∀ i, legendreSym p (d i) = 1 := by

    (hsplit : (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K) :
    legendreSym p (d i) = 1 := by

docstring: In a Galois number field, a rational prime `p` splits completely (there are `[K : ℚ]` primes of `𝓞 K` above `p`) iff its ramification index and inertia degree are both `1`.

theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff (K : Type*) [Field K] [NumberField K] [IsGalois ℚ K]
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      (span {(p : ℤ)}).ramificationIdxIn (𝓞 K) = 1 ∧
        (span {(p : ℤ)}).inertiaDegIn (𝓞 K) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_of_isGalois
code:
private theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_of_isGalois {A : Type*} [CommRing A]
    [IsDedekindDomain A] [Algebra A (𝓞 L)] [Module.Finite A (𝓞 L)]
    [IsTorsionFree A (𝓞 L)] [IsGaloisGroup Gal(L/K) A (𝓞 L)] (P : Ideal A)
    [P.IsMaximal] :
    (primesOver P (𝓞 L)).ncard = finrank K L ↔
      P.ramificationIdxIn (𝓞 L) = 1 ∧ P.inertiaDegIn (𝓞 L) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot
docstring: **Splitting completely ⟺ decomposition group trivial.** For a Galois number field `L` and a prime `Q` of `𝓞 L` above the rational prime `p`, the prime `p` splits completely (there are `[L : ℚ]` primes above it) iff the decomposition group of `Q` — its stabilizer under `Gal(L/ℚ)` — is trivial.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_eq_finrank_iff_stabilizer_eq_bot (L : Type*) [Field L]
    [NumberField L] [IsGalois ℚ L] {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (Q : Ideal (𝓞 L)) [Q.IsPrime]
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 L)).ncard = finrank ℚ L ↔
      stabilizer (L ≃ₐ[ℚ] L) Q = ⊥ := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_multiquadratic_iff
docstring: **The multiquadratic splitting law.** For `K = ℚ(√d₁, …, √dₙ)` generated over `ℚ` by square roots `r i` of integers `d i`, and an odd prime `p` dividing none of the `d i`, `p` splits completely in `K` iff every `d i` is a quadratic residue mod `p`.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_multiquadratic_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i, legendreSym p (d i) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_neg_four_five_iff
docstring: **Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-5)` genus-field generator list.** Let `K` be generated by square roots of the radicands attached to `[-4, 5]`, namely `-1` and `5`. An odd prime `p ≠ 5` splits completely in `K` exactly under the two character conditions `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)` and `(p / 5) = 1`.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_neg_four_five_iff (r : Fin 2 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K
      (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand
        (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.negFourFivePrimeDiscriminants i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hfive : p ≠ 5) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (RingOfIntegers K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      p % 4 = 1 ∧ @legendreSym 5 ⟨by decide⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_neg_four_neg_three_neg_seven_iff
docstring: **Complete splitting for the `ℚ(√-21)` genus-field generator list.** Let `K` be generated by square roots of the radicands attached to `[-4, -3, -7]`, namely `-1`, `-3`, and `-7`. An odd prime `p` not among `3` and `7` splits completely in `K` exactly under the three character conditions `p ≡ 1 (mod 4)`, `(p / 3) = 1`, and `(p / 7) = 1`.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_neg_four_neg_three_neg_seven_iff (r : Fin 3 → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K
      (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand

    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hthree : p ≠ 3) (hseven : p ≠ 7) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (RingOfIntegers K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔

        @legendreSym 7 ⟨by decide⟩ (p : ℤ) = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff
docstring: **Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of the radicands attached to a finite family of integers `D`. For an odd prime `p` dividing none of the `D i`, `p` splits completely in `K` exactly when every `D i` is a quadratic residue modulo `p`.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (D : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)

    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff_congruences
docstring: **Prime-discriminant-radicand multiquadratic splitting law, congruence form.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of the radicands attached to a finite family of prime discriminants `D`. For an odd prime `p` dividing none of the `D i`, `p` splits completely in `K` exactly when each even prime discriminant satisfies the corresponding supplementary congruence condition, and each odd prime discriminant satisfies the reciprocal Legendre-symbol condition.
code:
theorem ncard_primesOver_primeDiscriminantRadicands_iff_congruences {ι : Type*} [Finite ι]
    (D : ι → ℤ) (hD : ∀ i, TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 =
      algebraMap ℤ K (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i)))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ D i) :
    (primesOver (span {(p : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i,
        (TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) ∧
          (if D i = -4 then p % 4 = 1
          else if D i = 8 then p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 7
          else p % 8 = 1 ∨ p % 8 = 3)) ∨

docstring: **Prime-radicand multiquadratic splitting law.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of a finite family of rational primes `p i`.     (primesOver (span {(q : ℤ)}) (𝓞 K)).ncard = finrank ℚ K ↔
      ∀ i, legendreSym q (p i : ℤ) = 1 :=

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff
docstring: **Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of `2` and `3`. A rational prime `q` different from `2` and `3` splits completely in `K` exactly when both `2` and `3` are quadratic residues modulo `q`.

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_primesOver_sqrt_two_three_iff_mod_eight
docstring: **Complete splitting for `ℚ(√2, √3)`, with the `√2` character expanded.** Let `K` be generated over `ℚ` by square roots of `2` and `3`.     (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K ((![2, 3] : Fin 2 → ℕ) i : ℤ))

label: TauCeti.NumberField.ncard_setOf_finiteDimensional_abs_discr_le_le
docstring: **Effective Hermite--Minkowski.** Inside a fixed extension `A / ℚ`, the number of number fields `K` (finite extensions of `ℚ`) with `|discr K| ≤ N` is at most `(2 * coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^ (rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) * rankOfDiscrBdd N`, an explicit function of `N` alone.         |discr K| ≤ (N : ℤ)}.ncard ≤
      (2 * coeffBoundOfDiscrBdd N + 1) ^ (rankOfDiscrBdd N + 1) * rankOfDiscrBdd N := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.signPattern_frobenius
docstring: **The Frobenius sign pattern of a multiquadratic field is the Legendre encoding.** For the multiquadratic field `M = ℚ(√dᵢ : i) = adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)`, an odd prime `p ∤ dᵢ`, and an arithmetic Frobenius `σ` on `M` at a prime `Q` above `p`, the `i`-th coordinate of the sign pattern is `0` when `dᵢ` is a quadratic residue mod `p` and `1` otherwise.
code:
theorem signPattern_frobenius (hroot : ∀ i, root i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ L (d i))
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2) (hcop : ∀ i, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ d i)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))))
    [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})]
    {σ : ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root)) ≃ₐ[ℚ]
        ↥(IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root))}
    (hσ : IsArithFrobAt ℤ σ Q) (i : ι) :
    signPattern root σ i = if legendreSym p (d i) = 1 then 0 else 1 := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.stabilizer_eq_bot_of_forall_legendreSym_eq_one
docstring: Backward wrapper: for `K` generated over `ℚ` by the `r i` (`ℚ(rᵢ) = K`), if `p` is odd and every `d i` is a quadratic residue mod `p`, then the decomposition group of `Q` is trivial.
code:
private theorem stabilizer_eq_bot_of_forall_legendreSym_eq_one {ι : Type*} (d : ι → ℤ) (r : ι → K)
    (hr : ∀ i, r i ^ 2 = algebraMap ℤ K (d i))
    (htop : IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range r) = ⊤)
    {p : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] (hodd : p ≠ 2)
    (hqr : ∀ i, legendreSym p (d i) = 1)
    (Q : Ideal (𝓞 K)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver (span {(p : ℤ)})] :
    stabilizer (K ≃ₐ[ℚ] K) Q = ⊥ := by

TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative
docstring: **Dirichlet's unit theorem, structural form.** The unit group of the ring of integers of a number field is the product of its torsion subgroup and the free abelian group generated by the fundamental system: a unit corresponds to its unique decomposition as a root of unity times a product of powers of fundamental units (`NumberField.Units.exist_unique_eq_mul_prod`).
code:
noncomputable def unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative :
    (𝓞 F)ˣ ≃* torsion F × Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ) :=

label: TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_apply
docstring: The forward map of `TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative` reads off the Dirichlet decomposition: a unit presented as a root of unity `ζ` times a product of powers of the fundamental system is sent to the pair `(ζ, e)`.
code:
@[simp] theorem unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_apply
    (ζ : torsion F) (e : Fin (rank F) → ℤ) :
    unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative F
        ((ζ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) * ∏ i, fundSystem F i ^ e i) = (ζ, Multiplicative.ofAdd e) := by

docstring: The inverse of `TauCeti.NumberField.unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative` sends a pair to the root of unity times the product of powers of fundamental units.
code:
@[simp] theorem unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative_symm_apply
    (ζ : torsion F) (e : Multiplicative (Fin (rank F) → ℤ)) :
    (unitsMulEquivTorsionProdMultiplicative F).symm (ζ, e) =
      (ζ : (𝓞 F)ˣ) * ∏ i, fundSystem F i ^ Multiplicative.toAdd e i := by

docstring: **The exact unit-square index of genus theory.** For a number field `F`, `[𝓞 F^× : (𝓞 F^×)²] = 2 ^ (rank F + 1)`. This is the subgroup-index reading of `TauCeti.NumberField.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_units`; it sharpens the degree bound `TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le` to an equality.
code:
theorem units_sq_index_eq :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index = 2 ^ (rank F + 1) := by

label: TauCeti.NumberField.units_sq_index_le
docstring: **Squares have small index in the unit group.** `[O_F^× : (O_F^×)²] ≤ 2^[F:ℚ]`, stated using Mathlib's `Subgroup.square` for the subgroup of squares. By Dirichlet's unit theorem `O_F^×` is generated by the `rank`-element fundamental system together with a torsion generator, so `TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top` bounds the index by `2^(rank+1)`, and `rank + 1 ≤ [F:ℚ]`.
code:
theorem units_sq_index_le (F : Type*) [Field F] [NumberField F] :
    (Subgroup.square (𝓞 F)ˣ).index ≤ 2 ^ Module.finrank ℚ F := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn
docstring: Uniform ellipticity and boundedness with explicit constants on a domain. The predicate says that for every `x ∈ Ω`, the matrix `a x` has quadratic form bounded below by `λ‖ξ‖²` and bilinear form bounded above by `Λ‖η‖‖ξ‖`, uniformly in `x`, `η`, and `ξ`. The side conditions `0 < λ` and `λ ≤ Λ` are part of the predicate so later energy estimates can recover them directly.
code: def UniformlyEllipticOn (Ω : Set X) (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (lam Lam : ℝ) : Prop :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_bounded
docstring: Adding a bounded coefficient perturbation preserves uniform ellipticity after reducing the lower ellipticity constant by the perturbation size. If `a` is uniformly elliptic with constants `λ, Λ` and `b` has pointwise bilinear bound `μ`, then `a + b` is uniformly elliptic with constants `λ - μ, Λ + μ`, provided `μ < λ`. This is the finite-dimensional coefficient stability estimate used when perturbing a uniformly elliptic divergence-form operator.
code:
lemma add_bounded (h : UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam) {b : X → Matrix n n ℝ}
    {Mu : ℝ} (hMu_nonneg : 0 ≤ Mu) (hMu_lt : Mu < lam)
    (hb_upper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
      |η ⬝ᵥ (b x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + b x) (lam - Mu) (Lam + Mu) := by

    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + c • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam (Lam + c) :=

docstring: Adding a constant bounded scalar multiple of the identity preserves uniform ellipticity after reducing the lower ellipticity constant by the absolute value bound.

      (Lam + Mu) :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.UniformlyEllipticOn.add_nonneg
docstring: Adding a pointwise nonnegative bounded coefficient field preserves uniform ellipticity. The lower ellipticity constant is unchanged, while the upper bilinear-form constant is increased by the upper bound for the perturbation. This is the pointwise matrix estimate used when an energy form is split into a uniformly elliptic principal part plus a nonnegative bounded perturbation.

      |η ⬝ᵥ (b x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Mu * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => a x + b x) lam (Lam + Mu) := by

    (hpert : Integrable
      (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x - 1) (b x) (c x - m x) (U x) (V x)) μ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) m U V +
        energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => a x - 1) b (fun x => c x - m x) U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_eq_one_zero_mass_add_perturbation
docstring: The integrated full energy form is the shifted-Laplacian form with the same mass plus the principal-and-drift perturbation.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_eq_one_zero_mass_add_perturbation
    (hmodel : Integrable
      (fun x => energyIntegrand (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 (c x) (U x) (V x)) μ)
    (hpert : Integrable
      (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x - 1) (b x) 0 (U x) (V x)) μ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) c U V +
        energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => a x - 1) b (fun _ => 0) U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_neg_coefficients
docstring: Negating the coefficient triple negates the integrated energy form.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_neg_coefficients :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => -a x) (fun x => -b x) (fun x => -c x) U V =
      -energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_neg_left
docstring: Negating the left jet field negates the integrated energy form.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_neg_left :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c (fun x => -U x) V = -energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_neg_right
docstring: Negating the right jet field negates the integrated energy form.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_neg_right :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U (fun x => -V x) = -energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_const_mass_self_nonneg
docstring: Constant nonnegative mass gives a nonnegative shifted-Laplacian diagonal form.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_const_mass_self_nonneg {c : ℝ} (hc : 0 ≤ c) :
    0 ≤ energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => c) U U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass
docstring: The integrated shifted Laplacian model form `−Δ + c` is the sum of the Dirichlet density and the mass density.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass (m : X → ℝ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) m U V =
      ∫ x, ((V x).2 ⬝ᵥ (U x).2 + m x * (U x).1 * (V x).1) ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_comm
docstring: The shifted-Laplacian model integrated form `-Δ + c` is symmetric.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_comm :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) c V U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_self
docstring: The diagonal of the integrated shifted Laplacian model is the integral of `‖∇u‖² + c u²` at the jet level.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_self (m : X → ℝ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) m U U =
      ∫ x, (‖(U x).2‖ ^ 2 + m x * (U x).1 ^ 2) ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_self_nonneg
docstring: The shifted-Laplacian diagonal form is nonnegative when the mass is a.e. nonnegative.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_self_nonneg
    (hm : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ m x) :
    0 ≤ energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) m U U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_swap_eq
docstring: Bundled symmetry of the shifted-Laplacian model integrated form `-Δ + c`.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_mass_swap_eq :
    Function.swap (energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) c) =
      energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) c :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_zero
docstring: The integrated `−Δ` model form is the integral of the dot product of the two gradient components of the jet fields.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_zero :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) U V =
      ∫ x, ((V x).2 ⬝ᵥ (U x).2) ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_one_zero_zero_self_nonneg
docstring: The Dirichlet model `-Δ` has nonnegative diagonal energy.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_one_zero_zero_self_nonneg :
    0 ≤ energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) U U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_principal_add_lowerOrder
docstring: The integrated full energy form splits into its principal and lower-order parts.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_principal_add_lowerOrder
    (hprincipal : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 0 (U x) (V x)) μ)
    (hlower : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand 0 (b x) (c x) (U x) (V x)) μ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) U V +
        energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => 0) b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_principal_drift_mass
docstring: The integrated full energy form splits into its principal, drift, and mass pieces.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_principal_drift_mass
    (hprincipal : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 0 (U x) (V x)) μ)
    (hdrift : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand 0 (b x) 0 (U x) (V x)) μ)
    (hmass : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand 0 0 (c x) (U x) (V x)) μ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) U V +
        energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => 0) b (fun _ => 0) U V +
          energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_smul
docstring: The integrated energy form is homogeneous in the coefficient triple.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_smul :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => r • a x) (fun x => r • b x) (fun x => r * c x) U V =
      r * energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_smul_left
docstring: Homogeneity in the left jet field.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_smul_left (r : ℝ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c (fun x => r • U x) V =
      r * energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_smul_right
docstring: Homogeneity in the right jet field.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_smul_right (r : ℝ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U (fun x => r • V x) =
      r * energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_sub
docstring: The integrated energy form is subtractive in the coefficient triple, under the corresponding integrability assumptions for the two densities.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_sub
    (h : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x) (U x) (V x)) μ)
    (h' : Integrable (fun x => energyIntegrand (a' x) (b' x) (c' x) (U x) (V x)) μ) :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => a x - a' x) (fun x => b x - b' x) (fun x => c x - c' x)
        U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a b c U V - energyFormIntegral μ a' b' c' U V := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_coefficients
docstring: The zero coefficient triple gives the zero integrated energy form.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_coefficients :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) (fun _ => 0) U V = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm_ae
docstring: A.e. symmetric principal coefficients make the zero-drift integrated energy form symmetric.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm_ae
    (ha : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, (a x).IsSymm) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c V U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_comm_on
docstring: Symmetry on a domain when the measure is a.e. supported there and the principal coefficients are pointwise symmetric on that domain.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_comm_on {Ω : Set X}
    (hΩ : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ω) (ha : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → (a x).IsSymm) :
    energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c V U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_self_nonneg
docstring: A zero-drift diagonal integrated energy form is nonnegative when the principal quadratic form and mass coefficient are a.e. nonnegative.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_self_nonneg
    (ha : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, 0 ≤ ξ ⬝ᵥ (a x *ᵥ ξ))
    (hc : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ c x) :
    0 ≤ energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c U U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_swap_eq_of_isSymm_ae
docstring: Bundled-map form of symmetry for a zero-drift integrated energy form with a.e. symmetric principal coefficients.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_swap_eq_of_isSymm_ae
    (ha : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, (a x).IsSymm) :
    Function.swap (energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c) =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_swap_eq_on
docstring: Bundled-map symmetry on a domain when the measure is a.e. supported there and the principal coefficients are pointwise symmetric on that domain.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_swap_eq_on {Ω : Set X}
    (hΩ : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ Ω) (ha : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → (a x).IsSymm) :
    Function.swap (energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c) =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_transpose_apply
docstring: With zero drift, transposing the principal coefficient swaps the two jet fields under the integral.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_drift_transpose_apply :
    energyFormIntegral μ (fun x => (a x)ᵀ) (fun _ => 0) c U V =
      energyFormIntegral μ a (fun _ => 0) c V U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_left
docstring: The integrated energy form vanishes when the left jet field is zero.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_left :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c (fun _ => 0) V = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormIntegral_zero_right
docstring: The integrated energy form vanishes when the right jet field is zero.
code:
lemma energyFormIntegral_zero_right :
    energyFormIntegral μ a b c U (fun _ => 0) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp
docstring: The constant-coefficient divergence-form energy form on square-integrable value-gradient jets. This is the Hölder pairing induced by `energyIntegrand A b c`; in particular it is bundled as a continuous bilinear map, with no integrability hypotheses required at use sites.
code:
noncomputable def energyFormLp (μ : Measure X) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : ℝ) :
    Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ →L[ℝ]
      Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ →L[ℝ] ℝ :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpDecidableEq
docstring: The classical decidable equality used for finite-dimensional matrix computations.
code: noncomputable local instance energyFormLpDecidableEq : DecidableEq n := Classical.decEq n

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable
docstring: The variable-coefficient divergence-form energy form on square-integrable value-gradient jets. The `MemLp ... ⊤ μ` argument records exactly that the pointwise energy forms are strongly measurable and essentially bounded. Its proof is irrelevant to the resulting form.
code:
noncomputable def energyFormLpVariable (μ : Measure X) (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x)) ⊤ μ) :
    Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ →L[ℝ]
      Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ →L[ℝ] ℝ :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_apply
docstring: The variable-coefficient `L²` energy form is the integral of the pointwise jet energy density.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_apply (μ : Measure X) (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ a b c hcoeff U V =
      ∫ x, energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x) (U x) (V x) ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_self
docstring: Replacing the principal coefficient by its symmetric part does not change the diagonal variable energy form.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_self (μ : Measure X)
    (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (b : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
      (b x) (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (hcoeff' : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x)) b c hcoeff U U =
      energyFormLpVariable μ a b c hcoeff' U U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply
docstring: The symmetric-part variable zero-drift energy form is the average of the original form and its transpose.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply (μ : Measure X)
    (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hsymm : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart (a x)) 0
      (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
        (fun _ => 0) c hsymm U V =
      (energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff U V +
        energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff V U) / 2 := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_comm
docstring: The symmetric-part variable zero-drift energy form is symmetric.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_comm (μ : Measure X)
    (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart (a x)) 0
      (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
        (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff U V =
      energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
        (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff V U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq
docstring: The symmetric-part variable zero-drift energy form is equal to its flip.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq (μ : Measure X)
    (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (coefficientSymmetricPart (a x)) 0
      (c x)) ⊤ μ) :
    (energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
      (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff).flip =
      energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => coefficientSymmetricPart (a x))
        (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_congr_ae
docstring: Almost-everywhere equal coefficient fields induce the same variable-coefficient energy form.

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_proof_irrel
docstring: The variable-coefficient energy form is independent of the proof that its coefficient field belongs to `L∞`.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_proof_irrel (μ : Measure X) (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : X → EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff hcoeff' : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) (b x) (c x)) ⊤ μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ a b c hcoeff = energyFormLpVariable μ a b c hcoeff' := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm_ae
docstring: An a.e. symmetric principal coefficient gives a symmetric variable zero-drift energy form.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_comm_of_isSymm_ae {μ : Measure X}
    {a : X → Matrix n n ℝ} (ha : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, (a x).IsSymm) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff U V =
      energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff V U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_flip_eq_of_isSymm_ae
docstring: An a.e. symmetric principal coefficient makes the variable zero-drift energy form equal to its flip.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_flip_eq_of_isSymm_ae {μ : Measure X}
    {a : X → Matrix n n ℝ} (ha : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, (a x).IsSymm) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x)) ⊤ μ) :
    (energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff).flip =
      energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_transpose_apply
docstring: Transposing the principal coefficient swaps the arguments of a variable zero-drift energy form.
code:
theorem energyFormLpVariable_zero_drift_transpose_apply (μ : Measure X)
    (a : X → Matrix n n ℝ) (c : X → ℝ)
    (hcoeff : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x)ᵀ 0 (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (hcoeff' : MemLp (fun x => energyIntegrand (a x) 0 (c x)) ⊤ μ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLpVariable μ (fun x => (a x)ᵀ) (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff U V =
      energyFormLpVariable μ a (fun _ => 0) c hcoeff' V U := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_apply
docstring: The `L²` energy form is the integral of the pointwise jet energy density.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_apply (μ : Measure X) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : ℝ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ A b c U V =
      ∫ x, energyIntegrand A b c (U x) (V x) ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_self
docstring: Replacing the principal coefficient by its symmetric part does not change the diagonal `L²` energy form.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_self (μ : Measure X) (A : Matrix n n ℝ)
    (b : EuclideanSpace ℝ n) (c : ℝ)
    (U : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) b c U U =

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply
docstring: The symmetric-part zero-drift `L²` energy form is the average of the original form and its transpose.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_apply (μ : Measure X)
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c : ℝ) (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c U V =
      (energyFormLp μ A 0 c U V + energyFormLp μ A 0 c V U) / 2 := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_comm
docstring: The symmetric-part zero-drift `L²` energy form is symmetric.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_comm (μ : Measure X)
    (A : Matrix n n ℝ) (c : ℝ) (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c U V =
      energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c V U :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq
docstring: The symmetric-part zero-drift `L²` energy form is equal to its flip.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_coefficientSymmetricPart_zero_drift_flip_eq (μ : Measure X)

    (energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c).flip =
      energyFormLp μ (coefficientSymmetricPart A) 0 c :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_apply

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_comm
docstring: The shifted-Laplacian `L²` energy form is symmetric.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_comm (μ : Measure X) (c : ℝ)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 c U V =

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_flip_eq
docstring: The shifted-Laplacian `L²` energy form is equal to its flip.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_flip_eq (μ : Measure X) (c : ℝ) :
    (energyFormLp μ (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 c).flip =
      energyFormLp μ (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 c :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_self
docstring: The diagonal of the shifted-Laplacian `L²` energy form is the integral of the squared gradient norm plus the mass density.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_one_zero_mass_self (μ : Measure X) (c : ℝ)
    (U : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 c U U =

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_zero_apply
docstring: The Dirichlet energy form pairs the gradient components of two `L²` jets.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_one_zero_zero_apply (μ : Measure X)
    (U V : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :
    energyFormLp μ (1 : Matrix n n ℝ) 0 0 U V =
      ∫ x, (V x).2 ⬝ᵥ (U x).2 ∂μ := by

label: TauCeti.PDE.energyFormLp_one_zero_zero_self
docstring: The diagonal of the Dirichlet `L²` energy form is the integral of the squared gradient norm.
code:
theorem energyFormLp_one_zero_zero_self (μ : Measure X)
    (U : Lp (ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) 2 μ) :

label: TauCeti.PDE.garding_energyIntegrand_self_of_bounds
docstring: **Pointwise Gårding inequality.** With a nonnegative mass coefficient (`c ≥ 0`), the diagonal of the jet form is bounded below by `(λ/2)‖∇u‖² − (β²/2λ)|u|²`. The ellipticity floor `λ‖∇u‖²` pays for the drift term via Young's inequality, leaving half the floor and a mass defect proportional to `β²/λ`. Integrating over `Ω` this is Gårding's inequality `a(u, u) ≥ (λ/2)‖∇u‖²_{L²} − (β²/2λ)‖u‖²_{L²}`.

    {A : Matrix n n ℝ} {b₀ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n} {c₀ : ℝ}
    (hQ : ∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ A.toQuadraticForm' ξ)
    (hb : ‖b₀‖ ≤ beta) (hc : 0 ≤ c₀)
    (U : ℝ × EuclideanSpace ℝ n) :
    lam / 2 * ‖U.2‖ ^ 2 - beta ^ 2 / (2 * lam) * U.1 ^ 2
      ≤ energyIntegrand A b₀ c₀ U U := by

      ≤ energyIntegrand A b₀ c₀ U U := by

    (hlam_one : lam ≤ 1) (hone_Lam : 1 ≤ Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun _ => (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam Lam := by

docstring: In particular, the identity coefficient field is uniformly elliptic with constants `λ = Λ = 1`.

label: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_const_smul_one
docstring: A constant isotropic coefficient field is uniformly elliptic for any explicit constants `λ ≤ c ≤ Λ` with `0 < λ`.

label: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_iff
docstring: Characteristic restatement of uniform ellipticity and boundedness on a domain.
code:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_iff :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω a lam Lam ↔
      0 < lam ∧ lam ≤ Lam ∧
        ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω →
          (∀ ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n,
            lam * ‖ξ‖ ^ 2 ≤ (a x).toQuadraticForm' ξ) ∧
            ∀ η ξ : EuclideanSpace ℝ n, |η ⬝ᵥ (a x *ᵥ ξ)| ≤ Lam * ‖η‖ * ‖ξ‖ :=

label: TauCeti.PDE.uniformlyEllipticOn_smul_one
docstring: An isotropic scalar coefficient field is uniformly elliptic when its scalar coefficient lies between the lower and upper constants. This packages the common model `a(x) = c(x) I`: if `λ ≤ c x ≤ Λ` on `Ω`, then `c x • 1` satisfies the lower quadratic bound and the bilinear upper bound with constants `λ` and `Λ`.
code:
lemma uniformlyEllipticOn_smul_one (Ω : Set X) (c : X → ℝ) {lam Lam : ℝ}
    (hlam : 0 < lam) (hlamLam : lam ≤ Lam)
    (hbound : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ Ω → lam ≤ c x ∧ c x ≤ Lam) :
    UniformlyEllipticOn Ω (fun x => c x • (1 : Matrix n n ℝ)) lam Lam := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube
docstring: A plumbing-lattice cube generator: a lattice base point together with a finite set of basis directions. In Némethi's lattice homology this is the cubical generator usually denoted by a pair `(x, S)`.
code: structure PlumbingCube (V : Type*) where

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.base_mem_vertices
docstring: The base point is a vertex of every bundled cube.
code:
theorem base_mem_vertices (C : PlumbingCube V) :
    C.base ∈ C.vertices :=

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
docstring: The lower-lower codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent along either path.
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace v hv) w =
      characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C w +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace w hw) v := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
docstring: The lower-then-upper mixed codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent as the upper-then-lower path to the same corner.
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace v hv)
          (v := w)
          (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := w) hw +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace w hw) v := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff
docstring: The lower exponent is zero exactly when erasing the direction leaves the bundled weight unchanged.
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_eq_zero_iff [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v = 0 ↔
      characteristicWeight P k C = characteristicWeight P k (C.eraseDirection v) :=

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_mk
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_mk [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) (v : V) :
    characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) v =
      P.characteristicLowerFaceExponent k x S v :=

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast
docstring: The lower exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight and the weight after erasing the direction.
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) (v : V) :
    (characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v : ℤ) =
      characteristicWeight P k C - characteristicWeight P k (C.eraseDirection v) :=

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast_lowerFace
docstring: The lower-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight and the lower face weight.
code:
theorem characteristicLowerFaceExponent_natCast_lowerFace
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C v : ℤ) =
      characteristicWeight P k C - characteristicWeight P k (C.lowerFace v hv) := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
docstring: The upper-then-lower mixed codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent as the lower-then-upper path to the same corner.
code:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_lowerFace_comm
    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := v) hv +
        characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace v hv) w =
      characteristicLowerFaceExponent P k C w +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.lowerFace w hw)
          (v := v)
          (by rw [lowerFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv) := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_add_upperFace_comm
docstring: The upper-upper codimension-two square has the same total `U`-exponent along either path.
code:

    (hv : v ∈ C.directions) (hw : w ∈ C.directions) (hne : v ≠ w) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := v) hv +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace v hv)
          (v := w)
          (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne.symm hw) =
      characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C (v := w) hw +
        characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k (C.upperFace w hw)
          (v := v)
          (by rw [upperFace_directions]; exact Finset.mem_erase_of_ne_of_mem hne hv) := by

docstring: The upper-face exponent is zero exactly when the upper face has the same bundled weight as the ambient cube.
code:

    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C hv = 0 ↔

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_mk
code:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_mk [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (x : V → ℤ) (S : Finset V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k ({ base := x, directions := S } : PlumbingCube V) hv =

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast
docstring: The upper-face exponent, cast back to `ℤ`, is the difference between the bundled cube weight and the upper face weight.
code:
theorem characteristicUpperFaceExponent_natCast [Fintype V] (P : PlumbingGraph V)
    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    (characteristicUpperFaceExponent P k C hv : ℤ) =

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_eq_max_faces
docstring: In any present direction, the characteristic weight of a cube is the maximum of the weights of its lower and upper faces.
code:

    (k : P.characteristicVectors) (C : PlumbingCube V) {v : V} (hv : v ∈ C.directions) :
    characteristicWeight P k C =

label: TauCeti.PlumbingCube.characteristicWeight_mk
code:

docstring: The upper face's characteristic weight is bounded by the ambient cube weight.

label: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph
docstring: A plumbing graph: a simple graph together with an integer weight on each vertex. The vertices are the plumbed spheres, the edges record which pairs of spheres are plumbed together, and `weight v` is the self-intersection number (the framing / Euler number) of the sphere `v`. The combinatorics is modelled by a `SimpleGraph`: at most one edge between two distinct vertices, and no self-loops. The finite lattice API is provided by declarations that assume `[Fintype V]`.

docstring: The characteristic cube weight of the zero-dimensional cube is the point weight of its base point.

label: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_eq_max_erase
docstring: The cube weight is the maximum of its two face weights in any direction `v ∈ S`: the lower face (base point `x`, directions `S.erase v`) and the upper face (base point `x + E_v`, directions `S.erase v`). This is the cubical recursion at the heart of the lattice-homology differential.
code:
theorem characteristicCubeWeight_eq_max_erase (x : V → ℤ) {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ S) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S =
      max (P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (S.erase v))
        (P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) (S.erase v)) := by

label: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.characteristicCubeWeight_insert_eq_max
docstring: The "add a direction" form of the cube-weight recursion: adjoining a new direction `v ∉ S` to a cube gives the maximum of the original cube weight and the weight of the cube shifted by the new basis vector `E_v`.

theorem characteristicCubeWeight_insert_eq_max (x : V → ℤ) {S : Finset V} {v : V} (hv : v ∉ S) :
    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x (insert v S) =
      max (P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S)
        (P.characteristicCubeWeight k (x + Pi.single v (1 : ℤ)) S) := by

    P.characteristicCubeWeight k x S ≤ n := by

theorem characteristicCubeWeight_le_iff
