      f.ofConv (1 ⊗ₜ[k]
        MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) (1 : k)) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one
docstring: The inverse base-changed split-torus points equivalence takes the standard coordinate generator indexed by `i` to the chosen coordinate `c i`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single_one (c : σ → Aˣ) (i : σ) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (σ := σ)).symm c).ofConv
        (1 ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) (1 : k)) =
      (c i : A) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single
docstring: The inverse base-changed split-torus points equivalence sends a pure tensor `s ⊗ single (ofAdd m) r` to the scalar multiple of the monomial in the chosen coordinates with exponent vector `m`.
code:
theorem baseChangePointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_tmul_single (c : σ → Aˣ) (s : K)
    (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (r : k) :
    ((baseChangePointsMulEquiv (k := k) (K := K) (A := A) (σ := σ)).symm c).ofConv
        (s ⊗ₜ[k] MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) r) =
      s • (r • ((m.prod fun i n => c i ^ n : Aˣ) : A)) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.charPoints_comp_cocharPoints_ofAdd
docstring: **The dot-product pairing is realized on points as a power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ`.** Composing the character `ofAdd m` after the cocharacter `ψ` is the power endomorphism of `𝔾ₘ` with exponent the dot product `∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`, so on points it raises a unit to that power. This is the split-torus instance of `DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints_comp_cocharPoints`.
code:
theorem charPoints_comp_cocharPoints_ofAdd
    (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    (DiagonalizableGroup.charPoints (R := R) (A := A) (Multiplicative.ofAdd m)).comp
        (DiagonalizableGroup.cocharPoints ψ) =
      DiagonalizableGroup.powEnd (m.sum fun i c => c * cocharEquiv ψ i) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharAddEquiv
docstring: The **cocharacter lattice `X_*(T)`** as a `ℤ`-module, bundled: the additive form of `cocharEquiv`, identifying `Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)` (the cocharacter group with its natural additive structure) with `σ → ℤ` as an `AddEquiv`. This carries the algebraic compatibility that `cocharEquiv` reads off pointwise (`cocharEquiv_one`, `cocharEquiv_mul`), so it transports the natural `ℤ`-module structure.
code:
noncomputable def cocharAddEquiv :
    Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) ≃+ (σ → ℤ) :=

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharAddEquiv_apply
docstring: `cocharAddEquiv` agrees coordinatewise with the unbundled `cocharEquiv`.
code:
theorem cocharAddEquiv_apply (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (i : σ) :
    cocharAddEquiv (Additive.ofMul ψ) i = cocharEquiv ψ i := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv
docstring: The **cocharacter lattice `X_*(T)`** of the rank-`σ` split torus `T = D(Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))`, identified with `σ → ℤ`. A cocharacter `ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ` is read off on the standard generators `ofAdd (single i 1)`, its coordinate at `i` being `(ψ (ofAdd (single i 1))).toAdd`. This is `TauCeti.freeAbelianCharEquiv` (with target `Multiplicative ℤ`) followed by `Multiplicative.toAdd` in each coordinate.
code:
noncomputable def cocharEquiv :
    (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) ≃ (σ → ℤ) :=

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_apply
docstring: The `i`-th coordinate of a cocharacter is its value on the standard generator `ofAdd (single i 1)`, read as an integer through `Multiplicative.toAdd`.
code:
theorem cocharEquiv_apply (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (i : σ) :
    cocharEquiv ψ i = (ψ (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1))).toAdd := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_mul
docstring: Reading off cocharacter coordinates is additive: the product of cocharacters (the group operation on the cocharacter lattice) corresponds to pointwise addition of coordinates.
code:
theorem cocharEquiv_mul (ψ φ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    cocharEquiv (ψ * φ) = cocharEquiv ψ + cocharEquiv φ := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.cocharEquiv_one
docstring: Reading off cocharacter coordinates is additive: the trivial cocharacter has zero coordinates.
code: theorem cocharEquiv_one : cocharEquiv (1 : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.dotPairing
docstring: **The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing as a `ℤ`-bilinear map.** On the character lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = σ → ℤ` (via `cocharEquiv`) the pairing is the evaluation/dot product `⟨m, v⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ vᵢ`, packaged from Mathlib's `Finsupp.llift`. It agrees with the character–cocharacter pairing of `TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` through `cocharEquiv` (`pairing_eq_dotPairing`).
code: noncomputable def dotPairing : (σ →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] (σ → ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ :=

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.dotPairing_apply
code:
theorem dotPairing_apply (m : σ →₀ ℤ) (v : σ → ℤ) :
    dotPairing m v = m.sum fun i c => c * v i := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.eq_one_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero
docstring: **Right non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing.** A cocharacter `ψ` pairing to `0` against every character is trivial: `ψ = 1`. This holds for arbitrary `σ`; for finite `σ` the pairing is moreover perfect (`instIsPerfPair`).

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero
docstring: **Left non-degeneracy of the split-torus pairing.** A character `ofAdd m` pairing to `0` against every cocharacter is trivial: `m = 0`. This holds for arbitrary `σ`; for finite `σ` the pairing is moreover perfect (`instIsPerfPair`).
code:
theorem eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero {m : σ →₀ ℤ}
    (h : ∀ ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ,
      DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ = 0) :
    m = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.instIsPerfPair
docstring: **The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is perfect (finite rank).** For a finite-rank split torus (`Finite σ`), the dot-product pairing `dotPairing` between the character lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = σ → ℤ` is a perfect pairing in the sense of Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsPerfPair`: both induced maps to the `ℤ`-duals are isomorphisms. This is the split-torus perfect pairing that is the input to root data. (For arbitrary `σ` the pairing stays non-degenerate in each slot — `eq_zero_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero`, `eq_one_of_forall_pairing_eq_zero` — while perfectness is proved only in finite rank.)
code: instance instIsPerfPair [Finite σ] : (dotPairing (σ := σ)).IsPerfPair := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.instLatticePairingIsPerfPair
docstring: **The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is perfect (finite rank), on the genuine cocharacter lattice.** For a finite-rank split torus (`Finite σ`), `latticePairing` between the character lattice `X*(T) = σ →₀ ℤ` and the genuine cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)` is a perfect pairing in the sense of Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsPerfPair`, transported from `instIsPerfPair` along `cocharAddEquiv`.
code: instance instLatticePairingIsPerfPair [Finite σ] : (latticePairing (σ := σ)).IsPerfPair := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.latticePairing
docstring: **The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing on the genuine lattices.** The dot-product pairing `dotPairing`, with its coordinate model `σ → ℤ` of the cocharacter lattice transported back along `cocharAddEquiv` to the genuine cocharacter lattice `X_*(T) = Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ)`. On a cocharacter `ψ` it is still `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i` (`latticePairing_ofMul`).
code:
noncomputable def latticePairing :
    (σ →₀ ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ]
      Additive (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ :=

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.latticePairing_ofMul
docstring: `latticePairing` evaluated on a cocharacter is the character–cocharacter pairing, the dot product `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩ = ∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`.
code:
theorem latticePairing_ofMul (m : σ →₀ ℤ)
    (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) :
    latticePairing m (Additive.ofMul ψ) =
      DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: Naturality of the inverse split-torus points equivalence in the value algebra.
code:
theorem mapValue_pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (φ : A →ₐ[R] B) (c : σ → Aˣ) :
    AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))) φ
        ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c) =
      (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := B)).symm
        (fun i => Units.map φ.toMonoidHom (c i)) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pairing_eq_dotPairing
docstring: **The dot-product pairing computes the character–cocharacter pairing.** For a character `ofAdd m` and a cocharacter `ψ` (with coordinates `cocharEquiv ψ`), the pairing `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩` of `TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` is `dotPairing m (cocharEquiv ψ)`.
code:
theorem pairing_eq_dotPairing (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (m : σ →₀ ℤ) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ = dotPairing m (cocharEquiv ψ) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pairing_ofAdd_eq
docstring: **The split-torus character–cocharacter pairing is the dot product.** For a character `ofAdd m` of `T` (`m : σ →₀ ℤ = X*(T)`) and a cocharacter `ψ` (with coordinates `cocharEquiv ψ : σ → ℤ = X_*(T)`), the pairing `⟨ofAdd m, ψ⟩` of `TauCeti.Algebra.AlgebraicGroup.Cocharacter` is `∑ᵢ mᵢ · cocharEquiv ψ i`. This is the canonical evaluation pairing between the free `ℤ`-module `σ →₀ ℤ` and its dual `σ → ℤ`, extending the rank-`1` `DiagonalizableGroup.pairing_ofAdd` to arbitrary rank.
code:
theorem pairing_ofAdd_eq (ψ : Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ) →* Multiplicative ℤ) (m : σ →₀ ℤ) :
    DiagonalizableGroup.pairing (Multiplicative.ofAdd m) ψ =
      m.sum fun i c => c * cocharEquiv ψ i := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv
docstring: The functor of points of the rank-`σ` split torus `D(Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))`: for every commutative `R`-algebra `A`, the convolution group of `R`-algebra maps out of `R[Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)]` is the product group `σ → Aˣ`, under pointwise multiplication.
code:
noncomputable def pointsMulEquiv :
    WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A) ≃* (σ → Aˣ) :=

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
docstring: The points equivalence reads off the value of a point on the `i`-th standard generator `single (ofAdd (single i 1)) 1` of `R[Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)]`.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_apply_coe
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A)) (i : σ) :
    (pointsMulEquiv f i : A) =
      f.ofConv (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) 1) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_mapValue
docstring: The split-torus points equivalence is natural in the value algebra: post-composing a point with an `R`-algebra map `φ : A →ₐ[R] B` sends each coordinate through the induced map on units.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_mapValue (φ : A →ₐ[R] B)
    (f : WithConv (MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)) →ₐ[R] A)) (i : σ) :
    pointsMulEquiv (AlgHom.mapValue (H := MonoidAlgebra R (Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ))) φ f) i =
      Units.map φ.toMonoidHom (pointsMulEquiv f i) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply
docstring: The inverse points equivalence sends a family `c : σ → Aˣ` to the point extending the character of `Multiplicative (σ →₀ ℤ)` determined by `c`.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply (c : σ → Aˣ) :
    (pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c =
      toConv (DiagonalizableGroup.point (freeAbelianCharEquiv.symm c)) := by

label: TauCeti.SplitTorus.pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single
docstring: The inverse points equivalence sends a coordinate family to the point taking the `i`-th standard generator to the `i`-th coordinate.
code:
theorem pointsMulEquiv_symm_apply_single (c : σ → Aˣ) (i : σ) :
    ((pointsMulEquiv (R := R) (A := A)).symm c).ofConv
        (MonoidAlgebra.single (Multiplicative.ofAdd (Finsupp.single i 1)) 1) =
      (c i : A) := by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_mk
docstring: The induced equivalence on normalizer quotients sends a representative to the image representative.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_mk (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientEquivMap H e (normalizerQuotientMk H g) =
      normalizerQuotientMk (H.map (e : G →* K))
        (normalizerEquivMap H e g) :=

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_mk_coe
docstring: On representatives, `normalizerQuotientEquivMap` applies the original group isomorphism.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_mk_coe (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientEquivMap H e (normalizerQuotientMk H g) =
      normalizerQuotientMk (H.map (e : G →* K))
        ⟨e (g : G), by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_refl_mk
docstring: After identifying `H.map (MulEquiv.refl G)` with `H`, identity transport on normalizer quotients fixes representatives.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_refl_mk (H : Subgroup G)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientEquivMap H (MulEquiv.refl G) (normalizerQuotientMk H g) =
      normalizerQuotientMk (H.map ((MulEquiv.refl G : G ≃* G) : G →* G))
        ⟨(g : G), by simp [g.2]⟩ := by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_refl_mk_congr
docstring: After the subgroup equality `H.map id = H`, identity transport on normalizer quotients is the canonical identity on representatives.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_refl_mk_congr (H : Subgroup G)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientCongr
        (by rw [MulEquiv.coe_monoidHom_refl, _root_.Subgroup.map_id] :
          H.map ((MulEquiv.refl G : G ≃* G) : G →* G) = H)
      (normalizerQuotientEquivMap H (MulEquiv.refl G) (normalizerQuotientMk H g)) =
      normalizerQuotientMk H g := by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_symm_mk
docstring: The inverse induced equivalence sends a target representative to the inverse-image representative.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_symm_mk (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K)
    (k : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer ((H.map (e : G →* K)) : Set K)) :
    (normalizerQuotientEquivMap H e).symm
        (normalizerQuotientMk (H.map (e : G →* K)) k) =
      normalizerQuotientMk H ((normalizerEquivMap H e).symm k) :=

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_symm_mk'
docstring: Transporting a representative of `H.map e` along `e.symm` gives the stated inverse-image representative in `(H.map e).map e.symm`.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_symm_mk' (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K)
    (k : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer ((H.map (e : G →* K)) : Set K)) :
    normalizerQuotientEquivMap (H.map (e : G →* K)) e.symm
        (normalizerQuotientMk (H.map (e : G →* K)) k) =
      normalizerQuotientMk ((H.map (e : G →* K)).map (e.symm : K →* G))
        (normalizerEquivMap (H.map (e : G →* K)) e.symm k) := by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_trans_mk
docstring: Composing two normalizer-quotient transports sends representatives through the two successive normalizer transports.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_trans_mk (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K) (f : K ≃* L)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientEquivMap (H.map (e : G →* K)) f
        (normalizerQuotientEquivMap H e (normalizerQuotientMk H g)) =
      normalizerQuotientMk ((H.map (e : G →* K)).map (f : K →* L))
        (normalizerEquivMap (H.map (e : G →* K)) f (normalizerEquivMap H e g)) := by

label: TauCeti.Subgroup.normalizerQuotientEquivMap_trans_mk_congr
docstring: After identifying the twice-mapped subgroup with the subgroup mapped by `e.trans f`, composing normalizer-quotient transports agrees with transport by the composite isomorphism on representatives.
code:
lemma normalizerQuotientEquivMap_trans_mk_congr (H : Subgroup G) (e : G ≃* K) (f : K ≃* L)
    (g : _root_.Subgroup.normalizer (H : Set G)) :
    normalizerQuotientCongr
        (by rw [_root_.Subgroup.map_map, ← MulEquiv.coe_monoidHom_trans] :
          (H.map (e : G →* K)).map (f : K →* L) =
            H.map ((e.trans f : G ≃* L) : G →* L))
      (normalizerQuotientEquivMap (H.map (e : G →* K)) f
        (normalizerQuotientEquivMap H e (normalizerQuotientMk H g))) =
      normalizerQuotientEquivMap H (e.trans f) (normalizerQuotientMk H g) := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm
docstring: The complex form associated to a pair `(ω, J)`: `h(v, w) = ω(v, J w) + i ω(v, w)`. Its real part is the metric `ω(·, J ·)` and its imaginary part is the symplectic form `ω`. The bare definition needs no hypotheses on `(ω, J)`; the Hermitian-structure facts are each proved under the weakest hypothesis they need: complex linearity in the second argument from `J² = -1` alone (`complexAssociatedForm_smul_right`), conjugate symmetry and conjugate-linearity in the first argument from `ω.Invariant J` (`Invariant.complexAssociatedForm_conj_symm`, `Invariant.complexAssociatedForm_smul_left`), and positive definiteness from `ω.Tames J` (`Tames.complexAssociatedForm_self_re_pos`).

noncomputable def complexAssociatedForm (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v w : V) : ℂ :=

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_add_left
docstring: The complex associated form is additive in its first argument.
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_add_left (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v₁ v₂ w : V) :
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J (v₁ + v₂) w =
      ω.complexAssociatedForm J v₁ w + ω.complexAssociatedForm J v₂ w := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_add_right
docstring: The complex associated form is additive in its second argument.
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_add_right (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v w₁ w₂ : V) :
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J v (w₁ + w₂) =
      ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w₁ + ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w₂ := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_apply
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_apply (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v w : V) :
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w = (ω v (J w) : ℂ) + Complex.I * (ω v w : ℂ) := rfl

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_im
docstring: The imaginary part of the complex associated form is the symplectic form `ω(v, w)`.
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_im (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v w : V) :
    (ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w).im = ω v w := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_re
docstring: The real part of the complex associated form is the metric `g(v, w) = ω(v, J w)`.

lemma complexAssociatedForm_re (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (v w : V) :
    (ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w).re = ω v (J w) := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_self
docstring: The diagonal of the complex associated form is real and equals the metric diagonal `ω(v, J v)`.
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_self (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V) (v : V) :
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J v v = (ω v (J v) : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_smul_right
docstring: The complex associated form is complex linear in its second argument over the complex structure `J.complexModule`: `h(v, z • w) = z · h(v, w)`. This is one of the defining properties of a Hermitian inner product on the complex vector space `(V, J)`, and needs only `J² = -1`, not compatibility.
code:
lemma complexAssociatedForm_smul_right (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (z : ℂ) (v w : V) :
    letI := J.complexModule
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J v (z • w) = z * ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w := by

label: TauCeti.SymplecticForm.complexAssociatedForm_smul_right_aux
docstring: Auxiliary real-scalar form of complex linearity in the second argument: feeding the real decomposition `r.re • w + r.im • J w` of `r • w` to the second slot multiplies by `r`. This needs only `J² = -1`, not compatibility.
code:
private lemma complexAssociatedForm_smul_right_aux
    (ω : SymplecticForm V) (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (r : ℂ) (v w : V) :
    ω.complexAssociatedForm J v (r.re • w + r.im • J w) =
      r * ω.complexAssociatedForm J v w := by

label: TauCeti.abs_le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_eq_mul_abs_le_frontier

    (hsol : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →

    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → |f x| ≤ M) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → |f x| ≤ M := by

lemma bilinForm_comp_almostComplexStructure {U V : Type*} [AddCommGroup U] [Module ℝ U]

    B ((F.comp J₀.toLinearMap) v) ((F.comp J₀.toLinearMap) (J₀ v)) = B (F v) (F (J₀ v)) := by

label: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis
docstring: A rectangle with a horizontal edge *on* the real axis — one of its imaginary coordinates is `0` — has a vanishing boundary integral. This is `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis` in the case where the axis meets an edge rather than being avoided outright: an endpoint at `0` still keeps `0` out of the *open* imaginary interior. It is the form applied to the two axis-bounded halves of a straddling rectangle.
code:
private lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hFcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hFdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω) (haxis : z.im = 0 ∨ w.im = 0) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_straddling
docstring: A rectangle that *straddles* the real axis — `0` lies strictly inside its imaginary range — has a vanishing boundary integral: split it at the axis into a lower and an upper half, each an axis-bounded rectangle handled by `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_edge_on_axis`, and recombine, the shared axis edge cancelling. Same hypotheses as `boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis`, but with `0` in the open imaginary interior instead of outside it.
code:
private lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_of_straddling {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hFcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hFdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω)
    (hstr : (0 : ℝ) ∈ Set.Ioo (min z.im w.im) (max z.im w.im)) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis
docstring: A rectangle whose open interior avoids the real axis has a vanishing boundary integral for any function continuous on a domain `Ω` containing the (closed) rectangle and holomorphic on the part of `Ω` off the real axis. This is the per-rectangle input to Morera's theorem; it is applied both to axis-avoiding rectangles directly and to the two axis-bounded halves of a straddling rectangle.
code:
private lemma boundaryIntegral_eq_zero_off_axis {Ω : Set ℂ} {F : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hFcont : ContinuousOn F Ω)
    (hFdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ F (Ω ∩ {z : ℂ | z.im ≠ 0}))
    {z w : ℂ} (hsub : Complex.Rectangle z w ⊆ Ω)
    (haxis : (0 : ℝ) ∉ Set.Ioo (min z.im w.im) (max z.im w.im)) :
    ((∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + z.im * I)) - (∫ x : ℝ in z.re..w.re, F (x + w.im * I)) +
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (w.re + y * I)) -
        I • (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..w.im, F (z.re + y * I))) = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.boundary_term_decay

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_dvd_card
docstring: The cardinality of the maximal elementary-2 quotient of a commutative group divides the group cardinality.

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion
docstring: **The maximal elementary-2 quotient and the 2-torsion subgroup have the same cardinality.** `|G/G²| = |{g | g² = 1}|`. The squaring endomorphism `g ↦ g²` has range `G²` and kernel the 2-torsion; when its kernel has finite index, the index of the range equals the cardinality of the kernel.
code:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion
    [(powMonoidHom 2 : G →* G).ker.FiniteIndex] :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = Nat.card {g : G // g ^ 2 = 1} := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_index_square
docstring: The cardinality of `G/G²` is the index of the subgroup of squares.
code:

    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = (Subgroup.square G).index := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank
docstring: The maximal elementary-2 quotient has cardinality `2 ^ twoRank`: it is a finite `𝔽₂`-vector space of dimension the 2-rank.
code:

    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = 2 ^ twoRank G := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_le_card
docstring: The maximal elementary-2 quotient of a finite commutative group has cardinality at most the group cardinality.

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_multiplicative
docstring: **A finite-rank free abelian group has `2 ^ rank` square classes.** For a free `ℤ`-module `A` of finite rank, the maximal elementary-2 quotient of `Multiplicative A` has cardinality `2 ^ finrank ℤ A`. This is Mathlib's `ModN.natCard_eq` transported along the identification of `Additive (Multiplicative A)` with `A`.
code:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_multiplicative :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient (Multiplicative A)) = 2 ^ Module.finrank ℤ A := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_isCyclic
docstring: **The elementary-2 quotient of a cyclic group has `gcd |G| 2` elements.** For the finite case the subgroup of squares has index `gcd |G| 2` (Mathlib's `IsCyclic.index_powMonoidHom_range`, read through `G² = range (powMonoidHom 2)`); the infinite case is `G ≃* Multiplicative ℤ`, whose elementary-2 quotient is `2 ^ finrank ℤ ℤ = 2 = gcd 0 2`.
code:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_isCyclic :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = (Nat.card G).gcd 2 := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_isCyclic_of_even
docstring: A cyclic group of even order has exactly two square classes.
code:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_isCyclic_of_even (h : Even (Nat.card G)) :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = 2 := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_odd_card
docstring: **A group of odd order has a single square class.** For a finite commutative group of odd order, squaring is bijective (the exponent `2` is coprime to `|G|`), so `G/G²` is trivial. This is the odd-order half of the 2-rank computation — the even case genuinely needs more structure (a cyclic factor); this half holds for any commutative group.
code:
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_of_odd_card (h : Odd (Nat.card G)) :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient G) = 1 := by

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_pi
docstring: The cardinality reading of `TauCeti.elementaryTwoQuotientPiLinearEquiv`: `|(∀ i, G i)/(…)²| = ∏ i, |(G i)/(G i)²|`.

    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient (∀ i, G i)) =

label: TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_prod
docstring: The cardinality reading of `TauCeti.elementaryTwoQuotientProdLinearEquiv`: `|(G × H)/(G × H)²| = |G/G²| · |H/H²|`.

    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient (G × H)) =

label: TauCeti.card_nonempty_finset
docstring: **The number of nonempty subsets of a finite type is `2ⁿ - 1`.** The `2ⁿ` subsets of an `n`-element type are the nonempty ones together with the empty set, so the nonempty ones number `2ⁿ - 1`.

theorem card_nonempty_finset {ι : Type*} [Finite ι] :
    Nat.card {S : Finset ι // S.Nonempty} = 2 ^ Nat.card ι - 1 := by

label: TauCeti.chafaiDensity

label: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_ge_const_on_Icc
docstring: Pointwise lower bound for the density on `Icc (T/2) T`: at each such point `t`, `chafaiDensity f k` is at least the constant `(1/(k-1)!)·(T/2)^(k-1)·h T`.
code:
private lemma chafaiDensity_ge_const_on_Icc (f : ℝ → ℝ) (k : ℕ) (h : ℝ → ℝ)
    (T : ℝ) (hhT_nonneg : 0 ≤ h T) {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Icc (T / 2) T) (hT_le_ht : h T ≤ h t)
    (h_density_eq_t :
      chafaiDensity f k t = (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * t ^ (k - 1) * h t) :
    (1 / ↑((k - 1).factorial)) * (T / 2) ^ (k - 1) * h T ≤ chafaiDensity f k t := by

label: TauCeti.chafaiDensity_ibp_identity
docstring: **IBP identity** for the CM density: `∫₀ᵀ ρ_{m+2}(t) dt = B_{m+2}(T) + ∫₀ᵀ ρ_{m+1}(t) dt`.

private lemma chafaiDensity_ibp_identity (f : ℝ → ℝ) {m : ℕ}
    (hf : ContDiffOn ℝ ((m + 2 : ℕ) : WithTop ℕ∞) f (Ici 0)) (T : ℝ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f (m + 2) t =
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (m + 2) * T ^ (m + 1) / ↑(m + 1).factorial *
      iteratedDerivWithin (m + 1) f (Ici 0) T +
    ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..T, chafaiDensity f (m + 1) t := by

            iteratedDerivWithin (m + 1) f (Ici 0) t) +

            iteratedDerivWithin (m + 2) f (Ici 0) t) := by

label: TauCeti.chafai_repeated_ibp
docstring: **Repeated integration by parts for a completely monotone function.** For `n ≥ 1`, `0 ≤ x` and `f` tending to `L` at infinity, integrating the order-`n` kernel `(-1) ^ n / (n - 1)! * (t - x) ^ (n - 1)` against the `n`-th derivative of `f` over `(x, ∞)` recovers `f x - L`. This is the analytic identity behind the Chafaï reconstruction of `f` from its derivatives.
code:
private lemma chafai_repeated_ibp (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x)
    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ n / ↑(n - 1).factorial *
      (t - x) ^ (n - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin n f (Ici 0) t = f x - L := by

label: TauCeti.chafai_repeated_ibp_succ
docstring: For a completely monotone `f` with limit `L` at infinity, `0 ≤ x` and `k ≠ 0`, the order-`k` kernel identity implies the order-`k + 1` one: if the order-`k` kernel integrates against the `k`-th derivative to `f x - L` on `(x, ∞)`, then so does the order-`k + 1` kernel against the `(k + 1)`-st derivative.
code:
private lemma chafai_repeated_ibp_succ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L))
    (ih : ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t = f x - L) :
    ∫ t in Ioi x, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (t - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) f (Ici 0) t = f x - L := by

label: TauCeti.charFun_sum_mul_conj_eq_integral

label: TauCeti.complexLinearMapEquiv
docstring: The morphism-level form of the dictionary between almost complex structures and complex module structures: real-linear maps intertwining `J` and `J'` are in bijection with `ℂ`-linear maps for the induced complex module structures `J.complexModule` and `J'.complexModule`.

@[expose] noncomputable def complexLinearMapEquiv (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (J' : AlmostComplexStructure W) :
    letI := J.complexModule
    letI := J'.complexModule

    (J' : AlmostComplexStructure W)
    (Fc : letI := J.complexModule; letI := J'.complexModule;
      {F : V →ₗ[ℝ] W // IsComplexLinearMap J J' F}) (v : V) :
    letI := J.complexModule
    letI := J'.complexModule
    complexLinearMapEquiv J J' Fc v = (Fc : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) v :=

label: TauCeti.complexLinearMapEquiv_symm_apply
code:
theorem complexLinearMapEquiv_symm_apply (J : AlmostComplexStructure V)
    (J' : AlmostComplexStructure W)
    (G : letI := J.complexModule; letI := J'.complexModule; V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (v : V) :
    letI := J.complexModule
    letI := J'.complexModule
    letI := J.complexModule_isScalarTower
    letI := J'.complexModule_isScalarTower
    ((complexLinearMapEquiv J J').symm G : V →ₗ[ℝ] W) v = G v :=

label: TauCeti.finite_measure_cluster_limit
docstring: A tight, uniformly mass-bounded sequence of finite measures has a weak cluster limit. Given tightness of the sequence and a common total-mass bound, the conclusion is a finite limiting measure with the same mass bound and weak convergence of all bounded-continuous test-function integrals along an ultrafilter `U ≤ atTop`; no first-countability assumption on `FiniteMeasure α` is needed.
code:
lemma finite_measure_cluster_limit
    (σ : ℕ → Measure α) (C : ℝ≥0)
    (hmass : ∀ n, (σ n) univ ≤ (C : ENNReal))
    (hTight : IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range σ)) :
    ∃ (μ₀ : Measure α) (U : Ultrafilter ℕ), (U : Filter ℕ) ≤ atTop ∧ IsFiniteMeasure μ₀ ∧
      μ₀ univ ≤ (C : ENNReal) ∧
      ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction α ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun n => ∫ x, g x ∂(σ n)) (U : Filter ℕ)
          (nhds (∫ x, g x ∂μ₀)) := by

lemma finite_measure_subseq_limit
    [FirstCountableTopology (FiniteMeasure α)]
    (σ : ℕ → Measure α) (C : ℝ≥0)
    (hmass : ∀ n, (σ n) univ ≤ (C : ENNReal))
    (hTight : IsTightMeasureSet (Set.range σ)) :
    ∃ (μ₀ : Measure α) (φ : ℕ → ℕ), IsFiniteMeasure μ₀ ∧ StrictMono φ ∧
      μ₀ univ ≤ (C : ENNReal) ∧
      ∀ g : BoundedContinuousFunction α ℝ,
        Tendsto (fun k => ∫ x, g x ∂(σ (φ k))) atTop
          (nhds (∫ x, g x ∂μ₀)) := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_cexp_quadratic
docstring: Derivative of the entire function `z ↦ exp (x·z - z²/2)`: its value at `z` times `x - z`.

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_deriv_hermiteFunction
docstring: **Second derivative of the Hermite function** (the derivative form). The Hermite function `ψₙ` solves `ψₙ'' = (x² - (2n+1))·ψₙ`; this states that the derivative of `ψₙ'` at `x` equals `(x² - (2n+1))·ψₙ(x)`.
code:
theorem hasDerivAt_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (deriv (hermiteFunction n))
      ((x ^ 2 - (2 * n + 1)) * hermiteFunction n x) x := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_halfLinePrimitive
docstring: If `f` is continuous on `[0, ∞)`, then `halfLinePrimitive f` has derivative `f t` at every `t ≥ 0`. The `max` extension of the integrand makes the derivative at `t = 0` two-sided.
code:
theorem hasDerivAt_halfLinePrimitive (hf : ContinuousOn f (Ici 0)) (ht : 0 ≤ t) :
    HasDerivAt (halfLinePrimitive f) (f t) t := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction
docstring: **Target A2 (derivative ladder relation).** Differentiating `ψₙ` mixes the neighbouring modes: `ψₙ' = √(n/2)·ψ_{n-1} - √((n+1)/2)·ψ_{n+1}`.
code:
theorem hasDerivAt_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (hermiteFunction n)
      (Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x
        - Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x) x := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg
docstring: At a point in the open lower half-plane, the derivative of the Schwarz-reflection extension is the conjugate of the derivative of `f` at the conjugate point.
code:
lemma hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_neg {z f' : ℂ} (hz : z.im < 0)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f f' ((starRingEnd ℂ) z)) :
    HasDerivAt (schwarzReflection f) ((starRingEnd ℂ) f') z := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos
docstring: At a point in the open upper half-plane, the Schwarz-reflection extension has the same derivative as the original function.
code:
lemma hasDerivAt_schwarzReflection_of_im_pos {z f' : ℂ} (hz : 0 < z.im)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f f' z) :
    HasDerivAt (schwarzReflection f) f' z :=

label: TauCeti.hasDerivAt_unitDiscMoebiusFormula
docstring: The complex derivative of the scalar unit-disc Moebius factor `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` at a point `p` where the denominator is nonzero. Its value at `p = 0` (with center `-z`) is `1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2`, and at `p = a` it is `1 / (1 - ‖a‖ ^ 2)`, the two factors that appear in the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick estimate.
code:
lemma hasDerivAt_unitDiscMoebiusFormula (a p : ℂ)
    (hp : 1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * p ≠ 0) :
    HasDerivAt (fun z : ℂ => (z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))
      ((1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * p) ^ 2) p := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivWithinAt_Iio_of_tendsto_deriv
docstring: A function continuous at `t₀`, eventually differentiable on the left, whose derivative tends to `L` from the left, has left derivative `L` at `t₀`.

theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Iio_of_tendsto_deriv {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : E}

    HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Iio t₀) t₀ := by

label: TauCeti.hasDerivWithinAt_Ioi_of_tendsto_deriv
docstring: A function continuous at `t₀`, eventually differentiable on the right, whose derivative tends to `L` from the right, has right derivative `L` at `t₀`.
code:
theorem hasDerivWithinAt_Ioi_of_tendsto_deriv {γ : ℝ → E} {t₀ : ℝ} {L : E}

    (hγ_diff : ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝[>] t₀, DifferentiableAt ℝ γ t)

    HasDerivWithinAt γ L (Ioi t₀) t₀ := by

label: TauCeti.hasFDerivAt_exp_inner
docstring: The exponential barrier `y ↦ exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)` has derivative `exp (α ⟪u, x⟫) • (α • ⟪u, ·⟫)`. This is the shared first-derivative computation feeding both `laplacian_exp_inner` and `fderiv_exp_inner_apply`.

label: TauCeti.hasSum_hermite_generating_function
docstring: **Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials, summable form.** For all complex `x` and `t`, the family `Hₙ(x) · tⁿ / n!` is summable with sum `exp (x · t - t² / 2)`, where `Hₙ = Polynomial.hermite n`. This is the analytic heart of the identity: it carries the summability that the `tsum` form `hermite_generating_function` discards, and it holds over all of `ℂ` (the real case is a specialization by casting).
code:
theorem hasSum_hermite_generating_function (x t : ℂ) :
    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => aeval x (hermite n) * t ^ n / (n.factorial : ℂ))
      (Complex.exp (x * t - t ^ 2 / 2)) := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction
docstring: The real Hermite function `ψₙ(x) = Hₙ(x√2) exp(-x² / 2) / sqrt(n! sqrt π)`, using Mathlib's probabilists' Hermite polynomial `Polynomial.hermite`.
code: noncomputable def hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunctionLp
docstring: The `n`th Hermite function as a vector of `L²(ℝ, volume; 𝕜)`, with the real pointwise function cast through `algebraMap ℝ 𝕜`.
code:
noncomputable def hermiteFunctionLp (𝕜 : Type*) [RCLike 𝕜] (n : ℕ) :
    Lp 𝕜 2 (volume : Measure ℝ) :=

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_def
docstring: The defining equation for the real Hermite function.
code:
lemma hermiteFunction_def (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction n x =
      aeval (x * Real.sqrt 2) (hermite n) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) /
        Real.sqrt ((n.factorial : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi) :=

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_neg
docstring: **Target A2 (parity).** `ψₙ(-x) = (-1)ⁿ ψₙ(x)`: the Gaussian envelope `exp(-x²/2)` is even and the polynomial factor `Hₙ(x√2)` carries the parity of `Hₙ` (`Polynomial.hermite_aeval_neg`).
code:
theorem hermiteFunction_neg (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction n (-x) = (-1) ^ n * hermiteFunction n x := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_one
docstring: The first Hermite function is `sqrt 2 * x` times the zeroth Hermite function.
code:
lemma hermiteFunction_one (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 1 x = Real.sqrt 2 * x * hermiteFunction 0 x := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_one_eq
docstring: The first Hermite function as an explicit scalar multiple of the Gaussian envelope.
code:
lemma hermiteFunction_one_eq (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 1 x =
      Real.sqrt 2 * x * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi) := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_oscillator
docstring: **The harmonic-oscillator eigen-equation.** The Hermite function `ψₙ` is an eigenfunction of the Schrödinger operator `-d²/dx² + x²` with eigenvalue `2n+1`: `-ψₙ'' + x²·ψₙ = (2n+1)·ψₙ`.
code:
theorem hermiteFunction_oscillator (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    -deriv (deriv (hermiteFunction n)) x + x ^ 2 * hermiteFunction n x
      = (2 * n + 1) * hermiteFunction n x := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_two
docstring: The second Hermite function in pointwise form.
code:
lemma hermiteFunction_two (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 2 x =
      ((x * Real.sqrt 2) ^ 2 - 1) * Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) /
        Real.sqrt ((2 : ℝ) * Real.sqrt Real.pi) := by

label: TauCeti.hermiteFunction_zero
docstring: The zeroth Hermite function is the Gaussian divided by `sqrt (sqrt π)`.
code:
lemma hermiteFunction_zero (x : ℝ) :
    hermiteFunction 0 x = Real.exp (-(x ^ 2 / 2)) / Real.sqrt (Real.sqrt Real.pi) := by

label: TauCeti.hermite_generating_function
docstring: **Exponential generating function of the probabilists' Hermite polynomials.** For all real `x` and `t`, `∑' n, Hₙ(x) · tⁿ / n! = exp (x · t - t² / 2)`, where `Hₙ = Polynomial.hermite n`. This is target **A1** of the `OrthogonalL2Bases` roadmap; it is the real specialization of `hasSum_hermite_generating_function`.
code:
theorem hermite_generating_function (x t : ℝ) :
    ∑' n : ℕ, aeval x (hermite n) * t ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)
      = Real.exp (x * t - t ^ 2 / 2) := by

label: TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfOrthogonalSystem
docstring: **The `√w`-envelope basis of `L²(μ)`.** The `weightL2Isometry`-image (multiplication by `√w`) of the weighted-measure basis; the `√w`-normalized functions `fₙ·√w/√cₙ` form a Hilbert basis of the reference measure `L²(μ)`, obtained with no separate proof.
code:
noncomputable def hilbertBasisOfOrthogonalSystem {μ : Measure α}
    (hwpos : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 < w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) (hc : ∀ n, 0 < c n)
    (horth : ∀ m n, (∫ x, f m x * f n x * w x ∂μ) = if m = n then c n else 0)
    (hmem : ∀ n, MemLp (fun x => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (f n x / Real.sqrt (c n))) 2
      (μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))))
    (hcomplete :
      (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (bareNormalizedLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) f w c hmem)))ᗮ = ⊥) :
    HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 μ) :=

label: TauCeti.hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure
docstring: **The weighted-measure basis.** The normalized bare functions, orthonormal by the orthogonality relation and complete by hypothesis, form a Hilbert basis of `L²(w·μ)` — the textbook statement that a family of orthogonal functions is an orthonormal basis of its own weighted `L²` space.
code:
noncomputable def hilbertBasisOfWeightedMeasure {μ : Measure α}
    (hwnn : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) (hc : ∀ n, 0 < c n)
    (horth : ∀ m n, (∫ x, f m x * f n x * w x ∂μ) = if m = n then c n else 0)
    (hmem : ∀ n, MemLp (fun x => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (f n x / Real.sqrt (c n))) 2
      (μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x))))
    (hcomplete :
      (Submodule.span 𝕜 (Set.range (bareNormalizedLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) f w c hmem)))ᗮ = ⊥) :
    HilbertBasis ℕ 𝕜 (Lp 𝕜 2 (μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))) :=

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist
docstring: The hyperbolic (Poincaré) distance on the complex unit disc, written as a total real-valued function `Real.artanh p` of the pseudo-hyperbolic expression `p = pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w`. On the open unit disc this is the hyperbolic distance, normalised to agree with the infinitesimal Poincaré metric `|dz| / (1 - |z| ^ 2)`. Outside the disc, where `p` may reach or exceed one, the formula remains a total Lean expression with no geometric meaning.
code: noncomputable def hyperbolicDist (z w : ℂ) : ℝ :=

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_comm
docstring: The hyperbolic distance is symmetric.
code: lemma hyperbolicDist_comm (z w : ℂ) : hyperbolicDist z w = hyperbolicDist w z := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_def
docstring: The defining formula for the hyperbolic distance.
code:
lemma hyperbolicDist_def (z w : ℂ) :
    hyperbolicDist z w = Real.artanh (pseudoHyperbolicExpr z w) := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_eq_zero_iff_of_mem_ball
docstring: On the open unit disc the hyperbolic distance vanishes exactly on the diagonal.

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le
docstring: **Schwarz--Pick, distance form.** A holomorphic self-map of the complex unit disc does not increase the hyperbolic distance.
code:
theorem hyperbolicDist_map_le {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    {z w : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (hw : w ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    hyperbolicDist (f z) (f w) ≤ hyperbolicDist z w := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_map_le_unitDisc
docstring: Bundled unit-disc form of Schwarz--Pick in distance form.
code:
theorem hyperbolicDist_map_le_unitDisc {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (f z) (f w) ≤ hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ) :=

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_nonneg
docstring: The hyperbolic distance is nonnegative.
code: lemma hyperbolicDist_nonneg (z w : ℂ) : 0 ≤ hyperbolicDist z w := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_self
docstring: The hyperbolic distance from a point to itself is zero.
code: lemma hyperbolicDist_self (z : ℂ) : hyperbolicDist z z = 0 := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle
docstring: **Hyperbolic triangle inequality.** The hyperbolic (Poincaré) distance on the complex open unit disc satisfies `hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z u + hyperbolicDist u w`.

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle_unitDisc
docstring: **Hyperbolic triangle inequality (bundled unit-disc form).** `hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z u + hyperbolicDist u w`, proved by sending the middle point `u` to the origin with the Moebius isometry `unitDiscMoebius u`.
code:
theorem hyperbolicDist_triangle_unitDisc (u z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ)
      ≤ hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (u : ℂ) + hyperbolicDist (u : ℂ) (w : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_triangle_zero
docstring: **Hyperbolic triangle inequality against the origin.** For two points of the open unit disc, `hyperbolicDist z w ≤ hyperbolicDist z 0 + hyperbolicDist 0 w`.

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_unitDiscMoebius
docstring: The disc Moebius factor `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a hyperbolic isometry.
code:
theorem hyperbolicDist_unitDiscMoebius (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))
        (((w : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (w : ℂ)))
      = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
docstring: Every standard disc automorphism `z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` is a hyperbolic isometry.
code:
theorem hyperbolicDist_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv
    (u : Circle) (a z w : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    hyperbolicDist (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a z : ℂ)
        (unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a w : ℂ)
      = hyperbolicDist (z : ℂ) (w : ℂ) := by

label: TauCeti.hyperbolicDist_zero_right
docstring: The hyperbolic distance from a point of the disc to the origin has the closed form `artanh ‖z‖`.
code:
lemma hyperbolicDist_zero_right (z : ℂ) :
    hyperbolicDist z 0 = Real.artanh ‖z‖ := by

label: TauCeti.ibp_finite_interval
code:
private lemma ibp_finite_interval (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)
    (k : ℕ) (hk : k ≠ 0) (x T : ℝ) (hx : 0 ≤ x) (hxT : x < T) :
    ∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (t - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin (k + 1) f (Ici 0) t =
    (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑k.factorial * (T - x) ^ k *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) T -
    ∫ t in x..T, (-1 : ℝ) ^ (k + 1) / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t := by

private lemma ibp_kernel_integrableOn (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hcm : IsCompletelyMonotone f)

    (L : ℝ) (hL : Tendsto f atTop (nhds L)) :
    IntegrableOn (fun t => (-1 : ℝ) ^ k / ↑(k - 1).factorial * (t - x) ^ (k - 1) *
      iteratedDerivWithin k f (Ici 0) t) (Ioi x) := by

label: TauCeti.index_powMonoidHom_range_le_of_closure_eq_top
docstring: In a commutative group generated by a finite set `S`, the range of `powMonoidHom n` has index at most `n ^ S.card` when `n` is nonzero. This applies Mathlib's exponent/rank cardinality bound to the quotient by the `n`th powers. The public surface of this file is the squaring specialization `index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top`; this arbitrary-power form is the shared engine behind it.
code:
private theorem index_powMonoidHom_range_le_of_closure_eq_top {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
    {S : Finset G} {n : ℕ} (hn : n ≠ 0) (hS : Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = ⊤) :
    (powMonoidHom n : G →* G).range.index ≤ n ^ S.card := by

label: TauCeti.index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top
docstring: In a commutative group generated by a finite set `S`, the subgroup of squares has index at most `2 ^ S.card`. The quotient by the squares is an elementary abelian `2`-group spanned by the image of `S`.
code:
theorem index_square_le_of_closure_eq_top {G : Type*} [CommGroup G]
    {S : Finset G} (hS : Subgroup.closure (S : Set G) = ⊤) :
    (Subgroup.square G).index ≤ 2 ^ S.card := by

label: TauCeti.inner_L2prodMul
docstring: **The tensor inner-product identity.** The inner product of two pointwise-product vectors in `L²(μ ⊗ ν)` factors as the product of the inner products of the factors.
code:
theorem inner_L2prodMul [SFinite μ] [SFinite ν] (F₁ F₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 μ) (G₁ G₂ : Lp 𝕜 2 ν) :
    inner 𝕜 (L2prodMul F₁ G₁) (L2prodMul F₂ G₂) = inner 𝕜 F₁ F₂ * inner 𝕜 G₁ G₂ := by

label: TauCeti.inner_algebraMap_algebraMap
docstring: The inner product of two real scalar casts is the scalar cast of their product.

lemma inner_algebraMap_algebraMap (a b : ℝ) :
    inner 𝕜 ((algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) a) ((algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) b) =
      (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (a * b) := by

label: TauCeti.inner_bareNormalizedLp
docstring: The normalized bare functions have Kronecker-delta inner products in `L²(w·μ)`.
code:
theorem inner_bareNormalizedLp {μ : Measure α}
    (hwnn : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, 0 ≤ w x) (hwm : AEMeasurable w μ) (hc : ∀ n, 0 < c n)
    (horth : ∀ m n, (∫ x, f m x * f n x * w x ∂μ) = if m = n then c n else 0)
    (hmem : ∀ n, MemLp (fun x => (algebraMap ℝ 𝕜) (f n x / Real.sqrt (c n))) 2
      (μ.withDensity (fun x => ENNReal.ofReal (w x)))) (m n : ℕ) :
    inner 𝕜 (bareNormalizedLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) f w c hmem m) (bareNormalizedLp (𝕜 := 𝕜) f w c hmem n)
      = if m = n then 1 else 0 := by

label: TauCeti.inner_hermiteFunctionLp
docstring: **Target A3 (orthonormality, inner-product form).** The `Lp` Hermite vectors satisfy `⟪ψₘ, ψₙ⟫ = if m = n then 1 else 0`, over any `RCLike` scalar field, by evaluating the `L²` inner product as the pointwise integral `integral_hermiteFunction_mul_hermiteFunction`.
code:
theorem inner_hermiteFunctionLp (m n : ℕ) :
    inner 𝕜 (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 m) (hermiteFunctionLp 𝕜 n) = if m = n then (1 : 𝕜) else 0 := by

label: TauCeti.inner_hermiteFunctionLp_zero_zero
docstring: The zeroth `Lp` Hermite function has inner product one with itself, over any `RCLike` scalar field.
code:
lemma inner_hermiteFunctionLp_zero_zero :

label: TauCeti.laplacian_exp_inner
docstring: **The Laplacian of the exponential barrier.** For a fixed vector `u`, the function `y ↦ exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)` has Laplacian `α² ‖u‖² exp (α ⟪u, y⟫)`, because it is an exponential of a linear form: the second directional derivative along an orthonormal basis vector `eᵢ` contributes `α² ⟪u, eᵢ⟫²`, and these sum to `α² ‖u‖²`. This is the barrier for the weak maximum principle with drift.

      = α ^ 2 * ‖u‖ ^ 2 * Real.exp (α * ⟪u, x⟫) := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_forall_pos_exists_isMaxOn_perturbation
docstring: **The `ε → 0` perturbation engine of the weak maximum principles.** To bound `f x ≤ m` on a bounded set `K`, it suffices to produce, for every `ε > 0`, a point `z ∈ K` at which the perturbation `f + ε‖·‖²` attains its maximum over `K` and where `f z ≤ m`: bounding `‖·‖²` by a constant on the bounded `K` and letting `ε → 0` then gives `f x ≤ m`. The bare-Laplacian and `-Δ + c` weak maximum principles differ only in how they produce such a maximizer, so this lemma packages everything they share.
code:
theorem le_of_forall_pos_exists_isMaxOn_perturbation {K : Set E} (hK : Bornology.IsBounded K)
    {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ} {x : E} (hxK : x ∈ K)
    (H : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ z ∈ K, IsMaxOn (fun y : E => f y + ε • ‖y‖ ^ 2) K z ∧ f z ≤ m) :
    f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_forall_pos_mul_le
docstring: The `ε → 0` limit of a perturbation estimate: if `a ≤ m + ε * C` for every `ε > 0`, with a nonnegative constant `C`, then `a ≤ m`. This packages the endgame of the perturbation arguments in the weak maximum principles.
code:
theorem le_of_forall_pos_mul_le {a m C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (h : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → a ≤ m + ε * C) :
    a ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_of_le_frontier
docstring: **Comparison principle for `Δ + b·∇`.** Two functions acted on by the same bounded drift are ordered on a compact set if their operator values and frontier values are ordered.
code:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_of_le_frontier {K : Set E}
    (hK : IsCompact K) {f g : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β : ℝ}
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x) ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg_le_frontier
docstring: **Weak maximum principle for `Δ + b·∇` with bounded drift.** Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, the drift field is bounded there (`‖b x‖ ≤ β`), and `0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)` (a subsolution of `Δ + b·∇`), then any bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`.
code:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_nonneg_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_of_le_frontier
docstring: **Comparison principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.** Functions acted on by the same lower-order coefficients are ordered on a compact set when their operator values and frontier values are ordered.
code:
theorem le_of_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_sub_mul_of_le_frontier
    {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {c f g : E → ℝ}
    {b : E → E} {β : ℝ} (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hL : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K →
      Δ g x + fderiv ℝ g x (b x) - c x * g x ≤
        Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x) - c x * f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier
docstring: **Comparison principle for the Laplacian.** Let `K` be compact, and let `f`, `g` be continuous on `K` and `C²` on `interior K`. If `f` is at least as subharmonic as `g` there (`Δ g ≤ Δ f`) and `f ≤ g` on `frontier K`, then `f ≤ g` on all of `K`. This is the two-function form of the weak maximum principle `le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier`, applied to the difference `f - g`.
code:
theorem le_of_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier (hK : IsCompact K)
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ g x ≤ Δ f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier
docstring: **Weak maximum principle for subharmonic functions.** Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, and is subharmonic there (`0 ≤ Δ f`), then any bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`.
code:
theorem le_of_laplacian_nonneg_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x) (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_frontier
docstring: **Weak maximum principle for `-Δ - b·∇ + c`.** If `c` is nonnegative, `b` has norm at most `β` on the interior of a compact set, and `c x * f x ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x)`, then every nonnegative frontier bound for `f` is a bound on the whole set.
code:
theorem le_of_mul_le_laplacian_add_fderiv_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {c f : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {β m : ℝ} (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hb : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ‖b x‖ ≤ β)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → c x * f x ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_frontier
docstring: **Weak maximum principle for the operator `-Δ + c` with `c ≥ 0`.** Let `K` be compact. If `f` is continuous on `K`, is `C²` on `interior K`, and is a subsolution of `-Δ + c` there (`c x * f x ≤ Δ f x`) with a nonnegative coefficient (`0 ≤ c x`), then any **nonnegative** bound `m` that `f` respects on `frontier K` bounds `f` on all of `K`. The nonnegativity of `m` cannot be dropped once `c ≠ 0`; it encodes the `sup u ≤ sup_{∂} u⁺` shape of the estimate.
code:
theorem le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {c f : E → ℝ} {m : ℝ}
    (hm : 0 ≤ m) (hcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → c x * f x ≤ Δ f x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier
docstring: **Comparison principle for `-Δ + c` with `c ≥ 0`.** Let `K` be compact and let `f`, `g` be continuous on `K` and `C²` on `interior K`, with a nonnegative coefficient `c` there. If `f` is a subsolution and `g` a supersolution of `-Δ + c` (`c · f ≤ Δ f` and `Δ g ≤ c · g`) and `f ≤ g` on `frontier K`, then `f ≤ g` on all of `K`. This is the two-function form of `le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_frontier`.
code:
theorem le_of_mul_le_laplacian_le_of_le_frontier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K) {c f g : E → ℝ}
    (hfcont : ContinuousOn f K) (hgcont : ContinuousOn g K)
    (hfcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hgcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 g x)
    (hc : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ c x)
    (hsub : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → c x * f x ≤ Δ f x)
    (hsuper : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → Δ g x ≤ c x * g x)
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ g x) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ g x := by

label: TauCeti.le_of_strict_subsolution_barrier
docstring: **Weak maximum principle via a strict-subsolution barrier.** Let `K` be compact and `f` continuous on `K` and `C²` on `interior K`. If `f` is a subsolution of `Δ + b·∇` there (`0 ≤ Δ f + fderiv ℝ f (b)`) that is bounded by `m` on `frontier K`, and `w` is a barrier — continuous on `K` and a `C²` *strict* subsolution on `interior K` (`0 < Δ w + fderiv ℝ w (b)`) — then `f ≤ m` throughout `K`.
code:
private theorem le_of_strict_subsolution_barrier {K : Set E} (hK : IsCompact K)
    {f w : E → ℝ} {b : E → E} {m : ℝ} (hcont : ContinuousOn f K)
    (hcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 f x)
    (hlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 ≤ Δ f x + fderiv ℝ f x (b x))
    (hbdry : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ frontier K → f x ≤ m)
    (hwcont : ContinuousOn w K) (hwcd : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → ContDiffAt ℝ 2 w x)
    (hwlap : ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ interior K → 0 < Δ w x + fderiv ℝ w x (b x)) :
    ∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ K → f x ≤ m := by

label: TauCeti.linearIndependent_squareClass_iff
docstring: **Square-class independence is `ZMod 2`-linear independence.** For a finite family of units `d : ι → Kˣ`, the square classes `squareClass (d i)` are `ZMod 2`-linearly independent in the square-class group iff no nonempty subset product `∏_{i ∈ S} d i` is a square. label: TauCeti.mul_add_deriv_hermiteFunction
docstring: **Annihilation identity.** The combination `x·ψₙ + ψₙ' = √(2n)·ψ_{n-1}`; this is the ladder operator `a = (x + d/dx)/√2` acting as `a ψₙ = √n·ψ_{n-1}`.

theorem mul_add_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x + deriv (hermiteFunction n) x
      = Real.sqrt (2 * (n : ℝ)) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x := by

label: TauCeti.mul_hermiteFunction
docstring: **Target A2 (position ladder relation).** Multiplying `ψₙ` by `x` mixes the neighbouring modes: `x·ψₙ = √((n+1)/2)·ψ_{n+1} + √(n/2)·ψ_{n-1}`.

theorem mul_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x =
      Real.sqrt (((n : ℝ) + 1) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x
        + Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) / 2) * hermiteFunction (n - 1) x := by

label: TauCeti.mul_sub_deriv_hermiteFunction
docstring: **Creation identity.** The combination `x·ψₙ - ψₙ' = √(2(n+1))·ψ_{n+1}`; this is the ladder operator `a† = (x - d/dx)/√2` acting as `a† ψₙ = √(n+1)·ψ_{n+1}`.
code:
theorem mul_sub_deriv_hermiteFunction (n : ℕ) (x : ℝ) :
    x * hermiteFunction n x - deriv (hermiteFunction n) x
      = Real.sqrt (2 * ((n : ℝ) + 1)) * hermiteFunction (n + 1) x := by

label: TauCeti.normSq_one_sub_conj_mul_sub_normSq_sub
TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le
docstring: **The infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality.** A holomorphic self-map `f` of the open unit disc contracts the Poincaré metric: at every point `z` of the disc, `‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)`.

theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1) :
    ‖deriv f z‖ / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) := by

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le_unitDisc
docstring: Bundled unit-disc form of the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality: a holomorphic self-map `f` of the open unit disc contracts the Poincaré metric at every disc point `z`.
code:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le_unitDisc {f : ℂ → ℂ}
    (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (hmaps : MapsTo f (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) (ball (0 : ℂ) 1))
    (z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖deriv f (z : ℂ)‖ / (1 - ‖f (z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2) ≤ 1 / (1 - ‖(z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2) :=

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one
docstring: **The Moebius factor is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric.** For `‖a‖ < 1` the disc automorphism `z ↦ (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` attains equality in the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality `norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_le`: at every point of the open unit disc its Poincaré metric distortion is exactly `1`. This is the `u = 1` (no rotation) case of `norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one`.
code:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscMoebiusFormula_of_norm_lt_one {a : ℂ}
    (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => (ξ - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * ξ)) z‖
        / (1 - ‖(z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) := by

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
docstring: **The standard disc automorphism is an infinitesimal isometry of the Poincaré metric.** For a rotation factor `u` of norm `1` and `‖a‖ < 1` the automorphism `z ↦ u * (z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` attains equality in the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick inequality at every disc point: its Poincaré metric distortion is exactly `1`. The rotation factor `u` does not change the distortion.
code:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_of_norm_lt_one
    {u : ℂ} (hu : ‖u‖ = 1) {a : ℂ} (ha : ‖a‖ < 1) {z : ℂ} (hz : ‖z‖ < 1) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => u * ((ξ - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * ξ))) z‖
        / (1 - ‖u * ((z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z))‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) := by

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_unitDisc
docstring: Bundled unit-disc form of the automorphism Poincaré-isometry: for disc points `a z` the standard automorphism formula centred at `a` has Poincaré metric distortion exactly `1` at `z`.
code:
theorem norm_deriv_div_one_sub_norm_sq_unitDiscStandardAutomorphismFormula_unitDisc
    (u : Circle) (a z : Complex.UnitDisc) :
    ‖deriv (fun ξ : ℂ => (u : ℂ) * (((ξ : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) /
          (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * ξ))) (z : ℂ)‖
        / (1 - ‖(u : ℂ) * (((z : ℂ) - (a : ℂ)) /
          (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (a : ℂ) * (z : ℂ)))‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖(z : ℂ)‖ ^ 2) :=

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_norm_le
docstring: **Cauchy's estimate on a closed ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing `closedBall c r` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f c‖ ≤ M / r`. This is Mathlib's `Complex.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_sphere_norm_le` with its `DiffContOnCl` hypothesis and its bound on the boundary circle both supplied from a sup bound on a closed ball inside the domain of holomorphy, which is the form the family estimates below consume.

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le
docstring: **Cauchy's estimate, uniformly on a ball.** If `f` is holomorphic on an open set `U` containing `closedBall c (2 * r)` and `‖f‖ ≤ M` on that closed ball, then `‖deriv f z‖ ≤ M / r` at *every* point `z` of `ball c r`, not just at the centre. Halving the radius is what leaves room to recentre `norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_norm_le` at an arbitrary `z ∈ ball c r`: the ball `closedBall z r` is still inside `closedBall c (2 * r)`.
code:
theorem norm_deriv_le_of_forall_mem_closedBall_two_mul_norm_le (hf : DifferentiableOn ℂ f U)
    {c : ℂ} {r M : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hsub : closedBall c (2 * r) ⊆ U)
    (hM : ∀ w ∈ closedBall c (2 * r), ‖f w‖ ≤ M) {z : ℂ} (hz : z ∈ ball c r) :
    ‖deriv f z‖ ≤ M / r := by

label: TauCeti.norm_deriv_schwarzPickConjugate_at_zero
docstring: **Chain rule for the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick conjugate.** For the composite `target ∘ f ∘ source` of two unit-disc Moebius factors around `f`, given the factor derivatives `1 - conj z * z` (of `source` at `0`, where `source 0 = z`) and `1 / (1 - conj (f z) * f z)` (of `target` at `f z`), the norm of the derivative of the composite at the origin equals the Poincaré distortion `‖df‖ * (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2)`.
code:
private lemma norm_deriv_schwarzPickConjugate_at_zero {source target f : ℂ → ℂ} {df z : ℂ}
    (hz : ‖z‖ ≤ 1) (hfz : ‖f z‖ ≤ 1)
    (hs : HasDerivAt source (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) z * z) 0) (hsz : source 0 = z)
    (hf : HasDerivAt f df z)
    (ht : HasDerivAt target (1 / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) (f z) * f z)) (f z)) :
    ‖deriv (target ∘ f ∘ source) 0‖ = ‖df‖ * (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) / (1 - ‖f z‖ ^ 2) := by

label: TauCeti.poincare_defect_quotient
docstring: **Value-level equality case of the infinitesimal Schwarz--Pick lemma.** The quotient built from the Moebius derivative value `(1 - conj a * a) / (1 - conj a * z) ^ 2` and the Moebius image `(z - a) / (1 - conj a * z)` collapses to the reciprocal Poincaré factor `1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2)`. Both public isometry theorems below rewrite their derivative to this value and apply this computation.

        / (1 - ‖(z - a) / (1 - (starRingEnd ℂ) a * z)‖ ^ 2)
      = 1 / (1 - ‖z‖ ^ 2) := by

      (∫ y : ℝ in z.im..(0 : ℝ), F (↑a + ↑y * I)) +

Arithmetic function
snippet: An arithmetic function is a complex-valued function whose domain is the positive integers.

label: Bernoulli numbers
snippet: The Bernoulli numbers are the rational numbers $B_n$ that appear as coefficients of the formal power series \[ \frac{T}{e^T-1}=\sum_{n\ge 0}B_n\frac{T^n}{n!}, \] which has radius of convergence $2\pi$.

label: Divisor function
snippet: A **divisor function** is a multiplicative arithmetic function of the form \[ \sigma_\tau(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}d^\tau, \] for some fixed $\tau\in\mathbb{C}$.

label: Abelian surface
snippet: An **abelian surface** is an abelian variety of dimension 2. Examples are given by the product of two elliptic curves, or the Jacobian of a curve of genus 2.

label: Abelian variety
snippet: An **abelian variety** defined over the field $K$ is a smooth connected projective variety equipped with the structure of an algebraic group. The group law is automatically commutative. An abelian variety of dimension 1 is the same as an elliptic curve.

label: Affine space
snippet: **Affine space** $\mathbb{A}^n(K)$ of dimension $n$ over a field $K$ is the set $K^n$. If $P=(x_1,\dots,x_n)$ is a point in $\mathbb{A}^n(K)$, the $x_i$ are called the *affine coordinates* of $P$. Thus $$ \mathbb{A}^n(K) = \{(x_1,\dots,x_n)\mid x_1,\dots,x_n\in K\}. $$

label: Algebraic group
snippet: TBA

label: Base field
snippet: The **base field**, of an algebraic variety is the field over which it is defined; it necessarily contains the coefficients of a set of defining equations for the variety, but it is not necessarily a minimal field of definition.

label: Bielliptic curve
snippet: A smooth projective algebraic curve $X$ defined over a field $k$ of genus $g\ge 2$ is a **bielliptic curve** if and only if it satisfies one of the following conditions: - $X$ admits a 2-to-1 map $X\to E$ defined over the algebraic closure $\bar k$ onto an elliptic curve $E$. - There exists an involution $w \in \Aut(X)$ defined over $k$ such that $X/\langle w \rangle$ has genus $1$ and $X/\langle w \rangle (k) \ne \empty$. - There exists an involution $w \in \Aut(X)$ defined over $k$ having exactly $2g -2$ fixed points. The involution above is called the **bielliptic involution**.

label: Canonical height of an abelian variety
snippet: Let $A$ be a principally polarised abelian variety defined over a number field $L$. The **canonical height** on $A$ is a function $$ \hat{h}: A(L) \to \R_{ {}\ge0} $$ defined on the Mordell-Weil group $A(L)$ which induces a positive definite quadratic form on $A(L)\otimes\R$. One definition of $\hat{h}(P)$ is $\hat h(P)= h_{\mathrm{Kum}}(\sigma(P))$, where $\sigma \colon A \to K$ is the natural map from $A$ to its Kummer surface $K : = A/\{\pm 1\}$, and $h_\mathrm{kum} \colon K(L) \to \R$ the canonical height pairing associated to a theta divisor $\Theta$ on $K$, which can be defined by $$…

label: Complex multiplication
snippet: A simple abelian variety of dimension $g$ is said to have **complex multiplication** (CM) if its endomorphism algebra is a CM field of degree $2g$, or equivalently, if its endomorphism ring is an order in a CM field of degree $2g$.

label: Conductor of an abelian variety
snippet: The **conductor** of an abelian variety $A$ over $\Q$ is a positive integer $N$ whose prime factors are the primes $p$ where $A$ has bad reduction. The power to which $p$ divides $N$ depends on the type of bad reduction; it can be expressed in terms of ramification in the $\ell$-adic representation associated to $A$ for any prime $\ell \ne p$. The conductor of an abelian variety over a number field is defined similarly; it is an ideal that is a product of positive powers of the prime ideals where $A$ has bad reduction.

label: Algebraic curve
snippet: An **algebraic curve** is an algebraic variety of dimension $1.$

label: Smoothness of an algebraic curve
snippet: Let $C$ be an algebraic curve over a perfect field $k$. Then $C$ is called **smooth** if the extension of $C$ to the algebraic closure of $k$ is non-singular at all of its points.

label: Cyclic trigonal curve
snippet: An algebraic curve $X$ is a **cyclic trigonal curve** if there is an order $3$ subgroup $H$ of its automorphism group such that the quotient curve $X/H$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{P}^1$. A generator of such a subgroup $H$ is called a **trigonal automorphism**.

label: Dimension of an algebraic variety
snippet: The **dimension** of an algebraic variety $V$ is the maximal length $d$ of a chain $$ V_0 \subset V_1 \subset \cdots \subset V_d $$ of distinct irreducible subvarieties of $V$.

label: Endomorphism algebra
snippet: The **endomorphism algebra** of an abelian variety $A$ is the $\Q$-algebra $\textrm{End}(A)\otimes\Q$, where $\textrm{End}(A)$ is the endomorphism ring of $A$.

label: Endomorphism ring
snippet: An **endomorphism** of an abelian variety $A$ over a field $k$ is a homomorphism $\varphi \colon A \to A$ defined over $k$. The set of endomorphisms of an abelian variety $A$ can be given the structure of a ring in which addition is defined pointwise (using the group operation of $A$) and multiplication is composition; this ring is called the **endomorphism ring** of $A$, denoted $\textrm{End}(A)$. For endomorphisms defined over an extension of $k$, we instead speak about the geometric endomorphism ring.

label: Geometrically simple
snippet: An abelian variety over a field $k$ is **geometrically (or absolutely) simple** if it is simple when viewed as a variety over $\bar k$.

label: Gonality of a curve
snippet: The **gonality** (or **$k$-gonality**) of an integral algebraic curve $X$ over a field $k$ is the minimal degree of a dominant $k$-morphism $X \to \mathbb P^1_k$. Equivalently, it is the minimum of $[k(X):k(t)]$ as $t$ ranges over (transcendental) elements of the function field $k(X)$ of $X$. The base extension of any dominant morphism $X \to \mathbb{P}^1_k$ is a dominant morphism $X_{\overline{k}} \to \mathbb{P}^1_{\overline{k}}$, so the geometric gonality of $X$ is less than or equal to the $k$-gonality of $X$.

label: Geometric gonality
snippet: Let $X$ be a geometrically integral algebraic curve over a field $k$. Let $\overline{k}$ be an algebraic closure of $k$. Let $X_{\overline{k}}$ be the base extension. The **geometric gonality** (or **$\overline{k}$-gonality**) of $X$ is the gonality of $X_{\overline{k}}$, that is, the minimal degree of a dominant morphism $X_{\overline{k}} \to \mathbb P^1_{\overline{k}}$.

label: Good and bad reduction
snippet: A smooth proper variety $X$ over a number field $K$ is said to have **good reduction** at a prime $\mathfrak{p}$ if it has a model over $\mathcal{O}_{K, \mathfrak{p}}$ whose reduction modulo $\mathfrak{p}$ is a smooth variety over the residue field; more precisely, $X$ has good reduction if it is the generic fiber of a smooth proper scheme over $\mathcal{O}_{K, \mathfrak{p}}$. Otherwise, $\mathfrak{p}$ is said to be a prime of **bad reduction**. The set of primes at which a given $X$ has bad reduction is finite.

label: Hyperelliptic curve
snippet: A **hyperelliptic curve** $X$ over a field $k$ is a smooth projective algebraic curve of genus $g\ge 2$ that admits a 2-to-1 map $X\to \mathbb{P}^1$ defined over the algebraic closure $\bar k$. If $X$ is a hyperelliptic curve over $k$, then the canonical map $X \to \mathbb{P}^{g-1}$ is a 2-to-1 map onto a smooth genus 0 curve $Y$. The curve $Y$ is isomorphic to $\mathbb{P}^1$ if and only if $Y$ has a $k$-rational point.

label: Jacobian of a curve
snippet: The **Jacobian** of a (smooth, projective, geometrically integral) curve $X$ of genus $g$ over a field $k$ is a $g$-dimensional principally polarized abelian variety $J$ that is canonically associated to $X$. If $X$ has a $k$-rational point, then $J(k)$ is isomorphic to the group of degree zero divisors on $X$ modulo linear equivalence. A choice of rational point on $X$ determines a morphism $X \to J$ called an Abel-Jacobi map; it is an embedding if and only if $g \ge 1$, and an isomorphism if and only if $g=1$.

label: Modular curve $X_0(N)$
snippet: Let $N \ge 1$. The *modular curve* $X_0(N)$ is an algebraic curve defined over $\Q$ (or even $\Z[1/N]$) whose points over any algebraically closed field of characteristic not dividing $N$ correspond to isomorphism classes of pairs $(E,\phi)$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve and $\phi$ is an isogeny with domain $E$ and kernel a cyclic group of order $N$, with the exception of particular points called *cusps* which correspond to degenerate such pairs. The complex manifold $X_0(N)(\C)$ is biholomorphic to the quotient $\Gamma_0(N) \backslash \mathcal{H}^*$ of the completed upper half plane.

label: Modular curve $X_1(N)$
snippet: Let $N \ge 1$. The *modular curve* $X_1(N)$ is an algebraic curve defined over $\Q$ (or even $\Z[1/N]$) whose points over any algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic not dividing $N$ correspond to isomorphism classes of pairs $(E,P)$, where $E$ is an elliptic curve over $k$ and $P \in E(k)$ is a torsion point of order exactly $N$, with the exception of particular points called *cusps* which correspond to degenerate such pairs. If $N \ge 4$, the same description of points is valid even if $k$ is not algebraically closed.

label: Mordell-Weil group of an abelian variety
snippet: The **Mordell-Weil group** of an abelian variety $A$ over a number field $K$ is its group of $K$-rational points $A(K)$. Weil, building on Mordell's theorem for elliptic curves over $\Q$, proved that the abelian group $A(K)$ is finitely generated. Thus \[ A(K)\simeq \Z^r \oplus T, \] where $r$ is a nonnegative integer called the **Mordell-Weil rank** of $A$, and $T$ is a finite abelian group called the **torsion subgroup**. The torsion subgroup $T$ is the product of at most $2g$ cyclic groups, where $g$ is the dimension of $A$.

label: Projective space
snippet: **Projective space** $\mathbb{P}^n(K)$ of dimension $n$ over a field $K$ is the set $(K^{n+1}\setminus\{0\})/{}\sim{}$, where $$ (x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n) \sim (y_0,y_1,\dots,y_n) \iff x_0=\lambda y_0, \dots, x_n=\lambda y_n\quad\text{for some}\ \lambda\in K^*. $$ This is also known as the projectivization of the vector space $K^{n+1}$. The equivalence class of $(x_0,x_1,\dots,x_n)$ in $\mathbb{P}^n(K)$ is denoted by $(x_0:x_1:\dots:x_n)$, and the $x_i$ are called **homogeneous coordinates**. Thus $$ \mathbb{P}^n(K) = \{(x_0:\dots:x_n)\mid x_0,\dots,x_n\in K,\ \text{not all zero}\}. $$

label: Quotient curve
snippet: Let $X$ be an algebraic curve and let $H$ be a finite subgroup of its automorphism group. The **quotient curve** $X/H$ is the algebraic curve obtained by identifying points of $X$ that lie in the same $H$-orbit (equations defining $X/H$ as an algebraic variety of dimension one can be constructed from the equations defining $X$ and the automorphisms in $H$). The natural projection $X\to X/H$ that sends each point on $X$ to its $H$-orbit is a surjective morphism

label: Real multiplication
snippet: An abelian variety is said to have **real multiplication** (RM) if its endomorphism algebra is a totally real (number) field. (In most situations, we exclude the trivial case of RM by $\Q$.)

label: Regulator of an abelian variety
snippet: The **regulator** of an abelian variety $A$ defined over a number field $K,$ denoted $\operatorname{Reg}(A/K)$, is the volume of $A(K)/A(K)_{tor}$ with respect to the **height pairing** $\langle -,-\rangle$ associated to the canonical height $\hat{h}$, i.e. $\langle P,Q\rangle = \frac{1}{2}(\hat{h}(P+Q)-\hat{h}(P)-\hat{h}(Q))$. If the Mordell-Weil group $A(K)$ has rank $r$ and $P_1, \ldots, P_r \in E(K)$ generate $A(K)/A(K)_{\text{tors}}$, then \[ \operatorname{Reg}(A/K) = \left|\det (\langle P_i, P_j \rangle )_{1\leq i,j \leq r}\right|, \] which is independent of the choice of generators.

label: Selmer group of an abelian variety
