label: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic
snippet: For every integer $n$ such that $n > 1$, $n$ can be expressed as the product of one or more primes, uniquely up to the order in which they appear.

label: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus for Contour Integrals
snippet: Let $F, f: D \to \C$ be complex functions, where $D$ is a connected domain. Let $C$ be a contour that is a concatenation of the directed smooth curves $C_1, \ldots, C_n$. Let $C_k$ be parameterized by the smooth path $\gamma_k: \closedint {a_k} {b_k} \to D$ for all $k \in \set {1, \ldots, n}$. Suppose that $F$ is an antiderivative of $f$. If $C$ has start point $z$ and end point $w$, then: $\ds \int_C \map f z \rd z = \map F w - \map F z$ If $C$ is a closed contour, then: $\ds \oint_C \map f z \rd z = 0$

label: Fundamental Theorem of Finite Abelian Groups
snippet: Every finite abelian group is an internal group direct product of cyclic groups whose orders are prime powers. The number of terms in the product and the orders of the cyclic groups are uniquely determined by the group.

label: Fundamental Theorem of Galois Theory
snippet: Let $L / K$ be a finite Galois extension. Let $\Gal {L / K}$ denote the Galois group of the extension $L / K$. Let $H$ denote a subgroup of $\Gal {L / K}$ and $F$ denote an intermediate field. Let $L_H$ denote the fixed field of $H$. The mappings: $H \mapsto L_H$, and $F \mapsto \Gal {L / F}$ are inclusion-reversing and inverses. Moreover, these maps induce a bijection between the normal subgroups of $\Gal {L / K}$ and the normal, intermediate extensions of $L / K$.

label: Fundamental Theorem on Equivalence Relations
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times S$ be an equivalence on a set $S$. Then the quotient set $S / \RR$ of $S$ by $\RR$ forms a partition of $S$.

label: G-Tower is Well-Ordered under Subset Relation
snippet: Let $M$ be a class. Let $g: M \to M$ be a progressing mapping on $M$. Let $M$ be a $g$-tower. Then $M$ is well-ordered under the subset relation such that:

label: GCD from Prime Decomposition
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$. From Expression for Integers as Powers of Same Primes, let: {{eqn | l = a | r = p_1^{k_1} p_2^{k_2} \ldots p_r^{k_r} }} {{eqn | l = b | r = p_1^{l_1} p_2^{l_2} \ldots p_r^{l_r} }} {{eqn | q = \forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, r} | l = p_i | o = \divides | r = a | c = }} That is, the primes given in these prime decompositions may be divisors of either of the numbers $a$ or $b$. Then: $\gcd \set {a, b} = p_1^{\min \set {k_1, l_1} } p_2^{\min \set {k_2, l_2} } \ldots p_r^{\min \set {k_r, l_r} }$ where $\gcd \set {a, b}$ denotes the greatest common divisor of $a$ and $b$.

label: Gamma Difference Equation
snippet: The Gamma function satisfies: $\map \Gamma {z + 1} = z \, \map \Gamma z$ for an arbitrary $z$ which is not a nonpositive integer.

label: Gamma Function Extends Factorial
snippet: $\forall n \in \N: \map \Gamma {n + 1} = n!$

label: Gamma Function of One Half
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote the Gamma function. Then: $\map \Gamma {\dfrac 1 2} = \sqrt \pi$

label: Gauss's Digamma Theorem
snippet: Let $\dfrac p q$ be a positive rational number with $p < q$. Then: $\ds \map \psi {\dfrac p q} = -\gamma - \ln 2 q - \dfrac \pi 2 \map \cot {\dfrac p q \pi} + 2 \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^{\ceiling {q / 2} - 1} \map \cos {\dfrac {2 \pi p n} q} \map \ln {\map \sin {\dfrac {\pi n} q} }$ where: $\psi$ is the digamma function $\cot$ is the cotangent function $\ln$ is the natural logarithm.

label: Gauss's Hypergeometric Theorem
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \C$. Let $c \notin \Z_{\le 0}$. Let $\map \Re {c - a - b} > 0$. Then: $\map F {a, b; c; 1} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma c \map \Gamma {c - a - b} } {\map \Gamma {c - a} \map \Gamma {c - b} }$ where: $\map F {a, b; c; 1}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $1$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } { c^{\overline k} } \dfrac {1^k} {k!}$ $x^{\overline k}$ denotes the $k$th rising factorial power of $x$ $\map \Gamma {n + 1} = n!$ is the Gamma function.

label: Gauss's Integral Form of Digamma Function
snippet: Let $z$ be a complex number with a positive real part. Then: $\ds \map \psi z = \int_0^\infty \paren {\frac {e^{-t} } t - \frac {e^{-z t} } {1 - e^{-t} } } \rd t$ where $\psi$ is the digamma function.

label: Gauss's Lemma on Primitive Rational Polynomials
snippet: Let $\Q$ be the field of rational numbers. Let $\Q \sqbrk X$ be the ring of polynomials over $\Q$ in one indeterminate $X$. Let $\map f X, \map g X \in \Q \sqbrk X$ be primitive polynomials. Then their product $f g$ is also a primitive polynomial.

label: Gauss-Ostrogradsky Theorem
snippet: Let $U$ be a subset of $\R^3$ which is compact and has a piecewise smooth boundary $\partial U$. Let $\mathbf V: \R^3 \to \R^3$ be a smooth vector field defined on a neighborhood of $U$. Then: $\ds \iiint \limits_U \paren {\nabla \cdot \mathbf V} \rd v = \iint \limits_{\partial U} \mathbf V \cdot \mathbf n \rd S$ where $\mathbf n$ is the unit normal to $\partial U$, directed outwards. That is, the sum of all expansions of $\mathbf V$ within $U$ equals the flux of $\mathbf V$ across the boundary of $U$.

label: Gaussian Integers form Euclidean Domain
snippet:
Let $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, 	imes}$ be the integral domain of Gaussian Integers. Let $
u: \Z \sqbrk i 	o \R$ be the real-valued function defined as: $ orall a \in \Z \sqbrk i: \map 
u a = \cmod a^2$ where $\cmod a$ is the (complex) modulus of $a$. Then $
u$ is a Euclidean valuation on $\Z \sqbrk i$. Hence $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, 	imes}$ with $
u: \Z \sqbrk i 	o \Z$ forms a Euclidean domain.

label: Gaussian Integers form Integral Domain
snippet: The ring of Gaussian integers $\struct {\Z \sqbrk i, +, \times}$ is an integral domain.

label: Gelfond-Schneider Theorem
snippet: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be algebraic numbers (possibly complex) such that $\alpha \notin \set {0, 1}$. Let $\beta$ be irrational, that is: $\beta \notin \Q$ This includes $\beta$ being imaginary or complex. Then any value of $\alpha^\beta$ is transcendental.

label: General Antiperiodicity Property
snippet: Let $f: X \to X$ be an antiperiodic function, where $X$ is either $\R$ or $\C$. Let $L$ be an antiperiodic element of $f$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. If $n$ is even, then $n L$ is a periodic element of $f$. If $n$ is odd, then $n L$ is an antiperiodic element of $f$.

label: General Associativity Theorem
snippet: If an operation is associative on $3$ entities, then it is associative on any number of them.

label: General Distributivity Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {R, \circ, *}$ be a ringoid. Then for every pair of sequences $\sequence {a_i}_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le m}, \sequence {b_j}_{1 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n}$ of elements of $R$: $\ds \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^m a_i} * \paren {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n b_j} = \sum_{\substack {1 \mathop \le i \mathop \le m \\ 1 \mathop \le j \mathop \le n} } \paren {a_i * b_j}$ where: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^m a_i$ is the summation $a_1 \circ a_2 \circ \cdots \circ a_m$ $m$ and $n$ are strictly positive integers: $m, n \in \Z_{> 0}$

label: General Intersection Property of Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_n$ be open sets of $\struct {S, \tau}$. Then: $\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n S_i$ is also an open set of $\struct {S, \tau}$. That is, the intersection of any finite number of open sets of a topology is also in $\tau$. Conversely, if the intersection of any finite number of open sets of a topology is also in $\tau$, then: $(1): \quad$ The intersection of any two elements of $\tau$ is an element of $\tau$ $(2): \quad S$ is itself an element of $\tau$.

label: General Stokes' Theorem
snippet: Let $\omega$ be a smooth $\paren {n - 1}$-form with compact support on a smooth $n$-dimensional oriented manifold $X$. Let the boundary of $X$ be $\partial X$. Then: $\ds \int_{\partial X} \omega = \int_X \rd \omega$ where $\d \omega$ is the exterior derivative of $\omega$.

label: Generalized Sum is Monotone
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {a_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an $I$-indexed family of positive real numbers. That is, let $a_i \in \R_{\ge 0}$ for all $i \in I$. Then, for every finite subset $F$ of $I$: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in F} a_i \le \sum_{i \mathop \in I} a_i$ provided the generalized sum on the right converges.

label: Generated Sigma-Algebra Preserves Subset
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\FF, \GG \subseteq \powerset X$ be collections of subsets of $X$. Suppose that: $\FF \subseteq \GG$ Then: $\map \sigma \FF \subseteq \map \sigma \GG$ where $\map \sigma \GG$ denotes the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $\GG$

label: Generating Function for Constant Sequence
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be the sequence defined as: $\forall n \in \N: a_n = r$ for some $r \in \R$. Then the generating function for $\sequence {a_n}$ is given as: $\map G z = \dfrac r {1 - z}$ for $\size z < 1$

label: Generating Function for Fibonacci Numbers
snippet: Let $\map G z$ be the function defined as: $\map G z = \dfrac z {1 - z - z^2}$ Then $\map G z$ is a generating function for the Fibonacci numbers.

label: Generator of Vector Space Contains Basis
snippet: Let $E$ be a vector space of $n$ dimensions. Let $G$ be a generator for $E$. Then: $G$ contains a basis for $E$.

label: Geometrical Interpretation of Complex Addition
snippet: Let $a, b \in \C$ be complex numbers expressed as vectors $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ respectively. Let $OA$ and $OB$ be two adjacent sides of the parallelogram $OACB$ such that $OA$ corresponds to $\mathbf a$ and $OB$ corresponds to $\mathbf b$. Then the diagonal $OC$ of $OACB$ corresponds to $\mathbf a + \mathbf b$, the sum of $a$ and $b$ expressed as a vector.

label: Geometrical Interpretation of Complex Subtraction
snippet: Let $a, b \in \C$ be complex numbers expressed as vectors $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ respectively. Let $OA$ and $OB$ be two adjacent sides of the parallelogram $OACB$ such that $OA$ corresponds to $\mathbf a$ and $OB$ corresponds to $\mathbf b$. Then the diagonal $BA$ of $OACB$ corresponds to $\mathbf a - \mathbf b$, the difference of $a$ and $b$ expressed as a vector.

label: Gibbs Phenomenon
snippet: The Fourier series overshoots at a jump discontinuity, and adding more terms to the sum does not cause this overshoot to die out. 500px 500px

label: Goldbach Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Every even integer greater than $2$ is the sum of two primes.

label: Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be an inner product space over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $S = \set {v_n: n \in \N_{>0} }$ be a linearly independent subset of $V$. Then there exists an orthonormal subset $E = \set {e_n: n \in \N_{>0} }$ of $V$ such that: $\forall k \in \N: \span \set {v_1 , \ldots , v_k} = \span \set {e_1 , \ldots ,e_k}$ where $\span$ denotes linear span.

label: Greater Angle of Triangle Subtended by Greater Side
Greatest Element is Supremum
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $T$ have a greatest element $M$. Then $M$ is the supremum of $T$ in $S$.

label: Greatest Lower Bound Property
snippet: Let $S \subset \R$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers such that $S$ is bounded below. Then $S$ admits an infimum in $\R$. This is known as the greatest lower bound property of the real numbers.

label: Green's Theorem
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ be a positively oriented piecewise smooth Jordan curve in $\R^2$. Let $U = \Int \Gamma$, that is, the interior of $\Gamma$. Let $A$ and $B$ be functions of $\tuple {x, y}$ defined on an open region containing $U$ and have continuous partial derivatives in such a set. Then: $\ds \oint_\Gamma \paren {A \rd x + B \rd y} = \iint_U \paren {\frac {\partial B} {\partial x} - \frac {\partial A} {\partial y} } \rd x \rd y$ where the is a contour integral.

label: Grothendieck Universe is Closed under Subset
snippet: Let $\mathbb U$ be a Grothendieck universe. Let $u \in \mathbb U$. Let $v \subseteq u$ be a subset of $u$. Then $v \in \mathbb U$.

label: Group Action Induces Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $X$ be a set. Let $*: G \times S \to S$ be a group action. Let $\RR_G$ be the relation induced by $G$, that is: $\forall x, y \in X: x \mathrel {\RR_G} y \iff y \in \Orb x$ where: $\Orb x$ denotes the orbit of $x \in X$. Then: $\RR_G$ is an equivalence relation and: the equivalence class of an element of $X$ is its orbit.

label: Group Action defines Permutation Representation
snippet: Let $\map \Gamma X$ be the set of permutations on a set $X$. Let $G$ be a group. Let $\phi: G \times X \to X$ be a group action. For $g \in G$, let $\phi_g: X \to X$ be the mapping defined as: $\map {\phi_g} x = \map \phi {g, x}$ Let $\tilde \phi: G \to \map \Gamma X$ be the permutation representation associated to $\phi$, defined by: $\map {\tilde \phi} g := \phi_g$ Then $\tilde \phi$ is a group homomorphism.

label: Group Action determines Bijection
snippet: Let $*$ be a group action of $G$ on $X$. Then each $g \in G$ determines a bijection $\phi_g: X \to X$ given by: $\map {\phi_g} x = g * x$ Its inverse is: $\phi_{g^{-1} }: X \to X$. These bijection are sometimes called transformations of $X$.

label: Group Action on Sets with k Elements
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a finite group whose identity is $e$. Let $\Bbb S = \set {S \subseteq G: \card S = k}$, that is, the set of all of subsets of $G$ which have exactly $k$ elements. Let $G$ act on $\Bbb S$ by the rule: $\forall S \in \Bbb S: g * S = g S = \set {x \in G: x = g s: s \in S}$ This is a group action, and: $\forall S \in \Bbb S: \order {\Stab S} \divides \card S$ where $\Stab S$ denotes the stabilizer of $S$ by $G$.

label: Group Acts on Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ acts on itself by the rule: $\forall g, h \in G: g * h = g \circ h$

label: Group Direct Product of Cyclic Groups
snippet: Let $G$ and $H$ both be finite cyclic groups with orders $n = \order G$ and $m = \order H$ respectively. Then: The group direct product $G \times H$ is cyclic $n$ and $m$ are coprime, that is: $n \perp m$

label: Group Homomorphism Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to \struct {H, *}$ be a group homomorphism. Let: $e_G$ be the identity of $G$ $e_H$ be the identity of $H$. Then: $\map \phi {e_G} = e_H$

label: Group Homomorphism Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, *}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G, \circ} \to\struct {H, *}$ be a group homomorphism. Let: $e_G$ be the identity of $G$ $e_H$ be the identity of $H$ Then: $\forall x \in G: \map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$ Hence the notation $\map \phi x^{-1}$ can be used unambiguously.

label: Group Homomorphism Preserves Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G_1, \circ}$ and $\struct {G_2, *}$ be groups. Let $\phi: \struct {G_1, \circ} \to \struct {G_2, *}$ be a group homomorphism. Then: $H \le G_1 \implies \phi \sqbrk H \le G_2$ where: $\phi \sqbrk H$ denotes the image of $H$ under $\phi$ $\le$ denotes subgroup. That is, group homomorphism preserves subgroups.

label: Group has Latin Square Property
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then $G$ satisfies the Latin square property. That is, for all $a, b \in G$, there exists a unique $g \in G$ such that $a \circ g = b$. Similarly, there exists a unique $h \in G$ such that $h \circ a = b$.

label: Group is Normal in Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then $\struct {G, \circ}$ is a normal subgroup of itself.

label: Group is Subgroup of Itself
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then: $\struct {G, \circ} \le \struct {G, \circ}$ That is, a group is always a subgroup of itself.

label: Group is not Empty
snippet: A group cannot be empty.

label: Group of Order p q has Normal Sylow p-Subgroup
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be prime numbers such that $p > q$. Let $G$ be a group of order $p q$. Then $G$ has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup. This Sylow $p$-subgroup is normal.

label: Group of Units is Group
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Then the set of units of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ forms a group under $\circ$. Hence the justification for referring to the group of units of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$.

label: Group whose Order equals Order of Element is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group of order $n$. Let $g \in G$ have order $n$. Then $G$ is a cyclic group which is generated by $g$.

label: Grunblum's Criterion
snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\sequence {e_j}_{j \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of non-zero vectors in $X$. Then $\sequence {e_j}_{j \mathop \in \N}$ is a basic sequence there exists $K > 0$ such that for any sequence $\sequence {\alpha_j}_{j \mathop \in \N}$ in $\GF$ we have: $\ds 
orm {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^m \alpha_j e_j} \le K 
orm {\sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_j e_j}$ for $m \le n$.

label: Hadamard Factorization Theorem
snippet: Let $f: \C \to \C$ be an entire function of finite order $\omega$. Let $0$ be a zero of $f$ of multiplicity $m \ge 0$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be the sequence of non-zero zeroes of $f$, repeated according to multiplicity. Then: $f$ has finite rank $p \le \omega$ and: there exists a polynomial $g$ of degree at most $\omega$ such that: $\ds \map f z = z^m e^{\map g z} \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty E_p \paren {\frac z {a_n} }$ where $E_p$ denotes the $p$th Weierstrass elementary factor.

label: Handshake Lemma
snippet: Let $G$ be a $\tuple {p, q}$-undirected graph, which may be a multigraph or a loop-graph, or both. Let $V = \set {v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_p}$ be the vertex set of $G$. Then: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^p \map {\deg_G} {v_i} = 2 q$ where $\map {\deg_G} {v_i}$ is the degree of vertex $v_i$. That is, the sum of all the degrees of all the vertices of an graph is equal to twice its size. This result is known as the Handshake Lemma or Handshaking Lemma.

label: Harmonic Series is Divergent
snippet: The harmonic series: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 n$ diverges.

label: Hartogs' Lemma (Set Theory)
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Then there exists an ordinal $\alpha$ such that there is no injection from $\alpha$ to $S$.

label: Hat-Check Distribution Gives Rise to Probability Mass Function
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable on a probability space $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$. Let $X$ have the hat-check distribution with parameter $n$ (where $n > 0$). Then $X$ gives rise to a probability mass function.

label: Heine-Cantor Theorem
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $M_1$ be compact. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a continuous mapping. Then $f$ is uniformly continuous.

label: Helmholtz's Theorem
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of ordinary space. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field over $R$. Let $\mathbf V$ be both non-conservative and non-solenoidal. Then $\mathbf V$ can be decomposed into the sum of $2$ vector fields: one being conservative, with scalar potential $S$, but not solenoidal one being solenoidal, with vector potential $\mathbf A$, but not conservative.

label: Henry Ernest Dudeney/Puzzles and Curious Problems
Hermite-Lindemann-Weierstrass Theorem
snippet: Let $a_1, \cdots, a_n$ be algebraic numbers (possibly complex) that are linearly independent over the rational numbers $\Q$. Then: $e^{a_1}, \cdots, e^{a_n}$ are algebraically independent where $e$ is Euler's number.

label: Hermitian Conjugate is Involution
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ be a complex-valued matrix. Let $\mathbf A^*$ denote the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf A$. Then the operation of Hermitian conjugate is an involution: $\paren {\mathbf A^*}^* = \mathbf A$

label: Hermitian Conjugate of Matrix Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be matrices over a commutative ring such that $\mathbf A \mathbf B$ is defined. Then $\mathbf B^\dagger \mathbf A^\dagger$ is defined, and: $\paren {\mathbf A \mathbf B}^\dagger = \mathbf B^\dagger \mathbf A^\dagger$ where $\mathbf X^\dagger$ is the Hermitian conjugate of $\mathbf X$.

label: Hermitian Element of C*-Algebra Decomposes into Positive Elements
snippet:
Let $\struct {A, \ast, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $	ext C^\ast$-algebra. Let $b \in A$ be Hermitian. Then there exists positive elements $b^+$ and $b^-$ such that: $b^+ b^- = {\mathbf 0}_A$ $b^+ - b^- = b$ $
orm {b^+} \le 
orm b$ and $
orm {b^-} \le 
orm b$.

label: Heron's Formula
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with sides $a$, $b$ and $c$ opposite vertices $A$, $B$ and $C$ respectively. Then the area $\AA$ of $\triangle ABC$ is given by: $\AA = \sqrt {s \paren {s - a} \paren {s - b} \paren {s - c} }$ where $s = \dfrac {a + b + c} 2$ is the semiperimeter of $\triangle ABC$.

label: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz
snippet: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field. Let $n \geq 0$ be an natural number. Let $k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ be the polynomial ring in $n$ variables over $k$. Then for every ideal $J \subseteq k \sqbrk {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$, the associated ideal of its zero-locus equals its radical: $\map I {\map Z J} = \map \Rad J$

label: Hilbert-Waring Theorem
snippet: For each $k \in \Z: k \ge 2$, there exists a positive integer $\map g k$ such that every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of at most $\map g k$ positive $k$th powers.

label: Hilbert Sequence Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $A$ be the set of all real sequences $\sequence {x_i}$ such that the series $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \ge 0} {x_i}^2$ is convergent. Let $\ell^2 = \struct {A, d_2}$ be the Hilbert sequence space on $\R$. Then $\ell^2$ is a metric space.

label: Hodge Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == It is conjectured that: For projective algebraic varieties, Hodge cycles are rational linear combinations of algebraic cycles.

label: Holomorphic Function is Analytic
snippet: Let $a \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $r > 0$ be a real number. Let $f$ be a function holomorphic on some open disk $D = \map B {a, r}$. Then $f$ is complex analytic on $D$.

label: Homogeneous Quadratic Equation represents Two Straight Lines through Origin
snippet: Let $E$ be a homogeneous quadratic equation in two variables: $E: \quad a x^2 + 2 h x y + b y^2 = 0$ Then $E$ represents $2$ straight lines in the Cartesian plane: $y = \dfrac {h \pm \sqrt {h^2 - a b} } b x$

label: Homomorphic Image of Cyclic Group is Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group with generator $g$. Let $H$ be a group. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a (group) homomorphism. Let $\Img G$ denote the homomorphic image of $G$ under $\phi$. Then $\Img G$ is a cyclic group with generator $\map \phi g$. That is: $\phi \sqbrk {\gen g} = \gen {\map \phi g}$

label: Homomorphism of Generated Group
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, \circ}$ be groups. Let $\phi: G \to H$ and $\psi: G \to H$ be homomorphisms. Let $\gen S = G$ be the group generated by $S$. Let: $\forall x \in S: \map \phi x = \map \psi x$ Then: $\phi = \psi$

label: Homomorphism of Power of Group Element
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ and $\struct {H, \ast}$ be groups. Let $\phi: S \to T$ be a group homomorphism. Then: $\forall n \in \Z: \forall g \in G: \map \phi {g^n} = \paren {\map \phi g}^n$

label: Homomorphism of Powers
snippet: Let $\struct {T_1, \odot}$ and $\struct {T_2, \oplus}$ be semigroups. Let $\phi: \struct {T_1, \odot} \to \struct {T_2, \oplus}$ be a (semigroup) homomorphism.

label: Homomorphism on Induced Structure to Commutative Semigroup
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, \oplus}$ be a commutative semigroup. Let $T^S$ be the set of all mappings from $S$ to $T$. Let $f$ and $g$ be homomorphisms from $S$ into $T$. Let $f \oplus' g$ be the pointwise operation on $T^S$ induced by $\oplus$. Then $f \oplus' g$ is a homomorphism from $\struct {S, \circ}$ into $\struct {T, \oplus}$.

label: Homomorphism to Group Preserves Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, *}$ be a group. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Then: $\map \phi {e_S} = e_T$

label: Homomorphism to Group Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $\struct {T, *}$ be a group. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $x^{-1}$ be an inverse of $x$ for $\circ$. Then $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse of $\map \phi x$ for $*$.

label: Homomorphism with Identity Preserves Inverses
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a homomorphism. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, *}$ also have an identity $e_T = \map \phi {e_S}$. If $x^{-1}$ is an inverse of $x$ for $\circ$, then $\map \phi {x^{-1} }$ is an inverse of $\map \phi x$ for $*$. That is: $\map \phi {x^{-1} } = \paren {\map \phi x}^{-1}$

label: Honsberger's Identity
snippet: Let $F_k$ be the $k$th Fibonacci number. Then: $\forall m, n \in \Z_{>0}: F_{m + n} = F_{m - 1} F_n + F_m F_{n + 1}$

label: Horizontal Section of Continuous Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $T$ be topological spaces. Equip the Cartesian product $X \times Y$ with the product topology. Let $f : X \times Y \to T$ be a continuous mapping. Let $y \in Y$. Then the $y$-horizontal section $f^y : X \to T$ is continuous.

label: Horizontal Section of Measurable Set is Measurable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma_X}$ and $\struct {Y, \Sigma_Y}$ be measurable spaces. Let $E \in \Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ where $\Sigma_X \otimes \Sigma_Y$ is the product $\sigma$-algebra of $\Sigma_X$ and $\Sigma_Y$. Let $y \in Y$. Then: $E^y \in \Sigma_X$ where $E^y$ is the $y$-horizontal section of $E$.

label: Hyperbolic Cosecant Function is Odd
snippet: Let $\csch: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic cosecant function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\csch$ is odd: $\map \csch {-x} = -\csch x$

label: Hyperbolic Cosecant in terms of Cosecant
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \csch z = -\csc \paren {i z}$ where: $\csc$ denotes the cosecant function $\csch$ denotes the hyperbolic cosecant $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hyperbolic Cosecant of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\map \csch {a + b i} = \dfrac {\sinh a \cos b - i \cosh a \sin b} {\sinh^2 a \cos^2 b + \cosh^2 a \sin^2 b}$ where: $\csch$ denotes the hyperbolic cosecant function. $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

snippet: $\cosh x = \map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {\dfrac 1 2; \dfrac {x^2} 4}$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \in \R$ $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function $\map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {a; x}$ is the generalized hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac 1 { a^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

label: Hyperbolic Cosine Function is Even
snippet: Let $\cosh: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic cosine function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\cosh$ is even: $\map \cosh {-x} = \cosh x$

label: Hyperbolic Cosine in terms of Cosine
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\cosh z = \map \cos {i z}$ where: $\cos$ denotes the complex cosine $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hyperbolic Cosine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\map \cosh {a + b i} = \cosh a \cos b + i \sinh a \sin b$ where: $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

label: Hyperbolic Cotangent Function is Odd
snippet: Let $\coth: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic cotangent function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\coth$ is odd: $\map \coth {-x} = -\coth x$

snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\coth z = -\cot \paren {i z}$ where: $\cot$ denotes the cotangent function $\coth$ denotes the hyperbolic cotangent $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hyperbolic Secant Function is Even
snippet: Let $\sech: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic secant function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\sech$ is even: $\map \sech {-x} = \sech x$

label: Hyperbolic Secant in terms of Secant
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $\sech z = \sec \paren {i z}$ where: $\sec$ denotes the secant function $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hyperbolic Secant of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\sech \paren {a + b i} = \dfrac {\cosh a \cos b - i \sinh a \sin b} {\cosh^2 a \cos^2 b + \sinh^2 a \sin^2 b}$ where: $\sech$ denotes the hyperbolic secant function. $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function

label: Hyperbolic Sine Function in terms of Hypergeometric Function
snippet: $\sinh x = x \paren {\map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {\dfrac 3 2; \dfrac {x^2} 4} }$ where: $x$ is a real number with $x \in \R$ $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\map { {}_0 \operatorname F_1} {a; x}$ is the generalized hypergeometric function of $x$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac 1 { a^{\overline k} } \dfrac {x^k} {k!}$

label: Hyperbolic Sine Function is Odd
snippet: Let $\sinh: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic sine function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\sinh$ is odd: $\map \sinh {-x} = -\sinh x$

label: Hyperbolic Sine in terms of Sine
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \sinh z = \map \sin {i z}$ where: $\sin$ denotes the complex sine $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hyperbolic Sine of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then: $\sinh \paren {a + b i} = \sinh a \cos b + i \cosh a \sin b$ where: $\sin$ denotes the real sine function $\cos$ denotes the real cosine function $\sinh$ denotes the hyperbolic sine function $\cosh$ denotes the hyperbolic cosine function.

label: Hyperbolic Tangent Function is Odd
snippet: Let $\tanh: \C \to \C$ be the hyperbolic tangent function on the set of complex numbers. Then $\tanh$ is odd: $\map \tanh {-x} = -\tanh x$

label: Hyperbolic Tangent in terms of Tangent
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \tanh z = \map \tan {i z}$ where: $\tan$ denotes the tangent function $\tanh$ denotes the hyperbolic tangent $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Hypothetical Syllogism
snippet: The (rule of the) hypothetical syllogism is a valid deduction sequent in propositional logic:

label: Hölder's Inequality for Integrals
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $p, q \in \R_{>0}$ such that $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$. {{improve|the assumption should read $p,q\in\R_{>0}\cup\set{+\infty}$.Suggestion: make a page for defining $p,q$ as satisfying this relation, including the pair $\tuple{1,\infty}$}} Let $f \in \map {\LL^p} \mu, f: X \to \R$, and $g \in \map {\LL^q} \mu, g: X \to \R$, where $\LL$ denotes Lebesgue space.

label: Hölder's Inequality for Sums
snippet: Let $p, q \in \R_{>0}$ be strictly positive real numbers such that: $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$ Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$, that is, $\GF$ represents the set of either the real numbers or the complex numbers.

label: Ideal is Additive Normal Subgroup
snippet: Let $\left({R, +, \circ}\right)$ be a ring. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. Then $\left({J, +}\right)$ is a normal subgroup of $\left({R, +}\right)$.

label: Ideal is Filter in Dual Ordered Set
snippet: Let $P = \struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $X$ be a subset of $S$. Then $X$ is ideal in $P$ $X$ is filter in $P^{-1}$ where $P^{-1} = \struct {S, \succeq}$ denotes the dual of $P$.

label: Ideal of Unit is Whole Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity. Let $J$ be an ideal of $R$. If $J$ contains a unit of $R$, then $J = R$.

label: Identification Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T_1 = \struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ with respect to $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$. Then the identification mapping $f$ is continuous.

label: Identification Topology equals Quotient Topology on Induced Equivalence
snippet: Let $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$ be a topological space. Let $S_2$ be a set. Let $f: S_1 \to S_2$ be a surjective mapping. Let $\tau_2$ be the identification topology on $S_2$ $f$ and $\struct {S_1, \tau_1}$: $\tau_2 = \set {V \subseteq S_2 : f^{-1} \sqbrk V \in \tau_1}$ Let $\RR_f \subseteq S_1 \times S_1$ be the equivalence on $S_1$ induced by $f$: $\tuple {s_1, s_2} \in \RR_f \iff \map f {s_1} = \map f {s_2}$ Let $q_{\RR_f}$ be the quotient mapping induced by $\RR_f$.

label: Identity Element for Addition of Cuts
snippet: Let $\alpha$ be a cut. Let $0^*$ be the rational cut associated with the (rational) number $0$: $0^* = \set {r \in \Q: r < 0}$ Then: $\alpha + 0^* = \alpha$ where $+$ denotes the operation of addition of cuts.

label: Identity Element of Addition on Numbers
snippet: On all the number systems: natural numbers $\N$ integers $\Z$ rational numbers $\Q$ real numbers $\R$ complex numbers $\C$ the identity element of addition is zero ($0$).

label: Identity Mapping is Automorphism
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ on the algebraic structure $\struct {S, \circ}$ is an automorphism. Its image is $S$.

label: Identity Mapping is Bijection
snippet: The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ on the set $S$ is a bijection.

label: Identity Mapping is Continuous
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {I_S} x = x$ is a continuous mapping.

label: Identity Mapping is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. The identity mapping $I_T: T \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in T: \map {I_T} x = x$ is a homeomorphism.

label: Identity Mapping is Injection
snippet: On any set $S$, the identity mapping $I_S: S \to S$ is an injection.

label: Identity Mapping is Left Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $I_T \circ f = f$ where $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

label: Identity Mapping is Right Identity
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $f \circ I_S = f$ where $I_S$ is the identity mapping on $S$, and $\circ$ signifies composition of mappings.

label: Identity Morphism is Idempotent
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$ be a category. Let $X$ be an object of $\mathbf C$. Let $\operatorname{id}_X : X \to X$ denote the identity morphism of $X$. Then: $\operatorname{id}_X \circ \operatorname{id}_X = \operatorname{id}_X$

label: Identity of Cancellable Monoid is Identity of Submonoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid, all of whose elements are cancellable. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the identity of $\struct {T, \circ}$ is the same element as the identity of $\struct {S, \circ}$.

label: Identity of Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which has an identity element $e \in G$. Then $e$ is unique.

label: Identity of Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Then $S$ has a unique identity.

label: Identity of Subgroup
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of group $G$. Then the identity of $H$ is also $e$.

label: Identity of Submonoid is not necessarily Identity of Monoid
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be a submonoid of $\struct {S, \circ}$ whose identity is $e_T$. Then it is not necessarily the case that $e_T = e_S$.

label: Image is Subset of Codomain
snippet: Let $\RR = S \times T$ be a relation. For all subsets $A$ of the domain of $\RR$, the image of $A$ is a subset of the codomain of $\RR$: $\forall A \subseteq \Dom \RR: \RR \sqbrk A \subseteq T$ In the notation of direct image mappings, this can be written as: $\forall A \in \powerset S: \map {\RR^\to} A \in \powerset T$

label: Image of Closed Real Interval is Bounded
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Then $f$ is bounded on $\closedint a b$.

label: Image of Closed Set under Linear Isometry from Banach Space to Normed Vector Space is Closed
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_X}$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $\struct {Y, \norm {\, \cdot \,}_Y}$ be a normed vector space over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear isometry. Let $A$ be a closed subset of $X$. Then $T \sqbrk A$ is closed in $X$.

label: Image of Countable Set under Mapping is Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a countable set. Let $T$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then the image of $f$ is countable.

label: Image of Dilation of Set under Linear Transformation is Dilation of Image
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $E \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $\lambda \in K$. Then: $\map T {\lambda E} = \lambda \map T E$ where $\lambda E$ denotes the dilation of $E$ by $\lambda$.

label: Image of Empty Set is Empty Set
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. The image of the empty set is the empty set: $\RR \sqbrk \O = \O$

label: Image of Intersection under Injection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $\forall A, B \subseteq S: f \sqbrk {A \cap B} = f \sqbrk A \cap f \sqbrk B$ $f$ is an injection. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \subseteq S: \map {f^\to} {A \cap B} = \map {f^\to} A \cap \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Intersection under Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq f \sqbrk {S_1} \cap f \sqbrk {S_2}$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall S_1, S_2 \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq \map {f^\to} {S_1} \cap \map {f^\to} {S_2}$ That is, the image of the intersection of subsets of a mapping is a subset of the intersection of their images.

label: Image of Intersection under One-to-Many Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then: $\forall S_1, S_2 \subseteq S: \RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} = \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cap \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ $\RR$ is one-to-many.

label: Image of Intersection under Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cap S_2} \subseteq \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cap \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ That is, the image of the intersection of subsets of $S$ is a subset of the intersection of their images.

label: Image of Mapping from Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X, Y$ be sets. Let $f: X \to Y$ be a mapping. Let $X$ be a finite set. Then $f \sqbrk X$ is a finite set.

label: Image of Operator Generated by Closure System is Set of Closure System
snippet: Let $L = \struct {X, \vee, \wedge, \preceq}$ be a complete lattice. Let $S = \struct {T, \precsim}$ be a closure system of $L$. Then $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S \sqbrk X = T$ where $\map {\operatorname {operator} } S$ denotes the operator generated by $S$.

label: Image of Real Interval under Continuous Real Function is Real Interval
snippet: Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $f: I \to \R$ be a continuous real function. Then the image of $f$ is a real interval.

label: Image of Set Difference under Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk A \setminus \RR \sqbrk B \subseteq \RR \sqbrk {A \setminus B}$ where: $\setminus$ denotes set difference $\RR \sqbrk A$ denotes image of $A$ under $\RR$.

label: Image of Singleton under Mapping
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then the image of an element of $S$ is equal to the image of a singleton containing that element, the singleton being a subset of $S$: $\forall s \in S: \set {\map f s} = f \sqbrk {\set s}$

label: Image of Singleton under Relation
snippet: Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Then the image of an element of $S$ is equal to the image of a singleton containing that element, the singleton being a subset of $S$: $\forall s \in S: \map \RR s = \RR \sqbrk {\set s}$

label: Image of Small Class under Mapping is Small
snippet: Let $A$ be a mapping. Let $a$ be a small class. Then, the image of $a$ under $A$ is small.

label: Image of Submodule under Linear Transformation is Submodule
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_G}_R$ and $\struct {H, +_H, \circ_H}_R$ be $R$-modules. Let $\phi: G \to H$ be a linear transformation. Let $M$ be a submodule of $G$. Then $\phi \sqbrk M$ is a submodule of $H$.

label: Image of Subset under Mapping is Subset of Image
snippet: == Corollary to Image of Subset under Relation is Subset of Image == Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping from $S$ to $T$. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A \subseteq B$. Then the image of $A$ is a subset of the image of $B$: $A \subseteq B \implies f \sqbrk A \subseteq f \sqbrk B$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \in \powerset S: A \subseteq B \implies \map {f^\to} A \subseteq \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Subset under Relation equals Union of Images of Elements
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $X \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Then: $\ds \RR \sqbrk X = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \map \RR x$ where: $\RR \sqbrk X$ is the image of the subset $X$ under $\RR$ $\map \RR x$ is the image of the element $x$ under $\RR$.

label: Image of Subset under Relation is Subset of Image
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation from $S$ to $T$. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ such that $A \subseteq B$. Then the image of $A$ is a subset of the image of $B$: $A \subseteq B \implies \RR \sqbrk A \subseteq \RR \sqbrk B$ In the notation of direct image mappings, this can be written: $A \subseteq B \implies \map {\RR^\to} A \subseteq \map {\RR^\to} B$

label: Image of Translation of Set under Linear Transformation is Translation of Image
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Let $E \subseteq X$ be a non-empty set. Let $x \in X$. Then: $\map T {E + x} = \map T E + T x$ where $E + x$ denotes the translation of $E$ by $x$.

label: Image of Union under Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $f \sqbrk {A \cup B} = f \sqbrk A \cup f \sqbrk B$ This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings as: $\forall A, B \in \powerset S: \map {f^\to} {A \cup B} = \map {f^\to} A \cup \map {f^\to} B$

label: Image of Union under Relation
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be subsets of $S$. Then: $\RR \sqbrk {S_1 \cup S_2} = \RR \sqbrk {S_1} \cup \RR \sqbrk {S_2}$ That is, the image of the union of subsets of $S$ is equal to the union of their images.

label: Image of Vector Subspace under Linear Transformation is Vector Subspace
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ and $Y$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $U$ be a vector subspace of $X$. Let $T : X \to Y$ be a linear transformation. Then $T \sqbrk U$ is a vector subspace of $Y$.

label: Implicit Function Theorem
snippet: The Implicit Function Theorem gives conditions on derivatives which ensure that an implicitly defined set is the graph of a function.

label: Inclusion-Exclusion Principle
snippet: Let $\SS$ be an algebra of sets. Let $A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_n$ be finite sets. Let $f: \SS \to \R$ be an additive function. Then: {{eqn | l = \map f {\bigcup_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n \map f {A_i} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= - | r = \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop \le n} \map f {A_i \cap A_j} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= + | r = \sum_{1 \mathop \le i \mathop < j \mathop < k \mathop \le n} \map f {A_i \cap A_j \cap A_k} | c = }} {{eqn | o = | ro= + | r = \paren {-1}^{n - 1} \map f {\bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n A_i} | c = }}

label: Inclusion Mapping is Injection
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets such that $S$ is a subset of $T$. Then the inclusion mapping $i_S: S \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {i_S} x = x$ is an injection. For this reason the inclusion mapping can be known as the canonical injection of $S$ to $T$.

label: Increasing Sequence in Ordered Set Terminates iff Maximal Element
snippet: Let $\struct {P, \le}$ be an ordered set. $(1): \quad$ Every increasing sequence $x_1 \le x_2 \le x_3 \le \cdots$ with $x_i \in P$ eventually terminates: there is $n \in \N$ such that $x_n = x_{n + 1} = \cdots$. $(2): \quad$ Every non-empty subset of $P$ has a maximal element.

label: Index Laws for Monoids
snippet: These results are an extension of the results in Index Laws for Semigroup in which the domain of the indices is extended to include all integers. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $a \in S$ be invertible for $\circ$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $a^n$ be the $n$th power of $a$: $a^n = \begin{cases} e : & n = 0 \\ a^{n - 1} \circ a : & n > 0 \\ \paren {a^{-n}}^{-1} : & n < 0 \end{cases}$ Then we have the following results:

label: Indexed Summation does not Change under Permutation
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\sigma: \closedint a b \to \closedint a b$ be a permutation. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f {\map \sigma i}$

label: Indexed Summation of Multiple of Mapping
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $\lambda \in \mathbb A$. Let $g = \lambda \cdot f$ be the product of $f$ with $\lambda$. Then we have the equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map g i = \lambda \cdot \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i$

label: Indexed Summation of Sum of Mappings
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f, g: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be mappings. Let $h = f + g$ be their pointwise sum. Then we have the equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map h i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i + \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map g i$

label: Indexed Summation over Adjacent Intervals
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a, b, c$ be integers. Let $\closedint a c$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $c$. Let $b \in \closedint {a - 1} c$. Let $f : \closedint a c \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^c \map f i = \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i + \sum_{i \mathop = b + 1}^c \map f i$

label: Indexed Summation over Translated Interval
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ be the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f: \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Let $c\in\Z$ be an integer. Then we have an equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b f(i) = \sum_{i \mathop = a + c}^{b + c} \map f {i - c}$

label: Indiscrete Topology is Coarsest Topology
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an indiscrete topological space. $\tau$ is the coarsest topology on $S$. Hence it is comparable with all other topologies on $S$.

label: Indiscrete Topology is Topology
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau$ be the indiscrete topology on $S$. $\tau$ is a topology on $S$.

label: Induced Homomorphism of Polynomial Forms
snippet: Let $R$ and $S$ be commutative rings with unity. Let $\phi: R \to S$ be a ring homomorphism. Let $R \sqbrk X$ and $S \sqbrk X$ be the rings of polynomial forms over $R$ and $S$ respectively in the indeterminate $X$. Then the map $\overline \phi: R \sqbrk X \to S \sqbrk X$ given by: $\map {\overline \phi} {a_0 + a_1 X + \cdots + a_n X^n} = \map \phi {a_0} + \map \phi {a_1} X + \cdots + \map \phi {a_n} X^n$ is a ring homomorphism.

label: Induced Structure Identity
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $e$ be an identity for $\circ$. Then the constant mapping $f_e: S \to T$ defined as: $\forall x \in S: \map {f_e} x = e$ is the identity for the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$.

label: Induction of Finite Set
snippet: == Theorem Scheme == Let $A$ be finite set. Let $\map P -$ be a predicate. Let $\map P \O$. Let $\forall B \subseteq A, x \in A: \paren {\map P B \implies \map P {B \cup \set x} }$ Then: $\map P A$

label: Inductive Definition of Sequence
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $h \in \N$. Let $a_i \in X$ for all $i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, h}$. Let $S$ be the set of all finite sequences whose codomains are in $X$. Let $G: S \to X$ be a mapping. Then there is a unique sequence $f$ whose codomain is in $X$ such that: $f_i = \begin{cases} a_i & : i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, h} \\ \map G {f_1, f_2, \ldots, f_{i - 1} } & : i \ge h + 1 \end{cases}$

label: Inequality Rule for Real Convergent Nets
snippet: Let $\struct {\Lambda, \preceq}$ be a directed set. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ and $\family {y_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be indexed families of elements in $\R$. Let $\family {x_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ and $\family {y_\lambda}_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda}$ be convergent to the following limits: $\ds \lim_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} x_\lambda = l$ $\ds \lim_{\lambda \mathop \in \Lambda} y_\lambda = m$ Let there exist $\lambda \in \Lambda$ such that: $\forall \mu \in \Lambda : \lambda \preceq \mu: x_\mu \le y_\mu$ Then: $l \le m$

label: Inequality Rule for Real Sequences
snippet: Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be sequences in $\R$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ and $\sequence {y_n}$ be convergent to the following limits: {{eqn | l = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n | r = l }} {{eqn | l = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} y_n | r = m }} Let there exist $N \in \N$ such that: $\forall n \ge N: x_n \le y_n$ Then: $l \le m$

label: Inequality of Hölder Means
snippet: Let $p, q \in \overline \R$ be extended real numbers such that $p 0$. Then the Hölder mean satisfies the inequality: $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map {M_q} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ Equality holds : $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots = x_n$ or: $q < 0$ and $x_k = 0$ for at least one $k \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$. Note that in particular: $\forall p \in \R: \map {M_{-\infty} } {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \le \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ and: $\forall p \in \R: \map {M_\infty} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} \ge \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$

label: Infimum Plus Constant
snippet: Let $T$ be a subset of the set of real numbers. Let $T$ be bounded below. Let $\xi \in \R$. Then: $\ds \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } {x + \xi} = \xi + \map {\inf_{x \mathop \in T} } x$ where $\inf$ denotes infimum.

label: Infimum is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $T$ has at most one infimum in $S$.

label: Infimum of Empty Set is Greatest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Suppose that $\map \inf \O$, the infimum of the empty set, exists in $S$. Then $\forall s \in S: s \preceq \map \inf \O$. That is, $\map \inf \O$ is the greatest element of $S$.

label: Infimum of Infima
snippet: Let $\left({S, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $\mathbb T$ be a collection of subsets of $S$. Suppose all $T \in \mathbb T$ admit an infimum $\inf T$ in $S$. Then: $\inf \bigcup \mathbb T = \inf \left\{{\inf T: T \in \mathbb T}\right\}$ as soon as one of these two quantities exists.

label: Infimum of Subset
snippet: Let $\struct {U, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $S \subseteq U$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ admit an infimum in $U$. If $T$ also admits an infimum in $U$, then $\map \inf S \preceq \map \inf T$.

label: Infimum of Subset of Real Numbers is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers. Let $b$ be an infimum of $A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists x \in A: x - b < \epsilon$

label: Infinite Cyclic Group is Isomorphic to Integers
snippet: Let $G$ be an infinite cyclic group. Then $G$ is isomorphic to the additive group of integers: $G \cong \struct {\Z, +}$.
