label: Infinite Product of Analytic Functions is Analytic
snippet: Let $D \subset \C$ be an open set. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n: D \to \C$. Let $\ds \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty f_n$ converge locally uniformly to $f$. Then $f$ is analytic.

label: Infinite Product of Product of Sequence of n plus alpha over Sequence of n plus beta
snippet: $\ds \prod_{n \mathop \ge 1} \dfrac {\paren {n + \alpha_1} \cdots \paren {n + \alpha_k} } {\paren {n + \beta_1} \cdots \paren {n + \beta_k} } = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {1 + \beta_1} \cdots \map \Gamma {1 + \beta_k} } {\map \Gamma {1 + \alpha_1} \cdots \map \Gamma {1 + \alpha_k} }$ where: $\alpha_1 + \cdots + \alpha_k = \beta_1 + \cdots + \beta_k$ none of the $\beta$s is a negative integer.

label: Infinite Ramsey's Theorem
snippet: Let $k, n \in \N$. For any set $S$, let $S^{\paren n}$ denote the set $\set {\set {s_1, \ldots, s_n}: \text{each } s_i \in S}$ of cardinality $n$ subsets of $S$. Let $X$ be an infinite set. Then: for every partition $P$ of $X^{\paren n}$ into $k$ many components there is an infinite subset $Y \subseteq X$ such that: each member of $Y^{\paren n}$ is in the same component of $P$.

label: Infinite Sequence Property of Well-Founded Relation
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \RR}$ be a relational structure. Then $\RR$ is a well-founded relation there exists no infinite sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of elements of $S$ such that: $\forall n \in \N: \paren {a_{n + 1} \mathrel \RR a_n} \text { and } \paren {a_{n + 1} \ne a_n}$

label: Infinite Set has Countably Infinite Subset
snippet: Every infinite set has a countably infinite subset.

label: Infinite Set is Equivalent to Proper Subset
snippet: A set is infinite it is equivalent to one of its proper subsets.

label: Initial Segment of Ordinal is Ordinal
snippet: Let $S$ be an ordinal. Let $a \in S$. Then the initial segment $S_a = a$ of $S$ determined by $a$ is also an ordinal. In other words, every element of a (non-empty) ordinal is also an ordinal.

label: Initial Topology on Vector Space Generated by Linear Functionals is Locally Convex
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a vector space over $\GF$. Let $F$ be a set of linear functionals on $X$ that form a vector space over $\GF$. That is, for each $\lambda, \mu \in \GF$ and $f, g \in F$, we have: $\lambda f + \mu g \in F$ Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ generated by $F$. For each $f \in F$, define $p_f : X \to \R_{\ge 0}$ by: $\map {p_f} x = \cmod {\map f x}$ and let: $\PP = \set {p_f : f \in F}$ Then the standard topology on the locally convex space $\struct {X, \PP}$ is precisely $\tau$.

label: Injection Induces Well-Ordering
snippet: Let $\left({T, \le}\right)$ be a well-ordered set. Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\le_f$, the ordering induced by $f$, is a well-ordering.

label: Injection from Finite Set to Itself is Surjection
snippet: Let $S$ be a finite set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an injection. Then $f$ is also a surjection.

label: Injection has Surjective Left Inverse Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \ne \O$. Let $f: S \to T$ be a injection. Then there exists a surjection $g: T \to S$ such that: $g \circ f = I_S$

label: Injection iff Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $\card T$ denote the cardinal number of $T$. Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \sim \card S$ and $T \sim \card T$. Then: $\card S \le \card T $ there exists an injection $f: S \to T$.

label: Injection iff Left Cancellable
snippet: A mapping $f$ is an injection $f$ is left cancellable.

label: Injection iff Left Inverse
snippet: A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is an injection : $\exists g: T \to S: g \circ f = I_S$ where $g$ is a mapping. That is, $f$ has a left inverse.

label: Injection implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be an injection. Let $\card T$ denote the cardinal number of $T$. Let: $T \sim \card T$ where $\sim$ denotes set equivalence Then: $\card S \le \card T$

label: Injection is Bijection iff Inverse is Injection
snippet: Let $\phi: S \to T$ be an injection. Then $\phi$ is a bijection its inverse $\phi^{-1}$ is also an injection.

label: Injection to Image is Bijection
snippet: Let $f: S \rightarrowtail T$ be an injection. Let $X \subseteq T$ be the image of $f$. Then the restriction $f {\restriction_{S \times X}}: S \to X$ of $f$ to the image of $f$ is a bijection of $S$ onto $X$.

label: Injectively Path-Connected Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is injectively path-connected. Then $T$ is path-connected.

label: Inner Automorphism is Automorphism
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $x \in G$. Let $\kappa_x$ be the inner automorphism of $x$ in $G$. Then $\kappa_x$ is an automorphism of $G$.

label: Inner Limit in Hausdorff Space by Open Neighborhoods
snippet: Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in a Hausdorff topological space $\struct {\XX, \tau}$. Let $x \in \XX$. Let $\map \mho x := \set {V \in \tau:\ x \in V}$ denote the set of open neighborhoods of $x$. Let $\NN_\infty$ denote the set of cofinite subsets of $\N$: $\NN_\infty := \set {N \subset \N: \N \setminus N \text{ is finite} }$ Then the inner limit of $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set {x \in \XX: \forall V \in \map \mho x: \exists N \in \NN_\infty: \forall n \in N: C_n \cap V \ne \O}$ or equivalently: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set…

label: Inner Limit in Hausdorff Space by Set Closures
snippet: Let $\struct {\XX, \tau}$ be a Hausdorff space. Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in $\XX$. Then: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \bigcap_{N \mathop \in \NN_\infty^\#} \map \cl {\bigcup_{n \mathop \in N} C_n}$ where: $\cl$ denotes set closure $\NN_\infty^\#$ denotes the set of cofinal subsets of $\N$.

label: Inner Limit of Sequence of Sets in Normed Space
snippet: Let $\struct {\XX, \norm {\, \cdot \, } }$ be a normed vector space. Let $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of sets in $\XX$. The inner limit of $\sequence {C_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is: $\ds \liminf_n C_n = \set {x \in X: \lim_n \map d {x, C_n} = 0}$ where $d$ stands for the point-to-set distance mapping.

label: Inner Product is Continuous
snippet: Let $\struct {V, \innerprod \cdot \cdot}$ be a inner product space. Let $\norm \cdot$ be the inner product norm on $V$. Let $x, y \in V$. Let $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ and $\sequence {y_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be sequences converging in $\struct {V, \norm \cdot}$ to $x$ and $y$ respectively. Then we have: $\innerprod {x_n} {y_n} \to \innerprod x y$ as $n \to \infty$.

label: Inscribed Angle Theorem
snippet: An inscribed angle is equal to half the angle that is subtended by that arc. 300px Thus, in the figure above: $\angle ABC = \frac 1 2 \angle ADC$ In a circle the angle at the center is double of the angle at the circumference, when the angles have the same circumference as base.

label: Inscribing Circle in Regular Pentagon
snippet: In any given regular pentagon it is possible to inscribe a circle.

label: Integer Addition is Associative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x + \paren {y + z} = \paren {x + y} + z$

label: Integer Addition is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under addition: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a + b \in \Z$

label: Integer Addition is Commutative
snippet: The operation of addition on the set of integers $\Z$ is commutative: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x + y = y + x$

label: Integer Combination of Coprime Integers
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers, not both zero. Then: $a$ and $b$ are coprime there exists an integer combination of them equal to $1$: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a \perp b \iff \exists m, n \in \Z: m a + n b = 1$ In such an integer combination $m a + n b = 1$, the integers $m$ and $n$ are also coprime.

label: Integer Coprime to Factors is Coprime to Whole
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \Z$ be integers. Let: $a \perp b$ $a \perp c$ where $\perp$ denotes coprimality. Then: $a \perp b c$

label: Integer Coprime to all Factors is Coprime to Whole
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$. Let $\ds b = \prod_{j \mathop = 1}^r b_j$ Let $a$ be coprime to each of $b_1, \ldots, b_r$. Then $a$ is coprime to $b$.

label: Integer Divisor Results
snippet: Let $m, n \in \Z$ be integers. Let $m \divides n$ denote that $m$ is a divisor of $n$. The following results all hold:

label: Integer Multiples form Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, +, \times}$ is a commutative ring. Unless $n = 1$, $\struct {n \Z, +, \times}$ is not a ring with unity.

label: Integer Multiples under Addition form Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $n \Z$ be the set of integer multiples of $n$. Then $\struct {n \Z, +}$ is a countably infinite cyclic group. It is generated by $n$ and $-n$: $n \Z = \gen n$ $n \Z = \gen {-n}$ Hence $\struct {n \Z, +}$ can be justifiably referred to as the additive group of integer multiples.

label: Integer Multiplication Distributes over Addition
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is distributive over addition: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x \times \paren {y + z} = \paren {x \times y} + \paren {x \times z}$ $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: \paren {y + z} \times x = \paren {y \times x} + \paren {z \times x}$

label: Integer Multiplication has Zero
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ has a zero element, which is $0$.

label: Integer Multiplication is Associative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is associative: $\forall x, y, z \in \Z: x \times \paren {y \times z} = \paren {x \times y} \times z$

label: Integer Multiplication is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under multiplication: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a \times b \in \Z$

label: Integer Multiplication is Commutative
snippet: The operation of multiplication on the set of integers $\Z$ is commutative: $\forall x, y \in \Z: x \times y = y \times x$

label: Integer Subtraction is Closed
snippet: The set of integers is closed under subtraction: $\forall a, b \in \Z: a - b \in \Z$

label: Integer as Sum of Three Squares
snippet: Let $r$ be a positive integer. Then $r$ can be expressed as the sum of three squares it is not of the form: $4^n \paren {8 m + 7}$ for some $m, n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$.

label: Integer equals Ceiling iff Number between Integer and One Less
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\ceiling x$ be the ceiling of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ceiling x = n \iff n - 1 < x \le n$

label: Integer equals Floor iff Number between Integer and One More
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Let $\floor x$ denote the floor of $x$. Let $n \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\floor x = n \iff n \le x < n + 1$

label: Integer is Congruent to Integer less than Modulus
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$. Then each integer is congruent (modulo $m$) to precisely one of the integers $0, 1, \ldots, m - 1$.

label: Integer is Coprime to 1
snippet: Every integer is coprime to $1$. That is: $\forall n \in \Z: n \perp 1$

label: Integer is Expressible as Product of Primes
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that $n > 1$. Then $n$ can be expressed as the product of one or more primes.

label: Integer to Power of Multiple of Order
snippet: Let $a$ and $n$ be integers. Let $a \perp n$, that is, let $a$ and $b$ be coprime. Let $c \in \Z_{>0}$ be the multiplicative order of $a$ modulo $n$. Then $a^k \equiv 1 \pmod n$ $k$ is a multiple of $c$.

label: Integers Divided by GCD are Coprime
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$ be integers which are not both zero. Let $d$ be a common divisor of $a$ and $b$, that is: $\dfrac a d, \dfrac b d \in \Z$ Then: $\gcd \set {a, b} = d$ $\gcd \set {\dfrac a d, \dfrac b d} = 1$ that is: $\dfrac a {\gcd \set {a, b} } \perp \dfrac b {\gcd \set {a, b} }$ where: $\gcd$ denotes greatest common divisor $\perp$ denotes coprimality.

label: Integers Modulo m under Addition form Cyclic Group
snippet: Let $\Z_m$ be the set of integers modulo $m$. Let $+_m$ be the operation of addition modulo $m$. Let $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ denote the additive group of integers modulo $m$. Then $\struct {\Z_m, +_m}$ is a cyclic group of order $m$, generated by the element $\eqclass 1 m \in \Z_m$.

label: Integers are Countably Infinite
snippet: The set $\Z$ of integers is countably infinite.

label: Integers are Euclidean Domain
snippet: The integers $\Z$ with the mapping $\nu: \Z \to \Z$ defined as: $\forall x \in \Z: \map \nu x = \size x$ form a Euclidean domain.

label: Integers form Commutative Ring
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ forms a commutative ring under addition and multiplication.

label: Integers form Integral Domain
snippet: The set of integers $\Z$ form an integral domain under addition and multiplication.

label: Integers form Ordered Integral Domain
snippet: The integers $\Z$ form an ordered integral domain under addition and multiplication.

label: Integers form Subdomain of Rationals
snippet: The integral domain of integers $\left({\Z, +, \times}\right)$ forms a subdomain of the field of rational numbers.

label: Integers form Totally Ordered Ring
snippet: The structure $\struct {\Z, +, \times, \le}$ is a totally ordered ring.

label: Integers under Addition form Abelian Group
snippet: The set of integers under addition $\struct {\Z, +}$ forms an abelian group.

label: Integers under Addition form Infinite Cyclic Group
snippet: The additive group of integers $\struct {\Z, +}$ is an infinite cyclic group which is generated by the element $1 \in \Z$.

label: Integers under Multiplication form Monoid
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a monoid.

label: Integers under Multiplication form Semigroup
snippet: The set of integers under multiplication $\struct {\Z, \times}$ is a semigroup.

label: Integrable Function is A.E. Real-Valued
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then $\map f x \in \R$ for almost all $x \in X$.

label: Integral Multiple Distributes over Ring Addition
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \times}$ be a ring, or a field. Let $a, b \in R$ and $m, n \in \Z$. Then: $(1): \quad \paren {m + n} \cdot a = \paren {m \cdot a} + \paren {n \cdot a}$ $(2): \quad m \cdot \paren {a + b} = \paren {m \cdot a} + \paren {m \cdot b}$ where $m \cdot a$ is as defined in integral multiple.

label: Integral Representation of Riemann Zeta Function in terms of Gamma Function
snippet: For $\Re \paren s > 1$, the Riemann Zeta function is given by: $\ds \map \zeta s = \frac 1 {\map \Gamma s} \int_0^\infty \frac {t^{s - 1}} {e^t - 1} \rd t$ where $\Gamma$ is the Gamma function.

label: Integral of Characteristic Function
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $E \in \Sigma$ be a measurable set, and let $\chi_E: X \to \R$ be its characteristic function. Then $\map {I_\mu} {\chi_E} = \map \mu E$, where $\map {I_\mu} {\chi_E}$ is the $\mu$-integral of $\chi_E$.

label: Integral of Integrable Function is Additive
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \R$ be $\mu$-integrable functions. Then $f + g$ is $\mu$-integrable, with: $\ds \int \paren {f + g} \rd \mu = \int f \rd \mu + \int g \rd \mu$

label: Integral of Integrable Function is Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Let $\lambda \in \R$. Let $\lambda f$ be the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$. Then $\lambda f$ is $\mu$-integrable, and: $\ds \int \lambda f \rd \mu = \lambda \int f \rd \mu$

label: Integral of Integrable Function over Measurable Set is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $E \in \Sigma$. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then the $\mu$-integral of $f$ over $E$: $\ds \int_E f \rd \mu = \int f \cdot \chi_E \rd \mu$ is well-defined.

label: Integral of Positive Measurable Function as Limit of Integrals of Positive Simple Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. For each $n \in \N$, let $f_n : X \to \R$ be a positive simple function, such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} f_n = f$ and: for each $x \in X$, the sequence $\sequence {\map {f_n} x}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is increasing where $\lim$ denotes a pointwise limit. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the integral signs denote $\mu$-integration.

label: Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Monotone
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f, g: X \to \overline \R$ be positive $\Sigma$-measurable functions. Suppose that $f \le g$, where $\le$ denotes pointwise inequality. Then: $\ds \int f \rd \mu \le \int g \rd \mu$ where the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration. This can be summarized by saying that $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ is monotone.

label: Integral of Positive Measurable Function is Positive Homogeneous
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a positive $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $\lambda \in \overline \R$ be an extended real number with $\lambda \ge 0$. Then: $\ds \int \lambda f \rd \mu = \lambda \int f \rd \mu$ where: $\lambda f$ is the pointwise $\lambda$-multiple of $f$ The integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration This can be summarized by saying that $\ds \int \cdot \rd \mu$ is positive homogeneous.

label: Integral of Power
snippet: $\ds \forall n \in \R_{\ne -1}: \int_0^b x^n \rd x = \frac {b^{n + 1} } {n + 1}$

label: Integral of Series of Positive Measurable Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N} \in \MM_{\overline \R}^+$, $f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be a sequence of positive measurable functions. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n: X \to \overline \R$ be the pointwise series of the $f_n$. Then: $\ds \int \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} f_n \rd \mu = \sum_{n \mathop \in \N} \int f_n \rd \mu$ where the integral sign denotes $\mu$-integration.

label: Integral over 2 pi of Cosine of n x
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \cos m x \rd x = \begin {cases} 0 & : m \ne 0 \\ 2 \pi & : m = 0 \end {cases}$

label: Integral over 2 pi of Sine of n x
snippet: Let $m \in \Z$ be an integer. Then: $\ds \int_\alpha^{\alpha + 2 \pi} \sin m x \rd x = 0$

label: Integral to Infinity of Exponential of -t^2
snippet: $\ds \int_0^\infty \map \exp {-t^2} \rd t = \dfrac {\sqrt \pi} 2$

label: Integrating Factor for First Order ODE
snippet: Let the first order ordinary differential equation: $(1): \quad \map M {x, y} + \map N {x, y} \dfrac {\d y} {\d x} = 0$ be non-homogeneous and not exact. By Existence of Integrating Factor, if $(1)$ has a general solution, there exists an integrating factor $\map \mu {x, y}$ such that: $\ds \map \mu {x, y} \paren {\map M {x, y} + \map N {x, y} \frac {\d y} {\d x} } = 0$ is an exact differential equation.

label: Integration by Parts
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $f$ and $g$ have primitives $F$ and $G$ respectively on $\closedint a b$. Then:

label: Integration by Substitution
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a real function which has a derivative on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $I$ be an open interval which contains the image of $\closedint a b$ under $\phi$. Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on $I$.

label: Interior Extremum Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let $f$ have a local minimum or local maximum at $\xi \in \openint a b$. Then: $\map {f'} \xi = 0$

label: Interior equals Complement of Closure of Complement
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Let $H^-$ denote the closure of $H$ and $H^\circ$ denote the interior of $H$. Let $H^\prime$ denote the complement of $H$ in $T$: $H^\prime = T \setminus H$ Then: $H^\circ = H^{\prime \, - \, \prime}$

label: Interior of Finite Intersection equals Intersection of Interiors
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $n \in \N$. Let: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, n}: H_i \subseteq T$ Then: $\ds \paren {\bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i}^\circ = \bigcap_{i \mathop = 1}^n H_i^\circ$ where $H_i^\circ$ denotes the interior of $H_i$.

label: Interior of Open Set
snippet: Let $T = \left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $U \subseteq T$ be open in $T$. Then: $U^\circ = U \iff U \in \tau$ where $U^\circ$ is the interior of $U$. That is, a subset of $S$ is open in $T$ it equals its interior.

label: Interior of Simple Closed Contour is Well-Defined
snippet: Let $C$ be a simple closed contour in the complex plane. Let $f : \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve. Let $\phi : \R^2 \to \C$ be defined by: $\map \phi {x, y} = x + i y$ Let $\Img C = \map \phi {\Img f}$, where $\Img C$ denotes the image of $C$, and $\Img f$ denotes the image of $f$. Then the interior of $C$: $\Int C = \map \phi {\Int f}$ is well-defined. Here, $\Int f$ denotes the interior of $f$.

label: Interior of Subset
snippet: Let $\left({S, \tau}\right)$ be a topological space. Let $X$ and $Y$ be subsets of $S$, and suppose that $X \subseteq Y$. Then: $X^\circ \subseteq Y^\circ$ where $X^\circ$ denotes the interior of $X$.

label: Intermediate Value Theorem
snippet: Let $I \subseteq \R$ be a real interval. Let $f: I \to \R$ be continuous on $I$. Then $f$ is a Darboux function. That is: Let $a, b \in I$. Let $k \in \R$ lie between $\map f a$ and $\map f b$. That is, either: $\map f a < k < \map f b$ or: $\map f b < k < \map f a$ Then $\exists c \in \openint a b$ such that $\map f c = k$.

label: Internal Angles of Regular Polygon
snippet: The size $A$ of each internal angle of a regular $n$-gon is given by: $A = \dfrac {\paren {n - 2} 180 \degrees} n$

label: Internal Group Direct Product/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Internal Group Direct Products ==

label: Intersecting Chords Theorem
snippet: Let $AC$ and $BD$ both be chords of the same circle. Let $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at $E$. Then $AE \cdot EC = DE \cdot EB$. If in a circle two straight lines cut one another, the rectangle contained by the segments of the one is equal to the rectangle contained by the segments of the other.

label: Intersection Distributes over Union
snippet: Set intersection is distributive over set union: $R \cap \paren {S \cup T} = \paren {R \cap S} \cup \paren {R \cap T}$

label: Intersection Measure is Measure
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $F \in \Sigma$ be a measurable set. Then the intersection measure $\mu_F$ is a measure on the measurable space $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

label: Intersection With Singleton is Disjoint if Not Element
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\set x$ be the singleton of $x$. Then: $x \notin S$ $\set x \cap S = \O$

label: Intersection is Commutative
snippet: Set intersection is commutative: $S \cap T = T \cap S$

label: Intersection is Decreasing
snippet: Let $U$ be a set. Let $\FF$ and $\GG$ be sets of subsets of $U$. Then $\FF \subseteq \GG \implies \bigcap \GG \subseteq \bigcap \FF$, where by convention $\bigcap \O = U$. That is, $\bigcap$ is a decreasing mapping from $\struct {\powerset {\powerset U}, \subseteq}$ to $\struct {\powerset U, \subseteq}$, where $\powerset U$ is the power set of $U$.

label: Intersection is Largest Subset
snippet: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be sets. Then $T_1 \cap T_2$ is the largest set contained in both $T_1$ and $T_2$. That is: $S \subseteq T_1 \land S \subseteq T_2 \iff S \subseteq T_1 \cap T_2$

label: Intersection is Subset
snippet: The intersection of two sets is a subset of each: $S \cap T \subseteq S$ $S \cap T \subseteq T$

label: Intersection is Subset of Union
snippet: The intersection of two sets is a subset of their union: $S \cap T \subseteq S \cup T$

label: Intersection of Closed Sets is Closed
Intersection of Convex Sets is Convex Set (Vector Spaces)
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space over $\R$ or $\C$. Let $\CC$ be a family of convex subsets of $V$. Then the intersection $\ds \bigcap \CC$ is also a convex subset of $V$.

label: Intersection of Doubleton
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\set {x, y}$ be a doubleton. Then $\bigcap \set {x, y}$ is a set such that: $\bigcap \set {x, y} = x \cap y$

label: Intersection of Empty Set
snippet: Consider the set of sets $\mathbb S$ such that $\mathbb S$ is the empty set $\O$. Then the intersection of $\mathbb S$ is $\mathbb U$: $\mathbb S = \O \implies \bigcap \mathbb S = \mathbb U$ where $\mathbb U$ is the universal set. A paradoxical result.

label: Intersection of Finitely Many Kernels of Linear Functionals in Infinite-Dimensional Vector Space is Infinite-Dimensional with Finite Codimension
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $X$ be an infinite-dimensional vector space over $K$. Let $X^\#$ be the algebraic dual of $X$. Let $F$ be a non-empty finite subset of $X^\#$. We then have that: $\ds \map {\operatorname {dim} } {\bigcap_{f \in F} \map \ker f} = \infty$ and: $\ds \map {\operatorname {codim} } {\bigcap_{F \in F} \map \ker f} < \infty$ where $\ker$ denotes the kernel. In particular: $\ds \bigcap_{f \in F} \map \ker f \ne \set { {\mathbf 0}_X}$

label: Intersection of Neighborhoods in Topological Space is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $M, N$ be a neighborhoods of $x$ in $T$. Then $M \cap N$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. That is: $\forall x \in S: \forall M, N \in \NN_x: M \cap N \in N_x$ where $\NN_x$ is the neighborhood filter of $x$.

label: Intersection of Non-Empty Class is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a non-empty class. Let $\bigcap A$ denote the intersection of $A$. Then $\bigcap A$ is a set.

label: Intersection of Normal Subgroups is Normal
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {N_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a non-empty indexed family of normal subgroups of $G$. Then $\ds \bigcap_{i \mathop \in I} N_i$ is a normal subgroup of $G$.

label: Intersection of Order-Convex Sets is Order-Convex
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $\CC$ be a set of order-convex sets in $S$. Then $\bigcap \CC$ is order-convex.

label: Intersection of Singleton
snippet: Consider the set of sets $A$ such that $A$ consists of just one set $x$: $A = \set x$ Then the intersection of $A$ is $x$: $\bigcap A = x$

label: Intersection of Subgroups is Subgroup
snippet: The intersection of two subgroups of a group is itself a subgroup of that group: $\forall H_1, H_2 \le \struct {G, \circ}: H_1 \cap H_2 \le G$ It also follows that $H_1 \cap H_2 \le H_1$ and $H_1 \cap H_2 \le H_2$.

label: Intersection of Transitive Relations is Transitive
snippet: The intersection of two transitive relations is also a transitive relation.

label: Intersection with Complement
snippet: The intersection of a set and its complement is the empty set: $S \cap \map \complement S = \O$

label: Intersection with Complement is Empty iff Subset
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \cap \map \complement T = \O$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cap T$ denotes the intersection of $S$ and $T$ $\O$ denotes the empty set $\complement$ denotes set complement.

label: Intersection with Empty Set
snippet: The intersection of any set with the empty set is itself the empty set: $S \cap \O = \O$

label: Intersection with Relative Complement is Empty
snippet: The intersection of a set and its relative complement is the empty set: $T \cap \relcomp S T = \O$

label: Intersection with Set Difference is Set Difference with Intersection
snippet: Let $R, S, T$ be sets. Then: $\left({R \setminus S}\right) \cap T = \left({R \cap T}\right) \setminus S$ where: $R \setminus S$ denotes set difference $R \cap T$ denotes set intersection.

label: Intersection with Subset is Subset
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \cap T = S$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cap T$ denotes the intersection of $S$ and $T$.

label: Intersection with Universal Set
snippet: The intersection of a set with the universal set is the set itself: $\mathbb U \cap S = S$

label: Inverse Element of Bijection
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $f: S \to T$ be a bijection. Then: $\map {f^{-1} } y = x \iff \map f x = y$ where $f^{-1}$ is the inverse mapping of $f$.

label: Inverse Image Mapping of Relation is Mapping
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $\RR \subseteq S \times T$ be a relation on $S \times T$. Let $\RR^\gets$ be the inverse image mapping of $\RR$: $\RR^\gets: \powerset T \to \powerset S: \map {\RR^\gets} Y = \RR^{-1} \sqbrk Y$ Then $\RR^\gets$ is indeed a mapping.

label: Inverse for Complex Addition
snippet: Let $z = x + i y \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $-z = -x - i y \in \C$ be the negative of $z$. Then $-z$ is the inverse element of $z$ under the operation of complex addition: $\forall z \in \C: \exists -z \in \C: z + \paren {-z} = 0 = \paren {-z} + z$

label: Inverse for Complex Multiplication
Inverse for Real Addition
snippet: Each element $x$ of the set of real numbers $\R$ has an inverse element $-x$ under the operation of real number addition: $\forall x \in \R: \exists -x \in \R: x + \paren {-x} = 0 = \paren {-x} + x$

label: Inverse for Real Multiplication
Inverse in Group is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Then every element $x \in G$ has exactly one inverse: $\forall x \in G: \exists_1 x^{-1} \in G: x \circ x^{-1} = e^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ x$ where $e$ is the identity element of $\struct {G, \circ}$.

label: Inverse in Monoid is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid. Then an element $x \in S$ can have at most one inverse for $\circ$.

label: Inverse of Algebraic Structure Isomorphism is Isomorphism
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be a mapping. Then $\phi$ is an isomorphism $\phi^{-1}: \struct {T, *} \to \struct {S, \circ}$ is also an isomorphism.

label: Inverse of Commuting Pair
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e_S$. Let $x, y \in S$ such that $x$ and $y$ are both invertible. Then $x$ commutes with $y$ : $\struct {x \circ y}^{-1} = x^{-1} \circ y^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Diagonal Matrix
snippet: Let: $\mathbf D = \begin{bmatrix} a_{11} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & a_{22} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & a_{nn} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ be an $n \times n$ diagonal matrix. Then its inverse is given by: $\mathbf D^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac 1 {a_{11}} & 0 & \cdots & 0 \\ 0 & \dfrac 1 {a_{22}} & \cdots & 0 \\ \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0 & 0 & \cdots & \dfrac 1 {a_{nn}} \\ \end{bmatrix}$ provided that none of the diagonal elements are zero. If any of the diagonal elements are zero, $\mathbf D$ is singular.

label: Inverse of Group Product
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $a, b \in G$, with inverses $a^{-1}, b^{-1}$. Then: $\paren {a \circ b}^{-1} = b^{-1} \circ a^{-1}$

label: Inverse of Homeomorphism is Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T, T'$ be topological spaces. Let $f: T \to T'$ be a homeomorphism. Then $f^{-1}: T' \to T$ is also a homeomorphism.

label: Inverse of Linear Transformation is Linear Transformation
snippet: Let $K$ be a field. Let $V$ and $U$ be vector spaces over $K$. Let $A : V \to U$ be an invertible (in the sense of a mapping) linear transformation with inverse mapping $A^{-1} : U \to V$. Then $A^{-1}$ is a linear transformation.

label: Inverse of Matrix Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf {A, B}$ be square matrices of order $n$ Let $\mathbf I$ be the $n \times n$ unit matrix. Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be nonsingular. Then the matrix product $\mathbf {AB}$ is also nonsingular, and: $\paren {\mathbf A \mathbf B}^{-1} = \mathbf B^{-1} \mathbf A^{-1}$

label: Invertibility of Identity Minus Operator
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a Banach space over $\GF$. Let $T : X \to X$ be a bounded linear operator such that: $\norm T_{\map \BB X} < 1$ where $\norm {\, \cdot \,}_{\map \BB X}$ denotes the norm of a bounded linear operator. Then $I - T$ is invertible as a bounded linear operator. In particular: $\ds \paren {I - T}^{-1} = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty T^n$

label: Invertible Element of Associative Structure is Cancellable
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure where $\circ$ is associative. Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ have an identity element $e_S$. An element of $\struct {S, \circ}$ which is invertible is also cancellable.

label: Involution is Permutation
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $f: S \to S$ be an involution. Then $f$ is a permutation.

label: Irrational Slope Space is T2
snippet: Let $T$ be an irrational slope space. Then $T$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: Irreducible Hausdorff Space is Singleton
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a non-empty topological space which is irreducible and Hausdorff. Then $S$ is a singleton.

label: Irreducible Space is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is irreducible. Then $T$ is connected.

label: Isomorphism Preserves Commutativity
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ and $\struct {T, *}$ be algebraic structures. Let $\phi: \struct {S, \circ} \to \struct {T, *}$ be an isomorphism. Then $\circ$ is commutative $*$ is commutative.

label: Isosceles Triangle has Two Equal Angles
snippet: In isosceles triangles, the angles at the base are equal to each other. Also, if the equal straight lines are extended, the angles under the base will also be equal to each other.

label: Jensen's Inequality
snippet: Jensen's Inequality (Real Analysis) Jensen's Inequality (Complex Analysis) Jensen's Inequality (Measure Theory) Conditional Jensen's Inequality Category:Jensen's Inequality

label: Jensen's Inequality (Real Analysis)
snippet: Let $I$ be a real interval. Let $\phi: I \to \R$ be a convex function. Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in I$. Let $\lambda_1, \lambda_2, \ldots, \lambda_n \ge 0$ be real numbers, at least one of which is non-zero. Then: $\ds \map \phi {\frac {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k x_k} {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k} } \le \frac {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k \map \phi {x_k} } {\sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \lambda_k}$ For $\phi$ strictly convex, equality holds $x_1 = x_2 = \cdots = x_n$.

label: Joining Paths makes Another Path
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $I \subseteq \R$ be the closed real interval $\closedint 0 1$. Let $f, g: I \to T$ be paths in $T$ from $a$ to $b$ and from $b$ to $c$ respectively. Let $h: I \to T$ be the mapping given by: $\map h x = \begin{cases} \map f {2x} & : x \in \closedint 0 {\dfrac 1 2} \\ \map g {2x - 1} & : x \in \closedint {\dfrac 1 2} 1 \end{cases}$ Then $h$ is a path in $T$.

label: Jordan-Hölder Theorem
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ be two composition series for $G$. Then: $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ have the same length Corresponding factors of $\HH_1$ and $\HH_2$ are isomorphic.

label: Jordan Curve Theorem
snippet: Let $\gamma: \closedint 0 1 \to \R^2$ be a Jordan curve. Let $\Img \gamma$ denote the image of $\gamma$. Then $\R^2 \setminus \Img \gamma$ is a union of two disjoint connected components. Both components are open in $\R^2$, and both components have $\Img \gamma$ as their boundary. One component is bounded, and is called the interior of $\gamma$. The other component is unbounded, and is called the exterior of $\gamma$.

label: Kakutani's Theorem
snippet: Let $X$ be a normed vector space. Let $w$ be the weak topology on $X$. Let $B_X^-$ be the closed unit ball in $X$. Let $X^{\ast \ast}$ be the second normed dual of $X$. Then $X$ is reflexive $\struct {B_X^-, w}$ is compact.

label: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion
snippet: == Physical Laws == Kepler's laws of planetary motion are a set of three physical laws that describe the motion of planets in the solar system.

label: Kernel is Normal Subgroup of Domain
snippet: Let $\phi$ be a group homomorphism. Then the kernel of $\phi$ is a normal subgroup of the domain of $\phi$: $\map \ker \phi \lhd \Dom \phi$

label: Kernel of Group Homomorphism is Subgroup
snippet: The kernel of a group homomorphism is a subgroup of its domain: $\map \ker \phi \le \Dom \phi$

label: Kernel of Linear Transformation contains Zero Vector
snippet: == Corollary to Linear Transformation Maps Zero Vector to Zero Vector == Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0$. Likewise let $\mathbf V'$ be another vector space, with zero $\mathbf 0'$. Let $T: \mathbf V \to \mathbf V'$ be a linear transformation. Then: $\mathbf 0 \in \map \ker T$ where $\map \ker T$ is the kernel of $T$.

label: Kernel of Linear Transformation is Orthocomplement of Image of Adjoint
snippet: Let $\struct {\HH, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\HH}$ and $\struct {\KK, \innerprod \cdot \cdot_\KK}$ be Hilbert spaces. Let $\map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ denote the set of bounded linear transformations from $\HH$ to $\KK$. Let $A \in \map \BB {\HH, \KK}$ be a bounded linear transformation. Then $\ker A = \paren {\Img {A^*} }^\perp$, where: $A^*$ denotes the adjoint of $A$ $\ker A$ is the kernel of $A$ $\Img {A^*}$ is the image of $A^*$ $\perp$ signifies orthocomplementation

label: Kernel of Orthogonal Projection
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space. Let $K$ be a closed linear subspace of $H$. Let $P_K$ denote the orthogonal projection on $K$. Then: $\ker P_K = K^\bot$ where: $\ker P_K$ denotes the kernel of $P_K$ $K^\bot$ denotes the orthocomplement of $K$.

label: Kernel of Quotient Mapping
snippet: Let $V$ be a vector space. Let $M$ be a subspace of $V$. Let $Q: V \to V / M$ be the quotient mapping. Then: $\ker Q = M$ where $\ker Q$ is the kernel of $Q$.

label: Kernel of Ring Homomorphism is Ideal
snippet: Let $\phi: \struct {R_1, +_1, \circ_1} \to \struct {R_2, +_2, \circ_2}$ be a ring homomorphism. The kernel of $\phi$ is an ideal of $R_1$.

label: Kinetic Energy of Motion
snippet: == Physical Law == Let $B$ be a body of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ such that $v$ is very much less than the speed of light. Then its kinetic energy $K$ is given by: $K = \dfrac {m v^2} 2$

label: Kleene's Normal Form Theorem
snippet: For each integer $k \ge 1$, there exists: a primitive recursive $k + 1$-ary relation $T_k$ a primitive recursive function $U: \N \to \N$ such that a partial function $f: \N^k \to \N$ is recursive , for some $e \in \N$ and all $\tuple {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} \in \N^k$: $\map f {n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k} \approx \map U {\mu z \ \map {T_k} {e, n_1, n_2, \ldots, n_k, z} }$

label: Klein Four-Group/Cayley Table
snippet: == Cayley Table for Klein $4$-Group == The Klein $4$-group can be described completely by showing its Cayley table: $\quad \begin {array} {c|cccc} & e & a & b & c \\ \hline e & e & a & b & c \\ a & a & e & c & b \\ b & b & c & e & a \\ c & c & b & a & e \\ \end {array}$

label: Korselt's Theorem
snippet: Let $n \ge 2$ be an integer. Then $n$ is a Carmichael number : $(1): \quad n$ is odd and the following conditions hold for every prime factor $p$ of $n$: $(2): \quad p^2 \nmid n$ $(3): \quad \paren {p - 1} \divides \paren {n - 1}$ where: $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\nmid$ denotes non-divisibility.

label: Krull's Theorem
snippet: Let $R$ be a non-null ring with unity. Then $R$ has a maximal ideal.

label: Kruskal's Algorithm
snippet: == Algorithm == The purpose Kruskal's Algorithm is to produce a minimum spanning tree for any given weighted graph $G$. Step 1: Start with the edgeless graph $T$ whose vertices correspond with those of $G$. Step 2: Choose an edge $e$ of $G$ such that: a): Adding $e$ to $T$ would not make a cycle in $T$; b): $e$ has the minimum weight of all the edges remaining in $G$ that fulfil the condition in a). Step 3: Add $e$ to $T$. Step 4: If $T$ spans $G$, stop. Otherwise, go to Step 2. The above constitutes an algorithm, for the following reasons:

label: Kummer's Hypergeometric Theorem
snippet: Let $x, n \in \C$. Let $n \notin \Z_{ 0$. Then: $\map F {n, -x; x + n + 1; -1} = \dfrac {\map \Gamma {x + n + 1} \map \Gamma {\dfrac n 2 + 1} } {\map \Gamma {x + \dfrac n 2 + 1} \map \Gamma {n + 1} }$ where: $\map F {n, -x; x + n + 1; -1}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $-1$ $\map \Gamma {n + 1} = n!$ is the Gamma function.

label: Kummer's Quadratic Transformation
snippet: Let $a, b \in \C$. Let $z \in \R$ such that $z < 3 - 2 \sqrt 2$. Let $\size z < 1$. Then: $\ds \map F {a, b; 1 + a - b; z} = \paren {1 - z}^{-a} \map F {\dfrac a 2, \dfrac {1 + a} 2 - b; 1 + a - b; \dfrac {-4 z} {\paren {1 - z}^2} }$ where: $\map F {a, b; 1 + a - b; z}$ is the Gaussian hypergeometric function of $z$: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 0}^\infty \dfrac { a^{\overline k} b^{\overline k} } {\paren {1 + a - b}^{\overline k} } \dfrac {z^k} {k!}$ $x^{\overline k}$ denotes the $k$th rising factorial power of $x$ $\map \Gamma {n + 1} = n!$ is the Gamma function.

label: Kurtosis in terms of Non-Central Moments
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable with expectation $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. Then the kurtosis $\alpha_4$ of $X$ is given by: $\ds \alpha_4 = \dfrac {\expect {X^4} - 4 \mu \expect {X^3} + 6 \mu^2 \expect {X^2} - 3 \mu^4} {\sigma^4}$

label: König's Tree Lemma
snippet: Let $T$ be a rooted tree with an infinite number of nodes, each with a finite number of children. Then $T$ has a branch of infinite length.

label: L'Hôpital's Rule
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Let: $\forall x \in \openint a b: \map {g'} x \ne 0$ where $g'$ denotes the derivative of $g$ $x$. Let: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map f x = \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \map g x = 0$ Then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \frac {\map f x} {\map g x} = \lim_{x \mathop \to a^+} \frac {\map {f'} x} {\map {g'} x}$ provided that the second limit exists.

label: L-2 Space forms Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $\struct{ X, \Sigma, \mu }$ be a measure space. Let $\map {L^2} \mu$ be the $L^2$ space of $\mu$. Let $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ be the inner product on $\map {L^2} \mu$. Then $\map {L^2} \mu$ endowed with $\innerprod \cdot \cdot$ is a Hilbert space.

label: LCM from Prime Decomposition
snippet: Let $a, b \in \Z$. From Expression for Integers as Powers of Same Primes, let: {{eqn | l = a | r = p_1^{k_1} p_2^{k_2} \ldots p_r^{k_r} }} {{eqn | l = b | r = p_1^{l_1} p_2^{l_2} \ldots p_r^{l_r} }} {{eqn | q = \forall i \in \set {1, 2, \dotsc, r} | l = p_i | o = \divides | r = a | c = }} That is, the primes given in these prime decompositions may be divisors of either of the numbers $a$ or $b$. Then: $\lcm \set {a, b} = p_1^{\max \set {k_1, l_1} } p_2^{\max \set {k_2, l_2} } \ldots p_r^{\max \set {k_r, l_r} }$ where $\lcm \set {a, b}$ denotes the lowest common multiple of $a$ and $b$.

label: Lagrange's Formula
snippet: Let $\mathbf a$, $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ be vectors in a vector space $\mathbf V$ of $3$ dimensions. Then: $\mathbf a \times \paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf c} = \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf c} \mathbf b - \paren {\mathbf a \cdot \mathbf b} \mathbf c$

label: Lagrange's Four Square Theorem
snippet: Every positive integer can be expressed as a sum of four squares.

label: Lagrange's Theorem (Group Theory)
snippet: Let $G$ be a finite group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then: $\order H$ divides $\order G$ where $\order G$ and $\order H$ are the order of $G$ and $H$ respectively. In fact: $\index G H = \dfrac {\order G} {\order H}$ where $\index G H$ is the index of $H$ in $G$. When $G$ is an infinite group, we can still interpret this theorem sensibly: A subgroup of finite index in an infinite group is itself an infinite group. A finite subgroup of an infinite group has infinite index.

label: Laplace Expansion Theorem for Determinants
snippet: Let $\mathbf A = \sqbrk a_n$ be a square matrix of order $n$. Let $D = \map \det {\mathbf A}$ be the determinant of $\mathbf A$: $\ds \map \det {\mathbf A} := \sum_{\lambda} \paren {\map \sgn \lambda \prod_{k \mathop = 1}^n a_{k \map \lambda k} } = \sum_\lambda \map \sgn \lambda a_{1 \map \lambda 1} a_{2 \map \lambda 2} \cdots a_{n \map \lambda n}$ where: the summation $\ds \sum_\lambda$ goes over all the $n!$ permutations of $\set {1, 2, \ldots, n}$ $\map \sgn \lambda$ is the sign of the permutation $\lambda$. Let $a_{p q}$ be an element of $\mathbf A$.

label: Laplace Transform of Derivative
snippet: Let $f: \R \to \R$ or $\R \to \C$ be a continuous function, differentiable on any interval of the form $0 \le t \le A$. Let $f$ be of exponential order $a$. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of $f$. Let $f'$ be piecewise continuous with one-sided limits on said intervals. Then $\laptrans f$ exists for $\map \Re s > a$, and: $\laptrans {\map {f'} t} = s \laptrans {\map f t} - \map f 0$

label: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Cosine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {s - b} {\paren {s - b}^2 + a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of Exponential times Sine
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {e^{b t} \sin a t} } s = \dfrac a {\paren {s - b}^2 + a^2}$ where: $a$ and $b$ are real numbers $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a + b$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Cosine
snippet: Let $\cosh t$ be the hyperbolic cosine, where $t$ is real. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\cosh a t} = \dfrac s {s^2 - a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

label: Laplace Transform of Hyperbolic Sine
snippet: Let $\sinh t$ be the hyperbolic sine, where $t$ is real. Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of the real function $f$. Then: $\laptrans {\sinh a t} = \dfrac a {s^2 - a^2}$ where $a \in \R_{>0}$ is constant, and $\map \Re s > a$.

label: Laplace Transform of Positive Integer Power
snippet: Let $\laptrans f$ denote the Laplace transform of a function $f$. Let $t^n: \R \to \R$ be $t$ to the $n$th power for some $n \in \N_{\ge 0}$. Then: $\laptrans {t^n} = \dfrac {n!} {s^{n + 1} }$ for $\map \Re s > 0$.

label: Laplace Transform of Real Power
snippet: Let $n$ be a constant real number such that $n > -1$ Let $f: \R \to \R$ be the real function defined as: $\map f t = t^n$ Then $f$ has a Laplace transform given by: {{eqn | l = \laptrans {\map f t} | r = \int_0^\infty e^{-s t} t^n \rd t }} {{eqn | r = \frac {\map \Gamma {n + 1} } {s^{n + 1} } }} where $\Gamma$ denotes the gamma function.

label: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {2 s \paren {s^2 + 3 a^2} } {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t^2 cosine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {2 s \paren {s^2 - 3 a^2} } {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t^2 sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \sin a t} } s = 2 a \paren {\dfrac {3 s^2 - a^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^3} }$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t^2 sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t^2 \sinh a t} } s = 2 a \paren {\dfrac {3 s^2 + a^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^3} }$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t cosh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \cosh a t} } s = \dfrac {s^2 + a^2} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t cosine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \cos a t} } s = \dfrac {s^2 - a^2} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t sine a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \sin a t} } s = \dfrac {2 a s} {\paren {s^2 + a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplace Transform of t sinh a t
snippet: $\map {\laptrans {t \sinh a t} } s = \dfrac {2 a s} {\paren {s^2 - a^2}^2}$ where: $s$ is a complex number with $\map \Re s > a$ $\laptrans f$ denotes the Laplace transform of $f$ evaluated at $s$.

label: Laplacian on Scalar Field is Divergence of Gradient
snippet: Let $\R^n$ denote the real Cartesian space of $n$ dimensions. Let $U$ be a scalar field over $\R^n$. Let $\nabla^2 U$ denote the laplacian on $U$. Then: $\nabla^2 U = \operatorname {div} \grad U$ where: $\operatorname {div}$ denotes the divergence operator $\grad$ denotes the gradient operator.

label: Lattice is Complete iff it Admits All Suprema
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then $\struct {S, \preceq}$ is a complete lattice $\forall X \subseteq S: X$ admits a supremum.

label: Law of Cosines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2 a b \cos C$

label: Law of Excluded Middle
snippet: == Proof Rule == The law of (the) excluded middle is a valid argument in certain types of logic dealing with disjunction $\lor$ and negation $\neg$. This includes classical propositional logic and predicate logic, and in particular natural deduction, but for example not intuitionistic propositional logic.

label: Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
snippet: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct odd primes. Then: $\paren {\dfrac p q} \paren {\dfrac q p} = \paren {-1}^{\dfrac {\paren {p - 1} \paren {q - 1} } 4}$ where $\paren {\dfrac p q}$ and $\paren {\dfrac q p}$ are defined as the Legendre symbol. An alternative formulation is: $\paren {\dfrac p q} = \begin{cases} \quad \paren {\dfrac q p} & : p \equiv 1 \lor q \equiv 1 \pmod 4 \\ -\paren {\dfrac q p} & : p \equiv q \equiv 3 \pmod 4 \end{cases}$ The fact that these formulations are equivalent is immediate. This fact is known as the Law of Quadratic Reciprocity, or LQR for short.

label: Law of Sines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $\dfrac a {\sin A} = \dfrac b {\sin B} = \dfrac c {\sin C} = 2 R$ where $R$ is the circumradius of $\triangle ABC$.

label: Law of Tangents
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle whose sides $a, b, c$ are such that $a$ is opposite $A$, $b$ is opposite $B$ and $c$ is opposite $C$. Then: $\dfrac {a + b} {a - b} = \dfrac {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A + B} } {\tan \frac 1 2 \paren {A - B} }$

label: Laws of Logarithms
snippet: Let $x, y, b \in \R_{>0}$ be (strictly) positive real numbers. Let $a \in \R$ be any real number such that $a > 0$ and $a \ne 1$. Let $\log_a$ denote the logarithm to base $a$. Then:

label: Least Upper Bound Property
snippet: Let $S \subset \R$ be a non-empty subset of the set of real numbers such that $S$ is bounded above. Then $S$ admits a supremum in $\R$. This is known as the least upper bound property of the real numbers.

label: Lebesgue's Dominated Convergence Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f : X \to \overline \R$ be a $\Sigma$-measurable function. Let $g : X \to \overline \R_{\ge 0}$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of $\Sigma$-measurable functions $f_n : X \to \overline \R$ such that: $\ds \map f x = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map {f_n} x$ and: $\size {\map {f_n} x} \le \map g x$ hold for $\mu$-almost all $x \in X$. Then: $f$ is $\mu$-integrable and $f_n$ is $\mu$-integrable for each $n \in \N$ and: $\ds \int f \rd \mu = \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \int f_n \rd \mu$

label: Lebesgue Decomposition Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma}$ be a measurable space. Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\struct {X, \Sigma}$.

label: Left Congruence Class Modulo Subgroup is Left Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. Let $\RR^l_H$ be the equivalence defined as left congruence modulo $H$. The equivalence class $\eqclass g {\RR^l_H}$ of an element $g \in G$ is the left coset $g H$. This is known as the left congruence class of $g \bmod H$.

label: Left Congruence Modulo Subgroup is Equivalence Relation
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x \equiv^l y \pmod H$ denote the relation that $x$ is left congruent modulo $H$ to $y$. Then the relation $\equiv^l$ is an equivalence relation.

label: Left Coset Space forms Partition
snippet: Let $G$ be a group, and let $H \le G$ be a subgroup. The left coset space of $H$ forms a partition of its group $G$, and hence: {{eqn | l = \neg \paren {x \equiv^l y} \pmod H | o = \iff | r = x H \cap y H = \O }}

label: Left Cosets are Equal iff Element in Other Left Coset
snippet: Let $G$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Let $x, y \in G$. Let $x H$ denote the left coset of $H$ by $x$. Then: $x H = y H \iff x \in y H$

label: Left Inverse and Right Inverse is Inverse
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a monoid with identity element $e_S$. Let $x \in S$ such that $x$ has both a left inverse and a right inverse. That is: $\exists x_L \in S: x_L \circ x = e_S$ $\exists x_R \in S: x \circ x_R = e_S$ Then $x_L = x_R$, that is, $x$ has an inverse. Furthermore, that element is the only inverse (both right and left) for $x$

label: Left Whiskered Composite of Natural Transformation is Natural Transformation
snippet: Let $\mathbf C$, $\mathbf D$ and $\mathbf B$ be categories. Let $F, G : \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be covariant functors. Let $\eta: F \to G$ be a natural transformation. Let $H : \mathbf B \to \mathbf C$ be a covariant functor. Let $\eta H: F \circ H \to G \circ H$ denote the left whiskered composite of $\eta$ by $H$. Then: $\eta H$ is a natural transformation.

label: Legendre's Duplication Formula
snippet: Let $\Gamma$ denote the gamma function. Then: $\forall z \notin \set {-\dfrac n 2: n \in \N}: \map \Gamma z \map \Gamma {z + \dfrac 1 2} = 2^{1 - 2 z} \sqrt \pi \, \map \Gamma {2 z}$ where $\N$ denotes the natural numbers.

label: Legendre Polynomial/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Legendre Polynomials == The first few Legendre polynomials are:

label: Leibniz's Formula for Pi
snippet: $\dfrac \pi 4 = 1 - \dfrac 1 3 + \dfrac 1 5 - \dfrac 1 7 + \dfrac 1 9 - \cdots \approx 0 \cdotp 78539 \, 81633 \, 9744 \ldots$ That is: $\ds \pi = 4 \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} \paren {-1}^k \frac 1 {2 k + 1}$

label: Lemoine's Conjecture
snippet: == Conjecture == Every odd integer $n$ such that $n > 5$ can be written as: $2 p_1 + p_2$ where $p_1 \le p_2$ and both $p_1$ and $p_2$ are prime.

label: Length Function is Primitive Recursive
snippet: Let $n \in \N$. Let $\map \len n$ denote the length of $n$. Then the function $\len: \N \to \N$ is primitive recursive.

label: Length of Arc of Cycloid
snippet: Let $C$ be a cycloid generated by the equations: $x = a \paren {\theta - \sin \theta}$ $y = a \paren {1 - \cos \theta}$ Then the length of one arc of the cycloid is $8 a$.

label: Lifting The Exponent Lemma
Limit Point/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Limit Points ==

label: Limit of Composite Function
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions. Let: {{eqn | l = \ds \lim_{y \mathop \to \eta} \map f y | r = l }} {{eqn | l = \ds \lim_{x \mathop \to \xi} \map g x | r = \eta }} Then, if either: Hypothesis 1: $f$ is continuous at $\eta$ (that is $l = \map f \eta$) or: Hypothesis 2: for some open interval $I$ containing $\xi$, it is true that $\map g x \ne \eta$ for any $x \in I$ except possibly $x = \xi$ then: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to \xi} \map f {\map g x} = \lim_{y \mathop \to \eta} \map f y$

label: Limit of Function by Convergent Sequences
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $S \subseteq A_1$ be an open set of $M_1$. Let $f: S \to A_2$ be a mapping defined on $S$, except possibly at the point $c \in S$. Then $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to c} \map f x = l$ : for each sequence $\sequence {x_n}$ of points of $S$ such that $\forall n \in \N_{>0}: x_n \ne c$ and $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n = c$ it is true that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f {x_n} = l$

label: Limit of Hölder Mean as Exponent tends to Zero is Geometric Mean
snippet: Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n \in \R_{\ge 0}$ be real numbers. For $p \in \R_{\ne 0}$, let $\map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n}$ denote the Hölder mean with exponent $p$ of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$. Then: $\ds \lim_{p \mathop \to 0} \map {M_p} {x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n} = \paren {x_1 x_2 \cdots x_n}^{1 / n}$ which is the geometric mean of $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_n$.

label: Limit of Image of Sequence
snippet: Let $M_1 = \struct {A_1, d_1}$ and $M_2 = \struct {A_2, d_2}$ be metric spaces. Let $f: A_1 \to A_2$ be a mapping which is continuous at $a \in A_1$. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence of points in $A_1$ such that: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n = a$ where $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n$ is the limit of $x_n$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f {x_n} = \map f a$ That is: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} \map f {x_n} = \map f {\lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} x_n}$ That is, for a continuous mapping, the limit and function symbols commute.

label: Limit of Root of Positive Real Number
snippet: Let $x \in \R: x > 0$ be a real number. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be the sequence in $\R$ defined as: $x_n = x^{1 / n}$ Then $x_n \to 1$ as $n \to \infty$.

label: Limit of Sinc Function at Zero
snippet: $\ds \lim_{x \mathop \to 0} \frac {\sin x} x = 1$

label: Limit of Subsequence equals Limit of Sequence
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\sequence {x_n}$ be a sequence in $T$. Let $l \in S$ be a limit of $\sequence {x_n}$. Let $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ be a subsequence of $\sequence {x_n}$. Then $l$ is a limit of $\sequence {x_{n_r} }$ That is, the limit of a convergent sequence in a topological space equals the limit of any subsequence of it.

label: Lindelöf Hypothesis
snippet: == Hypothesis == The Lindelöf hypothesis is a conjecture about the rate of growth of the Riemann zeta function on the critical line that is implied by the Riemann Hypothesis. It states that: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{> 0}: \map \zeta {\dfrac 1 2 + i t} \text{ is } \map \OO {t^\epsilon}$ as $t \to \infty$ (see big-O notation). Since $\epsilon$ can always be replaced by a smaller value, we can also write the conjecture as: $\forall \epsilon \in \R_{> 0}: \map \zeta {\dfrac 1 2 + i t} \text{ is } \map o {t^\epsilon}$ as $t \to \infty$ (see little-o notation).

label: Line at Right Angles to Diameter of Circle
Linear Combination of Complex Integrals
snippet: Let $\closedint a b$ be a closed real interval. Let $f, g: \closedint a b \to \C$ be complex Riemann integrable functions over $\closedint a b$. Let $\lambda, \mu \in \C$ be complex constants. Then: $\ds \int_a^b \paren {\lambda \map f t + \mu \map g t} \rd t = \lambda \int_a^b \map f t \rd t + \mu \int_a^b \map g t \rd t$

label: Linear Combination of Continuous Functions valued in Topological Vector Space is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$ be a topological space. Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $Y$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $n \in \N$. Let $f_1, \ldots, f_n : X \to Y$ be continuous functions. Let $\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_n \in K$. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = 1}^n \alpha_k f_k$ is a continuous function.

label: Linear Combination of Contour Integrals
snippet: Let $C$ be a contour in $\C$. Let $f, g: \Img C \to \C$ be continuous complex functions, where $\Img C$ denotes the image of $C$. Let $\lambda, \mu \in \C$ be complex constants. Then: $\ds \int_C \paren {\lambda \map f z + \mu \map g z} \rd z = \lambda \int_C \map f z \rd z + \mu \int_C \map g z \rd z$

label: Linear Combination of Convergent Series
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ and $\sequence {b_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be sequences of real numbers. Let the two series $\ds\sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ and $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty b_n$ converge to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ respectively. Let $\lambda, \mu \in \R$ be real numbers. Then the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \paren {\lambda a_n + \mu b_n}$ converges to $\lambda \alpha + \mu \beta$.

label: Linear Combination of Indexed Summations
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N,\Z,\Q,\R,\C$. Let $a,b$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Let $f, g : \closedint a b \to \mathbb A$ be mappings. Let $\lambda, \mu \in \mathbb A$. Let $\lambda \cdot f + \mu \cdot g$ be the sum of the product of $f$ with $\lambda$ and the product of $g$ with $\mu$. Then we have the equality of indexed summations: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \paren {\lambda \cdot \map f i + \mu \cdot \map g i} = \lambda \cdot \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map f i + \mu \cdot \sum_{i \mathop = a}^b \map g i$

label: Linear Combination of Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ and $g$ be real functions which are integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $\lambda$ and $\mu$ be real numbers. Then the following results hold:
