snippet:
Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$ be the space of zero-limit sequences. Define $e_n \in \map {c_0} \GF$ by: $\ds \map {e_n} k =  egin{cases}1 & n = k \ 0 & n 
e k\end{cases}$ Then $\sequence {e_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ is a Schauder basis for $\struct {\map {c_0} \GF, 
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty}$.

label: Spectral Mapping Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be normal. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Let $\map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x}$ be the space of continuous functions on $\map {\sigma_A} x$. Let $f \in \map \CC {\map {\sigma_A} x}$. Let $\map {\Theta_x} f = \map f x$ be the continuous functional calculus of $x$ applied to $f$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} {\map f x} = f \sqbrk {\map {\sigma_A} x}$

label: Spectral Mapping Theorem for Polynomials
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $p : \C \to \C$ be a polynomial with: $\ds \map p z = \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^n a_j z^j$ for all $z \in \C$, for some $a_0, \ldots, a_n \in \C$. Define: $\ds \map p y = a_0 {\mathbf 1}_A + \sum_{j \mathop = 1}^n a_j y^j$ for each $y \in A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ and $\map {\sigma_A} {\map p x}$ be the spectrum of $x$ and $\map p x$ respectively. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} {\map p x} = p \sqbrk {\map {\sigma_A} x}$

label: Spectral Radius of Normal Element of C*-Algebra Equal to Norm
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $r_A$ be the spectral radius in $A$. Let $x \in A$ be normal. Then $\map {r_A} x = \norm x$.

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Bounded
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x$ is bounded, and in particular: $\cmod \lambda \le \norm x$ for all $\lambda \in \map {\sigma_A} x$

label: Spectrum of Element of Banach Algebra is Non-Empty
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \ne \O$.

label: Spectrum of Element of Unital C*-Subalgebra of Unital C*-Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra with identity element ${\mathbf 1}_A$. Let $B \subseteq A$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-subalgebra of $A$. Let $\sigma_A$ and $\sigma_B$ be the spectrum in $A$ and $B$ respectively. Let $x \in B$. Then we have: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \map {\sigma_B} x$

label: Spectrum of Element of Unital Commutative Banach Algebra
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a commutative unital Banach algebra over $\C$. Let $\Phi_A$ be the spectrum of $A$. Let $x \in A$. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ be the spectrum of $x$. Then: $\map {\sigma_A} x = \set {\map \phi x : \phi \in \Phi_A}$

label: Spectrum of Hermitian Element in Unital C*-Algebra is Real
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a unital $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $x \in A$ be Hermitian. Let $\map {\sigma_A} x$ denote the spectrum of $x$ in $A$. Then $\map {\sigma_A} x \subseteq \R$.

label: Spherical Law of Cosines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\cos a = \cos b \cos c + \sin b \sin c \cos A$

label: Spherical Law of Sines
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Then: $\dfrac {\sin a} {\sin A} = \dfrac {\sin b} {\sin B} = \dfrac {\sin c} {\sin C}$

label: Spherical Triangle is Polar Triangle of its Polar Triangle
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a spherical triangle on the surface of a sphere whose center is $O$. Let the sides $a, b, c$ of $\triangle ABC$ be measured by the angles subtended at $O$, where $a, b, c$ are opposite $A, B, C$ respectively. Let $\triangle A'B'C'$ be the polar triangle of $\triangle ABC$. Then $\triangle ABC$ is the polar triangle of $\triangle A'B'C'$.

label: Square Matrix with Duplicate Rows has Zero Determinant
snippet: If two rows of a square matrix over a commutative ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ are the same, then its determinant is zero.

label: Square Modulo 3
snippet: Let $x \in \Z$ be an integer. Then one of the following holds: where: $\divides$ denotes divisibility $\nmid$ denotes non-divisibility.

label: Square Modulo 4
snippet: Let $x \in \Z$ be an integer. Then $x$ is: even $x^2 \equiv 0 \pmod 4$ odd $x^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 4$

label: Square Modulo 8
snippet: Let $x \in \Z$ be an integer. If $x$ is even then: $x^2 \equiv 0 \pmod 8$ or $x^2 \equiv 4 \pmod 8$ If $x$ is odd then: $x^2 \equiv 1 \pmod 8$

label: Square Root/Examples
snippet: == Examples of Square Roots ==

label: Square Root of 2 is Irrational
snippet: $\sqrt 2$ is irrational.

label: Square Root of Prime is Irrational
snippet: The square root of a prime number is irrational.

label: Square of Difference
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x - y}^2 = x^2 - 2 x y + y^2$

label: Square of Golden Mean equals One plus Golden Mean
snippet: $\phi^2 = \phi + 1$ where $\phi$ denotes the golden mean.

label: Square of Real Number is Non-Negative
snippet: Let $x \in \R$. Then: $0 \le x^2$

label: Square of Small-Digit Palindromic Number is Palindromic
snippet: Let $n$ be an integer such that the sum of the squares of the digits of $n$ in decimal representation is less than $10$. Let $n$ be palindromic. Then $n^2$ is also palindromic. The sequence of such numbers begins: $0, 1, 2, 3, 11, 22, 101, 111, 121, 202, 212, 1001, 1111, \dots$

label: Square of Sum
snippet: $\forall x, y \in \R: \paren {x + y}^2 = x^2 + 2 x y + y^2$

label: Squaring the Circle
snippet: == Classic Problem == Squaring the Circle is creating a square with the same area as that of a given circle.

label: Stabilizer is Subgroup
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group which acts on a set $X$. Let $\Stab x$ be the stabilizer of $x$ by $G$. Then for each $x \in X$, $\Stab x$ is a subgroup of $G$.

label: Stabilizer of Coset Action on Set of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ denote the power set of $G$. Let $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ denote the set of subgroups of $G$. Let $*$ be the subset product action on $\HH \subseteq \powerset G$ defined as: $\forall g \in G: \forall H \in \HH: g * H = g \circ H$ where $g \circ H$ is the (left) coset of $g$ by $H$. Then the stabilizer of $H$ in $\powerset G$ is $H$ itself: $\Stab H = H$

label: Standard Ordered Basis is Basis
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n$ be a positive integer. For each $j \in \closedint 1 n$, let $e_j$ be the ordered $n$-tuple of elements of $R$ whose $j$th entry is $1_R$ and all of whose other entries is $0_R$. Then $\sequence {e_n}$ is an ordered basis of the $R$-module $R^n$. This ordered basis is called the standard ordered basis of $R^n$. The corresponding set $\set {e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_n}$ is called the standard basis of $R^n$.

label: Stewart's Theorem
snippet: Let $\triangle ABC$ be a triangle with sides $a, b, c$. Let $CP$ be a cevian from $C$ to $P$. 400px Then: $a^2 \cdot AP + b^2 \cdot PB = c \paren {CP^2 + AP \cdot PB}$

label: Stirling's Formula
snippet: The factorial function can be approximated by the formula: $n! \sim \sqrt {2 \pi n} \paren {\dfrac n e}^n$ where $\sim$ denotes asymptotically equal.

label: Stirling Number of the Second Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brace n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brace n - 1}$ denotes a Stirling number of the second kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Straight Line Commensurable with Medial Straight Line is Medial
Strictly Positive Real Numbers are Closed under Multiplication
snippet: The set $\R_{>0}$ of strictly positive real numbers is closed under multiplication: $\forall a, b \in \R_{> 0}: a \times b \in \R_{> 0}$

label: Strictly Positive Real Numbers under Multiplication form Uncountable Abelian Group
snippet: Let $\R_{>0}$ be the set of strictly positive real numbers: $\R_{>0} = \set {x \in \R: x > 0}$ The structure $\struct {\R_{>0}, \times}$ is an uncountable abelian group.

label: Structure Induced by Associative Operation is Associative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be associative. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also associative.

label: Structure Induced by Commutative Operation is Commutative
snippet: Let $\struct {T, \circ}$ be an algebraic structure, and let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {T^S, \oplus}$ be the structure on $T^S$ induced by $\circ$. Let $\circ$ be a commutative operation. Then the pointwise operation $\oplus$ induced on $T^S$ by $\circ$ is also commutative.

label: Structure Induced by Commutative Ring Operations is Commutative Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a commutative ring. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a commutative ring.

label: Structure Induced by Ring Operations is Ring
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring. Let $S$ be a set. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring, where $+'$ and $\circ'$ are the pointwise operations induced on $R^S$ by $+$ and $\circ$.

label: Structure Induced by Ring with Unity Operations is Ring with Unity
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ be a ring with unity whose unity is $1_R$. Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ be the structure on $R^S$ induced by $+'$ and $\circ'$. Then $\struct {R^S, +', \circ'}$ is a ring with unity whose unity is $f_{1_R}: S \to R$, defined by: $\forall s \in S: \map {f_{1_R} } s = 1_R$

label: Subclass of Set is Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a set. Let $\map \phi x$ be a condition in which $x$ is taken to be a set. Then there exists a set that consists of all of the elements of $A$ that satisfies this condition. In ZF, this result is known as the Axiom of Specification.

label: Subcover is Refinement of Cover
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\CC$ be a cover for $S$. Let $\VV$ be a subcover of $\CC$. Then $\VV$ is a refinement of $\CC$.

label: Subdomain Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of an integral domain $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subdomain of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these conditions hold: $(1): \quad \struct {S, + {\restriction_S}, \circ {\restriction_S} }$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ $(2): \quad$ The unity of $R$ is also in $S$, that is $1_R = 1_S$.

label: Subfield Test
snippet: Let $\struct {F, +, \times}$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $K$ be a subset of $F$.

label: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Abelian
snippet: A subgroup of an abelian group is itself abelian.

label: Subgroup of Abelian Group is Normal
snippet: Every subgroup of an abelian group is normal.

label: Subgroup of Cyclic Group is Cyclic
snippet: Let $G$ be a cyclic group. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Then $H$ is cyclic.

label: Subgroup of Finite Cyclic Group is Determined by Order
snippet: Let $G = \gen g$ be a cyclic group whose order is $n$ and whose identity is $e$. Let $d \divides n$, where $\divides$ denotes divisibility. Then there exists exactly one subgroup $G_d = \gen {g^{n / d} }$ of $G$ with $d$ elements.

label: Subgroup of Index 2 is Normal
snippet: A subgroup of index $2$ is always normal.

label: Subgroups of Additive Group of Integers
snippet: Let $\struct {\Z, +}$ be the additive group of integers. Let $n \Z$ be the additive group of integer multiples of $n$. Every non-trivial subgroup of $\struct {\Z, +}$ has the form $n \Z$.

label: Submodule Test
snippet: Let $\struct {R, +_R, \times_R}$ be a ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct {G, +, \circ}_R$ be a unitary $R$-module. Let $H$ be a non-empty subset of $G$. Then $\struct {H, +, \circ}_R$ is a submodule of $G$ :

label: Subring Test
snippet: Let $S$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $\struct {S, +, \circ}$ is a subring of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad S \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x + \paren {-y} \in S$ $(3): \quad \forall x, y \in S: x \circ y \in S$

label: Subset Product Action is Group Action
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let $\powerset G$ be the power set of $\struct {G, \circ}$. For any $S \in \powerset G$ and for any $g \in G$, the subset product action: $\forall g \in G: \forall S \in \powerset G: g * S = g \circ S$ is a group action.

label: Subset Product of Subgroups
snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H, K$ be subgroups of $G$. Then $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ $H$ and $K$ are permutable. That is: $H \circ K$ is a subgroup of $G$ : $H \circ K = K \circ H$ where $H \circ K$ denotes subset product.

label: Subset Product with Normal Subgroup as Generator
snippet: Let $G$ be a group whose identity is $e$. Let: $H$ be a subgroup of $G$ $N$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then: $N \lhd \gen {N, H} = N H = H N \le G$ where: $\le$ denotes subgroup $\lhd$ denotes normal subgroup $\gen {N, H}$ denotes a subgroup generator $N H$ denotes subset product.

label: Subset Relation is Compatible with Subset Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \circ}$ be a magma. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \circ_\PP}$ be the power structure of $\struct {S, \circ}$. Then the subset relation on $S$ is compatible with $\circ_\PP$. That is: {{eqn | q = \forall X, Y, Z \in \powerset S | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {X \circ_\PP Z} \subseteq \paren {Y \circ_\PP Z} | c = }} {{eqn | l = X \subseteq Y | o = \implies | r = \paren {Z \circ_\PP X} \subseteq \paren {Z \circ_\PP Y} | c = }}

label: Subset Relation is Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\mathbb S \subseteq \powerset S$ be any subset of $\powerset S$, that is, an arbitrary set of subsets of $S$. Then $\subseteq$ is an ordering on $\mathbb S$. In other words, let $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\mathbb S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\mathbb S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set.

label: Subset Relation is Transitive
snippet: The subset relation is transitive: $\paren {R \subseteq S} \land \paren {S \subseteq T} \implies R \subseteq T$

label: Subset Relation on Power Set is Partial Ordering
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\powerset S$ be the power set of $S$. Let $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ be the relational structure defined on $\powerset S$ by the subset relation $\subseteq$. Then $\struct {\powerset S, \subseteq}$ is an ordered set. The ordering $\subseteq$ is partial $S$ is neither empty nor a singleton; otherwise it is total.

label: Subset implies Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets such that $S \subseteq T$. Furthermore, let: $T \sim \card T$ where $\card T$ denotes the cardinality of $T$. Then: $\card S \le \card T$

label: Subset is Right Compatible with Ordinal Multiplication
snippet: Let $x, y, z$ be ordinals. Then: $x \le y \implies \paren {x \cdot z} \le \paren {y \cdot z}$

label: Subset of Codomain is Superset of Image of Preimage
snippet: Let $f: S \to T$ be a mapping. Then: $B \subseteq T \implies \paren {f \circ f^{-1} } \sqbrk B \subseteq B$ where: $f \sqbrk B$ denotes the image of $B$ under $f$ $f^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of $f$ $f \circ f^{-1}$ denotes composition of $f$ and $f^{-1}$. This can be expressed in the language and notation of direct image mappings and inverse image mappings as: $\forall B \in \powerset T: \map {\paren {f^\to \circ f^\gets} } B \subseteq B$

label: Subset of Countable Set is Countable
snippet: A subset of a countable set is countable.

label: Subset of Countably Infinite Set is Countable
snippet: Every subset of a countably infinite set is countable.

label: Subset of Empty Set
snippet: Let $A$ be a class. Then: $A$ is a subset of the empty set $\O$ $A$ is equal to the empty set: $A \subseteq \O \iff A = \O$

label: Subset of Empty Set iff Empty
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\O$ denote the empty set. Then $S \subseteq \O$ $S = \O$.

label: Subset of Finite Set is Finite
snippet: Let $X$ be a finite set. If $Y$ is a subset of $X$, then $Y$ is also finite.

label: Subset of Metric Space contains Limits of Sequences iff Closed
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Then $H$ is closed in $M$ : for each sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ of points of $H$ that converges to a point $a \in A$, it follows that $a \in H$.

label: Subset of Particular Point Space is either Open or Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau_p}$ be a particular point space. Let $H \subseteq S$ be any subset of $T$. Then $H$ is either open or closed in $T$. The only sets which are both closed and open in $T$ are $S$ and $\O$.

label: Subset of Partition Space is Open iff Closed
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $T$ is a partition space : $\forall U \subseteq S: U \in \tau \iff \relcomp S U \in \tau$ That is, a topological space is a partition space : all open sets are closed all closed sets are also open. That is, all open sets and closed sets of a partition space are clopen.

label: Subset of Real Numbers is Interval iff Connected
snippet: Let the real number line $\R$ be considered as a topological space. Let $S$ be a subspace of $\R$. Then $S$ is connected $S$ is an interval of $\R$. That is, the only subspaces of $\R$ that are connected are intervals.

label: Subset of Set Difference iff Disjoint Set
snippet: Let $S, T$ be sets. Let $A \subseteq S$ Then: $A \cap T = \O \iff A \subseteq S \setminus T$ where: $A \cap T$ denotes set intersection $\O$ denotes the empty set $S \setminus T$ denotes set difference.

label: Subset of Well-Ordered Set is Well-Ordered
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be a well-ordered set. Let $T \subseteq S$ be a subset of $S$. Let $\preceq'$ be the restriction of $\preceq$ to $T$. Then the relational structure $\struct {T, \preceq'}$ is a well-ordered set.

label: Subspace Topology on Initial Topology is Initial Topology on Restrictions
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {\struct {Y_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of topological spaces indexed by $I$. Let $\family {f_i: X \to Y_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of mappings indexed by $I$. Let $\tau$ be the initial topology on $X$ with respect to $\family {f_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$. Let $\struct {Y, \tau_Y}$ be a topological subspace of $X$. Then $\tau_Y$ is the initial topology on $Y$ with respect to $\family {f_i \restriction_Y}_{i \mathop \in I}$.

label: Subspace of Complete Metric Space is Closed iff Complete
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d}$ be a complete metric space. Let $\struct {S, d}$ be a subspace of $\struct {M, d}$. Then $S$ is closed $S$ is complete.

label: Subspace of Metric Space is Metric Space
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. Let $H \subseteq A$. Let $d_H: H \times H \to \R$ be the restriction $d \restriction_{H \times H}$ of $d$ to $H$. Let $\struct {H, d_H}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {A, d}$. Then $d_H$ is a metric on $H$.

label: Subspace of Product Space is Homeomorphic to Factor Space
snippet: Let $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of topological spaces where $I$ is an arbitrary index set. Let $\ds \struct {X, \tau} = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} \struct {X_i, \tau_i}$ be the product space of $\family {\struct {X_i, \tau_i} }_{i \mathop \in I}$. Suppose that $X$ is non-empty. Then for each $i \in I$ there is a subspace $Y_i \subseteq X$ which is homeomorphic to $\struct {X_i, \tau_i}$.

label: Subspace of Separable Metric Space is Separable
snippet: Let $\struct {X, d}$ be a separable metric space. Let $\struct {Y, d_Y}$ be a metric subspace of $\struct {X, d}$. Then $Y$ is separable.

label: Substitutivity of Class Equality
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be classes. Let $\map P A$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P B$ be the same proposition $\map P A$ with all instances of $A$ replaced with instances of $B$. Let $=$ denote class equality. $A = B \implies \paren {\map P A \iff \map P B}$

label: Substitutivity of Equality
snippet: Let $x$ and $y$ be sets. Let $\map P x$ be a well-formed formula of the language of set theory. Let $\map P y$ be the same proposition $\map P x$ with some (not necessarily all) free instances of $x$ replaced with free instances of $y$. Let $=$ denote set equality. $x = y \implies \paren {\map P x \iff \map P y}$

label: Successor Set of Ordinal is Ordinal
snippet: Let $\On$ denote the class of all ordinals. Let $\alpha \in \On$ be an ordinal. Then its successor set $\alpha^+ = \alpha \cup \set \alpha$ is also an ordinal.

label: Sufficient Conditions for Basis of Finite Dimensional Vector Space
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $n \ge 0$ be a natural number. Let $E$ be an $n$-dimensional vector space over $K$. Let $B \subseteq E$ be a subset such that $\card B = n$. $(1): \quad$ $B$ is a basis of $E$. $(2): \quad$ $B$ is linearly independent. $(3): \quad$ $B$ is a generator for $E$.

label: Sufficient Conditions for Uncountability
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. {{item|(3):|Every sequence of distinct points $\sequence {x_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ in $X$ omits at least one $x \in X$}} Assuming the Continuum Hypothesis holds, we also have the equivalent uncountability condition: $(6): \quad $There exist extended real numbers $a < b$ and a surjection $X \to \closedint a b$

label: Sum Rule for Derivatives
snippet: Let $\map f x, \map j x, \map k x$ be real functions defined on the open interval $I$. Let $\xi \in I$ be a point in $I$ at which both $j$ and $k$ are differentiable. Let $\map f x = \map j x + \map k x$. Then $f$ is differentiable at $\xi$ and: $\map {f'} \xi = \map {j'} \xi + \map {k'} \xi$ It follows from the definition of derivative that if $j$ and $k$ are both differentiable on the interval $I$, then: $\forall x \in I: \map {f'} x = \map {j'} x + \map {k'} x$

label: Sum of Angles of Triangle equals Two Right Angles
snippet: In a triangle, the sum of the three interior angles equals two right angles.

label: Sum of Arcsine and Arccosine
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number such that $-1 \le x \le 1$. Then: $\arcsin x + \arccos x = \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\arcsin$ and $\arccos$ denote arcsine and arccosine respectively.

label: Sum of Arctangent and Arccotangent
snippet: Let $x \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $\arctan x + \arccot x = \dfrac \pi 2$ where $\arctan$ and $\arccot$ denote arctangent and arccotangent respectively.

label: Sum of Binomial Coefficients over Lower Index
snippet: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n \binom n i = 2^n$ where $\dbinom n i$ is a binomial coefficient.

label: Sum of Complex Conjugates
snippet: Let $z_1, z_2 \in \C$ be complex numbers. Let $\overline z$ denote the complex conjugate of the complex number $z$. Then: $\overline {z_1 + z_2} = \overline {z_1} + \overline {z_2}$

label: Sum of Complex Number with Conjugate
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Let $\overline z$ be the complex conjugate of $z$. Let $\map \Re z$ be the real part of $z$. Then: $z + \overline z = 2 \, \map \Re z$

label: Sum of Even Integers is Even
snippet: The sum of any finite number of even integers is itself even.

label: Sum of Ideals is Ideal
snippet: Let $J_1$ and $J_2$ be ideals of a ring $\struct{R, +, \circ}$. Then: $J = J_1 + J_2$ is an ideal of $R$ where $J_1 + J_2$ is as defined in subset product with respect to $\struct{R, +}$.

label: Sum of Infinite Geometric Sequence
snippet: Let $S$ be a standard number field, that is $\Q$, $\R$ or $\C$. Let $z \in S$. Let $\size z < 1$, where $\size z$ denotes: the absolute value of $z$, for real and rational $z$ the complex modulus of $z$ for complex $z$. Then $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty z^n$ converges absolutely to $\dfrac 1 {1 - z}$.

label: Sum of Integrals on Adjacent Intervals for Continuous Functions
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on any closed interval $I$. Let $a, b, c \in I$. Then: $\ds \int_a^c \map f t \rd t + \int_c^b \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t$

label: Sum of Integrals on Adjacent Intervals for Integrable Functions
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is Darboux integrable on any closed interval $\mathbb I$. Let $a, b, c \in \mathbb I$. Then: $\ds \int_a^c \map f t \rd t + \int_c^b \map f t \rd t = \int_a^b \map f t \rd t$

label: Sum of Internal Angles of Polygon
snippet: The sum $S$ of all internal angles of a polygon with $n$ sides is given by the formula $S = \paren {n - 2} 180 \degrees$.

label: Sum of Positive and Negative Parts
snippet: Let $X$ be a set, and let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be an extended real-valued function. Let $f^+, f^-: X \to \overline \R$ be the positive and negative parts of $f$, respectively. Then $\size {f} = f^+ + f^-$, where $\size {f}$ is the absolute value of $f$.

label: Sum of Reciprocals of Powers as Euler Product
snippet: Let $\zeta$ be the Riemann zeta function. Let $s \in \C$ be a complex number with real part $\sigma > 1$. Then: $\ds \map \zeta s = \prod_{\text {$p$ prime} } \frac 1 {1 - p^{-s} }$ where the infinite product runs over the prime numbers.

label: Sum of Reciprocals of Squares Alternating in Sign
snippet: {{eqn | l = \dfrac {\pi^2} {12} | r = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \dfrac {\paren {-1}^{n + 1} } {n^2} | c = }} {{eqn | r = \frac 1 {1^2} - \frac 1 {2^2} + \frac 1 {3^2} - \frac 1 {4^2} + \cdots | c = }}

label: Sum of Reciprocals of Squares of Odd Integers
snippet: {{eqn | l = \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac 1 {\paren {2 n - 1}^2} | r = 1 + \dfrac 1 {3^2} + \dfrac 1 {5^2} + \dfrac 1 {7^2} + \dfrac 1 {9^2} + \cdots }} {{eqn | r = \dfrac {\pi^2} 8 }}

label: Sum of Roots of Quadratic Equation
snippet: Let $P$ be the quadratic equation $a x^2 + b x + c = 0$. Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of $P$. Then: $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac b a$

label: Sum of Sequence of Cubes
snippet: $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i^3 = \paren {\sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i}^2 = \frac {n^2 \paren {n + 1}^2} 4$

label: Sum of Sequence of Squares
snippet: $\ds \forall n \in \N: \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^n i^2 = \frac {n \paren {n + 1} \paren {2 n + 1} } 6$

label: Sum of Set and Open Set in Topological Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $K$ be a topological field. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $K$. Let $A$ and $B$ be subsets of $X$, with $A$ an open set. Then the linear combination $A + B$ is open.

label: Sum of Squares of Sine and Cosine
snippet: $\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1$ where $\sin$ and $\cos$ are sine and cosine.

label: Sum of Summations equals Summation of Sum
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let $\ds \sum_{\map R i} x_i$ denote a summation over $R$. Let the fiber of truth of $R$ be finite. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R i} \paren {b_i + c_i} = \sum_{\map R i} b_i + \sum_{\map R i} c_i$

label: Sum of Two Odd Powers
snippet: Let $\F$ be one of the standard number systems, that is $\Z, \Q, \R$ and so on. Let $n \in \Z_{\ge 0}$ be a positive integer. Then: {{eqn | l = a^{2 n + 1} + b^{2 n + 1} | r = \paren {a + b} \sum_{j \mathop = 0}^{2 n} \paren {-1}^j a^{2 n - j} b^j | c = }} {{eqn | r = \paren {a + b} \paren {a^{2 n} - a^{2 n - 1} b + a^{2 n - 2} b^2 - \dotsb - a b^{2 n - 1} + b^{2 n} } | c = }}

label: Sum of Two Positive Elements of C*-Algebra is Positive
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \ast, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a $\text C^\ast$-algebra. Let $a, b$ be positive. Then $a + b$ is positive.

label: Sum of Two Sides of Triangle Greater than Third Side
snippet: Given a triangle $ABC$, the sum of the lengths of any two sides of the triangle is greater than the length of the third side.

label: Sum over Disjoint Union of Finite Sets
snippet: Let $\mathbb A$ be one of the standard number systems $\N, \Z, \Q, \R, \C$. Let $S$ and $T$ be finite disjoint sets. Let $S \cup T$ be their union. Let $f: S \cup T \to \mathbb A$ be a mapping. Then we have the equality of summations over finite sets: $\ds \sum_{u \mathop \in S \mathop \cup T} \map f u = \sum_{s \mathop \in S} \map f s + \sum_{t \mathop \in T} \map f t$

label: Sum over k of r-tk Choose k by s-t(n-k) Choose n-k by r over r-tk
snippet: Let $r, s, t \in \R, n \in \Z$. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \ge 0} \binom {r - t k} k \binom {s - t \paren {n - k} } {n - k} \frac r {r - t k} = \binom {r + s - t n} n$ where $\dbinom {r - t k} k$ and so on are binomial coefficients.

label: Summation is Linear
snippet: Let $\tuple {x_1, \ldots, x_n}$ and $\tuple {y_1, \ldots, y_n}$ be finite sequences of numbers of equal length. Let $\lambda$ be a number. Then:

label: Summation over Union of Disjoint Finite Index Sets
snippet: Let $\struct{G, +}$ be a commutative monoid. Let $I$ and $J$ be disjoint finite indexing sets. Let $K = I \cup J$. Let $\family{g_k}_{k \mathop \in K}$ be an indexed family of elements of $G$. Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k = \paren{\sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i} + \paren{\sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j}$ where: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop \in K} g_k$ is the summation of $g$ over $K$ $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} g_i$ is the summation of the restriction of $g$ over $I$ $\ds \sum_{j \mathop \in J} g_j$ is the summation of the restriction of $g$ over $J$

label: Superset of Neighborhood in Topological Space is Neighborhood
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Let $N$ be a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. Let $N \subseteq N' \subseteq S$. Then $N'$ is a neighborhood of $x$ in $T$. That is: $\forall x \in S: \forall N \in \NN_x: N' \supseteq N \implies N' \in \NN_x$ where $\NN_x$ is the neighborhood filter of $x$.

label: Supremum Inequality for Ordinals
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \On$ and $B \subseteq \On$ be ordinals. Then: $\ds \forall x \in A: \exists y \in B: x \le y \implies \bigcup A \le \bigcup B$

label: Supremum Norm is Norm
snippet:
Let $S$ be a set. Let $\struct {X, 
orm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space over $K \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $\BB$ be the set of bounded mappings $S 	o X$. Let $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ be the supremum norm on $\BB$. Then $
orm {\, \cdot \,}_\infty$ is a norm on $\BB$.

label: Supremum is Unique
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a non-empty subset of $S$. Then $T$ has at most one supremum in $S$.

label: Supremum of Empty Set is Smallest Element
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Then: the supremum in $S$ of the empty set exists the smallest element of $S$ exists in which case: $\map \sup \O$ is the smallest element of $S$

label: Supremum of Subset
snippet: Let $\left({U, \preceq}\right)$ be an ordered set. Let $S \subseteq U$. Let $T \subseteq S$. Let $S$ admit a supremum (in $U$). If $T$ also admits a supremum (in $U$), then $\sup \left({T}\right) \preceq\sup \left({S}\right)$.

label: Supremum of Subset of Real Numbers is Arbitrarily Close
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be a subset of the real numbers. Let $b$ be a supremum of $A$. Let $\epsilon \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\exists x \in A: b − x < \epsilon$

label: Surjection from Natural Numbers iff Countable
snippet: Let $S$ be a non-empty set. Then $S$ is countable there exists a surjection $f: \N \to S$.

label: Surjection iff Cardinal Inequality
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be sets. Let $S$ be non-empty. Then: $0 < \card T \le \card S$ there exists a surjection $f: S \to T$ where $\card S$ denotes the cardinality of $S$.

label: Surjection iff Right Inverse
snippet: A mapping $f: S \to T, S \ne \O$ is a surjection : $\exists g: T \to S: f \circ g = I_T$ where: $g$ is a mapping $I_T$ is the identity mapping on $T$. That is, $f$ has a right inverse.

label: Sylow p-Subgroup is Unique iff Normal
snippet: A group $G$ has exactly one Sylow $p$-subgroup $P$ $P$ is normal.

label: Symmetric Difference is Associative
snippet: Symmetric difference is associative: $R \symdif \paren {S \symdif T} = \paren {R \symdif S} \symdif T$

label: Symmetric Group is Group
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\map \Gamma S$ denote the set of all permutations on $S$. Then $\struct {\map \Gamma S, \circ}$, the symmetric group on $S$, forms a group.

label: Symmetric Group on 3 Letters
snippet: == Group Example == Let $S_3$ denote the set of permutations on $3$ letters. The symmetric group on $3$ letters is the algebraic structure: $\struct {S_3, \circ}$ where $\circ$ denotes composition of mappings. It is usually denoted, when the context is clear, without the operator: $S_3$.

label: Symmetry Rule for Binomial Coefficients
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{>0}, k \in \Z$. Then: $\dbinom n k = \dbinom n {n - k}$ where $\dbinom n k$ is a binomial coefficient.

label: Synthetic Basis formed from Synthetic Sub-Basis
snippet: Let $X$ be a set. Let $\SS$ be a synthetic sub-basis on $X$. Define: $\ds \BB = \set {\bigcap \FF: \FF \subseteq \SS, \text{$\FF$ is finite} }$ Then $\BB$ is a synthetic basis on $X$. Thus, by this construction, an arbitrary collection of subsets of $X$ can form a synthetic basis and thus generate a topology on $X$.

label: T1 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_1$ space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_1$ space. That is: The property of being a $T_1$ space is hereditary.

label: T1 Property is Preserved under Expansion
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $T_A = \struct {S, \tau_1}$ and $T_B = \struct {S, \tau_2}$ be topological spaces such that $\tau_2$ is an expansion of $\tau_1$. If $T_A$ is a $T_1$ space, then so is $T_B$.

label: T2.5 Space is T2
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_{2 \frac 1 2}$ space. Then $\struct {S, \tau}$ is also a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space.

label: T2 Property is Hereditary
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Let $T_H = \struct {H, \tau_H}$, where $\O \subset H \subseteq S$, be a subspace of $T$. Then $T_H$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. That is: The property of being a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space is hereditary.

label: T2 Property is Preserved under Homeomorphism
snippet: Let $T_A = \struct {S_A, \tau_A}$ and $T_B = \struct {S_B, \tau_B}$ be topological spaces. Let $\phi: T_A \to T_B$ be a homeomorphism. If $T_A$ is a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space, then so is $T_B$.

label: T2 Space is T1
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_2$ (Hausdorff) space. Then $T$ is also a $T_1$ space.

label: Tail of Convergent Sequence
snippet: Let $\left\langle{a_n}\right\rangle$ be a real sequence. Let $m \in \N$ be a natural number. Let $a \in \R$ be a real number. Then: $a_n \to a$ $a_{n + m} \to a$

label: Tail of Convergent Series tends to Zero
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}_{n \mathop \ge 1}$ be a sequence of real numbers. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ be a convergent series. Let $N \in \N_{\ge 1}$ be a natural number. Let $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n$ be the tail of the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$. Then: $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n$ is convergent $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = N}^\infty a_n \to 0$ as $N \to \infty$. That is, the tail of a convergent series tends to zero.

label: Tangent-Chord Theorem
snippet: Let $EF$ be a tangent to a circle $ABCD$, touching it at $B$. Let $BD$ be a chord of $ABCD$. Then: the angle in segment $BCD$ equals $\angle DBE$ and: the angle in segment $BAD$ equals $\angle DBF$.

label: Tangent Secant Theorem
snippet: Let $D$ be a point outside a circle $ABC$. Let $DB$ be tangent to the circle $ABC$. Let $DA$ be a straight line which cuts the circle $ABC$ at $A$ and $C$. Then $DB^2 = AD \cdot DC$.

label: Tangent in terms of Hyperbolic Tangent
snippet: Let $z \in \C$ be a complex number. Then: $i \tan z = \map \tanh {i z}$ where: $\tan$ denotes the tangent function $\tanh$ denotes the hyperbolic tangent $i$ is the imaginary unit: $i^2 = -1$.

label: Tangent is Sine divided by Cosine
snippet: Let $\theta$ be an angle such that $\cos \theta \ne 0$. Then: $\tan \theta = \dfrac {\sin \theta} {\cos \theta}$ where $\tan$, $\sin$ and $\cos$ mean tangent, sine and cosine respectively.

label: Tangent of Complement equals Cotangent
snippet: $\map \tan {\dfrac \pi 2 - \theta} = \cot \theta$ for $\theta \ne n \pi$ where $\tan$ and $\cot$ are tangent and cotangent respectively. That is, the cotangent of an angle is the tangent of its complement. This relation is defined wherever $\sin \theta \ne 0$.

label: Tangent of Complex Number
snippet: Let $a$ and $b$ be real numbers. Let $i$ be the imaginary unit. Then:

label: Tangent of i
snippet: $\tan i = \paren {\dfrac {e^2 - 1} {e^2 + 1} } i$ where $\tan$ denotes the complex tangent function and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

label: Tautochrone Problem
snippet: == Problem == Let a point $A$ be joined by a wire to a lower point $B$. Let the wire be allowed to be bent into whatever shape is required. Let a bead be released at $A$ to slide down without friction to $B$. What is the shape of the wire so that it takes same time to descend to $B$ from wherever you release the bead between $A$ and $B$?

label: Taylor's Theorem
snippet: Every infinitely differentiable function can be approximated by a series of polynomials.

label: Telescoping Series/Example 2
snippet: Let $\sequence {b_n}$ be a sequence in $\R$. Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence whose terms are defined as: $a_k = b_k - b_{k - 1}$ Then: $\ds \sum_{k \mathop = m}^n a_k = b_n - b_{m - 1}$

label: Terms in Convergent Series Converge to Zero
snippet: Let $\sequence {a_n}$ be a sequence in any of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$, or $\C$. Suppose that the series $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty a_n$ converges in any of the standard number fields $\Q$, $\R$, or $\C$. Then: $\ds \lim_{n \mathop \to \infty} a_n = 0$

label: Test for Ideal
snippet: Let $J$ be a subset of a ring $\struct {R, +, \circ}$. Then $J$ is an ideal of $\struct {R, +, \circ}$ these all hold: $(1): \quad J \ne \O$ $(2): \quad \forall x, y \in J: x + \paren {-y} \in J$ $(3): \quad \forall j \in J, r \in R: r \circ j \in J, j \circ r \in J$

label: Thales' Theorem
snippet: Let $A$ and $B$ be two points on opposite ends of the diameter of a circle. Let $C$ be another point on the circle such that $C \ne A, B$. Then the lines $AC$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to each other. 400px

label: Theorem of Even Perfect Numbers
snippet: Let $a \in \N$ be an even perfect number. Then $a$ is in the form: $2^{n - 1} \paren {2^n - 1}$ where $2^n - 1$ is prime. Similarly, if $2^n - 1$ is prime, then $2^{n - 1} \paren {2^n - 1}$ is perfect.

label: Theorema Egregium
snippet: The Gaussian curvature of a surface does not change if one bends the surface without stretching it. That is, Gaussian curvature can be determined entirely by measuring angles, distances and their rates on the surface itself, without further reference to the particular way in which the surface is embedded in the ambient $3$-dimensional Euclidean space. Thus the Gaussian curvature is an intrinsic invariant of a surface.

label: Thurston's Geometrization Conjecture
snippet: When a topological manifold of dimension $3$ has been split into its connected sum and the Jaco-Shalen-Johannson torus decomposition, the remaining components each admit exactly one of the following geometries: $(1): \quad$ Euclidean geometry $(2): \quad$ Hyperbolic geometry $(3): \quad$ Spherical geometry $(4): \quad$ The geometry of $\mathbb S^2 \times \R$ $(5): \quad$ The geometry of $\mathbb H^2 \times \R$ $(6): \quad$ The geometry of the universal cover $S L_2 \R^~$ of the Lie group $S L_2 \R$ $(7): \quad$ Nil geometry $(8): \quad$ Sol geometry where: $\mathbb S^2$ is the 2-sphere…

label: Tietze Extension Theorem
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is normal. Let $A \subseteq S$ be a closed set in $T$. Let $f: A \to \R$ be a continuous mapping from $A \subseteq S$ to the real number line under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then there exists a continuous extension $g: S \to \R$, that is, such that: $\forall s \in A: \map f s = \map g s$

label: Topological Closure is Closed
snippet: Let $T$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq T$. Then the closure $\map \cl H$ of $H$ is closed in $T$.

label: Topological Closure of Subset is Subset of Topological Closure
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq K$ and $K \subseteq S$. Then: $\map \cl H \subseteq \map \cl K$ where $\map \cl H$ denotes the closure of $H$.

label: Topological Equivalence of Definitions of Spectrum of Locale
snippet: Let $\struct{L, \preceq}$ be a locale.

label: Topological Product of Compact Spaces
snippet: Let $T_1$ and $T_2$ be topological spaces. Let $T_1 \times T_2$ be the product space of $T_1$ and $T_2$. Then $T_1 \times T_2$ is compact both $T_1$ and $T_2$ are compact.

label: Topological Space is Discrete iff All Points are Isolated
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. $\tau$ is the discrete topology on $S$ all points in $S$ are isolated points of $T$.

label: Topological Space is Neighborhood of all its Points
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $x \in S$. Then $S$ is a neighborhood of $x$.

label: Topological Space may be Empty
snippet: == Philosophical Position == Notwithstanding the result Empty Set Satisfies Topology Axioms, it is frequently stipulated in the literature that the class of topological spaces does not include the empty set. This convention is sufficiently commonplace as to be often omitted in published texts, and taken for granted. When it is mentioned, it is usually given as an afterthought. However, there exists a philosophical position that disallowing the empty topological space is unhelpful, and even harmful.

label: Topological Subspace is Topological Space
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $H \subseteq X$ be a non-empty subset of $X$. Let $\tau_H = \set {U \cap H: U \in \tau}$ be the subspace topology on $H$. Then the topological subspace $\struct {H, \tau_H}$ is a topological space.

label: Topological Vector Space as Union of Dilations of Open Neighborhood of Origin
snippet: Let $\Bbb F \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\Bbb F$. Let $V$ be an open neighborhood of ${\mathbf 0}_X$. Let $\sequence {r_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of positive real numbers such that $r_n \to \infty$. Then: $\ds X = \bigcup_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty r_n V$ where $r_n V$ denotes the dilation of $V$ by $r_n$.

label: Topology Defined by Closed Sets
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Let $\tau$ be a set of subsets of $S$. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $S$ : $(1): \quad$ Any intersection of arbitrarily many closed sets of $S$ under $\tau$ is a closed set of $S$ under $\tau$ $(2): \quad$ The union of any finite number of closed sets of $S$ under $\tau$ is a closed set of $S$ under $\tau$ $(3): \quad S$ and $\O$ are both closed sets of $S$ under $\tau$ where a closed set $V$ of $S$ under $\tau$ is defined as a subset of $S$ such that $S \setminus V \in \tau$.

label: Topology forms Complete Lattice
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then $\struct {\tau, \subseteq}$ is a complete lattice.

label: Total Probability Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\set {B_1, B_2, \ldots}$ be a partition of $\Omega$ such that $\forall i: \map \Pr {B_i} > 0$. Then: $\ds \forall A \in \Sigma: \map \Pr A = \sum_i \condprob A {B_i} \map \Pr {B_i}$

label: Totally Disconnected and Locally Connected Space is Discrete
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is both totally disconnected and locally connected. Then $T$ is the discrete space on $S$.

label: Totally Separated Space is Totally Disconnected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is totally separated. Then $T$ is totally disconnected.

label: Tower Property of Conditional Expectation
snippet: Let $\struct {\Omega, \Sigma, \Pr}$ be a probability space. Let $\HH \subseteq \GG$ be sub-$\sigma$-algebras of $\Sigma$. Let $X$ be a integrable random variable. Let $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\GG$. Let $\expect {X \mid \HH}$ be a version of the conditional expectation of $X$ given $\HH$. Let $\expect {\expect {X \mid \GG} \mid \HH}$ be a a version of the conditional expectation of $\expect {X \mid \GG}$ given $\HH$. Then: $\expect {\expect {X \mid \GG} \mid \HH} = \expect {X \mid \HH}$ almost everywhere.

label: Transitive Law
snippet: The transitive law is the statement that the usual ordering on the real numbers is a transitive relation. Let $a, b, c \in \R$ such that $a > b$ and $b > c$. Then: $a > c$

label: Transitive Set is Proper Subset of Ordinal iff Element of Ordinal
snippet: Let $A$ be an ordinal. Let $B$ be a transitive set. Then: $B \subsetneq A \iff B \in A$

label: Translation of Index Variable of Product
snippet: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j = \prod_{\map R {c \mathop + j} } a_{c \mathop + j} = \prod_{\map R {c \mathop - j} } a_{c \mathop - j}$ where: $\ds \prod_{\map R j} a_j$ denotes the product over $a_j$ for all $j$ that satisfy the propositional function $\map R j$ $c$ is an integer constant which is not dependent upon $j$.

label: Translation of Index Variable of Summation
snippet: Let $R: \Z \to \set {\T, \F}$ be a propositional function on the set of integers. Let $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j$ denote a summation over $R$. Then: $\ds \sum_{\map R j} a_j = \sum_{\map R {c \mathop + j} } a_{c \mathop + j} = \sum_{\map R {c \mathop - j} } a_{c \mathop - j}$ where $c$ is an integer constant which is not dependent upon $j$.

label: Translation of Integer Interval is Bijection
snippet: Let $a, b, c \in \Z$ be integers. Let $\closedint a b$ denote the integer interval between $a$ and $b$. Then the mapping $T: \closedint a b \to \closedint {a + c} {b + c}$ defined as: $\map T k = k + c$ is a bijection.

label: Translation of Open Set in Topological Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological vector space. Let $U \subseteq X$ be an open set. Let $x \in X$. Then: $U + x$ is open.

label: Transpose of Matrix Product
snippet: Let $\mathbf A$ and $\mathbf B$ be matrices over a commutative ring such that $\mathbf A \mathbf B$ is defined. Then $\mathbf B^\intercal \mathbf A^\intercal$ is defined, and: $\paren {\mathbf A \mathbf B}^\intercal = \mathbf B^\intercal \mathbf A^\intercal$ where $\mathbf X^\intercal$ is the transpose of $\mathbf X$.

label: Trapezium Rule for Definite Integrals
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is integrable on the closed interval $\closedint a b$. Let $P = \set {x_0, x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{n - 1}, x_n}$ form a normal subdivision of $\closedint a b$: $\forall i \in \set {1, 2, \ldots, n}: x_i - x_{i - 1} = \dfrac {b - a} n$ Then the definite integral of $f$ $x$ from $a$ to $b$ can be approximated as: $\ds \int_a^b \map f x \rd x \approx \dfrac h 2 \paren {\map f {x_0} + \map f {x_n} + \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^{n - 1} 2 \map f {x_i} }$ where $h = \dfrac {b - a} n$.

label: Triangle Angle-Side-Angle Congruence
snippet: If two triangles have: two angles equal to two angles, respectively the sides between the two angles equal then the remaining angles are equal, and the remaining sides equal the respective sides. That is to say, if two pairs of angles and the included sides are equal, then the triangles are congruent.

label: Triangle Inequality for Integrals
snippet: Let $\struct {X, \Sigma, \mu}$ be a measure space. Let $f: X \to \overline \R$ be a $\mu$-integrable function. Then: $\ds \size {\int_X f \rd \mu} \le \int_X \size f \rd \mu$

label: Triangle Right-Angle-Hypotenuse-Side Congruence
snippet: If two right triangles have: their hypotenuses equal another of their respective sides equal they will also have: their third sides equal the remaining two angles equal to their respective remaining angles.

label: Triangle Side-Angle-Angle Congruence
snippet: If two triangles have: two angles equal to two angles, respectively the sides opposite one pair of equal angles equal then the remaining angles are equal, and the remaining sides equal the respective sides. That is to say, if two pairs of angles and a pair of opposite sides are equal, then the triangles are congruent.

label: Triangle Side-Angle-Side Congruence
snippet: If $2$ triangles have: $2$ sides equal to $2$ sides respectively the angles contained by the equal straight lines equal they will also have: their third sides equal the remaining two angles equal to their respective remaining angles, namely, those which the equal sides subtend.

label: Triangle Side-Side-Side Congruence
snippet: Let two triangles have all $3$ sides equal. Then they also have all $3$ angles equal. Thus two triangles whose sides are all equal are themselves congruent.

label: Triangle with Two Equal Angles is Isosceles
snippet: If a triangle has two angles equal to each other, the sides which subtend the equal angles will also be equal to one another. Hence, by definition, such a triangle will be isosceles.

label: Triangles with Equal Base and Same Height have Equal Area
Triangles with One Equal Angle and Two Sides Proportional are Similar
snippet: Let two triangles have two corresponding sides which are proportional. Let the angles adjacent to both of these sides be equal. Then all of their corresponding angles are equal. Thus, by definition, such triangles are similar.

label: Triangles with Two Equal Angles are Similar
snippet: Two triangles which have two corresponding angles which are equal are similar.

label: Trisecting the Angle
snippet: == Classic Problem == Trisecting the angle is dividing a given angle into three equal parts.

label: Trivial Relation is Equivalence
snippet: The trivial relation on $S$: $\RR = S \times S$ is always an equivalence in $S$.

label: Trivial Topological Space is Indiscrete
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a trivial topological space. Then $\tau$ is an indiscrete topology.

snippet: Let $\struct {G, \circ}$ be a group. Let $H$ be a subset of $G$. Then $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$ : {{item|(3):|$a \in H \implies a^{-1} \in H$.}} That is, $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a subgroup of $\struct {G, \circ}$ $\struct {H, \circ}$ is a $H$ be a nonempty subset of $G$ which is: closed under its operation and: closed under inversion.

Two Angles of Triangle are Less than Two Right Angles
Two Angles on Straight Line make Two Right Angles
Two Straight Lines make Equal Opposite Angles
Tychonoff's Theorem
snippet: Let $I$ be an indexing set. Let $\family {X_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be an indexed family of non-empty topological spaces. Let $\ds X = \prod_{i \mathop \in I} X_i$ be the corresponding product space. Then $X$ is compact each $X_i$ is compact.

label: URM Computable Function is Recursive
snippet: Every URM computable function is recursive.

label: Ultraconnected Space is Path-Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space which is ultraconnected. Then $T$ is path-connected.

label: Ultrafilter Lemma
snippet: Let $S$ be a set. Every filter on $S$ is contained in an ultrafilter on $S$.

label: Unary Representation of Natural Number
snippet: Let $x \in \N$ be a natural number. Then: $x = \map s {\map s {\dots \map s 0} }$ where there are $x$ applications of the successor mapping to the constant $0$.

label: Uncountable Discrete Space is not Lindelöf
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be an uncountable discrete topological space. Then $T$ is not a Lindelöf space.

label: Underlying Set of Topological Space is Clopen
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Then the underlying set $S$ of $T$ is both open and closed in $T$.

label: Uniform Limit Theorem
snippet: Let $\struct {M, d_M}$ and $\struct {N, d_N}$ be metric spaces. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ be a sequence of mappings from $M$ to $N$ such that: $(1): \quad \forall n \in \N: f_n$ is continuous at every point of $M$ $(2): \quad \sequence {f_n}$ converges uniformly to $f$ Then: $f$ is continuous at every point of $M$.

label: Uniform Limit of Analytic Functions is Analytic
snippet: Let $U$ be an open subset of $\C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}_{n \mathop \in \N}$ be a sequence of analytic functions $f_n : U \to \C$. Let $\sequence {f_n}$ converge locally uniformly to $f$ on $U$. Then $f$ is analytic.

label: Union Distributes over Intersection
snippet: Set union is distributive over set intersection: $R \cup \paren {S \cap T} = \paren {R \cup S} \cap \paren {R \cup T}$

label: Union from Synthetic Basis is Topology
snippet: Let $\BB$ be a synthetic basis on a set $X$. Let $\ds \tau = \set {\bigcup \AA: \AA \subseteq \BB}$. Then $\tau$ is a topology on $X$.

label: Union is Commutative
snippet: Set union is commutative: $S \cup T = T \cup S$

label: Union is Empty iff Sets are Empty
snippet: If the union of two sets is the empty set, then both are themselves empty: $S \cup T = \O \iff S = \O \land T = \O$

label: Union is Smallest Superset
snippet: Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be sets. Then $S_1 \cup S_2$ is the smallest set containing both $S_1$ and $S_2$. That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \iff \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

label: Union of Connected Sets with Common Point is Connected
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ be a family of connected sets of $T$. Let $\exists x \in \ds \bigcap \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$. Then $\ds \bigcup \family {B_\alpha}_{\alpha \mathop \in A}$ is a connected set of $T$.

label: Union of Disjoint Singletons is Doubleton
snippet: Let $\set a$ and $\set b$ be singletons such that $a \ne b$. Then: $\set a \cup \set b = \set {a, b}$

label: Union of Empty Set
snippet: Consider the set of sets $\mathbb S$ such that $\mathbb S$ is the empty set $\O$. Then the union of $\mathbb S$ is $\O$: $\mathbb S = \O \implies \bigcup \mathbb S = \O$

label: Union of Finite Sets is Finite
snippet: Let $S$ and $T$ be finite sets. Then $S \cup T$ is a finite set.

label: Union of Local Bases is Basis
snippet: Let $T = \struct {X, \tau}$ be a topological space. For each $x \in X$, let $\BB_x$ be a local basis at $x$ which consists entirely of open sets. Then $\ds \BB = \bigcup_{x \mathop \in X} \BB_x$ is a basis for the topology $\tau$.

label: Union of Open Sets of Metric Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {A, d}$ be a metric space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

label: Union of Open Sets of Normed Vector Space is Open
snippet: Let $M = \struct {X, \norm {\, \cdot \,} }$ be a normed vector space. The union of a set of open sets of $M$ is open in $M$.

label: Union of Ordinals is Least Upper Bound
snippet: Let $A \subset \On$. That is, let $A$ be a class of ordinals (every member of $A$ is an ordinal). Then $\bigcup A$, the union of $A$, is the least upper bound of $A$: $\ds \forall x \in A: x \le A$ $\ds \forall y \in A: y \le x \implies \bigcup A \le x$

label: Union of Set of Ordinals is Ordinal
snippet: Let $A$ be a set of ordinals. Then $\bigcup A$ is an ordinal.

label: Union of Singleton
snippet: Consider the set of sets $A$ such that $A$ consists of just one set $x$: $A = \set x$ Then the union of $A$ is $x$: $\bigcup A = x$

label: Union of Subsets is Subset
snippet: Let $S_1$, $S_2$, and $T$ be sets. Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ both be subsets of $T$. Then: $S_1 \cup S_2 \subseteq T$ That is: $\paren {S_1 \subseteq T} \land \paren {S_2 \subseteq T} \implies \paren {S_1 \cup S_2} \subseteq T$

label: Union of Two Compact Sets is Compact
snippet: Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological spaces. Let $H$ and $K$ be compact subsets of $T$. Then $H \cup K$ is compact in $T$.

label: Union with Complement
snippet: The union of a set and its complement is the universal set: $S \cup \map \complement S = \mathbb U$

label: Union with Empty Set
snippet: The union of any set with the empty set is the set itself: $S \cup \O = S$

label: Union with Relative Complement
snippet: The union of a set $T$ and its relative complement in $S$ is the set $S$: $\relcomp S T \cup T = S$

label: Union with Superset is Superset
snippet: $S \subseteq T \iff S \cup T = T$ where: $S \subseteq T$ denotes that $S$ is a subset of $T$ $S \cup T$ denotes the union of $S$ and $T$.

label: Unique Code for URM Instruction
snippet: Each basic instruction $I$ in a URM Program can be identified with a unique code number $\beta \left({I}\right)$. We also define the following sets: $\operatorname{Zinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Zero instructions $\operatorname{Sinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Successor instructions $\operatorname{Cinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Copy instructions $\operatorname{Jinstr}$ is the set of codes of all the Jump instructions. Then we define $\operatorname{Instr}$ to be the set of codes of all basic URM instructions.

label: Unique Code for URM Program
snippet: Any URM program can be assigned a unique code number.

label: Unique Point of Minimal Distance to Closed Convex Subset of Hilbert Space
snippet: Let $H$ be a Hilbert space, and let $h \in H$. Let $K \subseteq H$ be a closed, convex, non-empty subset of $H$. Then there is a unique point $k_0 \in K$ such that: $\norm {h - k_0} = \map d {h, K}$ where $d$ denotes distance to a set.

u G$ $(4):\quad  orall n \in \N: \map \mu {G_n}$ is finite Then: $\mu =

label: Unit Matrix is Identity for Matrix Multiplication
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\map {\MM_R} n$ denote the metric space of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. Let $\mathbf I_n$ denote the unit matrix of order $n$: Then: $\forall \mathbf A \in \map {\MM_R} n: \mathbf A \mathbf I_n = \mathbf A = \mathbf I_n \mathbf A$ That is, the unit matrix $\mathbf I_n$ is the identity element for (conventional) matrix multiplication over $\map {\MM_R} n$.

label: Unit Matrix is Unity of Ring of Square Matrices
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity whose zero is $0_R$ and whose unity is $1_R$. Let $n \in \Z_{>0}$ be a (strictly) positive integer. Let $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$ denote the ring of square matrices of order $n$ over $R$. The unit matrix over $R$: $\mathbf I_n = \begin {pmatrix} 1_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 1_R & 0_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ 0_R & 0_R & 1_R & \cdots & 0_R \\ \vdots & \vdots & \vdots & \ddots & \vdots \\ 0_R & 0_R & 0_R & \cdots & 1_R \end {pmatrix}$ is the identity element of $\struct {\map {\MM_R} n, +, \times}$.

label: Unity of Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

label: Unity of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with unity $1_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{R^S} : S \to R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{R^S}} s = 1_R$.

label: Unity of Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the unity of $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $1_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {1_{\R^S}} s = 1$.

label: Universal Property of Free Module on Set
snippet: Let $R$ be a ring with unity. Let $R^{\paren I}$ be the free $R$-module on $I$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $\family {m_i}_{i \mathop \in I}$ be a family of elements of $M$. Then there exists a unique $R$-module morphism: $\Psi: R^{\paren I} \to M$ that sends the $i$th canonical basis element to $m_i$, for all $i \in I$. Moreover: $\ds \map \Psi {\family {r_i}_{i \mathop \in I} } = \sum_{i \mathop \in I} r_i m_i$

label: Universal Property of Polynomial Ring
snippet: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unity. The different definitions of a polynomial ring $\struct {\map R x, \iota, x}$ on $R$ satisfy the universal property of a polynomial ring:

label: Unsigned Stirling Number of the First Kind of n with n-1
snippet: Let $n \in \Z_{> 0}$ be an integer greater than $0$. Then: $\ds {n \brack n - 1} = \binom n 2$ where: $\ds {n \brack n - 1}$ denotes an unsigned Stirling number of the first kind $\dbinom n 2$ denotes a binomial coefficient.

label: Upper Bound of Natural Logarithm
snippet: Let $\ln x$ be the natural logarithm of $x$ where $x \in \R_{>0}$. Then: $\ln x \le x - 1$

label: Upper Closure is Upper Section
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \preceq}$ be an ordered set. Let $T$ be a subset of $S$. Let $U$ be the upper closure of $T$. Then $U$ is an upper section.

label: Urysohn's Lemma
snippet: == Lemma == Let $T = \struct {S, \tau}$ be a $T_4$ topological space. Let $A, B \subseteq S$ be closed sets of $T$ such that $A \cap B = \O$. Then there exists an Urysohn function for $A$ and $B$.

label: Valuation Ring of Non-Archimedean Division Ring is Subring
snippet:
Let $\struct {R, 
orm{\,\cdot\,}}$ be a non-Archimedean normed division ring with zero $0_R$ and unity $1_R$. Let $\OO$ be the valuation ring induced by the non-Archimedean norm $
orm {\,\cdot\,}$, that is: $\OO = \set {x \in R : 
orm{x} \le 1}$ Then $\OO$ is a subring of $R$: with a unity: $1_R$ in which there are no (proper) zero divisors, that is: $ orall x, y \in \OO: x \circ y = 0_R \implies x = 0_R 	ext{ or } y = 0_R$

label: Valuation Ring of P-adic Norm on Rationals
snippet:
Let $
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p$ be the $p$-adic norm on the rationals $\Q$ for some prime $p$. The induced valuation ring on $\struct {\Q,
orm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ is the set: $\OO = \Z_{\paren p} = \set {\dfrac a b \in \Q : p 
mid b}$

label: Variance as Expectation of Square minus Square of Expectation
snippet: Let $X$ be a random variable. Then the variance of $X$ can be expressed as: $\var X = \expect {X^2} - \paren {\expect X}^2$ That is, it is the expectation of the square of $X$ minus the square of the expectation of $X$.

label: Variance of Binomial Distribution
snippet: Let $X$ be a discrete random variable with the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. Then the variance of $X$ is given by: $\var X = n p \paren {1 - p}$

label: Vector Cross Product is Anticommutative
snippet: The vector cross product is anticommutative: $\forall \mathbf a, \mathbf b \in \R^3: \mathbf a \times \mathbf b = -\paren {\mathbf b \times \mathbf a}$

label: Vector Field is Expressible as Gradient of Scalar Field iff Conservative
snippet: Let $R$ be a region of space. Let $\mathbf V$ be a vector field acting over $R$. Then $\mathbf V$ can be expressed as the gradient of some scalar field $F$ $\mathbf V$ is a conservative vector field.

label: Vector Inverse is Negative Vector
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$ and whose unity is $1_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: -\mathbf v = -1_F \ast \mathbf v$

label: Vector Scaled by Zero is Zero Vector
snippet: Let $F$ be a field whose zero is $0_F$. Let $\struct {\mathbf V, +, \ast}_F$ be a vector space over $F$, as defined by the vector space axioms. Then: $\forall \mathbf v \in \mathbf V: 0_F \ast \mathbf v = \bszero$

label: Vector Space has Basis
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $V$ be a vector space over $K$. Then $V$ has a basis.

label: Vector Space has Basis Between Linearly Independent Set and Finite Spanning Set
snippet: Let $K$ be a division ring. Let $G$ be a finitely generated $K$-vector space. Let $H$ be a linearly independent subset of $G$. Let $F$ be a finite generator for $G$ such that $H \subseteq F$. Then there is a basis $B$ for $G$ such that $H \subseteq B \subseteq F$.

label: Vector Space on Field Extension is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {K, +, \times}$ be a field. Let $L / K$ be a field extension over $K$. Let $\struct {L, +, \times}_K$ be the a vector space of $L$ over $K$. Then $\struct {L, +, \times}_K$ is a vector space.

label: Vector Space over Division Subring is Vector Space
snippet: Let $\struct {L, +_L, \times_L}$ be a division ring. Let $K$ be a division subring of $\struct {L, +_L, \times_L}$. Let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ}_L$ be a $L$-vector space. Let $\circ_K$ be the restriction of $\circ$ to $K \times G$. Hence let $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_K}_K$ be the vector space induced by $K$. Then $\struct {G, +_G, \circ_k}_k$ is indeed a $K$-vector space.

label: Vertical Section of Continuous Function is Continuous
snippet: Let $X$, $Y$ and $T$ be topological spaces. Equip the Cartesian product $X \times Y$ with the product topology. Let $f : X \times Y \to T$ be a continuous mapping. Let $x \in X$. Then the $x$-vertical section $f_x : Y \to T$ is continuous.

label: Viète's Formulas
snippet: Let $P_n$ be a polynomial of degree $n$ with real or complex coefficients: {{eqn | l = \map {P_n} x | r = \sum_{i \mathop = 0}^n a_i x^i }} {{eqn | r = a_n x^n + a_{n - 1} x^{n - 1} + \dotsb + a_1 x + a_0 }} where $a_n \ne 0$. Let $z_1, \ldots, z_n$ be the roots of $P_n$ (be they real or complex), not assumed distinct.

label: Von Neumann Construction of Natural Numbers is Minimally Inductive
snippet: Let $\omega$ denote the set of natural numbers as defined by the von Neumann construction. $\omega$ is a minimally inductive class under the successor mapping.

label: Wallis's Product
snippet: {{eqn | l = \prod_{n \mathop = 1}^\infty \frac {2 n} {2 n - 1} \cdot \frac {2 n} {2 n + 1} | r = \frac 2 1 \cdot \frac 2 3 \cdot \frac 4 3 \cdot \frac 4 5 \cdot \frac 6 5 \cdot \frac 6 7 \cdot \frac 8 7 \cdot \frac 8 9 \cdots | c = }} This is called Wallis's product.

label: Weak-* Topology is Hausdorff
snippet: Let $\GF \in \set {\R, \C}$. Let $X$ be a topological vector space over $\GF$. Let $X^\ast$ be the topological dual space of $X$. Let $w^\ast$ be the weak-$\ast$ topology on $X^\ast$. Then $\struct {X^\ast, w^\ast}$ is Hausdorff space.

label: Wedderburn's Theorem
snippet: Every finite division ring $D$ is a field.

label: Weierstrass's Theorem
snippet: There exists a real function $f: \closedint 0 1 \to \closedint 0 1$ such that: $(1): \quad f$ is continuous $(2): \quad f$ is nowhere differentiable.

label: Weierstrass Factorization Theorem
snippet: Let $f$ be an entire function. Let $0$ be a zero of $f$ of multiplicity $m \ge 0$. Let the sequence $\sequence {a_n}$ consist of the nonzero zeroes of $f$, repeated according to multiplicity.

label: Weierstrass M-Test
snippet: Let $f_n$ be a sequence of real functions defined on a domain $D \subseteq \R$. Let $\ds \sup_{x \mathop \in D} \size {\map {f_n} x} \le M_n$ for each integer $n$ and some constants $M_n$ Let $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty M_i < \infty$. Then $\ds \sum_{i \mathop = 1}^\infty f_i$ converges uniformly on $D$.

label: Well-Defined Mapping/Motivation
snippet: == Motivation for Well-Defined Mapping == Suppose we are given a mapping $f: S \to T$. Suppose we have an equivalence $\RR$ on $S$, and we want to define a mapping on the quotient set: $\phi: S / \RR \to T$ such that: $\map \phi {\eqclass \cdots \RR} = \map f \cdots$ That is, we want every element of a given equivalence class to map to the same element of the codomain of $f$. The only way this can be done is to set $\map \phi {\eqclass x \RR} = \map f x$.

label: Well-Ordered Class is not Isomorphic to Initial Segment
snippet: Let $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ be a well-ordered class. There exists no order isomorphism from $\struct {A, \preccurlyeq}$ to an initial segment of $A$.

label: Well-Ordering Principle
snippet: Every non-empty subset of $\N$ has a smallest (or first) element. That is, the relational structure $\struct {\N, \le}$ on the set of natural numbers $\N$ under the usual ordering $\le$ forms a well-ordered set. This is called the well-ordering principle.

label: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
snippet: == Unsolved Problem == To establish rigorously: the Yang-Mills quantum theory the mass of the least massive particle of the force field is strictly positive (that is, the mass of each type of elementary particle is bounded below by a strictly positive value).

label: Young's Inequality for Products
snippet: Let $p, q \in \R_{> 0}$ be strictly positive real numbers such that: $\dfrac 1 p + \dfrac 1 q = 1$ Then: $\forall a, b \in \R_{\ge 0}: a b \le \dfrac {a^p} p + \dfrac {b^q} q$ Equality occurs : $b = a^{p - 1}$

label: Zermelo's Well-Ordering Theorem
snippet: Let the Axiom of Choice be accepted. Then every set is well-orderable.

label: Zero Choose n
snippet: $\dbinom 0 n = \delta_{0 n}$ where: $\dbinom 0 n$ denotes a binomial coefficient $\delta_{0 n}$ denotes the Kronecker delta.

label: Zero Derivative implies Constant Function
snippet: Let $f$ be a real function which is continuous on the closed interval $\closedint a b$ and differentiable on the open interval $\openint a b$. Suppose that: $\forall x \in \openint a b: \map {f'} x = 0$ Then $f$ is constant on $\closedint a b$.

label: Zero Matrix is Identity for Hadamard Product
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \cdot}$ be a monoid whose identity is $e$. Let $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix space over $S$. Let $\mathbf e = \sqbrk e_{m n}$ be the zero matrix of $\map {\MM_S} {m, n}$. Then $\mathbf e$ is the identity element for Hadamard product.

label: Zero is Limit Point of Integer Reciprocal Space
snippet: Let $A \subseteq \R$ be the set of all points on $\R$ defined as: $A := \set {\dfrac 1 n : n \in \Z_{>0} }$ Let $\struct {A, \tau_d}$ be the integer reciprocal space under the usual (Euclidean) topology. Then $0$ is the only limit point of $A$ in $\R$.

label: Zero of Ring of Bounded Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of bounded continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map {C^*} {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{\R^S}} s = 0$

label: Zero of Ring of Continuous Mappings
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau_{_S} }$ be a topological space. Let $\struct {R, +, *, \tau_{_R} }$ be a topological ring with zero $0_R$. Let $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous mappings from $S$ to $R$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map C {S, R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{R^S} : S \to R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{R^S}} s = 0_R$

label: Zero of Ring of Continuous Real-Valued Functions
snippet: Let $\struct {S, \tau}$ be a topological space. Let $\R$ denote the real number line. Let $\struct {\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ be the ring of continuous real-valued functions from $S$. Then: the zero of $\struct{\map C {S, \R}, +, *}$ is the constant mapping $0_{\R^S} : S \to \R$ defined by: $\forall s \in S : \map {0_{\R^S}} s = 0$

label: Zero to the Power of Zero
snippet: == Examples == In light of some mathematicians' (or, indeed, muggles') reticence to define the zeroth power of zero as $1$, the following are examples of reasons why defining $0^0 = 1$ is a good idea.

label: sets-lemma-coverings-site
snippet: With notations as above. Let $\text{Cov}_0 \subset \text{Cov}(\mathcal{C})$ be a set contained in $\text{Cov}(\mathcal{C})$. There exist a cardinal $\kappa$ and a limit ordinal $\alpha$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item We have $\text{Cov}_0 \subset \text{Cov}(\mathcal{C})_{\kappa, \alpha}$. \item The set of coverings $\text{Cov}(\mathcal{C})_{\kappa, \alpha}$ satisfies (1), (2), and (3) of Sites, Definition \ref{sites-definition-site} (see above). In other words $(\mathcal{C}, \text{Cov}(\mathcal{C})_{\kappa, \alpha})$ is a site.

label: sets-lemma-abelian-injectives
snippet: Suppose given a big category $\mathcal{A}$ (see Categories, Remark \ref{categories-remark-big-categories}). Assume $\mathcal{A}$ is abelian and has enough injectives. See Homology, Definitions \ref{homology-definition-abelian-category} and \ref{homology-definition-enough-injectives}. Then for any given set of objects $\{A_s\}_{s\in S}$ of $\mathcal{A}$, there is an abelian subcategory $\mathcal{A}' \subset \mathcal{A}$ with the following properties: \begin{enumerate} \item the inclusion functor $\mathcal{A}' \to \mathcal{A}$ is exact, \item $\Ob(\mathcal{A}')$ is a set, \item…

label: categories-definition-category
snippet: A {\it category} $\mathcal{C}$ consists of the following data: \begin{enumerate} \item A set of objects $\Ob(\mathcal{C})$. \item For each pair $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ a set of morphisms $\Mor_\mathcal{C}(x, y)$. \item For each triple $x, y, z\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ a composition map $ \Mor_\mathcal{C}(y, z) \times \Mor_\mathcal{C}(x, y) \to \Mor_\mathcal{C}(x, z) $, denoted $(\phi, \psi) \mapsto \phi \circ \psi$.

label: categories-definition-isomorphism
snippet: A morphism $\phi : x \to y$ is an {\it isomorphism} of the category $\mathcal{C}$ if there exists a morphism $\psi : y \to x$ such that $\phi \circ \psi = \text{id}_y$ and $\psi \circ \phi = \text{id}_x$.

label: categories-example-group-groupoid
snippet: A group $G$ gives rise to a groupoid with a single object $x$ and morphisms $\Mor(x, x) = G$, with the composition rule given by the group law in $G$. Every groupoid with a single object is of this form.

label: categories-example-set-groupoid
snippet: A set $C$ gives rise to a groupoid $\mathcal{C}$ defined as follows: As objects we take $\Ob(\mathcal{C}) := C$ and for morphisms we take $\Mor(x, y)$ empty if $x\neq y$ and equal to $\{\text{id}_x\}$ if $x = y$.

label: categories-definition-functor
snippet: A {\it functor} $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ between two categories $\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B}$ is given by the following data: \begin{enumerate} \item A map $F : \Ob(\mathcal{A}) \to \Ob(\mathcal{B})$. \item For every $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ a map $F : \Mor_\mathcal{A}(x, y) \to \Mor_\mathcal{B}(F(x), F(y))$, denoted $\phi \mapsto F(\phi)$.

label: categories-definition-faithful
snippet: Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor. \begin{enumerate} \item We say $F$ is {\it faithful} if for any objects $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ the map $$ F : \Mor_\mathcal{A}(x, y) \to \Mor_\mathcal{B}(F(x), F(y)) $$ is injective. \item If these maps are all bijective then $F$ is called {\it fully faithful}. \item The functor $F$ is called {\it essentially surjective} if for any object $y \in \Ob(\mathcal{B})$ there exists an object $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ such that $F(x)$ is isomorphic to $y$ in $\mathcal{B}$. \end{enumerate}

label: categories-definition-subcategory
snippet: A {\it subcategory} of a category $\mathcal{B}$ is a category $\mathcal{A}$ whose objects and arrows form subsets of the objects and arrows of $\mathcal{B}$ and such that source, target and composition in $\mathcal{A}$ agree with those of $\mathcal{B}$ and such that the identity morphism of an object of $\mathcal{A}$ matches the one in $\mathcal{B}$. We say $\mathcal{A}$ is a {\it full subcategory} of $\mathcal{B}$ if $\Mor_\mathcal{A}(x, y) = \Mor_\mathcal{B}(x, y)$ for all $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{A})$.

label: categories-example-group-homomorphism-functor
snippet: A homomorphism $p : G\to H$ of groups gives rise to a functor between the associated groupoids in Example \ref{example-group-groupoid}. It is faithful (resp.\ fully faithful) if and only if $p$ is injective (resp.\ an isomorphism).

label: categories-example-category-over-X
snippet: Given a category $\mathcal{C}$ and an object $X\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ we define the {\it category of objects over $X$}, denoted $\mathcal{C}/X$ as follows. The objects of $\mathcal{C}/X$ are morphisms $Y\to X$ for some $Y\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Morphisms between objects $Y\to X$ and $Y'\to X$ are morphisms $Y\to Y'$ in $\mathcal{C}$ that make the obvious diagram commute. Note that there is a functor $p_X : \mathcal{C}/X\to \mathcal{C}$ which simply forgets the morphism.

label: categories-definition-equivalence-categories
snippet: An {\it equivalence of categories} $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ is a functor such that there exists a functor $G : \mathcal{B} \to \mathcal{A}$ such that the compositions $F \circ G$ and $G \circ F$ are isomorphic to the identity functors $\text{id}_\mathcal{B}$, respectively $\text{id}_\mathcal{A}$. In this case we say that $G$ is a {\it quasi-inverse} to $F$.

label: categories-definition-product-category
snippet: Let $\mathcal{A}$, $\mathcal{B}$ be categories. We define the {\it product category} $\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}$ to be the category with objects $\Ob(\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}) = \Ob(\mathcal{A}) \times \Ob(\mathcal{B})$ and $$ \Mor_{\mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{B}}((x, y), (x', y')) := \Mor_\mathcal{A}(x, x')\times \Mor_\mathcal{B}(y, y'). $$ Composition is defined componentwise.

label: categories-definition-opposite
snippet: Given a category $\mathcal{C}$ the {\it opposite category} $\mathcal{C}^{opp}$ is the category with the same objects as $\mathcal{C}$ but all morphisms reversed.

label: categories-example-hom-functor
snippet: Functor of points. For any $U\in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ there is a contravariant functor $$ \begin{matrix} h_U & : & \mathcal{C} & \longrightarrow & \textit{Sets} \\ & & X & \longmapsto & \Mor_\mathcal{C}(X, U) \end{matrix} $$ which takes an object $X$ to the set $\Mor_\mathcal{C}(X, U)$. In other words $h_U$ is a presheaf. Given a morphism $f : X\to Y$ the corresponding map $h_U(f) : \Mor_\mathcal{C}(Y, U)\to \Mor_\mathcal{C}(X, U)$ takes $\phi$ to $\phi\circ f$. We will always denote this presheaf $h_U : \mathcal{C}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.

label: categories-lemma-yoneda
snippet: [Yoneda lemma] Let $U, V \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$. Given any morphism of functors $s : h_U \to h_V$ there is a unique morphism $\phi : U \to V$ such that $h(\phi) = s$. In other words the functor $h$ is fully faithful. More generally, given any contravariant functor $F$ and any object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$ we have a natural bijection $$ \Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(h_U, F) \longrightarrow F(U), \quad s \longmapsto s_U(\text{id}_U). $$

label: categories-definition-representable-functor
snippet: A contravariant functor $F : \mathcal{C}\to \textit{Sets}$ is said to be {\it representable} if it is isomorphic to the functor of points $h_U$ for some object $U$ of $\mathcal{C}$.

label: categories-definition-has-products-of-pairs
snippet: We say the category $\mathcal{C}$ {\it has products of pairs of objects} if a product $x \times y$ exists for any $x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$.

label: categories-definition-has-fibre-products
